docs.title: GAMPredictionResult
docs.text:
GAMPredictionResult is returned by fit(..., result="prediction"). It is the only result of the streamed, discretized and operator routes, and is also available on the dense route. It is a small, picklable object: it keeps the coefficients, the fitted family, what prediction needs, and scalar diagnostics, but no training rows, no per-smooth EDF and, by default, no covariance. It has no summary() or plot().

Method What it does predict(newdata, pred_type="response", se_fit=False, offset=None) Predicts one batch of new data. se_fit=True needs FitControl(uncertainty="fisher") or "covariance", otherwise RuntimeError. An output larger than output_budget_bytes, or a workspace larger than memory_budget_bytes, raises MemoryError and suggests predict_iter(). predict_iter(source, batch_rows=None, *, pred_type="response", se_fit=False) Yields (row_positions, prediction) pairs, or (row_positions, (prediction, se)) with se_fit=True, for a row source. batch_rows=None uses FitControl.batch_rows. The source's offsets are applied. It raises RuntimeError if the source changes during the replay. predict_matrix(newdata) The constrained prediction matrix for one batch, subject to the same budgets. to_predictor() Returns the GAMPredictor the result holds. bulk_link_variance(...) Approximate link-scale variances for an operator result. See Approximate variances. Raises RuntimeError on other routes. materialize_covariance(memory_budget_bytes) Builds Vp from a retained Fisher factor, within the given budget. Raises RuntimeError when no factor was kept (uncertainty="none").

Attributes worth reading:

Attribute What it holds coefficients, family, formula The fitted coefficients, the family with its fitted link and theta, and the formula. converged, n_iter, convergence_info Whether and how the fit stopped. execution_route, execution_path, lambda_strategy, execution_fallback_reason Which route and smoothing selection ran, and why a Gaussian QR request was not met. deviance, score, scale, score_scale, theta, smoothing_params, edf_total, n Fit summaries. score, edf_total and scale can be None on the operator route. source_scans, batches_scanned, known_workspace_bytes Work and planned memory of the fit, excluding the setup pass. None on the dense route. optimizer_diagnostics, exact_optimizer_diagnostics, operator_diagnostics Route-specific optimizer records, None where they do not apply. smoothing_strategy, discretization_strategy, prediction_policy, discretization, working_model_proposal_evaluations, fit_peak_bytes, fit_memory_budget_bytes Discretized route only. score_error_bound, score_bound_method Operator Fellner-Schall only.

Vp is not an attribute of this class. With uncertainty="covariance" it is on fit.to_predictor().Vp; with "fisher", call materialize_covariance().

fit = GAM(
    'y ~ z + s(x, bs="cr")',
    control=FitControl(execution="stream", linear_solver="qr", uncertainty="fisher"),
).fit(source, result="prediction")
for positions, (prediction, se) in fit.predict_iter(
    DataFrameRowSource(newdata), batch_rows=2, se_fit=True
):
    print(positions, prediction.round(3), se.round(3))

docs.title: GAMPredictionResult(_predictor: GAMPredictor, deviance: float, score: float | None, scale: float | None, theta: float | None, smoothing_params: np.ndarray, edf_total: float | None, converged: bool, n_iter: int, convergence_info: str, method: str, lambda_strategy: str, execution_path: str, n: int, _batch_rows: int = 65536, *, execution_route: str = 'dense', execution_fallback_reason: str | None = None, score_scale: float | None = None, score_error_bound: float | None = None, score_bound_method: str | None = None, source_scans: int | None = None, batches_scanned: int | None = None, known_workspace_bytes: int | None = None, optimizer_diagnostics: EFSOptimizerDiagnostics | None = None, exact_optimizer_diagnostics: StreamExactOptimizerDiagnostics | None = None, smoothing_strategy: str | None = None, discretization_strategy: str | None = None, prediction_policy: str | None = None, discretization: ContinuousDiscretizationMetadata | None = None, working_model_proposal_evaluations: int | None = None, fit_peak_bytes: int | None = None, fit_memory_budget_bytes: int | None = None, operator_diagnostics: OperatorFitDiagnostics | None = None, _operator_source_fingerprint: str | None = None, _operator_source_replay_digest: str | None = None, _operator_family_static_config: tuple[object, ...] | None = None, _operator_family_parameter_snapshot: FamilyParameterSnapshot | None = None) dataclass
docs.text:
Small, picklable result surface for bounded new-data prediction.

This deliberately has no training rows, setup, EDF vectors, or mandatory covariance. It retains only scalar convergence diagnostics and a frozen :class:GAMPredictor. Discrete fits also record prediction_policy and discretization: a bounded per-group/per-term record of the fitted compress.df grids whose size does not depend on n.

source_scans and batches_scanned count the complete source scans and batches read by the fit itself, excluding Phase-1 setup scans, on the streamed, discrete and operator routes alike (operator preparation is in operator_diagnostics.preparation_*). On a streamed Fellner--Schall fit they count the final fit only; optimizer_diagnostics has the scans of the whole search. known_workspace_bytes is the route's conservative known fit-workspace bound, excluding retained Phase-1 preparation (None on fixed-sp operator fits and on streamed Fellner--Schall fits); on the discrete route it covers the indexed design (host tables, device actions) and the solver workspace. Discrete fits additionally report fit_peak_bytes, which adds the retained compact setup tables and is the bound that route checks against fit_memory_budget_bytes (FitControl.memory_budget_bytes); the streamed routes have no counterpart because their prepared setup is budgeted separately during preparation.

Fixed-sp operator fits have score=None and edf_total=None, since no score or trace provider runs, and scale=None for unknown-scale families; known-scale families report their actual scale of one. Calibrated operator EFS fits report the selected score, its score_error_bound and edf_total. Other routes retain their existing numeric score, scale, and EDF.

docs.title: bulk_link_variance(training_source: RowSource, calibration_data: Data, *, probes: int, seed: int, memory_budget_bytes: int, control: PCGControl | None = None, scale: float | None = None, max_calibration_standard_errors: float = BULK_CALIBRATION_MAX_STANDARD_ERRORS) -> tuple[BulkOperatorVariance, BulkVarianceCalibration]
docs.text:
Build calibrated bulk Fisher uncertainty for an operator fit.

The result retains no training rows or source. The caller replays the original training source, whose fingerprint and row digest must match the accepted fit. The returned provider streams arbitrary prediction sources through estimate_iter and reports approximate link-scale variances with Monte Carlo errors and solver/source diagnostics. Unknown-scale families require an externally established scale. Selected calibration checks those rows only and does not bound unselected rows or iterative-solve bias. Each selected row's probes * estimate / exact is chi-square with probes degrees of freedom; the call raises when its equivalent standard normal deviate exceeds max_calibration_standard_errors in absolute value (the default 5 is a two-sided level of 5.7e-7 per row).

docs.title: GAMPredictor
docs.text:
GAMPredictor is the prediction-only core. Inference and prediction results hold one and return it from to_predictor(); GAMResults.to_predictor() builds a new one. It is a frozen dataclass whose coefficients and Vp are read-only copies; Vp is None when the fit kept no covariance. It has predict(newdata, pred_type="response", se_fit=False, offset=None), predict_matrix(newdata), predict_iter(source, batch_rows, *, pred_type="response", se_fit=False) (here batch_rows is required), freeze_request(newdata) and the prediction_policy property (the discretized prediction policy, None on other routes). It holds no training arrays.

import pickle

full = GAM("y ~ s(x) + s(z)").fit(data)
predictor = full.to_predictor()  # a new, independent core
restored = pickle.loads(pickle.dumps(predictor))
print(np.allclose(restored.predict(newdata), full.predict(newdata)))

True

full.to_predictor() does not change full; discard the full result if you no longer need its training state.

Use the standard library pickle for a same-version, short-lived handoff. A predictor that uses a locally defined custom link or family needs cloudpickle. A predictor records the jaxgam version that pickled it and warns (UserWarning) when loaded under another version; pickles are not a cross-version format, and only trusted pickles should be loaded. jaxgam has no save()/load() API or file format.

docs.title: GAMPredictor(coefficients: npt.NDArray[np.floating], Vp: npt.NDArray[np.floating] | None, family: ExponentialFamily, formula: str, offset_was_nonzero: bool, _predict_spec: PredictSpec, _fisher_factor: npt.NDArray[np.floating] | None = None, _fisher_qr_factor: PivotedQRFisherFactor | None = None, _fisher_transforms: tuple[tuple[int, int, str, npt.NDArray[np.floating]], ...] = (), _fisher_scale: float = 1.0, _output_budget_bytes: int | None = None, _memory_budget_bytes: int | None = None, _prediction_policy: str | None = None, _request_compression: RequestCompressionSpec | None = None, _operator_geometry: OperatorPredictionGeometry | None = None, _jaxgam_version: str = (lambda: jaxgam.__version__)()) dataclass
docs.text:
Lean, training-data-free prediction state for a fitted GAM.

This is an optional boundary object for consumers that should receive only predict() and predict_matrix() state. A GAMInferenceResult is already lean and directly usable; its to_predictor() simply returns the predictor it already contains.

Pickles are intended for trusted, same-version transient handoff. The coefficients and posterior covariance are defensively copied and exposed as read-only arrays.

Source offsets are applied positionally for every batch. This adapter deliberately delegates matrix construction and response/SE finishing to the normal prediction core, preserving factor and link semantics.

Under mgcv_predict_bamd the whole source is the prediction request: a bounded pre-pass scans it here, before the iterator is returned, and freezes predict.bamd's compression grid. Every yielded batch is compressed with that frozen grid, so results do not depend on batch_rows. The source must not change afterwards.

docs.title: Families
docs.text:
A family sets the response distribution and the link. Pass a name to GAM for the default link, or an instance for any other link:

from jaxgam.families import Binomial, Gamma, Gaussian, NegativeBinomial, Poisson

log_gamma = Gamma(link="log")
print(type(log_gamma.link).__name__, type(Poisson().link).__name__)

LogLink LogLink
Family Name for GAM Default link Links mgcv offers for it Scale Gaussian "gaussian" identity identity, log, inverse estimated Binomial "binomial" logit logit, probit, cloglog, log 1 Poisson "poisson" log log, identity, sqrt 1 Gamma "gamma" inverse inverse, identity, log estimated NegativeBinomial "nb" log log, identity, sqrt 1

Each constructor takes link=None (the default link), a link name or a Link instance; another type raises TypeError and an unknown name raises ValueError("Unknown link function ..."). The registered link names are identity, log, logit, inverse, probit, cloglog, sqrt and inverse_squared. The constructor does not check that the link suits the family. Use the links in the table: those are the combinations the routes are tested with, and each route section lists which of them it supports. The response must lie in the family's support (for example, in [0, 1] for Binomial), checked when the fit starts.

docs.title: Negative binomial
docs.text:
NegativeBinomial(theta=1.0, *, fixed=False, link=None) models overdispersed counts with variance mu + mu**2 / theta (theta is mgcv's size; it must be positive). With fixed=False, theta is estimated starting from theta; with fixed=True it is held at theta. family="nb" is NegativeBinomial().

estimated = GAM("count ~ s(x)", family="nb").fit(data)
held = GAM("count ~ s(x)", family=NegativeBinomial(theta=2, fixed=True)).fit(data)
print(round(estimated.theta, 2), held.theta)

3.88 None

Where the estimate is reported:

  • fit.theta is the estimated theta when theta is estimated.
  • For a fixed theta it is None on the dense and streamed routes with the default optimizer, and the fixed value under optimizer="efs" and on the discretized and operator routes. The fitted family always holds it: fit.family.get_theta(transformed=True).
  • The family passed to GAM is copied before an estimated-theta fit, so your instance is not changed.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default theta float

Dispersion parameter (must be positive). When fixed=False (default), this is the starting value for estimation. When fixed=True, theta is held constant during fitting. Default is 1.0.

1.0 fixed bool

If False (default), theta is estimated during fitting (n_theta = 1). If True, theta is held constant (n_theta = 0).

False link str or Link or None

Link function. Default is log. Supported: "log", "identity", "sqrt".

Examples:

>>> fam = NegativeBinomial()                    # estimate theta, start at 1
>>> fam = NegativeBinomial(theta=3)             # estimate theta, start at 3
>>> fam = NegativeBinomial(theta=2, fixed=True) # fix theta = 2

docs.title: deviance_resids(y: np.ndarray, mu: np.ndarray, wt: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray
docs.text:
Per-observation deviance residuals.

R: efam.r lines 199-205.

Unit deviance: 2 * wt * [y * log(max(1,y)/mu) - (y+theta) * log1p((y-mu)/(mu+theta))]

The log1p rewrite avoids catastrophic cancellation when theta is large and (y+theta)/(mu+theta) ≈ 1.

docs.title: Formula syntax
docs.text:
Formulas follow R's notation for mgcv::gam:

formulas = [
    "y ~ s(x)",                     # one smooth (thin plate)
    "y ~ s(x) + z",                 # a smooth plus a numeric parametric term
    "y ~ te(x, z, k=5)",            # tensor product
    "y ~ s(x) + s(z) + ti(x, z)",   # main effects plus tensor interaction
    "y ~ s(x, z, bs='gp', k=30)",   # Gaussian process smooth
    "y ~ s(x, by=f) + f",           # factor-by smooth
    "y ~ s(x) + s(g, bs='re')",     # random intercept
    "y ~ 0 + s(x)",                 # no intercept
]
for formula in formulas:
    print(formula, GAM(formula).fit(data).converged)

y ~ s(x) True
y ~ s(x) + z True
y ~ te(x, z, k=5) True
y ~ s(x) + s(z) + ti(x, z) True
y ~ s(x, z, bs='gp', k=30) True
y ~ s(x, by=f) + f True
y ~ s(x) + s(g, bs='re') True
y ~ 0 + s(x) True

What the parser accepts:

  • Calls s(), te() and ti() only. Terms join with +. 0 +, - 1 or -1 drops the intercept. A bare name is a parametric term: a numeric column enters as is, a factor column (pandas categorical or string) with treatment contrasts, an ordered factor with polynomial contrasts.
  • Positional arguments of a smooth must be variable names.
  • k must be an integer literal and bs a string literal, so per-margin lists such as te(x, z, k=[5, 6]) raise ValueError.

What it rejects:

Input Error x1*x2 ValueError("Unsupported operator in formula: Mult. Only '+' and '-' are supported. ...") x1:x2 ValueError("Cannot parse formula RHS as an expression: ...") I(x), offset(o), factor(g), t2(x, z) ValueError("Unknown function 'I()' in formula. Supported: ['s', 'te', 'ti']") s(log(x)) ValueError("Positional arguments to s() must be variable names. ...") s(x, fx=True) NotImplementedError (fixed-df unpenalized splines are not supported) s(x, sp=1) NotImplementedError; use GAM(sp=[...]) instead s(x, id=1) NotImplementedError (linked smoothing parameters are not supported) s(x, bs="ps") and any other unregistered basis KeyError("Unknown basis type: 'ps'. Available: ...") when the fit runs

Other keyword arguments inside a smooth are evaluated as literals and passed to the smooth; keywords that no smooth reads (for example pc=) are silently ignored. Use the offset argument of fit() (dense route) or of the row source for an offset.

docs.title: Smooth term arguments
docs.text: Argument Applies to Default What it does k all -1 (automatic) Basis dimension. Automatic: 10 for one-variable tp and cubic smooths, 30 for two-variable tp; for gp see below. Ignored by re. bs s(), and the margins of te()/ti() "tp" for s(), "cr" for tensor margins Basis type. See the catalog below. by all None A factor (pandas categorical or string column) gives one smooth and one smoothing parameter per level; an ordered factor drops its first level. A numeric column multiplies the smooth (a varying-coefficient term). m tp, ts (also tensor margins) basis default Penalty order. xt tp, ts, gp {"max_knots": 2000, "seed": 1} Knot subsampling when there are more distinct covariate values than max_knots. tp and ts also accept max_knots= and seed= directly.

docs.title: Smooth catalog
docs.text:
Formula Basis s(x), s(x, bs='tp') Thin-plate regression spline (default); any number of variables s(x, bs='ts') Thin-plate spline with a shrinkage penalty on the null space s(x, bs='cr') Cubic regression spline; one variable s(x, bs='cs') Cubic regression spline with shrinkage s(x, bs='cc') Cyclic cubic regression spline s(x, z, bs='gp') Low-rank Gaussian process smooth; one to three variables, more with an explicit k s(g, bs='re') Random effect: one coefficient per level, identity penalty; s(x, g, bs='re') is a random slope te(x, z) Tensor product of one-variable margins, one penalty per margin ti(x, z) Tensor interaction, without the margins' main effects

te and ti are chosen by the function name; s(x, bs="te") is not valid. A bs="re" grouping variable must be a pandas categorical or string column: an integer column gives a single numeric coefficient.

docs.title: Gaussian process smooths
docs.text:
bs='gp' builds a low-rank Gaussian process (kriging) smooth: the leading eigenvectors of a correlation matrix evaluated at knots, as in mgcv's smooth.construct.gp.smooth.spec. With k=-1 the basis dimension is 12 for one variable, 33 for two and 104 for three; four or more variables need an explicit k.

Argument Default What it does kernel "matern_3_2" "spherical", "power_exponential", "matern_3_2", "matern_5_2" or "matern_7_2" (case-insensitive) rho automatic Positive range parameter; by default the largest distance between knots power 1.0 Power of kernel='power_exponential', in (0, 2] stationary False True drops the linear trend from the null space xt {"max_knots": 2000, "seed": 1} Knot subsampling

mgcv encodes these options in one signed numeric vector m; jaxgam uses named arguments instead, and m= on a gp smooth raises ValueError. Gaussian process options given to te() or ti() are not passed to the margins.

fit = GAM("y ~ s(x, bs='gp', kernel='power_exponential', rho=0.5, power=2.0)").fit(data)
print(fit.converged)

True

docs.title: Tensor product arguments
docs.text: Argument Default What it does k -1 (automatic) One integer applied to every margin; automatic is 5 per margin, as in mgcv's te() bs "cr" One basis type for every margin

docs.title: Custom registrations
docs.text:
Smooth types, families and links are looked up in registries. You can add entries at run time; built-in entries cannot be replaced or removed.

Registry Import Used by smooth_registry from jaxgam.smooths import smooth_registry bs= in formulas family_registry from jaxgam.families import family_registry GAM(family="name") link_registry from jaxgam.links import link_registry Family(link="name") 
from jaxgam.families import family_registry
from jaxgam.links import LogLink, link_registry
from jaxgam.smooths import smooth_registry
from jaxgam.smooths.cubic import CubicRegressionSmooth

print(smooth_registry.available, len(smooth_registry), "tp" in smooth_registry)


class MyCubic(CubicRegressionSmooth):
    """A cubic regression spline registered under a new name."""


class MyPoisson(Poisson):
    family_name = "mypoisson"


class MyLog(LogLink):
    pass


smooth_registry.register("mycr", MyCubic)
family_registry.register("mypoisson", MyPoisson)
link_registry.register("mylog", MyLog)

fit = GAM("count ~ s(x, bs='mycr')", family="mypoisson").fit(data)
fit_link = GAM("count ~ s(x)", family=Poisson(link="mylog")).fit(data)
print(fit.converged, fit_link.converged)

('cc', 'cr', 'cs', 'gp', 're', 'te', 'ti', 'tp', 'ts') 9 True
True True

What a new class must provide:

  • A smooth subclasses jaxgam.smooths.Smooth, takes a SmoothSpec in its constructor, and implements setup, build_design_matrix, build_penalty_matrices and predict_matrix. setup must leave the object marked as set up and keep the training basis, or model assembly raises RuntimeError.
  • A family subclasses jaxgam.families.ExponentialFamily, sets family_name, and implements default_link, variance, dvar, saturated_loglik, deviance_resids, aic, _initialize_impl, valid_mu and valid_eta. Looking a family up by name calls the class with no arguments and caches the instance.
  • A link subclasses jaxgam.links.Link and implements link, inverse and derivative.

Rules:

  • Keys are case-insensitive: "MYCR" and "mycr" are the same key.
  • Registering an existing key, built in or custom, raises ValueError("Key ... is already registered in the ... registry."). There is no way to unregister.
  • register() does not check the class type.
  • Registrations are global to the process and apply to every later GAM.
  • Custom classes are exercised on the dense route only.

docs.text: jaxgam is a Python port of Simon Wood's mgcv R package. The statistical methods are entirely his work. If you use jaxgam, please cite the relevant mgcv papers.

docs.title: References
docs.text:
GAM method (REML/ML estimation)

Wood SN (2011). "Fast stable restricted maximum likelihood and marginal likelihood estimation of semiparametric generalized linear models." Journal of the Royal Statistical Society (B), 73(1), 3--36. doi:10.1111/j.1467-9868.2010.00749.x

Beyond exponential family

Wood SN, Pya N, Säfken B (2016). "Smoothing parameter and model selection for general smooth models (with discussion)." Journal of the American Statistical Association, 111, 1548--1575. doi:10.1080/01621459.2016.1180986

Large datasets and discretized covariates (bam)

These are the methods behind jaxgam's discretized route (FitControl(execution="discrete")).

Wood SN, Goude Y, Shaw S (2015). "Generalized additive models for large datasets." Journal of the Royal Statistical Society (C), 64(1), 139--155. doi:10.1111/rssc.12068

Wood SN, Li Z, Shaddick G, Augustin NH (2017). "Generalized additive models for gigadata: modelling the UK black smoke network daily data." Journal of the American Statistical Association, 112(519), 1199--1210. doi:10.1080/01621459.2016.1195744

Li Z, Wood SN (2020). "Faster model matrix crossproducts for large generalized linear models with discretized covariates." Statistics and Computing, 30, 19--25. doi:10.1007/s11222-019-09864-2

Fellner-Schall smoothing parameter optimization

This is the method behind optimizer="efs".

Wood SN, Fasiolo M (2017). "A generalized Fellner-Schall method for smoothing parameter optimization with application to Tweedie location, scale and shape models." Biometrics, 73(4), 1071--1081. doi:10.1111/biom.12666

GCV-based model method and basics of GAMM

Wood SN (2004). "Stable and efficient multiple smoothing parameter estimation for generalized additive models." Journal of the American Statistical Association, 99(467), 673--686. doi:10.1198/016214504000000980

Overview

Wood SN (2017). Generalized Additive Models: An Introduction with R, 2 edition. Chapman and Hall/CRC.

Thin plate regression splines

Wood SN (2003). "Thin-plate regression splines." Journal of the Royal Statistical Society (B), 65(1), 95--114. doi:10.1111/1467-9868.00374

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
This tutorial walks through jaxgam's core features on data that fit in memory: fitting GAMs with different families, using several smooth types, and post-estimation (prediction, summary, plotting).

All examples assume:

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from jaxgam import GAM, GAMResults

docs.title: Choose a result type
docs.text:
Every fit returns one of three result types, chosen by the result argument of fit():

Fit call Return type Use it for model.fit(data, result="full") GAMResults Prediction, summary(), plot(), and in-sample values model.fit(data, result="inference") GAMInferenceResult New-data prediction with standard errors and fit diagnostics, without the training arrays model.fit(data, result="prediction") GAMPredictionResult New-data prediction only, with optional memory budgets; the only result of the routes for data that do not fit in memory

result="full" is the default, so model.fit(data) means exactly the same thing. Sections 1-10 and 12-14 use the full result. Section 11 introduces the inference result. Every result type predicts directly; to_predictor() is never required after fitting.

docs.title: 1. Gaussian GAM
docs.text:
The simplest case: a continuous response with a smooth effect.

rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
n = 200
x = rng.uniform(0, 1, n)
y = np.sin(2 * np.pi * x) + rng.normal(0, 0.3, n)
data = pd.DataFrame({"x": x, "y": y})

results = GAM("y ~ s(x, k=10, bs='cr')").fit(data, result="full")
print(f"Converged: {results.converged}")
print(f"EDF: {results.edf}")
print(f"Scale: {results.scale:.4f}")

The formula "y ~ s(x, k=10, bs='cr')" specifies:

  • y as the response variable
  • s(x, ...) as a smooth term over x
  • k=10 sets the basis dimension (for a cubic regression spline, the number of knots)
  • bs='cr' selects a cubic regression spline

If bs is omitted, a thin-plate regression spline (tp) is used.

Here result="full" is written explicitly to show the mode. Later examples use the shorter equivalent .fit(data).

Always check results.converged before using a fit. When it is False, results.convergence_info says how the fit stopped.

docs.title: 2. Binomial GAM
docs.text:
Binary response (0/1) with a logit link.

rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
n = 300
x = rng.uniform(0, 1, n)
eta = 2 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * x)
prob = 1 / (1 + np.exp(-eta))
y = rng.binomial(1, prob, n).astype(float)
data = pd.DataFrame({"x": x, "y": y})

results = GAM("y ~ s(x, k=10, bs='cr')", family="binomial").fit(data)

docs.title: 3. Poisson GAM
docs.text:
Count data with a log link.

rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
n = 200
x = rng.uniform(0, 1, n)
eta = np.sin(2 * np.pi * x) + 0.5
y = rng.poisson(np.exp(eta)).astype(float)
data = pd.DataFrame({"x": x, "y": y})

results = GAM("y ~ s(x, k=10, bs='cr')", family="poisson").fit(data)

docs.title: 4. Gamma GAM
docs.text:
Positive continuous response. A family name always uses that family's default link (inverse for Gamma). The data below are generated with mu = exp(eta), so we pass a family instance, Gamma(link="log"), to use the log link instead.

from jaxgam.families import Gamma

rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
n = 200
x = rng.uniform(0, 1, n)
eta = 0.5 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * x) + 1.0
mu = np.exp(eta)
y = rng.gamma(5.0, scale=mu / 5.0, size=n)
data = pd.DataFrame({"x": x, "y": y})

results = GAM("y ~ s(x, k=10, bs='cr')", family=Gamma(link="log")).fit(data)

docs.title: 5. Negative binomial GAM
docs.text:
Count data with overdispersion (variance larger than the mean). The dispersion parameter theta is estimated along with the smoothing parameters.

rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
n = 300
x = rng.uniform(0, 1, n)
eta = np.sin(2 * np.pi * x) + 0.5
mu = np.exp(eta)
theta = 2.0
y = rng.negative_binomial(n=theta, p=theta / (mu + theta), size=n).astype(float)
data = pd.DataFrame({"x": x, "y": y})

results = GAM("y ~ s(x, k=10, bs='cr')", family="nb").fit(data)
print(f"Estimated theta: {results.theta:.2f}")

To fix theta instead of estimating it:

from jaxgam.families import NegativeBinomial

results = GAM("y ~ s(x)", family=NegativeBinomial(theta=2, fixed=True)).fit(data)

With a fixed theta, results.theta is None; the fitted family still holds the value, results.family.get_theta(transformed=True).

docs.title: 6. Multiple smooths
docs.text:
Add several smooth terms with +.

rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
n = 200
x1 = rng.uniform(0, 1, n)
x2 = rng.uniform(0, 1, n)
y = np.sin(2 * np.pi * x1) + 0.5 * x2 + rng.normal(0, 0.3, n)
data = pd.DataFrame({"x1": x1, "x2": x2, "y": y})

results = GAM("y ~ s(x1, k=8, bs='cr') + s(x2, k=8, bs='cr')").fit(data)
print(f"Per-smooth EDF: {results.edf}")

docs.title: 7. Tensor product smooths
docs.text:
Model interactions between covariates with te().

results = GAM("y ~ te(x1, x2, k=5)").fit(data)

The scalar k=5 gives each margin 5 basis functions, a 5 x 5 = 25 basis function tensor product. Each margin uses a cubic regression spline by default.

Use ti() for tensor interaction terms (without main effects):

results = GAM("y ~ s(x1, k=8) + s(x2, k=8) + ti(x1, x2, k=5)").fit(data)

docs.title: 8. Factor-by smooths
docs.text:
Fit a separate smooth curve for each level of a factor variable.

rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
n = 300
x = rng.uniform(0, 1, n)
levels = ["a", "b", "c"]
fac = rng.choice(levels, n)

# Different functions per level
eta = np.where(
    fac == "a",
    np.sin(2 * np.pi * x),
    np.where(fac == "b", 0.5 * x, -0.3 * x),
)
y = eta + rng.normal(0, 0.3, n)

data = pd.DataFrame({
    "x": x,
    "fac": pd.Categorical(fac, categories=levels),
    "y": y,
})

results = GAM("y ~ s(x, by=fac, k=10, bs='cr') + fac").fit(data)

The + fac adds a parametric intercept shift per level, as in R. The by=fac argument creates a separate smooth per factor level, each with its own smoothing parameter.

Important: the factor column must be a pd.Categorical or a string column so jaxgam recognizes it as a factor. An integer-coded column is treated as numeric.

docs.title: 9. Random effects
docs.text:
Use bs='re' for simple independent random effects, represented as penalized smooths in the model matrix. This suits a modest number of levels; for random effects with very many levels, see the operator route in the user guide.

rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
n = 300
groups = [f"g{i}" for i in range(20)]
g = rng.choice(groups, size=n)
x = rng.uniform(0, 1, n)
group_effect = rng.normal(0, 0.7, len(groups))
effect_lookup = dict(zip(groups, group_effect, strict=True))
y = (
    np.sin(2 * np.pi * x)
    + np.array([effect_lookup[level] for level in g])
    + rng.normal(0, 0.25, n)
)

data = pd.DataFrame({
    "x": x,
    "g": pd.Categorical(g),
    "y": y,
})

results = GAM("y ~ s(x, k=10, bs='cr') + s(g, bs='re')").fit(data)

s(g, bs='re') adds one penalized coefficient per group level. A random-slope term without a random intercept is:

results = GAM("y ~ s(x, g, bs='re')").fit(data)

Use both terms when you want random intercepts and random slopes:

results = GAM("y ~ s(g, bs='re') + s(x, g, bs='re')").fit(data)

As with by=, the grouping column must be a categorical or string column.

When you predict for a group level that was not in the training data, or a missing group, the random-effect contribution is zero (the prior mean of the random effect), so the prediction is finite.

docs.title: 10. Prediction
docs.text:
The examples below use the random-intercept model from section 9.

results = GAM("y ~ s(x, k=10, bs='cr') + s(g, bs='re')").fit(data)

docs.title: Self-prediction
docs.text:
# Predictions on the training data
mu_hat = results.predict()                          # response scale
eta_hat = results.predict(pred_type="link")         # link scale
mu_hat, se = results.predict(se_fit=True)           # with standard errors

docs.title: New data
docs.text:
New data must hold every variable the formula uses.

newdata = pd.DataFrame({
    "x": np.linspace(0, 1, 100),
    "g": pd.Categorical(["g0"] * 100, categories=groups),
})
predictions = results.predict(newdata)
predictions, se = results.predict(newdata, se_fit=True)

docs.title: Prediction matrix
docs.text:
For manual inference, get the constrained prediction matrix (mgcv's predict.gam(type = "lpmatrix")):

X_new = results.predict_matrix(newdata)
eta_new = X_new @ results.coefficients  # equals predict(newdata, pred_type="link")

docs.title: 11. Lean inference result
docs.text:
When you keep a fitted object for new-data prediction rather than interactive analysis, request the lean result mode:

lean = GAM("y ~ s(x, k=10, bs='cr') + s(g, bs='re')").fit(data, result="inference")
predictions = lean.predict(newdata)

That is all you need for inference. The returned GAMInferenceResult is already lean and directly supports predict() and predict_matrix(). Do not call to_predictor() as a routine second step: it does not make an inference result smaller.

The lean result keeps diagnostics such as edf, deviance and converged, plus formula, smooth_info and term_names. It has no summary() or plot(), and prediction requires newdata. This mode reduces memory kept after the fit; it does not reduce peak memory during the fit.

A third mode, result="prediction", keeps even less (no per-smooth EDF, and no standard errors unless you ask for them). It is described in the API reference.

docs.title: Optional prediction-only handoff
docs.text:
Use to_predictor() only when another component should receive the narrower prediction-only interface, without the inference result's diagnostics:

import pickle

predictor = lean.to_predictor()  # returns lean's existing core; no copy
blob = pickle.dumps(predictor)
restored = pickle.loads(blob)
same_predictions = restored.predict(newdata)

If the receiving process needs diagnostics too, pickle lean directly. For a full GAMResults, to_predictor() instead builds an independent lean core; discard the full result afterward if you want its training-backed memory to be released.

Pickles are for trusted, same-version, short-lived handoff. Loading a predictor under another jaxgam version warns and is not guaranteed to work. Locally defined custom links or families require cloudpickle; built-in and module-level definitions work with the standard library pickle.

docs.title: 12. Summary
docs.text:
summary() prints and returns a summary object with parametric coefficient tests, smooth term significance tests (Wood 2013), and model-level statistics.

s = results.summary()

Output includes:

  • Parametric coefficients with z or t tests
  • Smooth terms with estimated degrees of freedom, F or chi-squared statistics, and p-values
  • Adjusted R-squared, deviance explained, scale estimate and REML score

docs.title: 13. Plotting
docs.text:
plot() produces one panel per smooth term and returns the figure and its axes.

fig, axes = results.plot()

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
# Select specific smooth terms (0-indexed)
fig, axes = results.plot(select=[0])

# Customize appearance
fig, axes = results.plot(
    rug=True,       # show data rug marks (default: True)
    se=True,        # show SE bands (default: True)
    shade=True,     # shaded bands vs dashed lines (default: True)
)

Panels show partial effects on the link scale. A one-variable smooth is drawn as a line with a shaded confidence band. A two-variable smooth or tensor product is drawn as a filled contour plot. A factor-by smooth gets one panel per level, and a bs='re' term a normal quantile plot of its coefficients.

docs.title: Smoothing parameter method
docs.text:
# REML (default, and the only supported method)
results = GAM("y ~ s(x)", method="REML").fit(data)

# Maximum likelihood (ML) is not available: method="ML" raises
# NotImplementedError.

docs.title: Fixed smoothing parameters
docs.text:
Hold the smoothing parameters at values you supply instead of estimating them:

results = GAM("y ~ s(x, k=10, bs='cr')", sp=[1.0]).fit(data)

The sp list must have one positive entry per penalty in the model. results.smoothing_params reports the values you supplied. For Gaussian, Gamma and estimated-theta negative binomial models, the scale or theta is still estimated.

docs.title: Weights and offset
docs.text:
weights = np.ones(len(data))
offset = np.zeros(len(data))
results = GAM("y ~ s(x)").fit(data, weights=weights, offset=offset)

When a model was fitted with a nonzero offset, pass offset= to predict() for new data; without it, jaxgam warns and omits the offset.

docs.title: Fellner-Schall optimizer
docs.text:
optimizer="efs" selects smoothing parameters with mgcv's extended Fellner-Schall update instead of Newton's method:

results = GAM("y ~ s(x, k=10, bs='cr') + s(g, bs='re')", optimizer="efs").fit(data)
print(results.lambda_strategy, results.convergence_info)

See Smoothing parameter selection for when to use it and which families it supports.

docs.title: 15. GAMResults attributes
docs.text:
By default, fit() returns a GAMResults frozen dataclass. Its fields cannot be reassigned, although the arrays inside are not themselves frozen. The most used attributes:

Attribute Description coefficients Coefficient vector (p,) fitted_values Fitted values on the response scale (n,) linear_predictor Linear predictor eta (n,) Vp Bayesian covariance matrix (p, p) edf Per-smooth effective degrees of freedom edf1 Alternative EDF used for significance tests edf_total Total effective degrees of freedom scale Scale (dispersion) parameter deviance Model deviance null_deviance Null model deviance smoothing_params Smoothing parameters, estimated or as supplied converged Whether the fit converged convergence_info How the fit stopped n_iter Number of outer iterations score REML criterion at the returned smoothing parameters X Model matrix (n, p) y Response vector (n,) weights Prior weights (n,) family Family object used for fitting formula Model formula string theta Estimated theta for a negative binomial with estimated theta; None otherwise method Smoothing parameter method ("REML") n Number of observations

The API reference lists every attribute.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• For data that do not fit in memory, for the Fellner-Schall optimizer and Gaussian QR compression, and for the streamed, discretized and operator routes, start with Choosing a route in the user guide.
  • The API reference lists every class, argument and result attribute.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
This page is the entry point to the maintainer documentation. It says what JaxGAM does, how the three phases split the code, which sub-package depends on which, which fitting routes exist and how one is selected, and defines the terms the other architecture pages use. It ends with a reading order.

JaxGAM is a Python port of R's mgcv. It fits generalized additive models: a response from an exponential family (Gaussian, Binomial, Poisson, Gamma, or negative binomial) whose link-scale mean is a sum of parametric terms and penalized smooth functions (thin plate, cubic, Gaussian process, random effect and tensor product bases). Smoothing parameters are chosen by REML or by an extended Fellner-Schall iteration, or fixed by the caller. The public entry is GAM in jaxgam/api.py: GAM(formula, family, ...).fit(data, ...) returns a frozen result object that predicts, and on the default route also summarises and plots. Besides the in-memory (dense) route, the package fits from a replayable row source by streaming, by a discretized compact design (the analogue of bam(discrete=TRUE) in mgcv's R/bam.r), and by a matrix-free operator route for random effects with very many levels.

docs.title: Where the code is
docs.text: Path Role jaxgam/__init__.py Enables float64 in JAX, configures the compilation cache, runs the Accelerate warning, exports the ten public names. jaxgam/api.py GAM: argument checks, route dispatch, and the per-route fit functions. jaxgam/control.py Frozen control dataclasses: FitControl, EFSControl, OperatorControl, ContinuousDiscretizationControl. jaxgam/results.py Result types GAMResults, GAMInferenceResult, GAMPredictionResult and their constructors. jaxgam/jax_utils.py Array dispatch, to_jax (the Phase 1 to 2 transfer) and to_numpy (the Phase 2 to 3 transfer). jaxgam/registry.py Registry, the case-insensitive string-to-class map used by families, links and smooths. jaxgam/platform_guard.py warn_if_accelerate_lapack, the Apple Accelerate warning. jaxgam/data/ Phase 1. RowSource protocol, RowBatch, built-in sources, fingerprints, discretization of row sources. jaxgam/formula/ Phase 1. Formula parser, term specs, dense ModelSetup, PredictSpec and the prepared model of the row-source routes; the discretized and operator setup are in jaxgam/formula/discrete/ and jaxgam/formula/operator/. jaxgam/smooths/ Phase 1. Smooth bases and penalties, the smooth registry, CoefficientMap identifiability constraints, pinned-arithmetic helpers. jaxgam/penalties/ Phase 1. Penalty, PenaltyStructure block descriptors, stable reparameterization of multi-penalty blocks. jaxgam/families/ Used by the fit and by prediction; Phase 1 receives family objects as arguments without importing the package. Family base classes, the five registered families, the execution-capability contract. jaxgam/links/ Used by the families. The eight link functions and their registry. jaxgam/fitting/ Phase 2 kernels. JAX code for PIRLS, the REML criterion, the dense Newton optimizer and Fellner-Schall algebra at the top level; one sub-package of kernels per route (gaussian_qr/, stream/, discrete/, operator/). jaxgam/execution/ Phase 2 host drivers. Python control loops that scan row sources, call fitting/ kernels, and own budgets and step control; one sub-package per route (gaussian_qr/, stream/, discrete/, operator/). jaxgam/inference/ Phase 3. GAMPredictor, the shared prediction finish (jaxgam/inference/_core.py), the operator prediction geometry. jaxgam/summary/ Phase 3. summary, GAMSummary, Davies' method for weighted chi-square tails. jaxgam/plot/ Phase 3. plot_gam (matplotlib).

docs.title: Layout by route
docs.text:
jaxgam/formula/, jaxgam/fitting/ and jaxgam/execution/ are laid out the same way. A module that only one route uses is in that route's sub-package, and the sub-package has the same name in each of the three packages. A module that the dense fit uses, or that more than one route uses, stays at the top level of its package.

Route Phase 1 setup Kernels (jaxgam/fitting/) Host drivers (jaxgam/execution/) Page Dense, Newton REML jaxgam/formula/design.py top level: jaxgam/fitting/pirls.py, jaxgam/fitting/reml.py, jaxgam/fitting/newton.py, jaxgam/fitting/stable_log_det.py, jaxgam/fitting/source_pirls.py none: the Newton loop is in jaxgam/fitting/newton.py Dense fitting Dense Fellner-Schall jaxgam/formula/design.py top level: jaxgam/fitting/efs.py, jaxgam/fitting/efs_regular_pirls.py, jaxgam/fitting/efs_theta.py top level: jaxgam/execution/efs.py, jaxgam/execution/efs_provider.py Dense fitting Gaussian QR jaxgam/formula/rank_coordinates.py jaxgam/fitting/gaussian_qr/ jaxgam/execution/gaussian_qr/ Dense fitting Streamed jaxgam/formula/prepare.py, jaxgam/formula/design_provider.py jaxgam/fitting/stream/ jaxgam/execution/stream/ Streamed fitting Discretized jaxgam/formula/discrete/, with jaxgam/data/ jaxgam/fitting/discrete/ jaxgam/execution/discrete/ Discretized fitting Operator jaxgam/formula/operator/ jaxgam/fitting/operator/ jaxgam/execution/operator/ Operator fitting

jaxgam/fitting/
├── pirls.py, reml.py, newton.py, initialization.py, stable_log_det.py, source_pirls.py   dense fit
├── efs.py, efs_regular_pirls.py, efs_theta.py                                            Fellner-Schall algebra
├── data.py, state.py, family_execution.py, penalty_ops.py, qr.py, signed_qr.py           shared by the routes
├── gaussian_qr/                kernel.py, rank_coordinates.py
├── stream/                     kernels.py, regular.py, nb_kernels.py, nb_theta.py, reml.py, nb_reml.py,
│                               efs_factor.py
├── discrete/                   ops.py, working.py, working_model.py
└── operator/                   actions.py, family.py, iterative.py, preconditioners.py, efs_score.py

jaxgam/formula/
├── parser.py, terms.py, design.py, predict_matrix.py                dense setup and prediction state
├── prepare.py, design_provider.py, fitting_prepare.py               prepared model of the row-source routes
├── kernel_groups.py, rank_coordinates.py                            shared helpers
├── discrete/                   continuous_setup.py, continuous_design.py, continuous_metadata.py, design.py,
│                               working_penalties.py
└── operator/                   prepare.py, modest.py, radial.py, workspace.py

Several file names occur in more than one place: for example jaxgam/fitting/reml.py (the dense criterion), jaxgam/fitting/stream/reml.py and jaxgam/execution/stream/reml.py, or jaxgam/formula/prepare.py and jaxgam/formula/operator/prepare.py. The package path tells them apart, so these pages always write the full path. A sub-package's initializer, such as jaxgam/execution/operator/__init__.py, holds a description and imports nothing, so importing one module of a route does not load the rest. The other packages (data/, smooths/, penalties/, families/, links/, inference/, summary/, plot/) are flat, and so are the test directories: the tests of jaxgam/execution/operator/fit.py are in tests/test_execution/test_operator_fit.py.

docs.title: The three phases
docs.text:
Every fit passes through three phases.

  • Phase 1, setup (NumPy, CPU). Parse the formula, build bases, penalties and identifiability constraints, and either assemble the dense model matrix (ModelSetup.build in jaxgam/formula/design.py) or prepare observation-independent metadata by scanning a row source (prepare_model in jaxgam/formula/prepare.py, build_continuous_discrete_setup in jaxgam/formula/discrete/continuous_setup.py, prepare_operator_model in jaxgam/formula/operator/prepare.py). Packages: data, formula, smooths, penalties.
  • Phase 2, fit (JAX). Arrays cross to a JAX device and the smoothing parameters and coefficients are estimated. JIT kernels live in jaxgam/fitting/; host-side drivers that iterate over row sources, hold accepted and trial states and enforce memory budgets live in jaxgam/execution/. Not all of fitting/ is jitted: the outer loop of NewtonOptimizer.run in jaxgam/fitting/newton.py is host Python, and jaxgam/fitting/stable_log_det.py runs in NumPy between jitted evaluations.
  • Phase 3, post-estimation (NumPy, CPU). Results return through to_numpy and become frozen result objects (jaxgam/results.py) holding a prediction core (jaxgam/inference/); summary and plot work on the full result only.
flowchart LR
    subgraph phase1["Phase 1 - setup, NumPy"]
        parse_formula["parse_formula"]
        ModelSetup["ModelSetup.build<br/>dense X, penalties, CoefficientMap"]
        rowsetup["row-source setup group<br/>prepare_model, build_continuous_discrete_setup,<br/>prepare_operator_model"]
    end
    subgraph phase2["Phase 2 - fit, JAX"]
        FittingData["FittingData.from_setup<br/>calls to_jax, jax.device_put"]
        execution["host drivers group<br/>jaxgam/execution/"]
        fitting["JIT kernels group<br/>jaxgam/fitting/"]
    end
    subgraph phase3["Phase 3 - post-estimation, NumPy"]
        builders["result builders group<br/>GAMResults._from_fit,<br/>GAMPredictionResult._from_stream_fit, _from_discrete, _from_operator_fit"]
        GAMPredictor["GAMPredictor"]
        summary["summary and plot_gam"]
    end
    parse_formula --> ModelSetup
    parse_formula --> rowsetup
    ModelSetup -->|"dense arrays"| FittingData
    FittingData --> fitting
    rowsetup -->|"metadata, then per-batch jax.device_put"| execution
    execution --> fitting
    fitting -->|"to_numpy, np.asarray"| builders
    execution -->|"row-free fit state"| builders
    builders --> GAMPredictor
    builders --> summary

Read left to right: the dense route hands a whole model matrix to JAX through FittingData.from_setup (which calls to_jax in jaxgam/jax_utils.py); the row-source routes hand over metadata and move each scanned batch to the device inside their host drivers. Only GAMResults reaches summary and plot_gam.

Which packages import JAX (an AST walk of the import statements at HEAD):

Package or module JAX imports fitting/ 32 of its 37 files at module level (all but the five __init__.py files). execution/ 18 of 40 files at module level; the other 22, five __init__.py files among them, use NumPy and SciPy only. families/ jaxgam/families/standard.py and jaxgam/families/negative_binomial.py at module level; jaxgam/families/base.py imports jaxgam.jax_utils. links/ jaxgam/links/links.py only under TYPE_CHECKING and inside functions, but it imports jaxgam.jax_utils at module level. jaxgam/api.py Under TYPE_CHECKING and inside functions only. jaxgam/__init__.py, jaxgam/jax_utils.py, jaxgam/platform_guard.py At module level. data/, formula/, smooths/, penalties/, inference/, summary/, plot/, jaxgam/control.py, jaxgam/registry.py, jaxgam/results.py None.

jaxgam/results.py has no JAX import of its own, but it imports jaxgam.fitting.state and jaxgam.jax_utils, which do. And because every import jaxgam.<module> first runs jaxgam/__init__.py, which imports jax, "no JAX import" is a property of the source text: the guard tests load a module under a stub parent package to check it (see Rules and invariants).

Directions that never occur:

  • No Phase 1 package (data, formula, smooths, penalties) imports fitting, execution, families, links, jax_utils, inference, results, summary, plot or api. Family objects reach Phase 1 code as arguments, without an import.
  • families and links import no Phase 1, Phase 2 or Phase 3 package.
  • execution never imports results, api, summary or plot.
  • fitting never imports inference, results or api.
  • inference never imports fitting or execution.

The one known exception to "kernels do not depend on drivers" is in jaxgam/fitting/data.py: _structural_penalty_roots imports structural_rank from jaxgam/execution/qr.py inside the function, with a comment giving the circular import as the reason. It runs from FittingData.from_setup for every dense model with penalties, so a dense fit loads jaxgam.execution. Two other edges cross the phase lines on purpose: jaxgam/execution/discrete/gaussian.py calls the Phase 1 setup builders for the discretized route, and GAMPredictionResult.bulk_link_variance in jaxgam/results.py calls into jaxgam/execution/ after the fit.
