GAM is a mutable specification object; fit may be called many times. The controls are frozen dataclasses in jaxgam/control.py that validate themselves in __post_init__ (for example execution="discrete" requires a discretization policy and the reverse). ContinuousDiscretizationControl has more fields than shown (selector_memmap_directory, max_pair_histogram_bytes, max_retained_representatives). The result types are drawn on Phase 3: results and prediction.

docs.title: Rules and invariants
docs.text:
• Phase 1 stays free of JAX. data, formula, smooths and penalties must not import jax, jaxgam.fitting, jaxgam.execution, jaxgam.families, jaxgam.links or jaxgam.jax_utils. Six tests load a Phase 1 module under a stub jaxgam package and assert that no jax module was imported: test_discretize_module_imports_without_jax (tests/test_data/test_discretize.py) and its siblings in tests/test_data/test_continuous_discretize.py, tests/test_data/test_continuous_frame.py, tests/test_data/test_continuous_request.py, tests/test_formula/test_continuous_metadata.py and tests/test_formula/test_rank_coordinates.py. No other import-boundary check (such as an import linter) runs in CI; the rest of this page's direction rules are kept by review.
  • Kernels do not import drivers. fitting/ imports execution/ only in _structural_penalty_roots. A new import in that direction is likely to create a circular import, because jaxgam/execution/ imports streamed routes that import jaxgam/fitting/data.py.
  • Float64 everywhere. jaxgam/__init__.py sets jax_enable_x64 before anything is compiled. See Numerics and platform.
  • Row-source routes return prediction results only. _fit_stream, _fit_discrete and _fit_operator raise NotImplementedError for result="full" or "inference", and take weights and offset from the source, never from fit(weights=, offset=).
  • Phase 3 operates on host arrays. Result builders convert with to_numpy before any covariance, EDF or prediction work.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• A plain import jaxgam.smooths.tprs imports JAX through jaxgam/__init__.py. Checking "no JAX in Phase 1" by importing a module in a normal interpreter proves nothing; use the stub-package pattern of the guard tests.
  • jaxgam/execution/__init__.py says execution code "does not construct formula bases or perform post-estimation work". The discretized route's driver calls Phase 1 setup builders, and bulk_link_variance runs after the fit, so treat that sentence as a guideline, not a fact about every module.
  • GAM does not validate family, sp or the formula at construction: an unknown family name raises KeyError only in fit, from Registry.get_class.
  • FitControl.smoothing_strategy defaults to "exact_reml" and is read only by the discretized route, which cannot use that default without an sp.

docs.title: Where to change things
docs.text:
To do this Edit Add a public name jaxgam/__init__.py (__all__) Add a fit argument or control field jaxgam/control.py and its readers in jaxgam/api.py; see Lifecycle of a fit Change route selection GAM.fit and the _fit_* methods in jaxgam/api.py Add a family, link or smooth see Extension points Change what a result keeps jaxgam/results.py, jaxgam/inference/predictor.py; see Phase 3 Change the Phase 1 to 2 transfer to_jax in jaxgam/jax_utils.py, FittingData.from_setup in jaxgam/fitting/data.py Add a module to a route That route's sub-package in jaxgam/formula/, jaxgam/fitting/ or jaxgam/execution/. Put it at the top level of the package instead when the dense fit or a second route uses it; see Layout by route.

A planned refactor will merge the per-route controllers in fitting/ and execution/ and the routing in jaxgam/api.py; see the unified fitting design.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text:
• Smoothing parameter. The weight lambda_j on penalty S_j. GAM(sp=) takes natural-scale values; the code optimizes log_lambda. Results report a supplied sp verbatim (_report_smoothing_params in jaxgam/results.py) and estimated ones as exp(log_lambda).
  • Penalty, S_lambda. The penalty matrix sum_j lambda_j S_j, held as local coefficient-block descriptors in PenaltyStructure (jaxgam/penalties/structure.py) and materialized by FittingData.S_lambda.
  • Scale. The dispersion phi; 1 for known-scale families (scale_known), estimated for Gaussian and Gamma.
  • Theta. The negative binomial shape parameter, fixed or estimated (NegativeBinomial(theta, fixed=...) in jaxgam/families/negative_binomial.py).
  • EDF. Effective degrees of freedom: the trace of F = (X'WX + S_lambda)^-1 X'WX over a smooth's coefficient block. edf1 is 2 edf - tr(F F) per block, which summary uses to set the reference degrees of freedom of the smooth tests (_compute_per_smooth_edf, _compute_per_smooth_edf1 in jaxgam/results.py).
  • PIRLS. Penalized iteratively reweighted least squares, the inner coefficient fit at fixed smoothing parameters: pirls_loop (jaxgam/fitting/pirls.py) and source_pirls (jaxgam/fitting/source_pirls.py, the port of gam.fit3 in mgcv's R/gam.fit3.r and gam.fit4 in R/gam.fit4.r).
  • REML. Restricted maximum likelihood, the smoothing-selection criterion (REMLCriterion in jaxgam/fitting/reml.py). method="REML" is the only accepted method; "ML" raises NotImplementedError.
  • Newton optimizer. The dense outer loop over log smoothing parameters, newton_optimize and NewtonOptimizer in jaxgam/fitting/newton.py, a port of newton in mgcv's R/gam.fit3.r.
  • Fellner-Schall (EFS). The extended Fellner-Schall update of smoothing parameters, selected by optimizer="efs", a port of efsudr in mgcv's R/gam.fit4.r. Dense in jaxgam/execution/efs.py, streamed in jaxgam/execution/stream/efs.py, operator in jaxgam/execution/operator/efs_controller.py; settings in EFSControl.
  • Row source. An object satisfying the RowSource protocol (jaxgam/data/source.py): n_rows, scan(batch_rows) yielding RowBatch objects in a stable order, and fingerprint(). Built-ins: ArrayRowSource, DataFrameRowSource, MemmapRowSource.
  • Scan. One full pass over a row source in batches of batch_rows rows. Results count fit scans in source_scans and batches_scanned.
  • Fingerprint. A content digest of a row source, compared at the start and end of a fit (single_fit_fingerprints) to detect data that changed.
  • Compact or discretized design. On the discrete route, the compact frame of representative covariate rows (build_compact_setup_frame in jaxgam/data/continuous_frame.py) plus row selectors, and the indexed design built on it (FrozenDiscreteDesign, DeviceDiscreteDesign), on which kernels such as discrete_xwxd act. The analogue of mgcv's discrete.mf and XWXd.
  • Working model. On the discrete route, the frozen coefficient-space Gaussian problem on which one Sl.fitChol proposal (mgcv R/fast-REML.r) is taken per iteration; repeated re-forming of it is the performance iteration of bgam.fitd (R/bam.r). Selected by smoothing_strategy="working_model_reml".
  • Prediction policy. On the discrete route, continuous_frozen_basis evaluates new covariate values exactly; mgcv_predict_bamd first compresses the whole request as mgcv's predict.bamd does.
  • CoefficientMap. The Phase 1 to 3 contract in jaxgam/smooths/constraints.py: per-term TermBlock entries holding the identifiability transform (Z_centering, del_index) that maps a raw basis block to the constrained coefficients (transform_X).
  • PredictSpec. The observation-free prediction state (CoefficientMap, factor levels, smooth metadata) in jaxgam/formula/predict_matrix.py.
  • Operator route. The matrix-free route for large random effects: indexed random effects (IndexedRandomEffect) never form dense columns, a small "modest" block holds the other terms, and systems are solved by preconditioned conjugate gradients (jaxgam/fitting/operator/iterative.py).
  • Gaussian QR compression. FitControl(gaussian_compression=True): one weighted QR reduction of a Gaussian identity model, then coefficient-space smoothing trials (jaxgam/execution/gaussian_qr/preparation.py).
  • Fisher factor. A retained triangular factor of the penalized Fisher information (lower Cholesky, or a PivotedQRFisherFactor) from which prediction standard errors are computed without a dense covariance.
  • Execution route. The execution_route string on every result, naming the sub-route that ran; lambda_strategy names how smoothing parameters were set; execution_fallback_reason records an unmet Gaussian QR request.
  • Host driver and kernel. A driver is Python in jaxgam/execution/ that loops, scans and decides; a kernel is a pure function in jaxgam/fitting/, usually jitted.
  • Memory budget. FitControl.memory_budget_bytes and output_budget_bytes: prospective estimates of known arrays, checked before allocation and raising MemoryError. Dense fitting is not budgeted.

docs.title: Reading order
docs.text:
1. Lifecycle of a fit - one GAM.fit() call end to end: checks, routing, the _fit_* methods, route labels.
  2. Phase 1: setup - formula parsing, smooth construction, CoefficientMap, penalties, and the streamed, discretized and operator setup.
  3. Data sources - RowSource, RowBatch, built-in sources, fingerprints and discretization.
  4. Phase 2: dense fitting - FittingData, PIRLS, the REML criterion, the Newton optimizer, dense EFS and Gaussian QR.
  5. Phase 2: streamed fitting - streamed PIRLS, QR reducers, exact streamed REML, streamed theta and EFS.
  6. Phase 2: discretized fitting - indexed design actions, the working-model REML proposal and the performance iteration.
  7. Phase 2: operator fitting - matrix-free actions, PCG, the operator EFS controller and bulk variance.
  8. Phase 3: results and prediction - result types, the prediction core, batched prediction, summary, plot and pickling.
  9. Extension points - family, link and smooth base classes, registries, and checklists for adding one.
  10. Testing and CI - test layout, the R bridge, tolerance classes, the validation matrix and CI jobs.
  11. Numerics and platform - float64, the pinned LAPACK provider, BLAS threads, the Accelerate guard, determinism.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: This page covers the jaxgam/data/ package: the RowSource protocol that the streamed, discretized and operator routes read rows from, the built-in sources, source fingerprints and the single-fit fingerprint scope, and lazily read batch columns. It then covers discretization for the discretized route, a port of compress.df and discrete.mf from R/bam.r: range grids, uniquecombs-style row indexing, compact frames, selectors and the DiscretizationBudget. The basis setup that runs on the compact frame is on setup.md; the discretized fit is on fitting_discrete.md.

docs.title: Where the code is
docs.text: Module Role jaxgam/data/__init__.py Public names: the sources, RowBatch, RowSource, DiscretizationBudget, ExactIndexUnavailable, RangeGridIndex, range_grid_index_columns, the compact-frame types and build_compact_setup_frame. None is re-exported from top-level jaxgam. jaxgam/data/source.py RowSource protocol, RowBatch, ArrayRowSource, DataFrameRowSource, MemmapRowSource, LazyColumns, overlay_columns, declared_row_vectors, single_fit_fingerprints, stage_fingerprint. jaxgam/data/source_tokens.py Ports of R 4.5 pieces: the Mersenne-Twister and rejection sampler (_RRandom), R's numeric text (r_row_token), uniquecombs(ordered=TRUE) row order (r_uniquecombs_ordered) and the large-data knot sample (r_sample_knot_rows). Also used by the thin-plate, GP and operator radial setups. jaxgam/data/discretize.py DiscretizationBudget, ExactIndexTable (unique rows plus an int32 selector), ExactIndexUnavailable, and exact_index_columns (exact indexing without rounding). jaxgam/data/continuous_discretize.py range_grid_index_columns: the exact-first range-grid policy of compress.df, producing a RangeGridIndex. jaxgam/data/continuous_frame.py build_compact_setup_frame: groups variables as discrete.mf does, indexes each group and pads the compact DataFrame (CompactSetupFrame, CompactGroup, CompactBatchSelectors, CompactFrameUnavailable). jaxgam/data/continuous_request.py Prediction-time compression of a whole request, as predict.bamd does (RequestCompressionSpec, FrozenRequestGrid).

docs.title: The RowSource protocol and RowBatch
docs.text:
RowSource is a typing.Protocol marked runtime_checkable, with three members: n_rows, scan(batch_rows) returning an iterator of RowBatch, and fingerprint() returning a string. isinstance(x, RowSource) only checks that the three attributes exist. GAM.fit uses that check to refuse a source on the dense route and to require one on the other routes.

RowBatch is a frozen dataclass with six fields:

Field Meaning columns A mapping from column name to a NumPy array or pandas Series of the batch's rows. y The response for these rows, or None for a source without one. Every fitting route requires it. weight Prior weights, shape (n,), present in every batch. offset Offset, shape (n,), present in every batch. valid Boolean mask, shape (n,), reserved for padding. row_positions Integer positions of these rows in the underlying source.

RowBatch.__post_init__ checks that weight, offset, valid and y have shape (n,) with n = len(row_positions). For a plain mapping it checks every column's length at once; for a LazyColumns mapping it registers the length and checks each column when it is read.

What consumers require of a producer (each check is in the consuming code, not in the protocol):

  • Replay in a stable order. Every scan yields the same rows in the same order. Consumers check this in different ways: prepare_model compares the first row_positions of two scan(1) calls; the streamed Gaussian QR route compares a digest of all row_positions with the one taken at setup; the discretized route indexes rows by scan ordinal (a running count over the batches), so its selectors are only correct if the order repeats; the operator route hashes every row of every scan (_CheckedSource in jaxgam/formula/operator/prepare.py).
  • Exactly n_rows rows per scan. Consumers raise RuntimeError when a scan yields more or fewer.
  • Batches no larger than requested. prepare_model raises ValueError and the discretization scans raise RuntimeError for a batch longer than batch_rows.
  • No padding. Every consumer refuses a batch with a false valid entry: NotImplementedError in setup, discretization and the stream and discrete fits, ValueError in operator preparation.
  • row_positions must be a one-dimensional, non-negative integer array.
  • Finite values. y, weight and offset finite and weights non-negative; the fit drivers check this per batch.
  • A fingerprint that changes when the data change. Every stage compares the fingerprint at its start and end and raises RuntimeError if it changed.

Weights and offset belong to the source: on the stream, discrete and operator routes, fit(weights=...) or fit(offset=...) raises ValueError.

Declared row vectors. A source may also define the booleans has_explicit_weights and has_explicit_offset. declared_row_vectors(source) reads them, treats a missing attribute as True (supplied), and raises TypeError for a non-boolean. Only the discretized route reads them: pinned discrete.mf compresses (weights) and (offset) columns whenever bam was given weights= or offset=, whatever their values, and those extra groups consume draws from the seeded sampler and can lengthen the padded frame (see "Compact frames" below). Built-in sources declare False when the caller passed None.

docs.title: Built-in sources
docs.text:
ArrayRowSource(columns, *, y=None, weights=None, offset=None, row_selection=None, version=None) replays aligned arrays, Series or memmaps.

  • Construction checks that all columns have one length, that there is a response or at least one column, that y, weights and offset have that length and are finite (weights non-negative), and that the selected weights do not sum to zero. Missing weights and offsets are not stored; each batch gets fresh ones and zeros.
  • row_selection is an optional integer array of positions into the columns. It must be non-empty and in range; it may reorder or repeat rows. n_rows is then its length, and each batch's row_positions are the selected positions.
  • scan(batch_rows) cuts the (selected) rows into consecutive batches. Columns are wrapped in LazyColumns, so a column is sliced only when read; a Series is sliced with iloc and its index reset.
  • version is an optional string mixed into the fingerprint (below). It is not a shortcut: the content is hashed either way.

DataFrameRowSource(data, *, response=None, **kwargs) is an ArrayRowSource over the frame's columns, with the response column taken out as y. Categorical and ordered categorical dtypes are kept as Series.

MemmapRowSource.from_npy_files(columns, *, y=None, weights=None, offset=None, **kwargs) opens each one-dimensional .npy file with np.load(path, mmap_mode="r") and builds an ArrayRowSource subclass instance from the memmaps. Reading a batch reads only those rows; computing the fingerprint reads every file once.

docs.title: Fingerprints
docs.text:
ArrayRowSource.fingerprint() returns a SHA-256 hex digest. _content_fingerprint starts from the tag jaxgam-row-source-v2 and then hashes:

  1. for each column, a schema token (name, dtype and shape; for a categorical Series, the categories and whether it is ordered) followed by the content in 65,536-row chunks: raw bytes for numeric arrays, int64 codes for categoricals, the repr of each value for object arrays;
  2. the names y, weights, offset and row_selection, each followed by its content when present;
  3. the version string, or content-addressed when there is none.

Outside a fingerprint scope it is recomputed on every call, so a mutation of the arrays shows at the next check. test_fingerprint_covers_content_schema_selection_and_version in tests/test_data/test_source.py covers each component.

The internal wrapper sources that discretization builds (_FormulaRowSource in jaxgam/data/continuous_frame.py, _RangeGridSource in jaxgam/data/continuous_discretize.py) hash a tag, the wrapped source's fingerprint and their own parameters (response name; metric names and grids).

docs.title: The single-fit fingerprint scope
docs.text:
Setup and fitting compare fingerprints before and after nearly every scan. For an ArrayRowSource each comparison rehashed all the data; the comment on single_fit_fingerprints records that this was more than half of setup time at 100 smooths.

single_fit_fingerprints(*, verify_on_exit=True) is a context manager backed by a ContextVar. Inside it, the first ArrayRowSource.fingerprint() call of each source computes the digest and stores it (keyed by id(source), with a reference to the source so the key stays valid); later calls return the stored digest. On a normal exit with verify_on_exit=True, every stored source is hashed once more, and a different digest raises RuntimeError("RowSource changed during the fit"). If the body raises, that exception propagates and no verification runs (test_single_fit_fingerprints_do_not_mask_an_error_from_the_fit). A nested scope joins the outer one.

What it guarantees: a built-in source is hashed twice per fit, at its first fingerprint request and at the end, and data changed during the fit are still reported, at the end of the fit rather than at the scan that would have seen them.

stage_fingerprint(source) is what a stage compares at its own end. With no scope, or inside a verifying scope, it is source.fingerprint() (the stored digest in a verifying scope, which then reports any change itself). Inside a non-verifying scope it switches the memo off and recomputes, so the stage's own error names the stage.

Who opens a scope:

  • GAM._fit_stream, around _fit_stream_routes (setup and fit).
  • GAM._fit_discrete, around fit_discrete_gaussian or fit_discrete_regular and the construction of the result.
  • build_continuous_discrete_setup in jaxgam/formula/discrete/continuous_setup.py, with verify_on_exit=False; called from _fit_discrete it joins the outer scope, called on its own it ends with stage_fingerprint.

The operator route opens no scope; _CheckedSource digests every row it replays instead.

sequenceDiagram
    participant U as User code
    participant G as GAM
    participant M as single_fit_fingerprints
    participant P as prepare_model
    participant S as ArrayRowSource
    participant C as stream controller
    U->>G: fit(source, result="prediction")
    G->>M: enter scope
    G->>P: prepare_model(spec, source, family=...)
    P->>S: fingerprint()
    S-->>P: full content hash, stored in the scope
    P->>S: scan(1), twice
    P->>S: scan(setup_rows) for knots, then for the design
    P->>S: fingerprint()
    S-->>P: stored digest, no rehash
    P->>S: scan(setup_rows), twice, for fitting preparation
    P-->>G: PreparedModel
    loop every PIRLS iteration or trial
        G->>C: fit on StreamDesign
        C->>S: scan(batch_rows)
        C->>S: fingerprint()
        S-->>C: stored digest
    end
    G->>M: exit scope
    M->>S: fingerprint() with the scope cleared
    S-->>M: full content hash
    M-->>G: RuntimeError if the two hashes differ
    G-->>U: GAMPredictionResult

Read it top to bottom: the content is hashed once when the first stage asks and once on exit; every check in between returns the stored digest. A one-smooth streamed setup with a family makes six scans (two probes, one knot scan, one design scan, two fitting-preparation scans), before any fit scan; the stream controllers are described on fitting_streamed.md.

docs.title: Lazy columns
docs.text:
LazyColumns(names, load) is a read-only Mapping. Iteration, len and in use the declared names; __getitem__ calls load(name) the first time a column is read, checks its length against the batch, and keeps it, so a second read returns the same object. The class docstring gives the reason: setup reads one or two columns per pass, and slicing hundreds of columns per batch was almost all wasted work. test_array_source_slices_a_column_only_when_it_is_read and test_prepared_batches_read_only_the_formula_columns pin this.

overlay_columns(base, overrides) returns a LazyColumns that is base with some columns replaced or added by zero-argument producers, still read on first use. Discretization uses it to add the response and the (weights)/(offset) columns (_FormulaRowSource) and to replace metric columns with their grid-rounded values (_RangeGridSource) without touching the other columns.

docs.title: Caller-written sources
docs.text:
A source written by the caller differs from the built-in ones in four ways:

  1. Declared vectors. Without has_explicit_weights and has_explicit_offset it counts as supplying both. On the discretized route that adds two replay-only groups, which changes the seeded padding and therefore the fitted numbers (tests/test_execution/test_discrete_supplied_vectors.py). Declare False for a vector the caller did not supply.
  2. Fingerprint caching. Only ArrayRowSource.fingerprint consults the scope. A caller's fingerprint() runs at every check, so it should be cheap, and it is never verified at scope exit; changes are caught by the per-stage comparisons only.
  3. Column laziness. A plain dict in RowBatch.columns is length-checked and must be fully built when the batch is created. Wrap columns in LazyColumns to get the built-in behaviour.
  4. No construction checks. The validation ArrayRowSource does at construction (lengths, finiteness, selection bounds, positive weight sum) does not happen; only the per-batch checks of each consumer apply.

docs.title: Discretization overview
docs.text:
build_compact_setup_frame(formula, source, *, factor_names, m, budget, selector_memmap_dir, batch_rows, seed) builds the discretized route's compact data:

  1. _discover_requests forms the groups as discrete.mf does: each by variable is a group; each te/ti margin is its own group; a multi-variable s() is one joint group; then the response and each parametric variable not already grouped. A smooth whose variables overlap an existing group with a different grouping raises ValueError("continuous discretization has incompatible nesting"), the analogue of check.term.
  2. _replay_only_requests adds (weights) and (offset) groups for a source that declares them.
  3. Each group is indexed with range_grid_index_columns on a _FormulaRowSource wrapper. All groups share one _RRandom(seed) stream, used for the shuffles and then the padding.
  4. Every group's representative columns are padded to the largest group's row count with draws from the same stream (_padded_column), giving one DataFrame. The replay-only groups are then dropped: they only consumed draws and set the frame length.

m sets the grid points per metric variable: None gives 1000, 100 or 25 for groups of one, two, or three or more variables; an integer is used as given for one variable and as round(m**(1/d)) + 1 for d variables (_points_per_metric, ties to even as R's round). A tuple gives one value per smooth term; the response and parametric groups use its maximum.

Factors are not inferred on this route: a column is a factor only if it is listed in factor_names. Any other column must be real numeric data; a categorical or object column raises TypeError with advice to declare it.

docs.title: Range grids, grouping and keying
docs.text:
range_grid_index_columns implements compress.df's exact-first policy for one group:

flowchart TD
    A["range_grid_index_columns"] --> B["_analyze_columns, scan 1:<br/>factor levels and metric ranges"]
    B --> C["threshold = product of factor counts<br/>times points per metric, to the number of metrics"]
    C --> D["_uniquecombs_index on the source, scan 2<br/>row cap = min of threshold and max_unique_rows"]
    D -->|"fits under the cap"| G["exact representatives"]
    D -->|"cap reached and cap is the threshold"| E["range_grid per metric variable"]
    D -->|"cap reached and cap is max_unique_rows"| X["ExactIndexUnavailable"]
    E --> F["_uniquecombs_index on _RangeGridSource, scan 3"]
    F --> H["rounded representatives"]
    G --> I["_uniquecombs_order"]
    H --> I
    I --> J["_shuffle_index with the shared R sampler,<br/>skipped when every row is unique"]
    J --> K["RangeGridIndex"]

A group keeps its distinct rows unless they outnumber the threshold; only then are its metric variables rounded. Each box labelled "scan" is one full pass over the source.

  • Range grid. range_grid(low, high, points) is seq(low, high, length=points). snap_to_range_grid ports kx <- round((x - xl[1]) / dx) + 1; x <- xu[kx] with round-half-to-even. A constant metric column in a group that must be rounded raises ValueError, because pinned compress.df produces an undefined grid there. When the threshold is above max_unique_rows, a group that pinned R would round is reported as unavailable instead.
  • Ordering. _uniquecombs_order reproduces uniquecombs(..., ordered=TRUE): one numeric column sorts by value, one factor column by level code, several columns by the byte order of their row tokens (R's C-locale collation).
  • Shuffle. _shuffle_index permutes the representatives with a port of R's sample and remaps the selector in chunks, as compress.df does to avoid induced dependence between discretized covariates. It does not touch NumPy's global RNG (test_group_shuffling_and_padding_leave_numpy_rng_untouched).

One batch of _uniquecombs_index:

flowchart TD
    A["RowBatch from scan(batch_rows)"] --> B["_validate_batch_positions"]
    B --> C{"rounding pass?"}
    C -->|"yes, batch from _RangeGridSource"| D["overlay_columns: snap_to_range_grid<br/>runs when a metric column is read"]
    C -->|"no"| E["np.asarray of each group column"]
    D --> E
    E --> F["_first_occurrence_groups:<br/>pd.factorize per column, combined codes"]
    F --> G{"one column?"}
    G -->|"yes"| H["key = _key of the value"]
    G -->|"no"| I["key = _r_row_token of the row"]
    H --> J{"key already indexed?"}
    I --> J
    J -->|"yes"| M["item = existing index"]
    J -->|"no"| K{"row cap or max_table_bytes exceeded?"}
    K -->|"yes"| N["remove claimed memmap,<br/>return ExactIndexUnavailable"]
    K -->|"no"| L["append a new unique row"]
    L --> M
    M --> O["selector[scan_offset:scan_stop] = items[group]"]

Only the first row of each group of equal rows is keyed, in order of first occurrence, so new keys are met exactly where a row-by-row walk would meet them (test_first_occurrence_groups_match_a_row_by_row_walk).

  • Grouping. _first_occurrence_groups factorizes each column with pd.factorize and combines the codes, treating NaN as equal to NaN and 0.0 as equal to -0.0. Columns of other dtype kinds than float, signed, unsigned and bool, and batches whose combined code could overflow, fall back to one group per row.
  • Keys. A one-column group uses _key, the value tagged with its Python type name (NaN tagged explicitly). A multi-column group uses _r_row_token: each metric value in R's 15-significant-digit text (_r_number_text) and each factor value as its 1-based level code, joined with *, as uniquecombs pastes rows. Two rows that differ beyond 15 digits therefore share a key, as in mgcv (test_joint_numeric_token_collision_matches_uniquecombs).
  • Selector write. Each source row's position in the unique list is written at its scan ordinal.

docs.title: Compact frames, groups and selectors
docs.text:
A RangeGridIndex wraps an ExactIndexTable (the unique values per column, an int32 selector of length n_rows, and storage, either memory or memmap) with the group's factor levels, metric ranges, points_per_metric, whether it was rounded, and the seed.

Selectors live in memory by default. With ContinuousDiscretizationControl.selector_memmap_directory, each group's selector is a .npy memmap at compact-selector-{k}.dat in that directory. The directory must exist; the file is claimed with O_CREAT | O_EXCL, so an existing file raises FileExistsError and is not removed. Files are removed if construction fails and by CompactSetupFrame.cleanup(), which _prepared_discrete in jaxgam/execution/discrete/gaussian.py calls when the fit ends.

CompactSetupFrame holds the padded frame, the CompactGroups (names, factor names, index, role and m), the mapping from variable to group, the selector paths and a byte ledger. batch_selectors(row_ordinals) gathers one selector slice per group for a batch, returned as CompactBatchSelectors, and raises MemoryError if that gather would exceed max_batch_bytes. The fit itself reads selectors through FrozenDiscreteDesign.batch_indices in jaxgam/formula/discrete/design.py, which gathers each distinct index once per batch.

exact_index_columns in jaxgam/data/discretize.py does the same indexing with exact equality and no rounding, and keys every row instead of grouping first. At HEAD it is called only by the exact descriptor builders in jaxgam/formula/discrete/design.py, which only tests use.

docs.title: Prediction requests
docs.text: With prediction_policy="mgcv_predict_bamd", prediction compresses the whole request first, as predict.bamd calls discrete.mf with m=NULL. RequestCompressionSpec holds the fitted groups (without the response). freeze (in-memory data) or freeze_source (a RowSource) makes a bounded pre-pass, keeping at most min(threshold, max_unique_rows) + 1 distinct keys per group, and returns a FrozenRequestGrid, which records per group whether to round and the request's ranges. FrozenRequestGrid.apply then snaps any batch of that request elementwise, so results do not depend on batch boundaries but do depend on the request's composition. Factor-only groups are never rounded. Its consumer is jaxgam/inference/predictor.py; see results_and_prediction.md.

docs.title: DiscretizationBudget and its limits
docs.text:
DiscretizationBudget is a frozen dataclass of four positive integers, set through ContinuousDiscretizationControl.budget:

Field Default Bounds max_table_bytes 64 MiB Construction and retained storage of unique-row tables and their discovery dictionaries, factor-level metadata, range grids, ordering and shuffle work, the padded compact frame, the prospective basis setup on the compact frame, the evaluated lookup tables of the descriptor, and the distinct-row state of request compression. max_selector_bytes 256 MiB Resident selectors: 4 bytes per source row per group held in memory, plus 1 byte per row of validation state. Memmapped selectors count only the validation state. max_batch_bytes 64 MiB Per-batch workspace: position validation, row tokens, range analysis, rounding, selector gathers, the descriptor's host batch and device action, and request compression batches. max_unique_rows 1,000,000 Distinct rows any one group may discover before its rounding decision.

When a limit is exceeded:

  • The data layer returns a typed value instead of raising. ExactIndexUnavailable has reason, required_bytes, budget_bytes and, for the row cap, required_rows and row_cap. build_compact_setup_frame turns it into a CompactFrameUnavailable, adding the budget_scope (table, selector or batch, chosen from the reason) and the group's names.
  • build_continuous_discrete_setup wraps that in a ContinuousSetupUnavailable, and build_continuous_discrete_design returns a DiscreteDesignUnavailable.
  • _prepared_discrete raises MemoryError(f"{reason}: requires {required_bytes} bytes, budget is {budget_bytes}.").
  • Some checks raise directly: CompactSetupFrame.batch_selectors and request compression raise MemoryError; a constant metric column that must be rounded raises ValueError; a non-numeric undeclared column raises TypeError; a changed source raises RuntimeError.

docs.title: Key types
docs.text:
classDiagram
    class RowSource {
        <<protocol>>
        +n_rows int
        +scan(batch_rows) Iterator~RowBatch~
        +fingerprint() str
    }
    class RowBatch {
        +columns Mapping
        +y ndarray
        +weight ndarray
        +offset ndarray
        +valid ndarray
        +row_positions ndarray
    }
    class ArrayRowSource {
        +n_rows int
        +column_names tuple~str~

    }
    RowSource <|.. ArrayRowSource
    ArrayRowSource <|-- DataFrameRowSource
    ArrayRowSource <|-- MemmapRowSource
    ArrayRowSource ..> RowBatch : yields
    RowBatch o-- LazyColumns : columns
    ArrayRowSource ..> LazyColumns : wraps its columns

RowSource is structural: any object with the three members satisfies it. LazyColumns is one possible value of RowBatch.columns; any Mapping is accepted.

range_grid_index_columns returns either a RangeGridIndex or an ExactIndexUnavailable, and build_compact_setup_frame either a CompactSetupFrame or a CompactFrameUnavailable; callers test with isinstance.

docs.title: Rules and invariants
docs.text:
• Phase 1, no JAX. Modules in jaxgam/data/ import NumPy and pandas only. test_discretize_module_imports_without_jax, test_range_grid_module_imports_without_jax, test_compact_frame_module_imports_without_jax and test_request_module_imports_without_jax (in tests/test_data/) load them with the package stubbed and assert JAX stays unloaded.
  • Mutation is detected. Every stage compares fingerprints, and the fingerprint covers content, schema, selection and version (tests/test_data/test_source.py). A change inside a single-fit scope raises when the scope ends.
  • Batch partition does not change results. Discretization is keyed by scan ordinal and first occurrence, so the compact frame and selectors are the same for any batch_rows (test_selected_reordered_repeated_rows_replay_across_batch_boundaries in tests/test_data/test_continuous_discretize.py).
  • Pinned R parity. Grid rounding, uniquecombs order and tokens, shuffles, padding and the discrete.mf groups are compared with pinned R in tests/test_data/test_continuous_discretize.py and tests/test_data/test_continuous_frame.py (R-gated tests).
  • Budgets are checked before allocation. Each limit is tested prospectively, before the array it bounds is created (test_shared_budgets_reject_growth_and_clean_failed_memmap, test_rounding_workspace_is_rejected_before_transform_scan, test_combined_selector_budget_includes_retained_groups).
  • Global RNG state is untouched. Sampling uses the local _RRandom port.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Undeclared factors. On the discretized route an integer-coded grouping variable not listed in factor_names is discretized as a metric and becomes one numeric coefficient, and a categorical one raises TypeError.
  • Undeclared row vectors. A caller-written source that omits has_explicit_weights/has_explicit_offset fits a slightly different discretized model than the equivalent ArrayRowSource.
  • The row-cap error reports bytes. When a group exceeds max_unique_rows, the reason is uniquecombs rows exceed row cap but required_bytes and budget_bytes are table bytes, so the MemoryError text shows bytes and the table budget, not rows and the cap.
  • Exact first means no rounding on small data. A group is rounded only when its distinct rows exceed the threshold, so on small data the compact frame is the distinct data and the fit equals the dense one. Because bases are built on compact rows, an m below a smooth's k fails with the basis's "exceeds number of unique data values" error.
  • Memmap files. selector_memmap_directory must not already hold compact-selector-{k}.dat files; leftover files from an interrupted process make the next fit raise FileExistsError.
  • Expensive caller fingerprints. A caller-written fingerprint() is not cached by the scope and runs at every stage check.

docs.title: Where to change things
docs.text:
• Add a built-in source: subclass ArrayRowSource or implement the three protocol members in jaxgam/data/source.py, export it from jaxgam/data/__init__.py, and add replay, fingerprint and lazy-column tests to tests/test_data/test_source.py.
  • Change what the fingerprint covers: ArrayRowSource._content_fingerprint (bump the jaxgam-row-source-v2 tag when the meaning changes).
  • Open the fingerprint scope on another route: wrap that route's setup and fit in single_fit_fingerprints() in jaxgam/api.py, and make its stages compare with stage_fingerprint.
  • Change grid resolution or rounding: _points_per_metric, range_grid and snap_to_range_grid in jaxgam/data/continuous_discretize.py; the R-gated tests there must still pass.
  • Change how variables are grouped: _discover_requests and _smooth_requests in jaxgam/data/continuous_frame.py, and _group_roles in jaxgam/formula/discrete/continuous_metadata.py, which must agree.
  • Add a budget limit: a field on DiscretizationBudget, its check before the allocation it bounds, and a reason string that _unavailable_scope maps to the right scope.

docs.title: Families, links and smooths: the extension points
Scope
docs.text: This page describes the three places a contributor extends JaxGAM's model space: distribution families (jaxgam/families/), link functions (jaxgam/links/) and smooth bases (jaxgam/smooths/). It covers the base-class contracts, the execution-capability contract that the fitting routes query, the registries and how strings are resolved at fit time, and the JAX or NumPy rule each extension must respect. It ends with checklists for adding a link, a family and a smooth.

docs.title: Where the code is
docs.text:
Module Role jaxgam/registry.py Generic Registry: case-insensitive string-to-class map with immutable built-ins. jaxgam/families/__init__.py Exports the family classes, the response supports, family_registry and get_family. jaxgam/families/base.py ExponentialFamily and the execution-contract descriptors FamilyExecutionCapabilities, StreamReductionPolicy, FamilyPadding, FamilyParameterSnapshot, FamilyInitialWorkingState; ResponseSupport and its constants. jaxgam/families/extended.py ExtendedFamily: families with extra parameters (theta) estimated with the smoothing parameters. jaxgam/families/standard.py Gaussian, Binomial, Poisson, Gamma. jaxgam/families/negative_binomial.py NegativeBinomial and its stable lgamma differences with custom JVPs. jaxgam/families/registry.py family_registry and get_family. jaxgam/families/execution_inventory.py FAMILY_EXECUTION_INVENTORY: a checked-in, descriptive record of every registered family, link and theta mode, with R constructor status and test evidence. Not read by any fit driver. jaxgam/links/__init__.py Exports the link classes, link_registry and get_link. jaxgam/links/links.py Link base class and the eight built-in links. jaxgam/links/registry.py link_registry and get_link. jaxgam/smooths/base.py Smooth base class. jaxgam/smooths/registry.py smooth_registry and get_smooth_class. jaxgam/smooths/gp_kernels.py GPKernel and gp_kernel_registry, the kernel extension point of bs="gp". jaxgam/fitting/family_execution.py Phase 2 consumer of the family contract: FamilyExecutionContext, FamilyExecutionLineage, batch working quantities for the bounded routes.

The smooth classes themselves are listed on setup.md.

docs.title: Families
docs.text:
ExponentialFamily is an abstract base class. A subclass sets the class attribute family_name and implements nine abstract members:

Member Used for default_link (property) The link when the constructor gets link=None. variance(mu) Working weights and the REML criterion (jaxgam/fitting/reml.py). dvar(mu) The Fletcher scale estimate in REML and in the regular EFS PIRLS. saturated_loglik(y, wt, scale, *, max_y=0) The saturated log-likelihood in the REML score (R's family$ls). deviance_resids(y, mu, wt) Signed deviance residuals; dev_resids sums their squares for the PIRLS deviance. aic(y, mu, wt, scale) Abstract, but no fit or result code calls it at HEAD; only tests/test_families.py does. _initialize_impl(y, wt) Starting mu. Called by the concrete initialize, which first checks y against response_support. valid_mu(mu), valid_eta(eta) Domain checks during initialization and PIRLS step control.

Concrete methods on the base class that the fit calls: working_weights (wt / (V(mu) * g'(mu)**2)), working_response (eta + (y - mu) * g'(mu)), dev_resids, initialize, and the explicit-parameter hooks working_weights_for_parameters, deviance_contributions_for_parameters, saturated_loglikelihood_for_parameters and deviance_derivative_contributions_for_parameters, which take a log_theta array and reject a non-empty one unless overridden.

Optional methods that some routes require, each raising NotImplementedError on the base class:

  • deviance_contributions (per-row deviance without the square root) and deviance_derivative_contributions (a smooth form for automatic differentiation). The dense route differentiates the latter to form observed-information weights, which mgcv uses in the REML log|H| for non-canonical links (jaxgam/fitting/pirls.py), so a custom family with a non-canonical link needs it even on the dense route.
  • source_dev_resids: pinned dev.resids arithmetic with no domain safeguard, for the discretized performance iteration (jaxgam/fitting/discrete/working.py).

Class attributes: n_theta (number of estimated extra parameters, 0 by default), scale_known, response_support (REAL, NON_NEGATIVE, POSITIVE or UNIT_INTERVAL) and canonical_link_cls. is_canonical is true when the link is an instance of canonical_link_cls; Gaussian, Binomial, Poisson and Gamma declare IdentityLink, LogitLink, LogLink and InverseLink. NegativeBinomial declares none, so it is never canonical.

The constructor is ExponentialFamily(link=None). link may be None, a link-registry name (resolved with Link.from_name) or a Link instance; anything else raises TypeError. The constructor does not check that the link suits the family: NegativeBinomial(link="logit") constructs, and the routes reject unsupported pairs later.

JIT identity. The dense kernels take the family as a static argument of jax.jit (for example static_argnames=("family", ...) in jaxgam/fitting/pirls.py). __hash__ and __eq__ therefore use _static_cache_key(): the class, link._cache_key(), n_theta and scale_known. Two equal families share compiled code. Any state that changes the traced arithmetic must be in this key; NegativeBinomial adds its fixed theta, because a fixed theta is read inside the trace.

docs.title: Extended families and the negative binomial
docs.text:
ExtendedFamily adds four abstract members for families whose extra parameters are estimated: get_theta(transformed=False) and put_theta(log_theta) (the mutable host state), deviance_fn(y, wt) and working_weights_fn(wt) (factories of pure functions of eta and log_theta, differentiated by the PIRLS custom JVP) and saturated_loglik_theta (the REML term with explicit theta). It also lists _log_theta in execution_dynamic_config_attributes, so the mutable value is kept out of the static configuration snapshot.

NegativeBinomial(theta=1.0, *, fixed=False, link=None), mgcv's nb() from R/efam.r, has V(mu) = mu + mu**2 / theta, known scale 1 and the log link by default. theta <= 0 raises ValueError.

  • fixed=False (the default): n_theta = 1 and theta is the starting value. On the dense route, when the model has penalties, the Newton optimizer appends log theta to the smoothing parameters and optimizes them jointly (_joint_theta in jaxgam/fitting/newton.py), then calls put_theta. GAM.fit deep-copies a family with n_theta > 0 before fitting, so a cached registry instance is never mutated.
  • fixed=True: n_theta = 0; theta is a constant baked into the trace and into _static_cache_key.

How the streamed, discretized and operator routes estimate theta is on their fitting pages (fitting_streamed.md, fitting_discrete.md, fitting_operator.md).

docs.title: The execution-capability contract
docs.text:
The bounded routes do not branch on family names. They ask the family what it can do:

  • execution_capabilities() returns a frozen FamilyExecutionCapabilities.
  • stream_reduction_policy() returns a StreamReductionPolicy naming the reported-scale and score-scale formulas (known_one, gaussian_fisher_edf_deviance, regular_fletcher, gaussian_fixed_sp, or unsupported).
  • execution_padding() returns finite response and eta values for masked rows.
  • execution_parameter_snapshot() returns the theta and scale modes and values as immutable scalars.
  • execution_static_config() freezes the family's and link's attributes, capabilities, padding and policy.

prepare_model stores the last two in FittingPreparation. FamilyExecutionLineage.validate in jaxgam/fitting/family_execution.py compares them again before each cached device dispatch, because JAX can reuse a compiled executable without retracing and so would not notice a family mutated after preparation.

The base class fills the capabilities from what the subclass implements: direct_deviance and differentiable_deviance are true only if the subclass overrides the corresponding method, dynamic_phi is not scale_known, and coefficient_system is "fisher" for a canonical link and "observed" otherwise. Subclasses override with dataclasses.replace.

Capability Meaning Read by row_separable Per-row quantities depend only on that row. jaxgam/api.py (_check_stream_fixed_family), jaxgam/execution/stream/pirls.py, jaxgam/execution/stream/regular.py, jaxgam/fitting/family_execution.py, jaxgam/fitting/operator/family.py fisher_working_system A positive Fisher working system exists. jaxgam/api.py, jaxgam/execution/stream/pirls.py, jaxgam/execution/stream/regular.py, jaxgam/fitting/family_execution.py observed_information Observed information is available through the direct deviance. jaxgam/api.py, jaxgam/execution/stream/regular.py, jaxgam/fitting/family_execution.py, jaxgam/fitting/operator/family.py direct_deviance deviance_contributions is implemented. jaxgam/api.py, jaxgam/execution/stream/pirls.py, jaxgam/execution/stream/regular.py, jaxgam/fitting/family_execution.py, jaxgam/fitting/operator/family.py differentiable_deviance deviance_derivative_contributions is implemented. jaxgam/api.py (required for unknown-scale streamed fixed-sp fits), jaxgam/fitting/family_execution.py, jaxgam/fitting/operator/family.py saturated_loglikelihood saturated_loglik is usable in a score. jaxgam/api.py, jaxgam/execution/stream/pirls.py, jaxgam/execution/stream/regular.py, jaxgam/fitting/family_execution.py dynamic_theta Theta is estimated and passed as a dynamic argument. jaxgam/api.py, jaxgam/execution/stream/regular.py, jaxgam/execution/stream/reml.py, jaxgam/fitting/family_execution.py, jaxgam/fitting/stream/reml.py dynamic_phi The scale is estimated. No reader outside jaxgam/families/ at HEAD. coefficient_system "fisher" or "observed" coefficient system. jaxgam/api.py, jaxgam/execution/stream/pirls.py, jaxgam/execution/stream/regular.py, jaxgam/fitting/family_execution.py, jaxgam/fitting/stream/reml.py fisher_equals_observed_for_score The two informations coincide in the score (canonical links). jaxgam/api.py, jaxgam/execution/efs.py, jaxgam/execution/stream/pirls.py, jaxgam/execution/stream/regular.py, jaxgam/fitting/stream/reml.py regular_fletcher_scale The Fletcher scale reduction applies (Gamma, non-canonical Gaussian). jaxgam/fitting/family_execution.py single_step_pirls The first accepted coefficient solve is final (Gaussian identity, gam.fit3's strictly additive branch). jaxgam/execution/operator/fit.py, jaxgam/execution/stream/regular.py, jaxgam/fitting/efs_regular_pirls.py initial_alpha_resolution Flags the Binomial/log start whose alpha is cancellation-sensitive. jaxgam/fitting/family_execution.py regular_performance_iteration bgam.fitd's Fisher performance iteration is validated for this family and link. jaxgam/api.py (_fit_discrete), jaxgam/execution/discrete/regular.py extended_performance_iteration bgam.fitd's extended-family iteration is validated (NB log, identity, sqrt). jaxgam/api.py, jaxgam/execution/discrete/regular.py

The dense route does not read the descriptor; it uses is_canonical, n_theta and scale_known directly. A route's own acceptance policy can be narrower than the capabilities: the streamed EFS check _check_stream_efs_family in jaxgam/api.py accepts only the built-in classes, by isinstance.

jaxgam/families/execution_inventory.py is a record, not policy: its module docstring says fit drivers must not consult it. It lists, for each registered family and link (and NB theta mode), whether pinned R's constructor accepts the pair, the dense and EFS evidence scope and the test names.

docs.title: Links
docs.text:
Link is an abstract base class with three abstract methods: link(mu), inverse(eta) and derivative(mu) (d eta / d mu). The other methods have defaults:

Method Default Who needs an override mu_eta(eta) 1 / derivative(inverse(eta)) Every built-in overrides it for stability; used by EFS, the discretized working model and the operator and stream initialization. second_derivative(mu) Raises NotImplementedError Required by the streamed fixed-sp route (_check_stream_fixed_family refuses a link without it) and the observed-Newton initialization. valid_eta(eta) All finite values Links with a restricted domain (SqrtLink requires eta > 0). linkinv(eta) Alias of inverse None. initial_link_cpu(mu) link(mu) as NumPy Links whose link clamps, so the R-style start can tell a clipped value from a valid one. source_g2g(mu) Raises NotImplementedError Only the negative binomial's extended route; IdentityLink, LogLink and SqrtLink implement it.

The built-in methods port R's make.link and mgcv's fix.family.link (R/gam.fit3.r) arithmetic. They clamp out-of-domain inputs rather than raise, so they stay usable inside jax.jit.

_stateless = True on a link makes _cache_key() return its class, so two instances share compiled code. A parameterized link must leave it False (the key is then id(self)) or override _cache_key to include its parameters; test_parameterized_custom_link_uses_identity in tests/test_families.py pins this.

docs.title: Smooths
docs.text:
The Smooth contract (details and the class hierarchy are on setup.md):

  • __init__(spec) receives the SmoothSpec; options come from spec.k, spec.bs and spec.extra_args.
  • setup(data) builds the training basis into self._X, sets n_coefs, rank, null_space_dim, and ends with self._is_setup = True. Without _X, training_design_matrix raises RuntimeError during assembly.
  • build_penalty_matrices() returns a list of Penalty objects, one per smoothing parameter, in the raw (unconstrained) basis.
  • predict_matrix(new_data) evaluates the raw basis on new data with the stored knots and transforms.
  • build_design_matrix(data) evaluates the raw basis on given data; the by-variable wrappers call it on the base smooth.
  • Optional: training_matrix (when training rows differ from prediction rows), copy_for_prediction (must drop every fit-only cache), copy_for_training.
  • Attributes model assembly reads with defaults: side_constrain (take part in gam_side, default true), _has_centering_constraint (read with getattr, default true; RandomEffectSmooth sets false), _random (summary test type), _noterp (skip tensor-margin reparameterization), _s_scale (the normalization factor te margins undo).

The penalty null space is declared through null_space_dim on the smooth and rank/null_space_dim on each Penalty.

docs.title: Registries
docs.text:
Registry(entries, name, cache_instances=False) in jaxgam/registry.py holds built-in entries in a read-only mapping and custom entries in a dict, both with lower-cased keys.

  • register(key, cls) adds a custom entry. A key that already exists, built-in or custom, raises ValueError. The class is not type-checked, and there is no way to unregister.
  • get_class(key) raises KeyError("Unknown {name}: 'key'. Available: ...") for a missing key.
  • get_instance(key) calls cls() with no arguments, and caches the instance when cache_instances is true.
Registry Module Keys Instances cached smooth_registry jaxgam/smooths/registry.py tp, ts, cr, cs, cc, gp, re, te, ti No family_registry jaxgam/families/registry.py gaussian, binomial, poisson, gamma, nb Yes link_registry jaxgam/links/registry.py identity, log, logit, inverse, probit, cloglog, sqrt, inverse_squared No gp_kernel_registry jaxgam/smooths/gp_kernels.py spherical, power_exponential, matern_3_2, matern_5_2, matern_7_2 No

The registries are exported from their packages (jaxgam.smooths, jaxgam.families, jaxgam.links), not from top-level jaxgam. There are no register_* helper functions: the registration API is <registry>.register(key, cls). Registration is process-global, so register before fitting, once per process.

docs.title: Resolution at fit time
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A["GAM.fit"] --> B["get_family(self.family)"]
    B -->|"str"| C["family_registry.get_instance:<br/>lower-cased key, cached no-argument instance"]
    B -->|"ExponentialFamily"| D["the instance as given"]
    B -->|"anything else"| E["TypeError"]
    C -->|"unknown key"| F["KeyError: Unknown family"]
    C --> G{"n_theta > 0?"}
    D --> G
    G -->|"yes"| H["copy.deepcopy of the family"]
    G -->|"no"| I["route on FitControl.execution"]
    H --> I
    I --> J["route checks: execution_capabilities,<br/>stream_reduction_policy"]
    A --> K["parse_formula: SmoothSpec"]
    K --> L["ModelSetup._build_smooth_components"]
    L --> M{"smooth_type is te or ti?"}
    M -->|"yes"| N["key = smooth_type"]
    M -->|"no"| O["key = bs"]
    N --> P["get_smooth_class: smooth_registry.get_class"]
    O --> P
    P -->|"unknown key"| Q["KeyError: Unknown basis type"]
    P --> R["cls(spec), then setup(data)"]
    R --> S["te or ti: get_smooth_class(spec.bs) per margin"]

A family string always yields the registry's shared instance with the default link; a non-default link needs an instance such as Gamma(link="log"). Links are resolved earlier, in the family constructor: Link.from_name(name) calls get_link, which returns a new instance from link_registry, and turns an unknown name into ValueError("Unknown link function ...").

The registry path for smooths runs inside ModelSetup.build, which the dense route and the discretized route's compact setup call. The other routes have their own term checks: streamed preparation accepts only cr/cs through _cubic_class in jaxgam/formula/prepare.py, and prepare_operator_model accepts only re, cr, cs, cc, tp, ts and gp. A registered custom smooth is therefore reachable on the dense route, and possibly the discretized one (not verified), but never on the stream or operator routes.
