docs.title: Rules and invariants
docs.text:
• Families and links run inside JIT. Their methods are called on JAX tracers in jaxgam/fitting/. They must use array_module(x) from jaxgam/jax_utils.py (NumPy for NumPy input, jax.numpy for JAX input), must not branch in Python on array values, and must not mutate arrays in place. test_link_methods_jax_match_numpy and test_link_jit_compiles in tests/test_links.py check the built-in links.
  • Static state is in the cache key. Anything a family or link reads inside a trace that can differ between instances must be part of _static_cache_key or _cache_key; otherwise two different models share one compiled executable.
  • Dynamic parameters are explicit. Estimated theta flows through the explicit-parameter hooks (such as working_weights_for_parameters) and the factories as an argument, never read from mutable storage inside a kernel; execution_dynamic_config_attributes names the storage to exclude from the static snapshot.
  • Smooths are Phase 1. Smooth code uses NumPy and SciPy (Numba and ctypes appear in the source-exact helpers) and never imports JAX.
  • Families are not imported by Phase 1. jaxgam/formula/prepare.py receives the family as an argument and duck-types it.
  • Built-in keys are immutable. tests/test_registry.py checks lower-casing, duplicate rejection and that built-ins are unchanged after a registration; the same file pins the nine smooth keys.
  • Every registered family and link has an inventory cell. test_execution_inventory_matches_pinned_r_constructors_and_evidence in tests/test_fitting/test_family_execution.py iterates family_registry.available and link_registry.available and requires a FAMILY_EXECUTION_INVENTORY entry for each pair.
  • Every registered smooth has a prediction-copy strategy. test_copy_for_prediction_registry_audit in tests/test_smooths/test_prediction_copy.py iterates smooth_registry.available.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Gamma.family_name is "Gamma" while its registry key is gamma; code comparing names must lower-case.
  • te and ti are registry keys but not bs values. They are selected by the function name; s(x, bs="te") recurses until Python raises a RecursionError.
  • String families are shared. family_registry caches one instance per key. Only families with n_theta > 0 are copied before fitting, so other mutable state on a custom family would be shared across fits.
  • Constructors do not validate links. A family accepts any registered link; refusal comes later and differs per route.
  • Registering in tests leaks. Registration cannot be undone, and the inventory and copy-audit tests iterate the registries, so a test that registers a custom class into a built-in registry affects later tests in the same process. Use a separate Registry instance in tests, as tests/test_registry.py does.
  • Default capabilities are conservative. A custom family that does not override deviance_contributions gets direct_deviance=False and is refused by the streamed fixed-sp route; one that does not override stream_reduction_policy and has unknown scale gets unsupported.

docs.title: Where to change things
docs.text:
• Change which routes accept a family or link: the family's execution_capabilities (for the discretized route, the regular_performance_iteration/extended_performance_iteration link lists in jaxgam/families/standard.py and jaxgam/families/negative_binomial.py), and the route checks in jaxgam/api.py (_check_stream_fixed_family, _check_stream_efs_family, the family checks in GAM._fit_discrete).
  • Add a GP kernel: subclass GPKernel in jaxgam/smooths/gp_kernels.py and add it to gp_kernel_registry (or call gp_kernel_registry.register); port the arithmetic of mgcv's gpE (R/smooth.r).

docs.title: Checklist: adding a link
docs.text:
1. Read R's make.link (R stats package) for the function, inverse and valideta, and mgcv's fix.family.link in R/gam.fit3.r for the derivative forms.
  2. In jaxgam/links/links.py, subclass Link; implement link, inverse, derivative, second_derivative and mu_eta with array_module; override valid_eta and initial_link_cpu if the domain is restricted or link clamps; set _stateless = True only if the class has no parameters.
  3. For a built-in link, add it to link_registry in jaxgam/links/registry.py and to jaxgam/links/__init__.py. For user code, call link_registry.register("name", MyLink) before constructing families with it.
  4. A built-in link becomes a cell of FAMILY_EXECUTION_INVENTORY: add it to _LINKS and the tables in jaxgam/families/execution_inventory.py.
  5. If a family should run it on the discretized or NB routes, extend that family's link lists in execution_capabilities and, for NB, _link_name in jaxgam/execution/stream/nb.py and _check_stream_efs_family.
  6. Tests in tests/test_links.py: round trip, mu_eta against finite differences, values against R make.link through the R bridge, JAX against NumPy, and JIT compilation. Add family fits with the new link to tests/test_validation_matrix.py if it is meant for R parity.

docs.title: Checklist: adding a family
docs.text:
1. Read the R family constructor (stats::family objects, or mgcv's R/efam.r for an extended family) and mgcv's fix.family.var and fix.family.ls in R/gam.fit3.r, which supply dvar and the saturated log-likelihood.
  2. Subclass ExponentialFamily (or ExtendedFamily for estimated parameters) in jaxgam/families/. Set family_name, scale_known, response_support, canonical_link_cls, and implement the nine abstract members with array_module. Give it a no-argument constructor if it should be usable by name.
  3. For the bounded routes, implement deviance_contributions and deviance_derivative_contributions, and override stream_reduction_policy and execution_capabilities to declare exactly what is implemented; source_dev_resids is needed for the discretized performance iteration.
  4. Extend _static_cache_key with any state read inside a trace. For an extended family, implement get_theta, put_theta, deviance_fn, working_weights_fn, saturated_loglik_theta, the four explicit-parameter hooks and execution_parameter_snapshot.
  5. For a built-in family, add it to family_registry in jaxgam/families/registry.py and jaxgam/families/__init__.py, and add inventory cells in jaxgam/families/execution_inventory.py. For user code, call family_registry.register("name", MyFamily) or pass an instance as GAM(..., family=MyFamily()).
  6. Tests: unit tests of each method against R in tests/test_families.py; JIT tests (compile the dense PIRLS with the family); R fits in tests/test_validation_matrix.py; and, for each bounded route it should run on, that route's tests under tests/test_execution/.

docs.title: Checklist: adding a smooth
docs.text:
1. Read the constructor smooth.construct.<bs>.smooth.spec and Predict.matrix.<class> in mgcv's R/smooth.r, and any C routine it calls in src/. Note how smoothCon (R/smooth.r) centers and scales the result.
  2. Subclass Smooth in a new module under jaxgam/smooths/, NumPy and SciPy only. In setup, build _X, the penalty, n_coefs, rank and null_space_dim, apply smoothCon's scaling (_smoothcon_normalize), and set _is_setup. Implement build_design_matrix, build_penalty_matrices and predict_matrix; override training_matrix if training rows differ from prediction rows, and copy_for_prediction if the class keeps caches other than _X and _S or nested smooths.
  3. Set the assembly flags if the basis needs them: side_constrain = False to stay out of gam_side, _has_centering_constraint = False to skip centering, _noterp = True if tensor margins should not be reparameterized.
  4. For a built-in smooth, add the key to smooth_registry in jaxgam/smooths/registry.py and the export to jaxgam/smooths/__init__.py, and update the expected keys in tests/test_registry.py. For user code, call smooth_registry.register("key", MySmooth); it is then selectable with s(x, bs="key") on the dense route.
  5. Add the class to the audit in tests/test_smooths/test_prediction_copy.py, either by overriding copy_for_prediction or by adding it to the audited default list there.
  6. Tests: a new tests/test_smooths/test_<name>.py comparing basis, penalty and prediction matrix with R's smoothCon output through the R bridge; prediction round trip; by= and te margin use if supported; and R fits in tests/test_validation_matrix.py.
  7. If the streamed, discretized or operator routes should accept it, extend _cubic_class in jaxgam/formula/prepare.py, the memory bounds in jaxgam/formula/discrete/continuous_setup.py and jaxgam/formula/discrete/design.py, or the term checks in jaxgam/formula/operator/prepare.py; see setup.md.

The proposed fitting-engine refactor in docs/unify_fit/design.md concerns jaxgam/fitting/, jaxgam/execution/ and routing in jaxgam/api.py; it describes the family capability contract as an abstraction to keep.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: This page follows one GAM(...).fit(...) call through jaxgam/api.py: the checks made when the GAM is constructed, the checks fit makes, how it picks a route and a sub-route, which setup and fitting modules each route calls, how prior weights and the offset travel, how each route builds its result, and every execution_route label and execution_fallback_reason the code can report. The algorithms behind each route are on the Phase 2 pages.

docs.title: Where the code is
docs.text: Path Role jaxgam/api.py GAM, GAM.fit, the _fit_* methods and module-level route functions, _check_scope_guards, _resolve_device. jaxgam/control.py FitControl and its nested controls; validation of field combinations in __post_init__. jaxgam/families/registry.py get_family, which turns GAM(family=) into a family instance. jaxgam/formula/parser.py parse_formula, called on every route. jaxgam/formula/design.py ModelSetup.build, dense Phase 1. jaxgam/formula/prepare.py, jaxgam/formula/design_provider.py prepare_model and StreamDesign, streamed Phase 1. jaxgam/formula/operator/prepare.py prepare_operator_model, operator Phase 1. jaxgam/fitting/data.py FittingData.from_setup (dense) and PreparedFittingMetadata.from_prepared (streamed), the Phase 1 to 2 hand-off. jaxgam/data/source.py RowSource, single_fit_fingerprints. jaxgam/results.py The result constructors each route ends in.

docs.title: Construction: GAM.__init__
docs.text:
GAM(formula, family="gaussian", method="REML", sp=None, control=None, **kwargs) first calls _check_scope_guards(method, kwargs), then stores formula, family, method.upper(), sp, device (from kwargs), optimizer (kwargs.get("optimizer") or "newton") and control (FitControl() when None). The extra keywords accepted are the set _ACCEPTED_KWARGS: device, backend, optimizer, select, gamma, knots.

_check_scope_guards runs these checks in order:

Condition Exception any keyword outside _ACCEPTED_KWARGS TypeError naming the unexpected keywords and the accepted arguments method.upper() == "ML" NotImplementedError (ML needs mgcv's range-space determinant, MLpenalty1 in src/gdi.c) any other method except "REML" ValueError backend not None or "jax" NotImplementedError device not None, "cpu" or "gpu" ValueError optimizer not None and not a str ValueError optimizer a string other than "newton" or "efs" NotImplementedError select truthy NotImplementedError gamma != 1.0 NotImplementedError knots is not None NotImplementedError

After the guards, __init__ raises TypeError if control is neither a FitControl nor None. Nothing else is validated here: an unknown family name, a malformed formula or a wrong-length sp fails only in fit. FitControl itself has already rejected inconsistent fields when it was built (for example execution="discrete" without discretization, or smoothing_strategy="working_model_reml" on another route), with ValueError or TypeError. tests/test_api/test_gam.py and tests/test_control.py cover these checks.

docs.title: What fit does before routing
docs.text:
fit(data, weights=None, offset=None, *, result="full"):

  1. Rejects a result other than "full", "inference" or "prediction" with ValueError.
  2. Calls get_family(self.family). A name is looked up in the family registry (KeyError if unknown) and returns a cached shared instance; an instance is used as given.
  3. If the family has n_theta > 0 (an estimated negative binomial theta), it is deep-copied, so the fit can update theta without mutating the registry's instance or the caller's object.
  4. Dispatches on self.control.execution, in this order: "operator" to _fit_operator, "stream" to _fit_stream, "discrete" to _fit_discrete; anything else (only "dense" can reach here) continues inline in fit.
flowchart TD
    fit["GAM.fit"] --> result_check{"result in full, inference, prediction"}
    result_check -->|"no"| result_error["ValueError"]
    result_check -->|"yes"| get_family["get_family, deepcopy if n_theta above 0"]
    get_family --> execution{"control.execution"}
    execution -->|"operator"| _fit_operator["_fit_operator"]
    execution -->|"stream"| _fit_stream["_fit_stream"]
    execution -->|"discrete"| _fit_discrete["_fit_discrete"]
    execution -->|"dense"| row_check{"data is a RowSource"}
    row_check -->|"yes"| row_error["TypeError"]
    row_check -->|"no"| solver_check{"linear_solver is cholesky"}
    solver_check -->|"no"| solver_error["NotImplementedError"]
    solver_check -->|"yes"| setup["parse_formula, ModelSetup.build,<br/>_resolve_device, FittingData.from_setup"]
    setup --> gaussian_compression{"gaussian_compression"}
    gaussian_compression -->|"false"| sp_check
    gaussian_compression -->|"true"| build_dense_gaussian_qr_provider["build_dense_gaussian_qr_provider<br/>unless optimizer efs with sp None"]
    build_dense_gaussian_qr_provider -->|"provider or fallback reason"| sp_check{"sp is not None"}
    sp_check -->|"yes"| _fit_fixed_sp["_fit_fixed_sp<br/>lambda_strategy fixed"]
    sp_check -->|"no"| penalty_check{"fd.n_penalties == 0"}
    penalty_check -->|"yes"| newton_plain["newton_optimize<br/>newton_reml"]
    penalty_check -->|"no"| optimizer_check{"optimizer == efs"}
    optimizer_check -->|"yes"| dense_efs["dense_efs_known_scale or<br/>dense_efs_unknown_scale, efs_reml"]
    optimizer_check -->|"no"| use_gaussian_qr_lbfgs{"use_gaussian_qr_lbfgs"}
    use_gaussian_qr_lbfgs -->|"yes"| optimize_gaussian_qr_lbfgs["optimize_gaussian_qr_lbfgs<br/>lbfgs_reml"]
    use_gaussian_qr_lbfgs -->|"no"| newton_optimize["newton_optimize<br/>newton_reml"]
    _fit_fixed_sp --> _from_fit["_warn_factor_regularization,<br/>GAMResults._from_fit"]
    newton_plain --> _from_fit
    dense_efs --> _from_fit
    optimize_gaussian_qr_lbfgs --> _from_fit
    newton_optimize --> _from_fit

Read from the top. The three row-source routes leave fit at the first branch; the dense route runs to the bottom. use_gaussian_qr_lbfgs is only consulted when a Gaussian QR provider was built (otherwise it is skipped and Newton runs); it is true above 50 penalties (GAUSSIAN_LBFGS_PENALTY_THRESHOLD in jaxgam/execution/gaussian_qr/preparation.py).

docs.title: The dense route, inline in fit
docs.text:
The dense route has no _fit_dense method; it is the tail of GAM.fit.

  1. data must not be a RowSource (TypeError), and control.linear_solver must be "cholesky" (NotImplementedError naming the route that solver belongs to).
  2. Phase 1: parse_formula(self.formula) then ModelSetup.build(spec, data, weights, offset).
  3. Phase 1 to 2: _resolve_device(self.device) (None keeps JAX's default device; "gpu" without a GPU backend raises RuntimeError), then FittingData.from_setup(setup, family_obj, device=jax_device), which transfers the arrays with to_jax.
  4. Gaussian QR request. With control.gaussian_compression: if optimizer == "efs" and sp is None the request is recorded as unmet; otherwise build_dense_gaussian_qr_provider(fd) (jaxgam/execution/gaussian_qr/optimizer.py) either returns a score provider and sets execution_route = "gaussian_qr", or raises GaussianQRIneligible, whose message becomes execution_fallback_reason while the ordinary dense fit runs.
  5. Phase 2, in this order of precedence:
  6. sp given: _fit_fixed_sp(fd, sp, method, score_provider=...), lambda_strategy = "fixed". It validates sp with _fixed_log_smoothing_parameters (ValueError for a wrong count or a non-positive or non-finite value). Families with estimated theta or unknown scale still run newton_optimize with pin_lambda=True, so theta or the scale is estimated at the fixed smoothing parameters, as in mgcv's gam.outer (R/mgcv.r); known-scale families run one PIRLS (source_pirls or pirls_loop) and evaluate REMLCriterion once. A Gaussian QR provider with more than 50 penalties sends a fixed-sp fit to optimize_gaussian_qr_lbfgs with pin_lambda=True.
  7. no penalties: newton_optimize(fd, method), whose purely parametric shortcut runs one inner fit; lambda_strategy = "newton_reml". This branch wins over optimizer="efs".
  8. optimizer == "efs": family checks (below), then dense_efs_known_scale or dense_efs_unknown_scale (jaxgam/execution/efs.py) started from efs_initial_log_lambda and, for unknown scale, efs_initial_log_scale; lambda_strategy = "efs_reml".
  9. otherwise Newton: newton_optimize(fd, method, score_provider=...), lambda_strategy = "newton_reml", or optimize_gaussian_qr_lbfgs and "lbfgs_reml" when a QR provider exists and there are more than 50 penalties.
  10. After an estimated-sp EFS fit with estimated theta, the selected theta is written back with family_obj.put_theta. (Newton synchronizes theta itself when it builds its result.)
  11. _warn_factor_regularization(fit_result) issues a RuntimeWarning if the final penalized Hessian needed a diagonal jitter in its Cholesky factor.
  12. Phase 2 to 3: GAMResults._from_fit(..., result_mode=result, ...) builds GAMResults, GAMInferenceResult or GAMPredictionResult.

Dense EFS refusals: an estimated-theta negative binomial with identity or sqrt link whose zero-coefficient means are invalid for the offset raises ValueError; a family or link outside _known_scale_family_supported or _unknown_scale_family_supported raises NotImplementedError.

sequenceDiagram
    participant GAM as GAM.fit
    participant parse_formula as parse_formula
    participant ModelSetup as ModelSetup.build
    participant FittingData as FittingData.from_setup
    participant NewtonOptimizer as NewtonOptimizer.run
    participant REMLCriterion as REMLCriterion
    participant GAMResults as GAMResults._from_fit
    GAM->>parse_formula: formula string
    parse_formula-->>GAM: FormulaSpec
    GAM->>ModelSetup: spec, data, weights, offset
    ModelSetup-->>GAM: ModelSetup with X, y, weights, penalties, coef_map
    GAM->>FittingData: setup, family, device
    FittingData-->>GAM: FittingData on the JAX device via to_jax
    GAM->>NewtonOptimizer: newton_optimize builds NewtonOptimizer and calls run
    NewtonOptimizer->>REMLCriterion: initial PIRLS fit, then score, gradient and Hessian
    loop outer Newton iterations, at most max_iter
        NewtonOptimizer->>NewtonOptimizer: _safe_newton_step
        NewtonOptimizer->>NewtonOptimizer: _step_halve calls _fit_and_score, jitted PIRLS plus score
        NewtonOptimizer->>REMLCriterion: _make_criterion and _check_convergence
    end
    NewtonOptimizer-->>GAM: NewtonResult from _build_result
    GAM->>GAM: _warn_factor_regularization
    GAM->>GAMResults: fit_result, setup, spec, data, family, fd, result_mode
    GAMResults->>GAMResults: to_numpy, Vp, per-smooth EDF and edf1, null deviance
    GAMResults-->>GAM: GAMResults, GAMInferenceResult or GAMPredictionResult

Each arrow into NewtonOptimizer is host Python; the jitted work is inside _fit_and_score (one fused XLA program for the penalty, the PIRLS loop and the criterion score) and inside the gradient and Hessian evaluation. _step_halve_gaussian replaces _step_halve for Gaussian identity fits.

docs.title: The streamed route: _fit_stream and _fit_stream_routes
docs.text:
_fit_stream checks, in order: linear_solver == "pcg" (ValueError), data not a RowSource (TypeError), weights or offset passed (ValueError), result != "prediction" (NotImplementedError). It then classifies the fit:

  • estimated_efs: optimizer == "efs" and sp is None;
  • estimated_exact: optimizer == "newton" and sp is None;
  • fixed: sp given.

_gaussian_qr_request_fallback returns a reason when a Gaussian QR request cannot apply (EFS selection, or not exactly Gaussian with IdentityLink); otherwise the fit is a Gaussian QR candidate. Family and solver checks follow: estimated EFS needs linear_solver="qr" and passes _check_stream_efs_family; estimated exact REML needs "qr" unless it is a Gaussian QR candidate, and passes _check_stream_fixed_family(family, "qr"); a fixed fit passes _check_stream_fixed_family(family, linear_solver). All raise NotImplementedError. The rest runs inside single_fit_fingerprints(), so an in-memory source is hashed once at the start and once at the end, and a change raises RuntimeError.

_fit_stream_routes does Phase 1 with prepare_model(spec, data, family=..., batch_rows=..., maximum_bytes=...) and wraps the result in StreamDesign(prepared, data). Then:

flowchart TD
    prepare_model["prepare_model, StreamDesign"] --> candidate{"Gaussian QR candidate"}
    candidate -->|"yes"| weights_check{"weights within 1e-10 to 1e10"}
    weights_check -->|"no"| reason_weights["fallback reason, continue"]
    weights_check -->|"yes"| preflight_streamed_gaussian_qr_workspace["preflight_streamed_gaussian_qr_workspace<br/>MemoryError if over budget"]
    candidate -->|"no"| efs_check
    reason_weights --> efs_check
    preflight_streamed_gaussian_qr_workspace --> efs_check{"estimated_efs"}
    efs_check -->|"yes, no penalties"| _fit_stream_parametric_bypass["_fit_stream_parametric_bypass<br/>stream_parametric_qr"]
    efs_check -->|"yes"| fit_streamed_efs["fit_streamed_efs<br/>stream_efs_qr"]
    efs_check -->|"no"| qr_ready{"QR workspace preflighted"}
    qr_ready -->|"yes"| build_stream_gaussian_qr_provider["build_stream_gaussian_qr_provider"]
    build_stream_gaussian_qr_provider -->|"provider"| _fit_stream_gaussian_qr["_fit_stream_gaussian_qr<br/>stream_gaussian_qr"]
    build_stream_gaussian_qr_provider -->|"GaussianQRIneligible"| exact_solver
    qr_ready -->|"no"| exact_solver{"estimated_exact without qr solver"}
    exact_solver -->|"yes"| exact_error["NotImplementedError"]
    exact_solver -->|"no"| _preflight_stream_workspace["_preflight_stream_workspace<br/>MemoryError if over budget"]
    _preflight_stream_workspace --> exact_check{"estimated_exact"}
    exact_check -->|"yes"| _fit_stream_exact_reml["_fit_stream_exact_reml<br/>stream_exact_reml_qr"]
    exact_check -->|"no, NegativeBinomial"| _fit_stream_fixed_nb["_fit_stream_fixed_nb<br/>stream_qr"]
    exact_check -->|"no, QR-only family or qr with known scale"| _fit_stream_fixed_regular["_fit_stream_fixed_regular<br/>stream_qr"]
    exact_check -->|"no, otherwise"| fit_streamed_pirls["fit_streamed_pirls<br/>stream or stream_qr"]

Read from the top; each leaf shows the function that fits and the execution_route it reports. "QR-only family" means _stream_legacy_fisher_eligible(family) is false. The last leaf reports "stream_qr" when linear_solver == "qr" and "stream" otherwise.

What each streamed leaf calls:

  • fit_streamed_pirls (jaxgam/execution/stream/pirls.py): fixed-sp streamed PIRLS with a Cholesky or QR solve.
  • _fit_stream_fixed_regular: known scale uses fit_regular_streamed_pirls (jaxgam/execution/stream/regular.py); unknown scale uses optimize_regular_stream_reml (jaxgam/execution/stream/reml.py) with the smoothing parameters pinned and the log scale free.
  • _fit_stream_fixed_nb: fixed theta uses fit_nb_streamed_pirls (jaxgam/execution/stream/nb.py); estimated theta uses optimize_nb_stream_reml (jaxgam/execution/stream/nb_reml.py) with the smoothing parameters pinned, then put_theta.
  • _fit_stream_exact_reml: two startup scans in prepare_stream_reml_start (jaxgam/execution/stream/efs_start.py) when there are penalties, then optimize_nb_stream_reml or optimize_regular_stream_reml over log smoothing parameters plus log theta or log scale. With no penalty, known scale and no theta it delegates to the fixed-sp functions and relabels the result (lambda_strategy = "exact_reml_no_parameters").
  • fit_streamed_efs (jaxgam/execution/stream/efs.py) with control.efs.
  • _fit_stream_parametric_bypass: one streamed coefficient fit (fit_nb_streamed_pirls or fit_regular_streamed_pirls), plus one replay for the saturated likelihood when the scale is unknown; lambda_strategy = "newton_reml".
  • _fit_stream_gaussian_qr: newton_optimize with the QR score provider, or optimize_gaussian_qr_lbfgs above 50 penalties; pin_lambda when sp is given.

Every streamed leaf ends in GAMPredictionResult._from_stream_fit, called with the row-free StreamFitState, the PreparedModel, the PreparedFittingMetadata and, for optimizer routes, a selected_fit that carries the outer score and convergence: built by _selected_stream_fit, or the accepted fit of the EFS execution on stream_efs_qr. _with_execution_fallback_reason then records any unmet Gaussian QR request.

docs.title: The discretized route: _fit_discrete
docs.text:
_fit_discrete checks, in order: data not a RowSource (TypeError); weights or offset passed (ValueError); result != "prediction", linear_solver != "cholesky", sp is None without smoothing_strategy="working_model_reml", sp is None with optimizer != "newton", an ExtendedFamily without the extended_performance_iteration capability, and any family that is neither Gaussian with its canonical link nor declares regular_performance_iteration or extended_performance_iteration (all NotImplementedError). It then parses the formula, resolves the device and, inside single_fit_fingerprints(), calls fit_discrete_gaussian (Gaussian identity) or fit_discrete_regular (every other admitted family), and builds the result with GAMPredictionResult._from_discrete. The route never reads optimizer when sp is given, and ignores gaussian_compression except to report it.

Phase 1 for this route is called from the driver: _prepared_discrete in jaxgam/execution/discrete/gaussian.py runs build_continuous_discrete_setup (which scans the source to build the compact frame and runs ModelSetup.build on it), build_discretization_metadata, build_request_compression (only for prediction_policy="mgcv_predict_bamd") and build_continuous_discrete_design (no source scan), and releases the compact selectors when the fit ends.

sequenceDiagram
    participant GAM as GAM._fit_discrete
    participant single_fit_fingerprints as single_fit_fingerprints
    participant fit_discrete_gaussian as fit_discrete_gaussian
    participant build_continuous_discrete_setup as build_continuous_discrete_setup
    participant RowSource as RowSource
    participant discrete_ops as fitting/discrete/ops.py kernels
    participant fit_gaussian_working_model_statistics as fit_gaussian_working_model_statistics
    participant GAMPredictionResult as GAMPredictionResult._from_discrete
    GAM->>GAM: route checks, parse_formula, _resolve_device
    GAM->>single_fit_fingerprints: enter, first digest of the source is kept
    GAM->>fit_discrete_gaussian: spec, source, sp, control, device
    fit_discrete_gaussian->>build_continuous_discrete_setup: via _prepared_discrete
    build_continuous_discrete_setup->>RowSource: setup scans, scan with batch_rows
    build_continuous_discrete_setup-->>fit_discrete_gaussian: compact setup, ModelSetup.build on compact rows
    fit_discrete_gaussian->>fit_discrete_gaussian: metadata, indexed design, _solver_plan, _check_fit_budget
    fit_discrete_gaussian->>discrete_ops: to_device_discrete_design
    loop fit scan 1, one batch at a time
        fit_discrete_gaussian->>RowSource: scan with batch_rows
        fit_discrete_gaussian->>discrete_ops: discrete_xwxd and discrete_xwyd add to XtWX and XtWy
    end
    alt sp is None
        fit_discrete_gaussian->>fit_gaussian_working_model_statistics: Sl.fitChol proposals on frozen statistics
    else sp given
        fit_discrete_gaussian->>fit_discrete_gaussian: host Cholesky solve
    end
    loop fit scan 2, one batch at a time
        fit_discrete_gaussian->>RowSource: scan with batch_rows
        fit_discrete_gaussian->>discrete_ops: discrete_xbd gives fitted values for the residual deviance
    end
    fit_discrete_gaussian-->>GAM: DiscreteFit, row-free
    GAM->>GAMPredictionResult: fit_state, family, formula, method, control, sp
    GAMPredictionResult-->>GAM: execution_route discrete
    GAM->>single_fit_fingerprints: exit, source hashed again, RuntimeError if changed
    GAM->>GAM: _with_execution_fallback_reason

Read top to bottom: setup scans happen before any fit scan, and source_scans on the result counts only the two fit scans. For the other families fit_discrete_regular (jaxgam/execution/discrete/regular.py) replaces the middle part with the performance iteration of bgam.fitd (R/bam.r): every outer iteration rescans the source to form working weights and takes one Sl.fitChol proposal (R/fast-REML.r), and an estimated negative binomial theta adds scans of its own.

docs.title: The operator route: _fit_operator and _fit_operator_efs
docs.text:
_fit_operator checks, in order: linear_solver != "pcg" (ValueError); result != "prediction", uncertainty != "none", sp is None without optimizer="efs", an estimated theta, more than one theta, device other than None or "cpu" (all NotImplementedError); data not a RowSource (TypeError); weights or offset passed (ValueError). With sp=None and optimizer="efs" it hands over to _fit_operator_efs. Otherwise it validates sp (count, real values, positive and finite: ValueError; a 16-bytes-per-value check against the budget: MemoryError), calls prepare_operator_model with an OperatorPreparationControl built from the smaller of batch_rows and the source's row count (_operator_fit_batch_rows), memory_budget_bytes and OperatorControl.max_modest_coefficients, rechecks the sp count against model.penalties.n_penalties, fits with fit_operator_fixed_sp (jaxgam/execution/operator/fit.py) and builds the result with GAMPredictionResult._from_operator_fit.

_fit_operator_efs admits only a canonical Poisson family and batch_rows inside CALIBRATED_OPERATOR_EFS_DOMAIN before any scan, then prepares the model with one eighth of the memory budget, checks the prepared shape against the calibrated domain (one indexed random effect, at most CALIBRATED_OPERATOR_EFS_MAX_MODEST modest coefficients), builds the start with prepare_indexed_operator_efs_start, and runs run_operator_efs_known_scale over a SourceOperatorEFSFitProvider (jaxgam/execution/operator/efs_controller.py). Outside the domain it raises NotImplementedError; a result that cannot fit the remaining budget raises MemoryError. The result is _from_operator_fit on the accepted fit, then dataclasses.replace with the selected score, its error bound, scale, edf_total, convergence fields and lambda_strategy = "efs_reml". The operator route does not open a single_fit_fingerprints scope; its preparation and fit verify replay themselves.

docs.title: How weights and the offset travel
docs.text: Route Where they come from Where they go dense fit(weights=, offset=), each of shape (n,). ModelSetup.build defaults weights to ones, rejects a wrong shape, negative or non-finite weights, all-zero weights and a non-finite offset with ValueError. setup.weights and setup.offset, transferred to the device as fd.wt and fd.offset; used again in _from_fit for the null deviance, and _offset_was_nonzero(setup) tells the predictor to warn when new data come without an offset. stream RowBatch.weight and RowBatch.offset of each scanned batch; fit refuses separate arrays. Reduced per batch by the drivers. prepare_model records their range in prepared.fitting.response, which decides Gaussian QR weight eligibility and the predictor's offset_was_nonzero. discrete RowBatch.weight and RowBatch.offset. declared_row_vectors reads the source's has_explicit_weights and has_explicit_offset; an undeclared attribute counts as supplied, which changes the seeded compact-frame padding as supplied vectors do in bam. Accumulated into the indexed statistics in every fit scan; DiscreteFit.offset_was_nonzero reaches the predictor. operator RowBatch.weight and RowBatch.offset. Moved to the device per batch in jaxgam/execution/operator/fit.py; the fit reports offset_was_nonzero. Operator EFS additionally requires unit weights and a zero offset.

docs.title: How each route builds its result
docs.text:
Route Constructor Notes dense GAMResults._from_fit result_mode picks GAMResults, GAMInferenceResult or GAMPredictionResult from the same fit. stream GAMPredictionResult._from_stream_fit Recomputes the REML score from the stream state unless a selected_fit supplies it. discrete GAMPredictionResult._from_discrete Records prediction_policy and the bounded discretization metadata. operator GAMPredictionResult._from_operator_fit Fixed sp: score=None, edf_total=None, scale=None for unknown-scale families.

Phase 3: results and prediction describes what each constructor keeps.

docs.title: execution_route labels
docs.text:
Label Set in Meaning dense GAM.fit; also the field default on _FitDiagnostics and GAMPredictionResult ordinary dense fit gaussian_qr GAM.fit dense fit through a Gaussian QR score provider stream _fit_stream_routes (and the default of _from_stream_fit) fit_streamed_pirls with the Cholesky solver stream_qr _fit_stream_routes, _fit_stream_fixed_regular, _fit_stream_fixed_nb fixed-sp streamed fit with the QR solver stream_gaussian_qr _fit_stream_gaussian_qr streamed Gaussian QR route stream_exact_reml_qr _fit_stream_exact_reml (both branches) exact streamed REML stream_efs_qr _fit_stream_routes streamed EFS stream_parametric_qr _fit_stream_parametric_bypass optimizer="efs" on a model with no penalties discrete GAMPredictionResult._from_discrete discretized route operator GAMPredictionResult._from_operator_fit, _fit_operator_efs operator route

lambda_strategy takes the values fixed, newton_reml, lbfgs_reml, efs_reml, exact_reml, exact_reml_no_parameters (all set in jaxgam/api.py) and working_model_reml (from the discrete fit state). execution_path is "jax" except on the discretized route, where _from_discrete reports jax_actions_numpy_solve, jax_actions_working_model_numpy_postestimation or jax_actions_performance_iteration_numpy_postestimation.

docs.title: execution_fallback_reason values
docs.text:
The field is set only for a Gaussian QR request that did not apply; the fit then runs on the route it would have taken without the request.

Reason Set in "Gaussian QR compression requires Newton smoothing selection." GAM.fit (dense) and _gaussian_qr_request_fallback (stream) "Gaussian QR requires the exact Gaussian family with identity link" _gaussian_qr_request_fallback (stream); also a GaussianQRIneligible message "Gaussian QR currently requires unclipped finite positive weights" _fit_stream_routes; also a GaussianQRIneligible message the message of a caught GaussianQRIneligible GAM.fit (dense, from build_dense_gaussian_qr_provider) and _fit_stream_routes (from build_stream_gaussian_qr_provider). Messages include "Gaussian QR smoothing optimization requires at least one penalty", "Gaussian QR currently requires a full identifiable coefficient map" and "Gaussian QR requires finite dense fitting data" (jaxgam/execution/gaussian_qr/optimizer.py, jaxgam/execution/gaussian_qr/preparation.py). "Gaussian QR compression requires execution 'dense' or 'stream'." _discrete_gaussian_qr_request_fallback

The operator route never reads gaussian_compression, so its results always carry None.

DiscreteFit (jaxgam/execution/discrete/gaussian.py) is the row-free state of a discretized fit. The class diagram shows only the members that this page discusses.

docs.title: Rules and invariants
docs.text:
• Route checks run before data access. Every row-source route rejects a wrong solver, a wrong result and separate weights or offset before it parses the formula or scans the source; tests/test_execution/test_stream_api.py, tests/test_execution/test_discrete_routes.py and tests/test_execution/test_operator_routes.py assert these refusals, and tests/test_inference/test_operator_geometry.py checks that the operator refusals precede any source access.
  • The registry family is never mutated. Families with estimated theta are deep-copied in fit; result builders snapshot the family again (tests/test_result_mode.py, test_from_fit_owns_independent_family_snapshots_with_final_theta).
  • A supplied sp is reported verbatim. All constructors pass the caller's sp through _report_smoothing_params (tests/test_supplied_smoothing_params.py).
  • An unmet Gaussian QR request never changes the fit. The fit takes the route it would take without the request and records why (tests/test_execution/test_gaussian_stream_routes.py, tests/test_execution/test_gaussian_optimizer.py, test_discrete_gaussian_qr_request_keeps_the_discrete_fit_bitwise in tests/test_execution/test_discrete_routes.py).
  • Other routes do not change the dense result. test_operator_control_leaves_existing_routes_bitwise_unchanged in tests/test_execution/test_operator_routes.py and test_published_routes_never_enter_the_discrete_route in tests/test_execution/test_discrete_routes.py guard the dispatch.
  • One fingerprint scope per fit. The stream and discrete routes wrap the whole fit in single_fit_fingerprints(); nested stages join it.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• fit defaults to result="full", which every row-source route refuses: examples for those routes must pass result="prediction".
  • sp with optimizer="efs" runs the fixed-sp path on every route; the optimizer only matters when sp is None. On the discrete route optimizer="efs" is refused only when sp is None.
  • A fixed sp does not always mean "no optimization" on the dense route: Gaussian, Gamma and estimated-theta negative binomial fits still run newton_optimize with pin_lambda=True to estimate scale or theta, and report its n_iter.
  • Estimated streamed REML without linear_solver="qr" passes the first check when Gaussian QR was requested, and fails later with NotImplementedError only if the QR route turns out to be ineligible.
  • _preflight_stream_workspace charges the requested batch_rows, not the source's row count, so a small source can fail the preflight at the default batch_rows with a large coefficient count.

docs.title: Where to change things
docs.text:
To do this Edit Accept a new GAM keyword _ACCEPTED_KWARGS and _check_scope_guards in jaxgam/api.py; store it in GAM.__init__ Add a field to FitControl jaxgam/control.py (field and __post_init__ rule), then its reader in the relevant _fit_* function Add a streamed sub-route _fit_stream (classification and checks) and _fit_stream_routes (dispatch); give it a new execution_route label and add it to the table above Change dense smoothing selection the dense tail of GAM.fit and _fit_fixed_sp Change what a route refuses the check list at the top of its _fit_* method; keep refusals before any source scan Change result construction the constructor named in the table above, in jaxgam/results.py

A planned refactor will replace the per-route methods in jaxgam/api.py with a shared fitting engine; see the unified fitting design.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: This page covers the default in-memory fit (FitControl(execution="dense")): the Phase 1 to Phase 2 boundary object FittingData, the inner coefficient loops (PIRLS and the pinned ports of mgcv's gam.fit3 and gam.fit4), the REML criterion, the outer Newton optimizer for the log smoothing parameters, fixed-sp fits, negative-binomial theta, the dense extended Fellner-Schall (EFS) optimizer and the opt-in Gaussian QR route. How GAM.fit() reaches this code is on the fit lifecycle page; how the result is built afterwards is on the results page.

docs.title: Where the code is
docs.text:
Module Role jaxgam/fitting/data.py FittingData: device arrays, reparameterized penalty blocks, starts, null anchor and rank metadata built from ModelSetup; also PreparedFittingMetadata for the streamed routes. jaxgam/fitting/initialization.py initialize_beta_cpu (PIRLS start) and r_null_coefficients (port of mgcv's get.null.coef anchor), both NumPy. jaxgam/fitting/pirls.py pirls_loop, the ordinary jax.lax.while_loop PIRLS with step halving, PIRLSResult, and the NB in-loop theta solver efs_theta_pirls_loop. jaxgam/fitting/efs_regular_pirls.py efs_regular_pirls_loop: the jitted port of the gam.fit3 coefficient loop (Fisher retry, sequential recovery, convergence test, final gdi1 solve). jaxgam/fitting/source_pirls.py source_pirls: selects the pinned gam.fit3 or gam.fit4 loop for a dense inner fit; SOURCE_EPSILON; status messages. jaxgam/fitting/reml.py The REML criterion (_criterion_core, reml_criterion, REMLCriterion, JointREMLCriterion), fletcher_scale, estimate_edf, fisher_edf. jaxgam/fitting/stable_log_det.py Host NumPy port of gam.reparam/get_stableS for multi-penalty blocks: StableSystem, stable_system. jaxgam/fitting/penalty_ops.py JAX algebra on local penalty blocks: materialize, log_pdet, augmented_root, JaxPenaltyRoots, JaxCoefficientRotation. jaxgam/fitting/newton.py NewtonOptimizer / newton_optimize: the host outer loop, the differentiable score _diff_score with its jax.custom_jvp, NewtonResult, OuterScoreProvider. jaxgam/fitting/efs.py Jitted EFS algebra: prepare_efs_statistics, efs_statistics (d, t, q), efs_raw_update, efs_fisher_factor. jaxgam/fitting/efs_theta.py Conditional NB theta Newton kernel (port of mgcv's estimate.theta branch used by gam.fit4 under EFS). jaxgam/fitting/stream/efs_factor.py efs_factor_statistics: d, t, q computed from a coefficient-factor object; used by streamed EFS only. jaxgam/fitting/gaussian_qr/kernel.py FrozenGaussianQR and gaussian_qr_reml_score: the Gaussian REML score from frozen QR statistics. jaxgam/fitting/gaussian_qr/rank_coordinates.py reduced_augmented_qr JAX kernel for rank-coordinate Gaussian QR solves; no module in jaxgam/ imports it today, only tests. jaxgam/execution/efs.py Host EFS controller (dense_efs_known_scale, dense_efs_unknown_scale, _run_efs_known_scale, _run_efs_unknown_scale), EFSFitState, EFSResult, start values. jaxgam/execution/efs_provider.py The provider seam: EFSFitRequest, EFSControllerContext, EFSFitProvider protocol. jaxgam/execution/gaussian_qr/preparation.py Host preparation of the frozen Gaussian QR (prepare_frozen_gaussian_qr), GaussianQRIneligible, the penalty-count threshold, workspace estimates. jaxgam/execution/gaussian_qr/optimizer.py DenseGaussianQROuterProvider, build_dense_gaussian_qr_provider, optimize_gaussian_qr_lbfgs, use_gaussian_qr_lbfgs.

Phase 2 is split as on every route: jitted kernels in jaxgam/fitting/, host control in jaxgam/execution/. The dense route is the exception that its main optimizer, NewtonOptimizer, lives in jaxgam/fitting/newton.py and is itself a host Python loop around jitted pieces.

docs.title: Dispatch inside GAM.fit
docs.text:
After parse_formula and ModelSetup.build (Phase 1), GAM.fit in jaxgam/api.py builds FittingData.from_setup(setup, family, device) and then chooses, in this order:

  1. If FitControl.gaussian_compression is set, try build_dense_gaussian_qr_provider (see Gaussian QR).
  2. sp supplied: _fit_fixed_sp (see Fixed-sp fits), lambda_strategy="fixed".
  3. No penalties: newton_optimize, which takes its parametric shortcut.
  4. optimizer="efs": dense_efs_known_scale or dense_efs_unknown_scale, lambda_strategy="efs_reml".
  5. Otherwise Newton (newton_optimize), or SciPy L-BFGS-B when a Gaussian QR provider exists and the model has more than 50 penalties.

Every branch returns an object with the NewtonResult field names (EFS returns EFSResult), which _warn_factor_regularization inspects and GAMResults._from_fit consumes.

docs.title: FittingData: the Phase 1 to Phase 2 boundary
docs.text:
FittingData.from_setup does all of its numerical preparation in NumPy, then moves arrays with to_jax (jax.device_put of float64). In order:

  • Initial smoothing parameters. _initial_sp forms diag(X'WX) in 8192-row batches and calls initial_log_sp_from_diagonal, the port of mgcv's initial.sp (R/mgcv.r).
  • Reparameterization. reparameterize_structure (jaxgam/formula/fitting_prepare.py) rotates each penalty block so its coordinates split into the null and range space of the block's total penalty, mgcv's totalPenaltySpace (R/gam.fit3.r). A single penalty becomes an exact 0/1 diagonal; overlapping penalties use the eigenbasis of the norm-balanced sum sum_j S_j / |S_j|_F. The transformed penalties hold exact zeros on null rows and columns, which keeps a large smoothing parameter from amplifying roundoff into a spurious null-space penalty. apply_transforms_to_design applies the same block transforms to X, so the whole fit runs in these "fitting coordinates".
  • Start values. initialize_beta_cpu (see Starting values) gives beta_init; _null_beta gives null_beta from r_null_coefficients (None when the link of the response mean is not finite).
  • Penalty metadata. _build_block_metadata classifies blocks into singletons (rank and log-eigenvalue constant, so log|S+| is exactly rank * rho + const) and multi-penalty blocks (range-space projections multi_block_proj_S).
  • Rank. _unpenalized_rank_deficit counts aliasing among unpenalized columns and penalty null spaces.
  • Structural penalty roots. _structural_penalty_roots repeats mgcv's lambda-free identifiability test from pls_fit1 (src/gdi.c): it QR-factors sqrt(w) X and asks structural_rank whether [R1; E] has full column rank. If so it stores unscaled roots (JaxPenaltyRoots) and the inner fit solves by QR (penalized_qr_solve, a port of pls_fit1's arithmetic) instead of the normal equations; if not, penalty_roots is None and the Cholesky solve is kept, because pls_fit1's unidentifiable-column drop is not ported.
  • NB counts. For family_name == "nb" a CountPrefixPlan records integer counts for the lgamma recurrences; other families keep max_y = 0 so the response does not split JIT cache entries.

_structural_penalty_roots imports structural_rank from jaxgam.execution.qr inside the function. A module-level import would be circular: jaxgam/execution/__init__.py imports jaxgam/execution/stream/pirls.py, which imports _to_jax_structure from jaxgam/fitting/data.py. As a consequence a dense penalized fit loads jaxgam.execution (and its stream module) even though the dense route uses nothing else from it. This is the only import from jaxgam/fitting/ into jaxgam/execution/.

FittingData.uses_source_loop is true when null_beta exists, rank_deficit is 0 and the family is one of the five registered classes (uses_source_loop in jaxgam/fitting/source_pirls.py). It decides which inner loop runs.

docs.title: The inner fit
docs.text:
_inner_fit in jaxgam/fitting/newton.py is the single entry point used by Newton and by fixed-sp fits:

  • with a null_beta (full-rank models of the five registered families) it calls source_pirls, which runs
  • efs_regular_pirls_loop for Gaussian, Binomial, Poisson and Gamma: the port of gam.fit3 (R/gam.fit3.r);
  • _efs_theta_pirls_loop_jit with estimate_theta=False for NegativeBinomial: the port of gam.fit4 (R/gam.fit4.r), with theta as dynamic data so one compiled loop serves every theta;
  • without one (structurally rank-deficient models, hand-built fixtures) it calls the ordinary pirls_loop.

Both source loops converge at SOURCE_EPSILON = 1e-11, R's gam.control(epsilon=1e-11) rather than R's default 1e-7, and run at most 200 iterations. Called from Newton, the ordinary loop runs at the optimizer's PIRLS tolerance (min(tol / 100, 1e-8)); called from _fit_fixed_sp it keeps pirls_loop's default 1e-7. Either way it runs at most 100 iterations.

docs.title: The pinned gam.fit3 loop
docs.text:
_efs_regular_pirls_loop_jit is one jax.lax.while_loop; every decision is a jnp.where on traced values.

stateDiagram-v2
    state "Start shrink<br/>eta = 0.9 eta + 0.1 null_eta, at most 20 times" as StartShrink
    state "Working system<br/>_regular_factors, observed and Fisher solves" as WorkingSystem
    state "Same-step Fisher retry" as FisherRetry
    state "Raw proposal beta_raw" as Proposal
    state "Non-finite deviance recovery<br/>halve toward the anchor" as NonfiniteRecovery
    state "Domain recovery<br/>halve while mu or eta is invalid" as DomainRecovery
    state "Divergence recovery<br/>halve while pdev exceeds the baseline, at most 100" as DivergenceRecovery
    state "Convergence test<br/>pdev change and max gradient against epsilon" as ConvergenceTest
    state "Final gdi1 solve and factors" as FinalSolve
    state "Loop exits with a failure status" as Failed
    [*] --> StartShrink
    StartShrink --> Failed : start still invalid
    StartShrink --> WorkingSystem : valid start
    WorkingSystem --> FisherRetry : observed system indefinite, non-canonical link
    WorkingSystem --> Proposal : solved
    FisherRetry --> Proposal
    Proposal --> Failed : coefficients not finite
    Proposal --> NonfiniteRecovery
    NonfiniteRecovery --> DomainRecovery
    DomainRecovery --> DivergenceRecovery
    DivergenceRecovery --> Failed : a recovery did not succeed
    DivergenceRecovery --> ConvergenceTest : step accepted, anchor moves
    ConvergenceTest --> WorkingSystem : not converged
    ConvergenceTest --> FinalSolve : converged or iteration limit
    Failed --> FinalSolve
    FinalSolve --> [*]

Read it top to bottom; each box between the start and the final solve is one stage of one while_loop iteration. Every exit, including a failure, passes through the final solve; a failure is carried in the status code. The details, all from jaxgam/fitting/efs_regular_pirls.py:

  • Working system. _regular_factors returns gam.fit3's weights and working response. Canonical links use Fisher weights. Non-canonical links use the full Newton system, Fisher weights times alpha = 1 + (y - mu) (V'/V + g'' mu.eta), whose weights can be negative. _checked_exact_solve classifies the curvature of the unit-diagonal H; a material negative eigenvalue triggers the same-step Fisher retry, as in gam.fit3. With penalty_roots, every nonnegative-weight system is solved by _positive_qr_solve.
  • Recovery. The order is R's: a non-finite coefficient stops the loop; then non-finite deviance, then invalid mu/eta, then penalized-deviance divergence beyond 10 (0.1 + |old pdev|) sqrt(eps) (at most 100 halvings). Each halving moves beta and eta half-way toward the anchor, which starts at null_beta and becomes the last accepted state.
  • Convergence. Converged when the penalized-deviance change is below epsilon (|scale| + |pdev|) and max|2 X'W(X beta - z) + 2 S beta| is at most epsilon (|pdev| + |scale|). A family whose capability single_step_pirls is set (Gaussian with identity link) is converged at its first accepted step, R's "strictly additive" branch.
  • Final solve. After the loop, gam.fit3's closing gdi1 call is ported: weights are rebuilt at the final state, XtWX (observed) and XtWX_fisher are formed, and one last penalized solve gives the reported coefficients, unless that candidate leaves the family domain, in which case the pre-solve coefficients are kept. The reported deviance is the pre-solve deviance, and penalized_deviance adds the candidate's penalty, as R's Dp does.
  • Status. A failure is reported in inner_status with one of the EFS_REGULAR_STATUS_* codes, never as convergence; status_message maps it to R's wording ("inner loop 3; can't correct step size ...").

The NB loop (_efs_theta_pirls_loop_jit in jaxgam/fitting/pirls.py) follows gam.fit4 instead: observed weights 0.5 d2D/deta2, a positive-weight retry for an indefinite system, the same recovery order and gam.fit4's convergence test.

docs.title: The ordinary PIRLS loop
docs.text:
_pirls_loop_jit (behind pirls_loop) is a jax.lax.while_loop over _PIRLSState. Its body calls _beta_step, which forms the weighted system, solves it (penalized_solve, or penalized_qr_solve when a root is given) and runs an inner while_loop over _StepHalvingState: a trial is accepted when its penalized deviance is finite, valid_mu/valid_eta hold, and it is no more than 1e-7 |pdev| above the current value (any valid finite trial is accepted on the first iteration). At most 25 halvings toward the previous coefficients are tried; if none is accepted the iteration keeps the old state. Convergence is tested only from iteration index 3, when both the relative penalized-deviance change and the relative maximum coefficient change are below tol.

After the loop, the curvature is rebuilt at the final mu following mgcv's information split: the XtWX that enters log|H| uses observed information for non-canonical links (signed weights from _observed_weights, built by _signed_XtWX), while XtWX_fisher and L_fisher use Fisher weights for EDF and covariance. For canonical links the two are the same array. Standard families use Fisher scoring (gam.fit3); a family with n_theta > 0 uses observed weights and working response (gam.fit4).

The plain Cholesky used here is cho_factor in jaxgam/jax_utils.py: it adds a diagonal-relative jitter (1e-12, then 1e-6) only when the plain factor fails, and records the level in factor_regularization.

docs.title: The REML criterion
docs.text:
_criterion_core in jaxgam/fitting/reml.py computes, for converged inner-fit outputs,

Dp / (2 phi) - ls_sat + log|H| / 2 - log|S+| / 2

with Dp = deviance + beta' S_lambda beta and H = XtWX + S_lambda; the caller subtracts Mp / 2 log(2 pi phi), where Mp is the total penalty null-space dimension. This is the Laplace REML of gam.fit3 (R/gam.fit3.r). The terms:

  • ls_sat is the family's saturated log-likelihood (saturated_loglik, or saturated_loglik_theta when theta is a free coordinate).
  • log|H| comes from one of three places in _criterion_log_determinants: qr_log_det (jaxgam/fitting/qr.py, the QR of [sqrt(W) X; E], with a jax.custom_jvp whose tangent is tr(H^-1 dH)) when uses_qr_log_det holds (roots present, no rank deficit, canonical link, no theta); otherwise a Cholesky of H scaled to unit diagonal; or, for a structurally rank-deficient H, the sum of log eigenvalues after dropping the rank_deficit smallest.
  • log|S+| comes from penalty_ops.log_pdet: the exact rank * rho + const for singletons and a block log-determinant for multi-penalty blocks.

For multi-penalty blocks, mgcv calls gam.reparam (R/gam.fit3.r, which calls the C routine get_stableS in src/gdi.c) at every evaluation. That routine branches on the smoothing parameters, so jaxgam/fitting/stable_log_det.py runs it on the host, in NumPy, between jitted calls: stable_system returns a StableSystem (block rotations, rotated penalties and roots, and StableLogDetTerms holding log|S+| with its first and second derivatives at that point). The jitted criterion evaluates the quadratic expansion of those terms, which is exact at that point and NaN anywhere else, so it cannot be used away from the host's evaluation point. The inner fit is then run in the rotated coordinates and mapped back by pirls_from_stable.

Scale and EDF: fisher_edf takes the QR trace fisher_edf recorded by the inner fit when available, else estimate_edf (tr(H^-1 XtWX_fisher)). fletcher_scale is the Fletcher (2012) Pearson estimate used by gam.fit3; estimate_scale returns 1 for known-scale families.

REMLCriterion and JointREMLCriterion wrap this core with fixed inner-fit outputs. They are used to report edf and scale at an accepted point, by the parametric shortcut, and by _fit_fixed_sp. They are not what Newton differentiates: the outer gradient and Hessian come from _diff_score. Only REML is implemented; NewtonOptimizer raises ValueError for any other method.

docs.title: The Newton outer loop
docs.text:
NewtonOptimizer ports mgcv's newton (R/gam.fit3.r) for non-Gaussian families and the step handling of fast.REML.fit (an mgcv routine in R/fast-REML.r) for Gaussian. Its parameter vector is [log_lambda, <log_theta>, <log_phi>]: log_theta only for an NB family with estimated theta (_joint_theta), log_phi only for unknown-scale families (_joint_scale), and both only when the model has penalties.

sequenceDiagram
    participant Api as GAM.fit in api.py
    participant Opt as NewtonOptimizer.run
    participant Fwd as _jit_fit_and_score
    participant Inner as _inner_fit
    participant Crit as _criterion_core
    participant Diff as _jit_diff_grad_hess
    participant Step as _safe_newton_step
    Api->>Opt: newton_optimize(fd, method)
    Opt->>Fwd: params, beta_init
    Fwd->>Inner: S_lambda from log_lambda
    Inner-->>Fwd: PIRLSResult
    Fwd->>Crit: XtWX, beta, deviance, ls_sat
    Crit-->>Fwd: score
    Fwd-->>Opt: score and PIRLSResult
    Opt->>Diff: params, accepted coefficients
    Diff-->>Opt: gradient and Hessian through custom_jvp
    loop each outer iteration, at most max_iter
        Opt->>Opt: _compute_uconv_ind
        Opt->>Step: gradient and Hessian on unconverged coordinates
        Step-->>Opt: capped step and is_pdef
        loop _step_halve or _step_halve_gaussian
            Opt->>Fwd: trial params, warm start from accepted beta
            Fwd-->>Opt: trial score
        end
        Opt->>Diff: accepted params
        Diff-->>Opt: gradient and Hessian
        Opt->>Opt: _check_convergence
    end
    Opt-->>Api: NewtonResult from _build_result

The outer loop and all decisions are host Python (for outer_iter in range(self._max_iter)); each arrow into _jit_fit_and_score, _jit_diff_grad_hess and _safe_newton_step is one jitted dispatch. With multi-penalty blocks, every evaluation first calls stable_system on the host.

Forward pass. _fit_and_score_impl, jitted as _jit_fit_and_score, fuses S_lambda construction, the inner fit and the score into one XLA program. Trial fits during step halving use only this.

Derivatives. _diff_score is the same computation written for differentiation. Inside it the inner fit is wrapped in a jax.custom_jvp (_pirls_out, or _pirls_out_ext when theta is a coordinate). The JVP rule applies the implicit function theorem at the converged state instead of differentiating through the while_loop:

  • d beta = -H^-1 (dS beta) with H = XtWX + S_lambda (for joint theta, the observed Hessian X' d2D X + 2 S and an extra X' d2D/(deta dtheta) dtheta term);
  • dXtWX from the JVP of the weight function at the converged eta: Fisher weights for canonical links, observed weights 0.5 d2D/deta2 otherwise and for NB;
  • the deviance change from the JVP of the deviance at eta.

jax.grad and jax.hessian of _diff_score then give the full first and second derivatives, the role mgcv's gdi.c and Sl.ift play in R. They are compiled once per static configuration at module level (_jit_diff_grad, _jit_diff_hess, _jit_diff_grad_hess). The penalty root and the scale enter _pirls_out as primals whose tangents are ignored: they change the solver and the convergence threshold, not the stationary point.

Step. _safe_newton_step (jitted) eigendecomposes the Hessian, flips negative eigenvalues, floors small ones at max|eig| * eps^0.7 (eps^0.5 for Gaussian), and caps the largest step component at 5. _compute_uconv_ind restricts the step to coordinates whose gradient or Hessian diagonal is not negligible, R's uconv.ind. Free log smoothing parameters are clamped to [-40, 40] (lsp_max), a safety bound that mgcv's newton does not have.

Step control.

  • Gaussian (_step_halve_gaussian, as fast.REML.fit): halve while the trial is non-finite or strictly worse, at most 25 times or until four consecutive insignificant changes; a step failure ends the optimization. Small changes are compared with _gaussian_score_change, an exact difference of the criterion that avoids subtracting two large scores near a flat optimum.
  • Other families (_step_halve, as newton): accept immediately when the score falls, the Hessian is positive definite and the quadratic model's relative error is below 0.8; otherwise halve (at most 30 times), switching once to a steepest-descent step after three halvings in the first ten iterations, with the error threshold lowered to 0.4 after more than four halvings. The outcome is ACCEPTED, STUCK or FAILED (_StepOutcome).

Convergence. _check_convergence uses score_scale = 1 + |score| for Gaussian and |log scale| + |score| otherwise. Gaussian converges when max|grad| <= tol * score_scale and the score change is at most tol * score_scale; other families additionally need a positive-definite Hessian and test the projected gradient (zeroed at active lsp_max bounds) against 5 * tol * score_scale. tol is sqrt(eps) for Gaussian and 1e-6 otherwise, mgcv's newton.conv.tol. A step failure while the gradient is already within tolerance counts as convergence (_gradient_within_tol); three consecutive STUCK outcomes also end the loop as converged.

What it reports. _build_result sets convergence_info to "full convergence", "step failed", "iteration limit", or "non-finite REML score or gradient" (the last is never converged). When the source inner loop did not converge at the final point it appends "; inner fit did not converge: ..." and marks the fit not converged. factorization_fallbacks re-checks every factorization of the reported fit; a fired jitter is appended as "; fallback jitter in " and GAM.fit raises a RuntimeWarning. With multi-penalty blocks, stable_rotation carries the block maps needed to form Vp in Phase 3.

Parametric shortcut. With no penalties, run performs one inner fit, builds a criterion and returns n_iter=0, converged. NB theta is not estimated there: _joint_theta requires penalties.

docs.title: Starting values
docs.text:
• initialize_beta_cpu: mu = family.initialize(y, wt), eta = link(mu), then a least-squares projection onto X. If the fitted start leaves the family's domain, it projects the constant link(weighted mean of y) instead. It is computed once in FittingData.from_setup; NewtonOptimizer._initial_beta reuses it.
  • r_null_coefficients: the unweighted response mean through the link, projected onto X with no offset; the recovery anchor of the source loops.
  • log_lambda_init: R's initial.sp, from FittingData._initial_sp.
  • log_phi start: one eager inner fit at log_lambda_init (_eager_inner_fit), then fletcher_scale with the Fisher EDF.
  • log_theta start: the family's current theta (get_theta).

docs.title: Fixed-sp fits
docs.text:
_fit_fixed_sp in jaxgam/api.py validates sp (one positive finite value per penalty) and then:

  • with a Gaussian QR provider and more than 50 penalties: optimize_gaussian_qr_lbfgs with pin_lambda=True;
  • for an NB family with estimated theta, or any unknown-scale family: newton_optimize(..., pin_lambda=True). The smoothing parameters are held bitwise and only log_theta/log_phi move, as mgcv's gam.outer keeps theta and log scale free for a supplied sp. Such a fit can report n_iter > 0;
  • otherwise one inner fit (source_pirls or pirls_loop, in gam.reparam coordinates when there are multi-penalty blocks), then REMLCriterion for the reported score. convergence_info is "fixed sp", or names the inner-loop failure or a non-finite score, and n_iter=0.

docs.title: Negative-binomial theta
docs.text: family="nb" is a NegativeBinomial with estimated theta; GAM.fit deep-copies it so the registry instance is never changed. Under Newton, log_theta is a joint coordinate: _diff_score takes it as a traced primal, the saturated likelihood uses saturated_loglik_theta, and the custom JVP adds the theta cross-terms. _build_result writes the final theta into the copied family with put_theta and reports it as NewtonResult.theta; a fixed-theta NB reports theta=None. Under EFS, theta is updated inside the coefficient loop instead (below).

docs.title: The dense extended Fellner-Schall path
docs.text:
optimizer="efs" with estimated smoothing parameters and at least one penalty runs the host controller in jaxgam/execution/efs.py, a port of efsudr (R/gam.fit4.r). Supported: Poisson and Binomial, NB with log, identity or sqrt link (theta fixed or estimated), Gaussian and Gamma (_known_scale_family_supported, _unknown_scale_family_supported). The model must be identifiable (rank_deficit == 0) and prior weights must lie in [1e-10, 1e10] (zero weights are allowed only for Gaussian log and inverse links); violations raise ValueError.

Start. efs_initial_log_lambda ports mgcv's initial.spg; the controller adds efsudr's +2.5 once. For unknown scale, efs_initial_log_scale gives the incoming scale null.scale / 10 from the null deviance.

One fit. _fit_state refits the coefficients at the requested log_lambda with the inner loop matching mgcv's EFS call: efs_theta_pirls_loop for NB (with conditional theta for estimated theta), efs_regular_pirls_loop for non-canonical regular links, pirls_loop for canonical ones. Except after the gam.fit3 loop, which already forms plain Cholesky factors, it then replaces the Fisher factor by efs_fisher_factor, an unjittered Cholesky of X'W_F X + S_lambda (a failure invalidates the fit instead of being repaired). It computes EFSStatistics with efs_statistics (d: derivative of log|S+|; t: tr(H_F^-1 S_j) per penalty from triangular solves against local roots; q: beta' S_j beta), the scalar REML score at the incoming scale score_phi, and the Fletcher scale update_phi of the new fit. The result is an immutable EFSFitState.

The update. efs_raw_update reproduces efsudr's arithmetic: numerator = max(0, exp(-rho) d - t), ratio = phi * numerator / max(0, q), ratio 1 when both are zero, 1e6 when not finite, and trial = min(rho + log(ratio) * multiplier, log_lambda_max).

flowchart TD
    A["accepted EFSFitState"] --> B["efs_raw_update<br/>ratio and trial log_lambda"]
    B --> C{"finite_positive?"}
    C -- no --> X1["stop: invalid_update"]
    C -- yes --> D["provider refit at trial<br/>warm start from accepted beta"]
    D --> E{"candidate valid?"}
    E -- no --> X2["stop: failure label"]
    E -- yes --> F{"candidate score <= accepted score?"}
    F -- yes --> G{"largest step < 0.05?"}
    G -- no --> K["accept candidate"]
    G -- yes --> H["refit with multiplier x 2"]
    H --> I{"extension valid and better?"}
    I -- yes --> J["accept extension, double multiplier"]
    I -- no --> K
    F -- no --> L["halve multiplier while above 1, refit"]
    L --> M["accept last candidate, multiplier at least 1"]
    K --> N["append score to history"]
    J --> N
    M --> N
    N --> O{"score_window or deviance_change?"}
    O -- yes --> Y["stop: converged"]
    O -- no --> A

Read from the top: every iteration proposes one trial, may try one extension or several contractions, and always accepts a valid state before testing the stop rules. score_window needs iteration > 3, a largest proposed step below 0.05, and the last four accepted scores differing by less than score_tolerance; deviance_change needs |dev change| < 100 * pirls_tolerance * |dev|. Every refit starts from the old accepted coefficients (and theta), never from a rejected trial. Reaching outer_limit reports "iteration limit reached", not converged, even if a stop rule first held on that iteration.

Scale. Unknown scale is not a coordinate. _run_efs_unknown_scale scores each fit at the incoming score_phi and feeds the fit's Fletcher estimate (update_phi) into the next ratio. After a winning extension the next score uses the candidate's scale while the next ratio uses the extension's, as R does; the field carried_phi records this. The reported scale is the accepted fit's Fletcher estimate, while score was evaluated at the incoming scale.

Theta. For estimated-theta NB, efs_theta_pirls_loop runs the conditional theta Newton of jaxgam/fitting/efs_theta.py inside each coefficient iteration, as gam.fit4 does under EFS. Theta lives in EFSFitState.log_theta, never in the family object during the loop; GAM.fit writes the selected theta with put_theta afterwards. A fixed-theta NB reports its fixed value as theta.

Provider interface. The controller functions _run_efs_known_scale and _run_efs_unknown_scale never touch data. They call an EFSFitProvider (a callable taking an EFSFitRequest and returning an EFSFitState) with an EFSControllerContext. _dense_fit_provider wraps _fit_state for the dense route; the streamed route passes its own providers to the same two functions (see the streamed fit).

Diagnostics. _EFSDiagnosticsAccumulator counts on the host and finish returns EFSOptimizerDiagnostics (jaxgam/fitting/state.py), exposed as result.optimizer_diagnostics: reference_profile ("mgcv-1.9-3-efsudr-dense"), trace_method, step_policy, stop_reason, outer, inner and theta iteration counts, the accepted score history (and score phi history for unknown scale), the multiplier, the last update residual, the largest proposed and accepted moves, counts of numerator clamps, ratio replacements and log_lambda_max caps, and flags for invalid fits and stabilized solves.

docs.title: The Gaussian QR route
docs.text:
FitControl(gaussian_compression=True) asks for a reduction that freezes the weighted data once and evaluates every REML trial in coefficient space.

flowchart TD
    A["GAM.fit, gaussian_compression=True"] --> B{"optimizer efs and sp is None?"}
    B -- yes --> F1["record fallback reason<br/>ordinary dense fit"]
    B -- no --> C["build_dense_gaussian_qr_provider"]
    C --> D{"exact Gaussian, identity link?"}
    D -- no --> F2["GaussianQRIneligible"]
    D -- yes --> E{"at least one penalty?"}
    E -- no --> F2
    E -- yes --> G{"rank_deficit == 0?"}
    G -- no --> F2
    G -- yes --> H{"finite data, weights in 1e-10 to 1e10?"}
    H -- no --> F2
    H -- yes --> I["prepare_frozen_gaussian_qr<br/>one host weighted QR"]
    F2 --> F3["execution_fallback_reason = message<br/>ordinary dense fit"]
    I --> J{"sp supplied?"}
    J -- yes --> K["_fit_fixed_sp with provider<br/>log_lambda pinned, log_phi free"]
    J -- no --> L{"use_gaussian_qr_lbfgs: more than 50 penalties?"}
    L -- no --> M["newton_optimize with score_provider"]
    L -- yes --> N["optimize_gaussian_qr_lbfgs"]
    M --> O["provider.finalize: one pass over X"]
    N --> O
    K --> O
    O --> P["execution_route = gaussian_qr"]

Read from the top: every "no" on the eligibility chain raises GaussianQRIneligible, which GAM.fit catches; the ordinary dense fit then runs with execution_route="dense" and the message in execution_fallback_reason. Other errors from preparation are not caught.

Frozen statistics. prepare_frozen_gaussian_qr (jaxgam/execution/gaussian_qr/preparation.py, modelled on qr_update in mgcv's R/bam.r and Sl.fit in R/fast-REML.r) QR-reduces [sqrt(w) X, sqrt(w)(y - offset)] with reduce_positive_qr, re-expresses the factor in the coordinate map's global coordinates (on the dense route, the public coefficients) with a second small QR, and stores a FrozenGaussianQR: R, qtz, the residual tail, n_obs, n_positive_weights and the sum of log positive weights; compact penalty roots, coordinate bases and the penalty range basis sit beside it in FrozenGaussianQRPreparation. The dense design is still built first, because FittingData.from_setup runs before the provider.

Scoring. DenseGaussianQROuterProvider implements the four-method OuterScoreProvider protocol of jaxgam/fitting/newton.py: initial_parameters (adds log_phi from a unit-scale evaluation), evaluate (jit_gaussian_qr_reml_score on coefficient-sized arrays only), differentiate (jit_gaussian_qr_reml_value_and_grad and jit_gaussian_qr_reml_hessian, JAX autodiff through the QR-based score, with no custom JVP), and finalize, the one call that touches X to build a PIRLSResult for Phase 3. With a provider, NewtonOptimizer skips _diff_score and the stable-system work.

Optimizer choice. Up to 50 penalties (GAUSSIAN_LBFGS_PENALTY_THRESHOLD), the same NewtonOptimizer runs (lambda_strategy="newton_reml"). Above 50, optimize_gaussian_qr_lbfgs runs SciPy L-BFGS-B on exact gradients with no outer Hessian (lambda_strategy="lbfgs_reml"): maxcor=10, gtol=1e-10, ftol=0, log smoothing parameters bounded to [-40, 40], log scale unbounded. It converges when the projected-gradient max-norm is at most gtol (1 + |score|); after a line-search stop it may profile the log scale exactly (phi = penalized RSS / (n_positive - Mp)) or apply mgcv's relative test (mgcv_relative_convergence) before reporting.

Known limit with many penalties. The L-BFGS-B branch is tested at one size, 51 penalties (tests/test_execution/test_gaussian_optimizer.py), and its agreement with Newton is asserted at MODERATE tolerance, not STRICT. On that fixture both optimizers converge and the scores agree to about 8e-8 relative, but the REML surface is flat and L-BFGS-B stops with log10(sp) near 10 where dense Newton stops near 6.7. Expect the same fitted model and different smoothing parameters at such optima. Its behaviour above 51 penalties is not covered by tests.
