docs.title: Rules and invariants
docs.text:
• Phase boundary. Everything numerical in FittingData.from_setup happens in NumPy before to_jax; after that, the fit sees only device arrays. The exceptions on the host are deliberate and documented in their modules: the Newton and EFS controllers, stable_system (get_stableS branches on the smoothing parameters), and the Gaussian QR preparation.
  • Inner loops are jit-compatible. pirls_loop, efs_regular_pirls_loop, the NB loop and source_pirls contain no Python branching on array values; Python if is used only on static arguments (family, flags). Enforced by tests/test_fitting/test_pirls.py (TestJITCompilation) and tests/test_fitting/test_dense_source_parity.py (test_source_inner_loops_compile_and_converge_under_jit, test_source_loops_hold_the_hard_gates_under_jit).
  • family is a static JIT argument. Mutable family state read inside a jitted function is baked into the executable, so theta is passed as dynamic log_theta (see pirls_loop's docstring). Do not read get_theta() inside a jitted body.
  • Failures are never convergence. A non-converged source loop, a non-finite score or gradient, or a failed EFS refit is reported as not converged (tests/test_fitting/test_newton.py TestPinnedSmoothingParameters, tests/test_execution/test_efs.py test_production_controller_named_stops_and_iteration_200).
  • Jitter is visible. Any fallback regularization appears in convergence_info and raises a RuntimeWarning (test_every_fallback_jitter_is_visible_in_the_result, test_dense_fit_warns_only_when_the_fallback_regularizes).
  • Derivatives are checked. The custom JVP gradient and Hessian are compared with finite differences in tests/test_fitting/test_newton.py (TestCustomJVP) and tests/test_fitting/test_nb_custom_jvp.py; the host get_stableS terms in tests/test_fitting/test_stable_log_det.py.
  • Hard gates. Outer Hessian symmetry and positive semi-definiteness and REML monotonicity are in tests/test_fitting/test_newton.py (TestInvariants, test_reml_monotonicity); the full set of hard-gate invariants over the validation matrix is TestHardGateInvariants in tests/test_validation_matrix.py.
  • EFS refits start from the accepted state. Extension and contraction trials use the old accepted coefficients, theta and scale (test_production_controller_extension_and_contraction_keep_old_warm_start, test_unknown_scale_extension_uses_old_accepted_phi).
  • Gaussian QR threshold. use_gaussian_qr_lbfgs(50) is false and use_gaussian_qr_lbfgs(51) true (test_lbfgs_selection_threshold_is_strictly_above_fifty); the scoring arrays contain no observation-sized array (test_provider_score_and_derivative_jaxprs_have_no_observation_arrays).

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Rank-deficient models take a different inner loop. With rank_deficit > 0 there is no null_beta path and no QR roots, so the ordinary pirls_loop and Cholesky solve run, and log|H| drops the smallest eigenvalues. Dense EFS and Gaussian QR reject such models.
  • log_phi and score under EFS. The EFS score is the criterion at the incoming scale, not at the reported Fletcher scale. Do not "fix" this by rescoring; EFSFitState keeps score_phi, update_phi and carried_phi separate on purpose.
  • A supplied sp does not always mean one PIRLS fit. Gaussian, Gamma and estimated-theta NB still run Newton with the smoothing parameters pinned.
  • Parametric NB models keep their starting theta under Newton, because theta is a coordinate only when there are penalties.
  • The PIRLS tolerance is not the source epsilon. The Newton optimizer's _pirls_tol reaches only the ordinary loop; the source loops use SOURCE_EPSILON (test_source_loop_epsilon_is_an_explicit_parameter).
  • Flat optima. The REML surface is often flat near the optimum, so smoothing parameters can differ between equally valid fits (see the Gaussian QR limit above). Compare deviance, coefficients and score, not sp.
  • The criterion classes are not the optimizer's derivative. REMLCriterion.grad_hess treats the inner-fit outputs as constants; _diff_score is what the Newton loop differentiates.

docs.title: Where to change things
docs.text:
• To change how an inner fit iterates or recovers for a standard family, edit _efs_regular_pirls_loop_jit in jaxgam/fitting/efs_regular_pirls.py; for NB, _efs_theta_pirls_loop_jit in jaxgam/fitting/pirls.py; for rank-deficient models, _pirls_loop_jit.
  • To change which inner loop a family uses, edit uses_source_loop in jaxgam/fitting/source_pirls.py and _inner_fit in jaxgam/fitting/newton.py.
  • To change a REML term, edit _criterion_core or _criterion_log_determinants in jaxgam/fitting/reml.py, then check _diff_score, which calls the same core.
  • To change outer step control or convergence, edit _step_halve, _step_halve_gaussian, _check_convergence and _build_result in NewtonOptimizer.
  • To change how derivatives pass through the inner fit, edit the defjvp rules inside _diff_score.
  • To add an EFS family, extend _known_scale_family_supported or _unknown_scale_family_supported and the inner-loop choice in _fit_state (jaxgam/execution/efs.py); the controller itself does not change.
  • To change the Gaussian QR eligibility or threshold, edit build_dense_gaussian_qr_provider and use_gaussian_qr_lbfgs (jaxgam/execution/gaussian_qr/optimizer.py) and GAUSSIAN_LBFGS_PENALTY_THRESHOLD (jaxgam/execution/gaussian_qr/preparation.py).

A proposed refactor would merge the several inner loops and outer controllers across routes; see the unified fitting design.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: This page covers FitControl(execution="discrete"), the JaxGAM analogue of mgcv::bam(discrete=TRUE). It describes how the compact discretized design is acted on without an n-by-p model matrix, how the shared prepared problem is built and budgeted, the additive Gaussian fit, the performance iteration for regular families and the negative binomial (a port of bgam.fitd in mgcv's R/bam.r), and the working-model REML proposal (a port of Sl.fitChol in R/fast-REML.r). How the compact frame and its selectors are chosen belongs to setup and data sources; the result class and predictor are in results and prediction.

docs.title: Where the code is
docs.text:
Module Role jaxgam/api.py (GAM._fit_discrete) Route entry: refusals, family admission, dispatch to the Gaussian or regular driver, result construction. jaxgam/execution/discrete/gaussian.py Shared prepared problem (_prepared_discrete), fit memory plan, the additive Gaussian driver (fit_discrete_gaussian), fixed-sp REML score and scale iteration, DiscreteFit. jaxgam/execution/discrete/regular.py Regular-family and negative-binomial driver (fit_discrete_regular): source-scanning working rows, theta nuisance, budget and compile, final fields. jaxgam/execution/discrete/regular_working_model.py Host port of bgam.fitd's outer loop for non-additive families: coefficient step control, convergence test, iteration trace. jaxgam/execution/discrete/working_model.py Host trial control around one Sl.fitChol proposal: the host pivoted-Cholesky boundary, Nstep halving, the frozen-statistic Gaussian controller, compile-time memory measurement. jaxgam/execution/discrete/working_theta.py Host port of estimate.theta (mgcv R/efam.r) for one log theta, each objective one source scan. jaxgam/fitting/discrete/ops.py JIT kernels for the indexed design: forward, transpose, X'WX, X'Wy, diag(X V X'), and their cost and scratch models. jaxgam/fitting/discrete/working.py JIT per-batch working statistics: Fisher weights and pseudodata, NB dDeta weights, estimate.theta row terms. jaxgam/fitting/discrete/working_model.py JIT kernels of the Sl.fitChol proposal: reparameterization, factor inputs, REML value, gradient, Hessian, Newton step, H^-1. jaxgam/fitting/penalty_ops.py Device-side local penalty algebra (JaxPenaltyStructure, stacked groups) used by the proposal kernels. jaxgam/formula/discrete/continuous_setup.py Phase 1: ordinary basis setup on the compact frame (build_continuous_discrete_setup). jaxgam/formula/discrete/continuous_design.py Phase 1: evaluates the frozen bases on compact representatives into lookup tables (build_continuous_discrete_design). jaxgam/formula/discrete/design.py Phase 1: descriptor types (FrozenDiscreteDesign, LookupBlock, TensorLookupBlock) and the per-batch memory plan (_memory_plan). jaxgam/formula/discrete/continuous_metadata.py Phase 1: the row-free record of the fitted discretization and the predict.bamd request grouping. jaxgam/formula/kernel_groups.py Pair schedule and pair_reduction_plan (histogram or direct rows). jaxgam/smooths/source_lapack.py The pinned DPSTRF (source_pivoted_cholesky) used by every working-model trial.

The Phase 1 modules import no JAX. The outer iterations of this route are host Python loops in jaxgam/execution/; only the per-batch kernels and the per-trial proposal kernels are JIT-compiled.

A planned refactor will fold this route's controller into a shared engine; see the unified fit design.

docs.title: Entry and admission
docs.text: GAM._fit_discrete runs every refusal before the formula is parsed: the data must be a RowSource; weights= and offset= must come from the source; result must be "prediction"; linear_solver must be "cholesky"; without sp the control must name smoothing_strategy="working_model_reml", and optimizer must be "newton". The family is then admitted by its execution capabilities: canonical Gaussian identity goes to fit_discrete_gaussian; families with regular_performance_iteration or extended_performance_iteration go to fit_discrete_regular. A gaussian_compression=True request is not refused; the result reports it in execution_fallback_reason. The whole fit runs inside single_fit_fingerprints(), so the source is content-hashed when the fit starts and ends rather than around every scan.

docs.title: The compact design
docs.text:
Discretization replaces each group of covariates (a multi-variable s(), a tensor margin, a by variable, a parametric covariate) by a small table of unique, possibly rounded, rows plus one integer selector per observation (the ExactIndexTable built by the data layer). The basis is constructed once, on the compact rows. The fit then never holds an n-by-p matrix: every term is a lookup block whose design rows are table[selector].

FrozenDiscreteDesign (in jaxgam/formula/discrete/design.py) holds:

  • LookupBlock: one constrained table (q unique rows by k columns) and its selector, for an ordinary smooth or parametric block.
  • TensorLookupBlock: one table per margin, an optional centering transform, the retained columns keep, and optionally a numeric by multiplier table or a factor by with level_codes and n_levels. A single margin represents an ordinary smooth whose by variable stays a separate indexed multiplier.

batch_indices(row_positions) gathers one host batch of selectors, one per distinct index table, for the next JIT dispatch. evaluate_batch is a CPU oracle that materializes the batch rows; tests use it, the fit does not.

docs.title: Indexed design operators
docs.text:
to_device_discrete_design copies the compact tables, transforms, multipliers and level codes to the device as a DeviceDiscreteDesign (with DeviceLookupBlock and DeviceTensorLookupBlock). Selectors are never transferred as a whole: each batch's selectors are passed into each kernel call, and _validate_device_batch refuses a batch larger than the descriptor's batch_rows.

The kernels port the linear algebra of mgcv's Xbd, XWyd, XWXd and diagXVXd helpers (mgcv R/misc.r, C in src/discrete.c):

  • discrete_xbd(design, selectors, beta): for a lookup block, (table @ beta_block)[selector], so the product is formed on the q compact rows and gathered; a tensor block maps its coefficients through the frozen constraint transform and contracts them with each margin's selected rows in turn (_tensor_matvec), never forming batch-by-tensor rows, with a separate path for factor by.
  • discrete_xb_transpose(design, selectors, values): scatter-adds values into a length-q vector per block and multiplies by table.T.
  • discrete_xwyd is discrete_xb_transpose(design, selectors, w * y).
  • discrete_xwxd accumulates X'WX block pair by block pair (next section).
  • discrete_row_xwxd is an alternative X'WX that materializes row chunks.
  • discrete_diag_xvxd gives diag(X V X') for a supplied covariance.

docs.title: How X'WX is accumulated
docs.text:
discrete_xwxd builds a host schedule with discrete_pair_schedule (jaxgam/formula/kernel_groups.py) over all block pairs (l, r) with r >= l, groups pairs by reduction kind and block shape, and runs one lax.scan per group, so the compiled graph grows with the number of distinct shapes rather than the number of smooth pairs. Each pair is reduced by _pair_part in one of four ways:

  • lookup_diagonal (a lookup block with itself): scatter the weights into a length-q histogram h, then T' diag(h) T.
  • lookup_histogram (two lookup blocks): scatter weights into a q_left by q_right histogram C, then T_l' C T_r (lookup_pair_histogram_crossproduct).
  • lookup_direct (two lookup blocks, histogram not chosen): gather both blocks' rows and form rows_l' (w * rows_r).
  • tensor (either block a tensor): _subblock_pair_crossproduct loops over the combinations of the leading margins and reduces only the final-margin pair by histogram or direct rows (_final_margin_crossproduct), then maps the result through the block's constraint transform. This is the final-margin reuse of mgcv's XWXijs.

pair_reduction_plan chooses the histogram only when the policy is "histogram_or_direct", the q_left * q_right * 8 histogram bytes fit max_pair_histogram_bytes, and they are no larger than gathering the batch rows (n_rows * (k_left + k_right) * 8). With pair_policy="direct_only" every lookup pair uses direct rows.

The row-chunk path discrete_row_xwxd(..., chunk_rows=c) expands c rows at a time into a dense c by p matrix (lookup tables gathered per equal-shape group, tensor blocks by their row product), forms only the upper panels of a 4 by 4 panel split (_ROW_XWXD_PANELS) and mirrors them, so the result is exactly symmetric. Rows past the batch are padded with weight zero. It equals the pair reductions up to rounding (tests/test_fitting/test_stacked_kernels.py).

The choice is made once per fit by _row_xwxd_chunk in jaxgam/execution/discrete/gaussian.py:

  1. Compare the flop-equivalent estimates discrete_row_xwxd_cost(p, batch_rows) (n p^2 matrix-product work) and discrete_xwxd_cost(design, batch_rows) (per pair: a row touch charged _ROW_TOUCH_FLOPS = 1000 flops, plus the histogram or direct-row work). If row chunks are not cheaper, use the pair kernels. Row chunks win for many smooths against few coefficients; a few wide blocks, such as a random effect with many levels, keep the pair kernels.
  2. Otherwise take the largest chunk in _ROW_XWXD_CHUNKS = (2048, 1024, 512, 256, 128, 64) whose scratch discrete_row_xwxd_bytes(p, c) = 8 * (3 * c * p + 2 * p * p) fits the budget left after the fit plan (memory_budget_bytes - fit_peak_bytes). If none fits, use the pair kernels.

The row-chunk kernel is used only in the statistics scan of the additive Gaussian fit. The regular-family kernels in jaxgam/fitting/discrete/working.py always call discrete_xwxd.

flowchart TD
    Start["fit_discrete_gaussian: statistics scan"] --> Plan["_row_xwxd_chunk"]
    Plan --> Cost{"discrete_row_xwxd_cost<br/>below discrete_xwxd_cost?"}
    Cost -->|"no"| Pair["discrete_xwxd"]
    Cost -->|"yes"| Fit{"some chunk in _ROW_XWXD_CHUNKS<br/>has discrete_row_xwxd_bytes<br/>within remaining budget?"}
    Fit -->|"no"| Pair
    Fit -->|"yes"| Rows["discrete_row_xwxd<br/>chunk_rows = largest fitting chunk"]
    Pair --> Sched["discrete_pair_schedule<br/>groups pairs by kind and shape"]
    Sched --> Kind{"pair kind"}
    Kind -->|"lookup_diagonal"| Diag["weight histogram h<br/>T' diag h T"]
    Kind -->|"lookup_histogram"| Hist["lookup_pair_histogram_crossproduct"]
    Kind -->|"lookup_direct"| Direct["gather rows<br/>rows_l' w rows_r"]
    Kind -->|"tensor"| Tensor["_subblock_pair_crossproduct"]
    Tensor --> Final["_final_margin_crossproduct<br/>histogram or direct"]
    Diag --> Acc["add block and its transpose<br/>into p x p gram"]
    Hist --> Acc
    Direct --> Acc
    Final --> Acc
    Rows --> Panels["upper panels of 4 x 4 split<br/>mirrored to symmetric"]
    Panels --> Acc

Read it top to bottom: the chunk decision is taken once per fit; inside discrete_xwxd each scheduled pair group runs one scan whose pair kind was fixed on the host by pair_reduction_plan.

docs.title: The shared prepared problem
docs.text:
Every discrete fit enters _prepared_discrete(spec, source, control), a context manager that yields a _PreparedDiscrete and always calls setup.cleanup() on exit, which releases the compact selectors (including any memmap files under selector_memmap_directory). In order:

  1. _reject_unsupported_formula refuses a multi-variable s(..., bs="re"): pinned bam discretizes each of its variables as a separate tensor margin, which the compact setup does not reproduce.
  2. build_continuous_discrete_setup builds the compact frame (build_compact_setup_frame in jaxgam/data/continuous_frame.py), checks the prospective basis bytes plus retained compact tables against DiscretizationBudget.max_table_bytes, runs ModelSetup.build on the compact frame with source_penalty_coordinates=True, and freezes a PredictSpec, the PenaltyStructure and the separate source_determinant_penalties. The compact training matrix is discarded. A budget failure comes back as ContinuousSetupUnavailable and is raised as MemoryError.
  3. build_discretization_metadata copies a bounded, row-free record of every group (policy, whether it was rounded, grid, ranges, compact row count, and representatives only up to max_retained_representatives). build_request_compression adds the fitted grouping when the effective prediction policy is "mgcv_predict_bamd".
  4. build_continuous_discrete_design evaluates each term's frozen basis on its compact representatives into lookup tables, with no source scan. It checks retained tables against max_table_bytes, retained selectors against max_selector_bytes, each term's evaluation temporaries, and finally max(host_batch_bytes, device_action_bytes) from _memory_plan against max_batch_bytes. A failure is a DiscreteDesignUnavailable, raised as MemoryError.

docs.title: Memory planning
docs.text:
The descriptor's DiscreteMemoryPlan bounds one action batch: host selector gathering, and on the device the retained tables plus the largest of the Xbd, adjoint, XWXd (including the largest pair reduction) and diagXVXd workspaces. Pairs are charged sequentially, not as if all coexisted.

The driver then builds a DiscreteFitMemoryPlan. _solver_plan (Gaussian) and _regular_solver_plan (regular and NB) add a solver workspace: a fixed count of p-by-p matrices (more when uncertainty="covariance"), explicit materializations of non-dense local penalties, and a per-row workspace of batch_rows times a fixed count of float64 vectors (the NB route adds the estimate.theta row vectors and long-double accumulators). fit_peak_bytes is the retained compact setup plus descriptor host and selector bytes plus the descriptor device peak plus the solver workspace; _check_fit_budget raises MemoryError when it exceeds FitControl.memory_budget_bytes, before any device transfer. The working-model compile step later adds its measured workspace to the same plan. The result reports fit_peak_bytes, the budget, and known_workspace_bytes (the plan's fit_workspace_bytes, which excludes the retained compact setup).

docs.title: The additive Gaussian fit
docs.text:
fit_discrete_gaussian (also reached as fit_fixed_sp_discrete_gaussian) makes exactly two fitting scans:

  1. Statistics scan. For each batch it validates finite inputs and nonnegative weights (padded invalid rows are refused), gathers selectors, and accumulates X'WX (pair kernels or row chunks) and X'W(y - offset); for the working model also sum(w (y - offset)^2). CenteredMoments merges batch moments of unweighted y around the first value, because R initializes the scale from var(y).
  2. Solve. With an explicit sp, the host forms H = sym(X'WX) + S_lambda, factors it with NumPy Cholesky (a non-positive-definite H raises LinAlgError: rank-deficient QR fitting is not implemented on this route) and solves for beta. Without sp, fit_gaussian_working_model_statistics runs the frozen-statistic working model (below), with no further row scans.
  3. Residual scan. The deviance is the direct sum of w (y - X beta - offset)^2 over a second scan, which is stable for nearly exact fits where y'Wy - beta'X'Wy would cancel.

EDF is tr(H^-1 X'WX). For fixed sp, _pinned_fixed_scale ports bgam.fitd's damped log-scale Newton sequence (hard-coded tolerance 1e-7 and 200 iterations, starting at log(var(y) * 0.05)) and _reml_score evaluates the criterion, with log|S|+ from _log_pdet on setup-owned structural range spaces (a port of Sl.setup plus ldetS; coupled blocks use SciPy's dpstrf in _pivoted_cholesky_root and _positive_logdet). The null dimension in the normalization is _pinned_criterion_null_dimension, which reproduces bgam.fitd's final Mp reset. A fixed-sp Gaussian fit always reports converged=True.

docs.title: The regular-family and negative-binomial fits
docs.text:
fit_discrete_regular enters regular_working_components, which prepares the problem, budgets _regular_solver_plan, compiles the proposal (compile_working_model_proposal), transfers the design and builds a RegularWorkingComponents bundle:

  • rows: a _DiscreteWorkingRows (or _DiscreteExtendedRows for the NB). Every call is one complete source scan. initial() evaluates at eta = linkfun(mustart) from the family initializer; evaluate(beta, statistics=...) evaluates at X beta + offset. Each batch runs a JIT kernel from jaxgam/fitting/discrete/working.py and returns per-row deviance plus, when requested, X'WX, X'Wz and sum(w z^2). Per-row deviances are reduced on the host by source_sum, R's left-to-right long-double sum, because step-control decisions compare two such sums near convergence.
  • propose: transfers each iteration's statistics to the device once (CompiledWorkingModelProposal.transfer) and evaluates trials on them.
  • penalty: source_penalty_quadratic, b'Sb in the Sl.setup coordinates, so a very large smoothing parameter cannot cancel against null-space coefficients.
  • start: iteration one's free parameters, initial.sp from the diagonal of the iteration-one X'WX (initial_log_sp_from_diagonal) when smoothing is selected, then log(var(y) * 0.05) when the scale is estimated.
  • nuisance: _ThetaNuisance for an NB with estimated theta.

The working model is bgam.fitd's, not the dense route's gam.fit3:

  • Regular families use Fisher weights and pseudodata (_fisher_working_quantities): w = prior * mu.eta^2 / V(mu), z = (eta - offset) + (y - mu) / mu.eta, with a zero mu.eta replaced by 0.1 before both are formed; no observed-curvature split, weight clipping or row filtering, and no validmu/valideta check.
  • The NB uses bgam.fitd's dDeta Newton weights at the current theta (discrete_extended_working_batch, family method source_newton_working).
  • The scale is fixed at one for Poisson and Binomial; for Gamma it is a working-model parameter log.phi.

docs.title: The performance iteration
docs.text:
fit_regular_working_model loops advance_regular_working_model until convergence or working_model_max_iterations. One outer iteration:

  1. Iteration one scans at linkfun(mustart); there are no coefficients yet.
  2. Iteration two scans at the first proposal's coefficients with no step control. A non-finite deviance raises FloatingPointError("Non-finite working-model deviance at iteration 2."), which is where pinned bam also stops.
  3. From iteration three the step is halved toward the previous accepted coefficients (coef0 / 2 + coef / 2) while the penalized deviance dev + b'Sb exceeds the accepted one or is non-finite, at most 29 times (_MAX_COEFFICIENT_TRIALS = 30, R's kk < 30). Each trial's relative margin is kept in RegularWorkingModelIteration.step_control_margins.
  4. With an estimated theta (NB), dev0 is first re-evaluated at the current theta, trial scans compute deviance only, then estimate.theta runs at the step-controlled coefficients (from iteration two), and one more scan forms the statistics with the new theta. Without a nuisance, an accepted trial's scan already formed the statistics, so it costs one scan.
  5. Convergence test, before any proposal: from iteration three, stop when |pdev - pdev_old| / (0.1 + |pdev|) < working_model_epsilon and, if the scale is estimated, the last log-scale step is below epsilon * (|log phi| + 1).
  6. Proposal: accept_working_model_proposal (below), then the next criterion crit = (pdev / phi - log|S|+ + log|H|) / 2.

After a converged iteration the final coefficients are its step-controlled ones, paired with the previous proposal's factor and smoothing parameters; at the iteration limit they are the last proposal's coefficients, whose deviance needs one more deviance-only scan. In both cases the result keeps converged, and fit_discrete_regular emits a RuntimeWarning when the limit is reached. An explicit sp runs the same loop with every smoothing parameter fixed: Sl.fitChol then updates only an estimated scale.

flowchart TD
    Top["advance_regular_working_model<br/>iteration i"] --> First{"i == 1?"}
    First -->|"yes"| Init["rows.initial<br/>scan at linkfun mustart"]
    First -->|"no"| Eval["rows.evaluate at carried coefficients"]
    Eval --> Ctl{"i > 2 and pdev worse<br/>or non-finite?"}
    Ctl -->|"yes, under 29 halvings"| Halve["halve toward accepted coefficients"]
    Halve --> Eval
    Ctl -->|"no"| Theta{"nuisance and i > 1?"}
    Init --> Theta
    Theta -->|"yes"| Est["_ThetaNuisance.update<br/>source_estimate_theta"]
    Est --> Stats["rows.evaluate with statistics"]
    Theta -->|"no"| Finite{"penalized deviance finite?"}
    Stats --> Finite
    Finite -->|"no"| Fail["FloatingPointError"]
    Finite -->|"yes"| Conv{"i > 2 and deviance change<br/>and log-scale step below epsilon?"}
    Conv -->|"yes"| Done["RegularWorkingModelFit<br/>converged"]
    Conv -->|"no"| Prop["accept_working_model_proposal"]
    Prop --> Next["RegularWorkingModelState<br/>parameters, step, coefficients, crit"]
    Next --> Limit{"completed below<br/>working_model_max_iterations?"}
    Limit -->|"yes"| Top
    Limit -->|"no"| Max["deviance-only scan<br/>converged False"]

Each box that says "rows" is one complete source scan; everything else is coefficient-space work on the host or in the proposal kernels.

docs.title: Theta
docs.text: source_estimate_theta in jaxgam/execution/discrete/working_theta.py ports estimate.theta for one log theta with known scale: a Newton iteration on nll = sum(dev.resids)/2 - ls at fixed mu, with the absolute value of a non-positive Hessian (and a 1e-5 relative floor), a step capped at 4, halving while the objective rises by more than eps^0.75 relative (at most 25 times), and convergence when |g| <= 1e-7 (|nll| + 1). A step failure warns and keeps the last theta. Each objective is _DiscreteExtendedRows.objective, one full scan of discrete_theta_batch, so source_scans grows faster than the iteration count for an estimated theta. A fixed theta (NegativeBinomial(theta, fixed=True)) skips the nuisance.

docs.title: The working-model REML proposal
docs.text:
The proposal is shared by every family. It ports Sl.fitChol's trial, not the dense route's nested exact REML: the Gaussian controller passes frozen X'X, X'y, y'y; the regular controller passes each iteration's Fisher X'WX, X'Wz, sum(w z^2).

Reparameterization. WorkingModelCriterionMetadata.from_structure builds Sl.setup-style blocks (build_working_penalty_blocks in jaxgam/formula/discrete/working_penalties.py): per block a coefficient transform, local penalties declared diagonal when they are, and for coupled multi-penalty blocks the projected roots used by the determinant. The statistics are transformed once per set by working_model_statistics, the block transform of Sl.initial.repara; trials reuse the transformed arrays.

Pivoted Cholesky at a host boundary. Each trial crosses the host once:

  1. working_model_factor_inputs (JIT) forms H = X'WX + S_lambda in working coordinates, scales it by d = sqrt(diag H) as t(A/d)/d, and forms the scaled combined root products of each coupled penalty block.
  2. factor_working_model factors each matrix on the host with source_pivoted_cholesky, R's chol(pivot=TRUE) (LAPACK DPSTRF) from the pinned scipy-openblas32 wheel that matches the OpenBLAS 0.3.26 pinned R links, run single-threaded (jaxgam/smooths/source_lapack.py). The pivot order and rank decision are part of the criterion's arithmetic, so the provider is pinned to reproduce R's. The factor is a host operation with no derivatives.
  3. gaussian_working_model_proposal (JIT) consumes the factors.

exp(log sp) is evaluated once per trial with the C library exp (source_exponentials), as R does; source_exp and source_log serve the same purpose in the controllers.

Criterion and derivatives (_source_gaussian_state): beta from the scaled pivoted solve (_source_cholesky_solve, which pads dropped coordinates); log|H| from the factor diagonal; log|S|+ and its derivatives in closed form for singleton blocks and from the host factors for coupled blocks; the penalized residual yy - sum(beta * f); and its first and second derivatives in log smoothing parameters from _source_ift_chol, a port of Sl.iftChol (the implicit-function-theorem solve db/drho = -H^-1 S_j beta lambda_j). The value is (pdev / phi - log|S|+ + log|H| + (n - M_p) log(2 pi phi)) / 2; when the scale is free, a log-phi coordinate is appended to the gradient and Hessian. With fixed_smoothing only the log-phi coordinate stays free.

Newton step on log smoothing parameters (_sl_newton_step): coordinates are active when |g| or |H_ii| exceeds the tolerance |crit| * sqrt(eps); the restricted Hessian's eigenvalues are made absolute and floored at max * sqrt(eps); the step -V diag(1/|lambda|) V' g is zeroed on inactive coordinates and scaled so its largest entry is at most 4.

Step control (accept_working_model_proposal, bgam.fitd's update loop): the carried step Nstep from the previous proposal is tried from the current parameters; it is accepted at once when it is empty or max(Nstep) == 0, and otherwise halved while the directional derivative sum(grad * Nstep) exceeds pdev * 1e-7. The accepted trial's own step becomes the next iteration's Nstep. A non-finite proposal raises FloatingPointError.

EDF and covariance. working_model_hessian_inverse forms H^-1 from the accepted factor (dropped coordinates get zero rows and columns); the block transforms map it back to public coordinates. EDF is sum(H^-1 * X'WX'), that is tr(H^-1 X'WX), pairing the last accepted proposal's factor with the last iteration's X'WX as bgam.fitd does; Vp = scale * H^-1 when uncertainty="covariance", and a PivotedQRFisherFactor plus transforms is retained when uncertainty="fisher".

Compile-time memory. compile_working_model_proposal first charges _prospective_memory (metadata, statistics, state, trace) against the budget left after the fit plan, then lowers and compiles the three kernels (working_model_statistics, working_model_factor_inputs, gaussian_working_model_proposal) and adds their measured memory_analysis() temporaries and outputs (less aliases) plus the DPSTRF workspace (source_pivoted_cholesky_workspace_bound). Either check raises MemoryError before any proposal runs. A backend whose compiled memory_analysis() is None is refused with NotImplementedError.

docs.title: The Gaussian working-model controller
docs.text: fit_gaussian_working_model_statistics starts from initial.sp on the diagonal of X'X and log(var(y) * 0.05), then loops advance_gaussian_working_model: the penalized deviance at the top of an iteration is yy - beta'X'y from the frozen statistics; the convergence test (iteration above two, relative deviance change and log-scale step below working_model_epsilon) precedes each proposal; then one accept_working_model_proposal. The trace keeps accepted iterations only.

docs.title: Sequence of a discretized fit
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant API as GAM._fit_discrete
    participant Drv as fit_discrete_regular
    participant Prep as _prepared_discrete
    participant Comp as compile_working_model_proposal
    participant Rows as _DiscreteWorkingRows
    participant Loop as fit_regular_working_model
    participant Res as GAMPredictionResult
    API->>Drv: spec, RowSource, family, sp, control
    Drv->>Prep: enter context
    Prep->>Prep: build_continuous_discrete_setup
    Prep->>Prep: build_discretization_metadata
    Prep->>Prep: build_continuous_discrete_design
    Prep-->>Drv: _PreparedDiscrete
    Drv->>Drv: _regular_solver_plan and _check_fit_budget
    Drv->>Comp: penalties, n, remaining budget
    Comp-->>Drv: CompiledWorkingModelProposal
    Drv->>Rows: to_device_discrete_design
    Drv->>Loop: rows, propose, penalty, start
    loop each outer iteration
        Loop->>Rows: initial or evaluate, one source scan each
        Rows-->>Loop: WorkingEvaluation
        Loop->>Comp: trial parameters on transferred statistics
        Comp-->>Loop: GaussianWorkingModelProposal
    end
    Loop-->>Drv: RegularWorkingModelFit
    Drv->>Drv: RegularWorkingComponents.result
    Drv->>Prep: exit context, release selectors
    Drv-->>API: DiscreteFit
    API->>Res: _from_discrete

The additive Gaussian fit follows the same preparation and budget steps but calls fit_discrete_gaussian: one statistics scan, then either a host Cholesky solve or fit_gaussian_working_model_statistics with no further scans, then one residual scan.

docs.title: What the result reports
docs.text:
GAMPredictionResult._from_discrete builds a row-free result:

  • execution_route="discrete", discretization_strategy="mgcv_range_grid", smoothing_strategy and lambda_strategy ("fixed" or "working_model_reml"), prediction_policy and the discretization record.
  • execution_path: "jax_actions_numpy_solve" (fixed-sp Gaussian), "jax_actions_working_model_numpy_postestimation" (selected Gaussian) or "jax_actions_performance_iteration_numpy_postestimation" (regular and NB).
  • n_iter is the scale-iteration count for fixed-sp Gaussian and the outer iteration count otherwise; convergence_info names the strategy and counts.
  • working_model_proposal_evaluations: proposal trials, including halved ones (zero for fixed-sp Gaussian, nonzero for fixed-sp regular fits).
  • source_scans and batches_scanned count fit scans only, not setup.
  • fit_peak_bytes, fit_memory_budget_bytes, known_workspace_bytes.
  • theta for the NB only (its final fixed or estimated value).
  • score is bgam.fitd's criterion with the Mp reset; edf_total is tr(H^-1 X'WX). The per-iteration trace is not copied to the result.

docs.title: Prediction policies
docs.text:
ContinuousDiscretizationControl.prediction_policy is recorded on the result and the predictor. Both policies reuse the fitted knots, constraints and transforms:

  • "continuous_frozen_basis" (default): every new value is evaluated exactly by the frozen basis, so predictions never depend on the request or its batching.
  • "mgcv_predict_bamd": pinned predict.bamd semantics. A bounded pre-pass over the whole request (jaxgam/data/continuous_request.py) freezes each group's rounding decision and grid with discrete.mf's default m; batches are then compressed elementwise. Results depend on the request's composition but not on batch boundaries. A model without smooth terms records "continuous_frozen_basis" and keeps the request in discretization.requested_prediction_policy (effective_prediction_policy).

Factor semantics are the same under both: a missing or unseen random-effect level contributes zero.

docs.title: Rules and invariants
docs.text:
• No n-row array is retained. Rows are reached only by complete bounded source scans; finished batches are deleted before the next is built. tests/test_execution/test_discrete.py (test_completed_fitting_scan_releases_batch_arrays_before_residual_scan) and tests/test_scaling_allocation_guards.py (test_source_routes_never_build_the_training_design) enforce this.
  • Selectors stay on the host. to_device_discrete_design transfers tables only; kernels refuse batches above batch_rows.
  • Budget before allocation. The fit plan is checked before device transfer and the working-model workspace before any proposal (test_fit_workspace_rejects_before_device_transfer, tests/test_execution/test_working_model.py test_gaussian_compiled_budget_rejects_before_proposal, tests/test_execution/test_regular_working_model.py test_budget_rejects_before_device_transfer).
  • Source identity. A changed fingerprint during or after a scan raises RuntimeError; row counts must match the declared n_rows.
  • R arithmetic is part of the port. Deviance sums use source_sum (long double, row order); exp and log use the C library; the pivoted Cholesky is the pinned DPSTRF. Step-control ties near convergence depend on these (tests/test_execution/test_regular_working_model.py test_source_sum_is_left_to_right_in_long_double, tests/test_execution/test_working_model.py test_source_exp_and_log_are_the_c_library_functions).
  • Parity with pinned bam. Fixed and selected fits are compared to bam(discrete=TRUE) in tests/test_execution/test_discrete.py, tests/test_execution/test_discrete_regular.py, tests/test_execution/test_discrete_nb.py and tests/test_execution/test_working_model.py; proposals at matched states in tests/test_fitting/test_working_model.py (test_proposal_matches_pinned_sl_fitchol); estimate.theta in tests/test_execution/test_working_theta.py; predictions in tests/test_execution/test_discrete_prediction.py; the indexed kernels against explicit designs and pinned R layouts in tests/test_fitting/test_discrete_ops.py.
  • Batch invariance. Fits must not depend on batch_rows (test_fit_is_batch_invariant_and_cleans_owned_selector_files, test_public_regular_fit_is_batch_invariant_and_pickles).
  • The oracle hook is private. _oracle_replay_halvings replays a recorded R step-control outcome at rounding-level ties for matched-state tests only; GAM never sets it (test_oracle_replay_hook_is_unreachable_from_the_public_api).
  • Phase 1 stays NumPy. jaxgam/formula/ modules used here import no JAX.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• fit() defaults to result="full", which this route refuses; every call needs result="prediction", and the result has no summary() or plot().
  • working_model_reml is bgam.fitd's performance iteration, not the dense route's nested exact REML. In tests/test_execution/test_discrete_regular.py every comparison with pinned bam is STRICT except two documented flat smoothing-parameter vectors.
  • Step-control decisions near convergence can be rounding-level ties whose outcome flips under a one-ulp perturbation even in R; matched-state tests replay R's outcome there through _oracle_replay_halvings.
  • Iteration two has no step control and there is no validmu check, so a first proposal that leaves the family domain raises at iteration two, as pinned bam does (test_domain_exit_without_step_control_stops_like_pinned_bam).
  • The fixed-sp Gaussian scale iteration hard-codes 1e-7 and 200; the working_model_epsilon and working_model_max_iterations controls do not apply to it, but they do govern fixed-sp regular fits.
  • source_scans is not the iteration count: estimated theta adds one scan per estimate.theta objective.
  • Because the basis is built on the compact rows, an m smaller than a smooth's k fails in basis construction with a message about unique data values.
  • The default policy's table and batch budgets can be too small for radial smooths or many-level factors at scale; the errors are MemoryError naming the stage.
  • The coefficients of a thin-plate smooth on a symmetric grid may differ from bam's by a change of coordinates (tests/test_execution/test_discrete_prediction.py).
  • A missing random-effect group predicts a zero contribution where pinned R gives NA (test_random_effect_missing_and_unseen_levels_contribute_zero).
  • Memory bounds cover known arrays; native compiler and allocator memory are outside them.

docs.title: Where to change things
docs.text:
• Admit a new family or link: give the family the regular_performance_iteration or extended_performance_iteration capability (see families, links and smooths) and check GAM._fit_discrete's admission; extended families also need the source_* row methods used in jaxgam/fitting/discrete/working.py.
  • Change how X'WX is reduced: _pair_part and the schedule in jaxgam/formula/kernel_groups.py; keep discrete_xwxd_cost and the descriptor's _memory_plan in step with any new reduction.
  • Change the row-chunk choice: _row_xwxd_chunk and _ROW_XWXD_CHUNKS in jaxgam/execution/discrete/gaussian.py, the cost constants in jaxgam/fitting/discrete/ops.py.
  • Change the proposal arithmetic: jaxgam/fitting/discrete/working_model.py; rerun the matched-state R tests in tests/test_fitting/test_working_model.py.
  • Change step control or convergence: accept_working_model_proposal and advance_gaussian_working_model in jaxgam/execution/discrete/working_model.py, and advance_regular_working_model in jaxgam/execution/discrete/regular_working_model.py.
  • Change memory accounting: _solver_plan, _regular_solver_plan, _prospective_memory and compile_working_model_proposal.
  • Change what the result reports: DiscreteFit and GAMPredictionResult._from_discrete in jaxgam/results.py.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: This page covers FitControl(execution="operator", linear_solver="pcg"): matrix-free fitting for models whose random effects have too many levels for a dense or discretized design. It describes how preparation bounds the model, the matrix-free actions, the frozen system and its positive-definiteness certificate, preconditioned conjugate gradients (PCG), the fixed-smoothing coefficient driver, the operator Fellner-Schall (EFS) controller with its score error bounds, score assembly, and the bulk link-scale variance. Routing into the route is in the fit lifecycle; the dense EFS it is compared with is in the dense fit.

The PCG solver and the preconditioners are documented in code as new algorithms, not mgcv ports. The Newton loop and the PCG driver are host Python loops in jaxgam/execution/; only per-batch kernels and PCG recurrences are JIT-compiled. solve_resident_pcg, the lax.while_loop solver in jaxgam/fitting/operator/iterative.py, has no caller outside that module. The The modules of jaxgam/formula/operator/ import no JAX.

A planned refactor will move this route onto a shared engine; see the unified fit design.

docs.title: Entry and refusals
docs.text: GAM._fit_operator refuses, before any source access: linear_solver other than "pcg"; result other than "prediction"; uncertainty other than "none"; sp=None unless optimizer="efs"; an estimated theta (use NegativeBinomial(theta, fixed=True)) or more than one theta; a device other than None or "cpu". The data must be a RowSource that owns weights and offset. With sp=None and optimizer="efs" it calls _fit_operator_efs; otherwise it validates sp (length, real, positive, finite; a quick length check before preparation when every smooth is a plain s() without by, and the exact check against penalties.n_penalties after it), prepares the model, and calls fit_operator_fixed_sp. A formula with no penalty still needs sp=[].

docs.title: Prepared geometry
docs.text:
prepare_operator_model(spec, source, control=OperatorPreparationControl(...)) splits the model into two parts and never builds an n-by-p matrix, a dense random-effect design or a p-by-p penalty:

  • Indexed random effects (s(..., bs="re")): an IndexedRandomEffect holds the term's factors (FactorEncoding, a frozen level tuple and lookup) and numeric variables. evaluate(columns) returns one level id and one amplitude per row: the id is the mixed-radix product of the factor codes, numeric variables multiply the amplitude (random slopes), and an unknown level or a non-finite amplitude contributes zero. The width is the product of the level counts. The penalty is one IdentityPenalty(width, scale) per term, with scale the squared largest absolute amplitude seen in training. Levels are a categorical's declared categories (unused ones included), otherwise the sorted observed values; a missing training level is an error.
  • Modest block: intercept, numeric parametric terms and s/te/ti smooths with cr, cs, cc, tp, ts, gp bases (with numeric or factor by). Its raw width is capped by OperatorControl.max_modest_coefficients (default 64) before anything is built. Plain cubic terms go through the ordinary prepare_model; any by, tensor or radial term goes through prepare_modest_cubic_by, which calls prepare_radial_smooth for tp/ts/gp (knots harvested from bounded scans, mgcv's sampler run locally). A modest penalty block is copied into the global PenaltyStructure at its global columns.

Every scan runs through _CheckedSource, which checks positions, validity, finite response, weights and offset, the column schema, and pickles and SHA-256-hashes every row to prove identical replay (source_replay_digest), charging each row's bound before serializing it. Memory is checked by _check_budget at each stage; failures are MemoryError before allocation. The result PreparedOperatorModel records metadata_bound_bytes, preparation_peak_bound_bytes and preparation scan counts, and evaluate_batch turns a RowBatch into an OperatorBatch (modest rows plus (ids, amplitudes, start, size) per indexed term) under batch_workspace_bound.

flowchart TD
    Start["prepare_operator_model"] --> Terms{"every term re, cr/cs/cc,<br/>tp/ts/gp or numeric?"}
    Terms -->|"no"| Refuse["NotImplementedError"]
    Terms -->|"yes"| Width{"modest raw width within<br/>max_modest_coefficients?"}
    Width -->|"no"| Cap["MemoryError"]
    Width -->|"yes"| Budget["_check_budget<br/>modest and symbolic bounds"]
    Budget --> Checked["_CheckedSource<br/>fingerprint and replay digest"]
    Checked --> Scan["scan: discover re levels,<br/>max amplitude per term"]
    Scan --> Enc["FactorEncoding per factor"]
    Enc --> Kind{"any by, tensor or radial term?"}
    Kind -->|"no"| Plain["prepare_model on modest terms"]
    Kind -->|"yes"| ModestBy["prepare_modest_cubic_by"]
    ModestBy --> Radial["prepare_radial_smooth<br/>for tp, ts, gp"]
    Plain --> Place["place modest columns and<br/>IndexedRandomEffect blocks"]
    Radial --> Place
    Place --> Pen["IdentityPenalty per re term<br/>plus modest penalty blocks"]
    Pen --> Verify{"fingerprint unchanged?"}
    Verify -->|"yes"| Model["PreparedOperatorModel"]
    Verify -->|"no"| Changed["RuntimeError"]

Every scan in this flow is a _CheckedSource scan; the replay digest from the first complete scan is checked by every later scan in preparation and in the fit.

docs.title: Matrix-free actions
docs.text:
to_device_operator_batch validates one OperatorBatch (finite modest values, ids in range, non-overlapping coefficient intervals), charges its transfer, and makes a DeviceOperatorBatch with DeviceIndexedRows. The kernels in jaxgam/fitting/operator/actions.py follow Xbd/XWyd's gather/reduce contract in public coordinates:

  • matvec_batch: modest_values @ v[modest_columns] plus, per indexed term, amplitudes * v[start + ids].
  • rmatvec_batch: scatter-add of modest_values.T @ u and of amplitudes * u into start + ids.
  • normal_matvec_batch and accumulate_normal_matvec_batch: X'W X v, the latter adding into a donated p-vector across host batches so no extra p-vector is allocated per batch; accumulate_rmatvec_batch likewise for right-hand sides and gradients.
  • penalty_matvec: S_lambda v from local penalty blocks (penalty_ops.apply, mgcv's Sl.Sb pattern).

operator_family_rows (jaxgam/fitting/operator/family.py) evaluates one batch's family rows at eta: it takes the first and second derivatives of the row deviance with JAX AD, giving half_gradient = D'/2, the observed curvature observed_weight = D''/2, and the working response W (eta - offset) - D'/2 (the form pinned gam.fit4 uses, which avoids dividing by zero curvature). There is no Fisher substitution or curvature clipping; it requires the family capabilities row_separable, observed_information, direct_deviance and differentiable_deviance.

docs.title: The frozen system and its certificate
docs.text:
FrozenScanSystem(model, source, log_sp, curvature_from_rows=..., memory_budget_bytes=..., use_coarse=...) represents H = X'WX + S_lambda at one frozen curvature. Construction:

  1. Checks the construction bound (65p + 288K^2 + 32pK and further terms, where K is the modest width) and copies and freezes the modest metadata and penalties.
  2. Weights the penalties with the C library exp. Each modest penalty must be positive semidefinite (ValueError otherwise); every other block must be a full-rank IdentityPenalty (NotImplementedError otherwise, though preparation never builds one).
  3. One certificate scan accumulates the modest Gram matrix (also split into positive- and negative-curvature parts), the assembled diagonal, indexed off-diagonal bounds, the indexed-to-modest coupling (p by K), and a SHA-256 digest of the row curvature.
  4. Certifies positive definiteness without forming H:
  5. With no negative rows: S_modest + G / (1 + t) must have a Cholesky factor, where t is the trace of the indexed Gram relative to the indexed penalty (an upper bound on its spectral radius).
  6. With negative rows and no indexed effect: S_modest + G itself must have a Cholesky factor.
  7. With negative rows and indexed effects: first a Schur-complement test that replaces the indexed block by a lower bound on its diagonal (diagonal minus the off-diagonal bound), when that bound is positive; otherwise a leverage test (total negative-row leverage below one in a block lower-bound metric); otherwise a low-rank certificate for at most _MAX_SIGNED_DOWNDATE_RANK = 8 independent negative directions; otherwise LinAlgError("Actual signed system has no sufficient Schur SPD certificate.").
  8. The data curvature must be positive definite on the modest penalty's null directions (LinAlgError otherwise). The certificate is sufficient, not necessary: a refusal does not prove H is indefinite (tests/test_execution/test_operator.py, test_signed_certificate_cap_is_not_a_claim_of_indefiniteness).
  9. Builds the preconditioner (below), compiles the normal-action and penalty kernels, reads their measured scratch, and checks the action peak bound.

matvec(v) is one complete checked source scan: start from S_lambda v, add each batch's X'WXv, and verify that the curvature digest is unchanged. Each matvec, right-hand side and objective is therefore one full scan.

has_exact_diagonal (one indexed effect and nothing else) and has_exact_arrowhead (one modest block of at most 64 columns coupled to one indexed identity block) mark the structured shapes for which the log-determinant and traces are computed exactly.

docs.title: Preconditioned conjugate gradients
docs.text:
prepare_preconditioner builds an InversePreconditioner: the reciprocal of the assembled diagonal for every coordinate, a Cholesky-factored SmallBlockInverse for the modest columns (G + S_modest), and with OperatorControl.use_coarse=True an additive CoarseInverse on the modest penalty-null directions. Large blocks retain only the diagonal; the construction bound is 17p plus the capped block terms.

solve_host_pcg (reached through FrozenScanSystem.solve) charges 14 float64 p-vectors plus the measured scratch of its four compiled kernels before allocating, then iterates on the host with JIT steps from jaxgam/fitting/operator/iterative.py. The threshold is max(atol, rtol * ||rhs||). A recursive residual below the threshold only moves the state to VERIFY_RESIDUAL; convergence (CONVERGED) needs a fresh true residual rhs - H x from another matvec, and a failed verification restarts CG without resetting the iteration count. Other statuses are MAX_ITERATIONS, NONFINITE and NONPOSITIVE_CURVATURE. Every matvec is counted in HostPCGResult.matvec_count.

docs.title: The fixed-smoothing coefficient driver
docs.text:
fit_operator_fixed_sp is a host observed-Newton loop:

  1. Budget. fit_bound (metadata, family snapshot, 80p for retained vectors, extra terms for no-intercept layouts, 128 * max_iterations) plus a row bound plus the measured scratch of the compiled family, forward and adjoint kernels must fit memory_budget_bytes; the remainder is the frozen system's budget.
  2. Start. _initial_null_beta ports mgcv's get.null.coef for layouts it can prove: with an intercept, the intercept alone at link(mean(initialized y)); for no-intercept layouts, bounded source QR projections, some of which refuse with NotImplementedError. Unknown-scale families also reduce a null scale, used in the convergence test and reported as initial_null_scale.
  3. Each iteration builds a FrozenOperatorWorkingState (iteration one at the family's mustart, later at the current beta), a FrozenScanSystem with its observed curvature, the right-hand side X'(W(eta - offset) - D'/2) by _reduce_rhs, and solves H beta_new = rhs by PCG. A failed PCG ends the loop with converged=False and the last accepted state.
  4. Gaussian identity (single_step_pirls) is solved once and refined against its true residual up to _STRICTLY_ADDITIVE_REFINEMENTS = 3 times, then accepted.
  5. Step halving: while the penalized deviance _reduce_objective (direct row deviance plus beta'S beta, infinite outside the domain) exceeds the previous value plus a small allowance, halve toward the previous beta; after 100 halvings RuntimeError.
  6. Convergence: relative objective change below OperatorControl.tolerance and 2 max|X'D'/2 + S beta| <= tolerance * (|objective| + null scale). At max_iterations the result is returned with converged=False.
sequenceDiagram
    participant API as GAM._fit_operator
    participant Prep as prepare_operator_model
    participant Fit as fit_operator_fixed_sp
    participant Sys as FrozenScanSystem
    participant PCG as solve_host_pcg
    participant Src as RowSource
    participant Res as GAMPredictionResult
    API->>Prep: spec, source, OperatorPreparationControl
    Prep->>Src: checked scans
    Prep-->>API: PreparedOperatorModel
    API->>Fit: model, source, family, sp, OperatorControl
    Fit->>Src: _initial_null_beta scans
    loop until converged or max_iterations
        Fit->>Sys: construct with observed curvature
        Sys->>Src: certificate scan
        Fit->>Src: _reduce_rhs scan
        Fit->>Sys: solve rhs
        Sys->>PCG: matvec, preconditioner, PCGControl
        loop PCG iterations and true-residual checks
            PCG->>Sys: matvec
            Sys->>Src: one checked scan
        end
        PCG-->>Fit: HostPCGResult
        Fit->>Src: _reduce_objective scans with halving
        Fit->>Src: _reduce_rhs gradient scan
    end
    Fit-->>API: OperatorFitResult
    API->>Res: _from_operator_fit

Every arrow into the source is a complete, replay-checked scan, so the scan count per Newton iteration is roughly one certificate, one right-hand side, one per PCG matvec, at least one objective and one gradient.

OperatorFitResult carries coefficients, log_lambda, the model, the family snapshot, deviance, converged, n_iter, convergence_info and OperatorFitDiagnostics: source counters, initialization_scans, rhs_scans, objective_scans, certificate_scans, certificate_actions, krylov_actions, krylov_iterations, completed_solves (Newton solves only), peak_bound_bytes, the three measured kernel temporaries, accepted_objectives, inner_status (the last PCG status), final_gradient_norm, initial_null_scale, the preparation_* counts, efs_indeterminate_comparisons, and preconditioner sizes reported apart from the peak. There is no PCG residual norm in the fit diagnostics.

GAMPredictionResult._from_operator_fit keeps an OperatorPredictionGeometry in the predictor, score=None, edf_total=None, no covariance, scale=1.0 for known-scale families and None otherwise, lambda_strategy="fixed", execution_route="operator", and fit-only source_scans and batches_scanned.

docs.title: The arrowhead exact algebra
docs.text: For H = [[A, B'], [B, D]] with a positive diagonal indexed block D, ExactArrowheadFactorization.from_system replays one checked scan to recover the coupling B (FrozenScanSystem.exact_arrowhead_coupling, which also checks the curvature digest), forms the modest Schur complement A - B' D^-1 B and factors it. It gives log_determinant, inverse_diagonal, modest_inverse, and spectral lower and condition estimates in O(pK + K^2) storage. Its floating result is conditional on the assembled H; it is not by itself a score error bound.

docs.title: The operator Fellner-Schall controller
docs.text:
_fit_operator_efs admits only:

  • Poisson with the log link;
  • batch_rows from 64 to 65536 (checked before any scan);
  • after preparation, exactly one indexed effect with 257 <= L <= 4096 levels and L <= n_obs <= 16 L (CALIBRATED_OPERATOR_EFS_DOMAIN.admits), plus at most CALIBRATED_OPERATOR_EFS_MAX_MODEST = 4 modest columns, and no other coefficients;
  • from the start provider, a factor-only effect with an identity penalty and unit weights and zero offset (NotImplementedError otherwise).

It splits memory_budget_bytes: one eighth for preparation and the start, a quarter for each refit, half for the score components, and the rest less a result reserve as the aggregate budget. prepare_indexed_operator_efs_start replays the initial.spg working diagonal and balances one smoothing parameter by factors of 10. SourceOperatorEFSFitProvider refits with fit_operator_fixed_sp and evaluates states with MatchedOperatorEFSProvider; run_operator_efs_known_scale runs _run_operator_efs, which follows pinned efsudr (mgcv R/gam.fit4.r) for known scale.

Matched components (MatchedOperatorEFSProvider.evaluate, all at one beta, theta and rho, bound by operator_efs_fit_fingerprint):

  • score rows: MatchedOperatorScoreReducer.reduce, one replay giving penalized deviance, the saturated log-likelihood term and diagnostics such as unit_weights, zero_offset, maximum_response, maximum_row_l1_norm;
  • log|S|+ and its gradient: LocalOperatorPenaltyDeterminant, with the range fixed by the unscaled local penalties;
  • log det H on an observed-curvature system: exact_structured_diagonal (decimal logarithms with a rounding bound), exact_structured_arrowhead, or otherwise the stochastic estimate (Rademacher probes and Lanczos);
  • Fisher traces tr(H_F^-1 S_j) and quadratics beta'S_j beta on a second system with Fisher curvature (FrozenOperatorWorkingState.fisher_curvature): structured for the diagonal and arrowhead shapes, else coordinate solves capped at 256 coordinates (ExactOperatorPenaltyStatistics);
  • EDF p - sum_j lambda_j tr(H_F^-1 S_j).

assemble_operator_score combines them with operator_reml_score: pdev / (2 phi) - ls + (log|H| - log|S|+) / 2 - M_p log(2 pi phi) / 2, where M_p is the penalty null dimension. The observed log-determinant is used, not the Fisher one. For every shape GAM.fit admits, the determinant and traces are structured, so no probes or Lanczos run; the OperatorLogDetControl(probes=4, lanczos_depth=4) passed by _fit_operator_efs only sizes the output reservation.

Score bounds. admitted_operator_efs_score_bound returns a bound and a method label, "indexed_poisson_empirical_v2", "arrowhead_poisson_empirical_v2" (or "indexed_gaussian_empirical_v2", whose Gaussian runner run_operator_efs_gaussian_scale GAM.fit cannot reach), or (None, "unavailable"). Each bound is the total of an OperatorScoreEnvelope:

  • arithmetic: 32 * eps * (n + p) * M (plus K^2 for the arrowhead), where M sums the score's term magnitudes;
  • coefficient: the effect of the final coefficient residual, from the final gradient and the identity-penalty floor (indexed) or the Schur spectral lower estimate (arrowhead);
  • determinant: the structured log-determinant's rounding bound.

A state is admitted only inside the calibrated domain and with: unit weights, zero offset, Poisson responses at most 32, converged PCG, tolerance <= 1e-7, cg_rtol <= 1e-10, cg_atol <= 1e-12, final gradient at most 1e-5, all |beta| <= 20, and conditioning gates (diagonal condition ratio at most 1e4 and minimum diagonal at least 1e-6 for the indexed shape; spectral lower estimate at least 1e-3 and condition at most 1e5 for the arrowhead). The three control thresholds equal the OperatorControl defaults, so loosening any one leaves every comparison undecided. The code calls these empirical envelopes, not certificates.

Comparison. compare_operator_scores requires identical probes and strategy. With both bounds present and radius r = bound_old + bound_trial, the trial is an improvement if diff + r < 0, worsening if diff - r > 0, equal only if both diff and r are zero, and otherwise indeterminate; a missing bound is always indeterminate. The paired standard error is reported but never decides. Only a stochastic_lanczos score is refined (probes and depth doubled up to 256 and 128); structured scores return indeterminate directly.

One outer iteration of _run_operator_efs:

flowchart TD
    Ratio["_raw_ratio and _trial_rho<br/>efsudr update times multiplier"] -->|"FloatingPointError"| Invalid["stop invalid_update"]
    Ratio --> Refit["provider.fit at trial rho"]
    Refit -->|"not converged"| Inner["stop inner_failure"]
    Refit --> Eval["provider.evaluate<br/>components and admitted bound"]
    Eval --> Cmp{"compare_operator_scores"}
    Cmp -->|"indeterminate"| Indet["stop indeterminate_score<br/>keep accepted state"]
    Cmp -->|"improvement or equal"| Small{"max step below 0.05?"}
    Small -->|"no"| Accept["accept trial"]
    Small -->|"yes"| Ext["refit at doubled multiplier"]
    Ext --> ExtCmp{"extension compare"}
    ExtCmp -->|"improvement"| AcceptExt["accept extension<br/>multiplier doubled"]
    ExtCmp -->|"otherwise"| Accept
    Cmp -->|"worsening"| Mult{"multiplier above 1?"}
    Mult -->|"yes"| Halve["halve multiplier, refit, compare"]
    Halve -->|"indeterminate, multiplier above 1"| Indet
    Halve --> Mult
    Mult -->|"no"| AcceptMin["accept minimum-multiplier step"]
    Accept --> Stop{"stop tests"}
    AcceptExt --> Stop
    AcceptMin --> Stop
    Stop -->|"iteration above 3, step below 0.05,<br/>score window within tolerance"| Window["stop score_window"]
    Stop -->|"deviance change below<br/>100 pirls_tolerance"| Dev["stop deviance_change"]
    Stop -->|"neither"| Ratio

_raw_ratio is efsudr's max(0, exp(-rho) d - t) / max(0, q) * phi (1 when both numerator and q are zero, 1e6 when non-finite), and _trial_rho clips at EFSControl.log_lambda_max. The first fit is at the start plus 2.5 on the log scale; if it does not converge the controller raises RuntimeError. An undecided extension is declined and counted. The score window (_score_window_certified) needs the last four accepted scores and bounds, with every adjacent change plus both bounds below EFSControl.score_tolerance. score_window and deviance_change are converged outcomes, except that convergence on the last allowed outer iteration is relabelled iteration_limit; indeterminate_score, iteration_limit, inner_failure and invalid_update are not converged. No exception or warning is raised for an indeterminate stop: the result has converged=False, convergence_info set to the stop reason and operator_diagnostics.efs_indeterminate_comparisons.

The EFS result adds score, score_error_bound, score_bound_method, edf_total, scale and score_scale (1.0), lambda_strategy="efs_reml", n_iter as outer iterations, cumulative source_scans, and known_workspace_bytes. Its operator_diagnostics describe only the accepted state's refit.

Calibration. The domain and envelope constants were measured with scripts/benchmark_operator_efs_calibration.py (make benchmark-operator-efs-calibration) against an independent 50-digit decimal REML reference (tests/operator_efs_calibration.py). The tests in tests/test_execution/test_operator_efs_calibrated.py check that at domain boundaries the matched-state score error stays inside the admitted bound, that just outside the domain (or past a conditioning gate) the bound is refused, and that the domain constants are the recorded ones; complete operator EFS fits are compared with dense EFS. tests/test_validation_matrix.py compares operator EFS for y~x+s(g,bs='re') with pinned R at STRICT, using tightened EFS and operator controls.

docs.title: Uncertainty
docs.text:
Operator fits retain no covariance: predict(se_fit=True) raises and materialize_covariance has no provider. The uncertainty path is GAMPredictionResult.bulk_link_variance(training_source, calibration_data, *, probes, seed, memory_budget_bytes, control=None, scale=None, max_calibration_standard_errors=5.0), which returns a (BulkOperatorVariance, BulkVarianceCalibration) pair:

  1. It requires a converged operator result, unchanged family and theta, and the original training source (row count and fingerprint). Known-scale families use their scale; others need scale=.
  2. It re-runs prepare_operator_model on the training source (the replay digest must match), builds a FrozenScanSystem with Fisher curvature at the fitted coefficients and smoothing parameters, using half the budget, and PCGControl() defaults (rtol=1e-10, atol=0, 1000 iterations) unless control is passed. FitControl.operator is not consulted.
  3. BulkOperatorVariance.build draws probes (at least 2) right-hand sides b = X'W^(1/2) z + S^(1/2) q (one scan each, local penalty blocks factored with null spaces preserved by _penalty_noise) and solves H u = b for each, keeping a probes-by-p sketch. Since E[(x'u)^2] = x'H^-1 x, the variance of a row is scale * mean((x'u)^2) with a Monte Carlo standard error. A failed probe solve raises BulkVarianceSolveError; no partial sketch is kept.
  4. calibrate(calibration_data) solves exactly for at most min(256, batch_rows) selected rows with SelectedOperatorVariance (one PCG solve per row), and maps each row's pivot probes * estimate / exact, which is chi-square with probes degrees of freedom, to an equivalent standard normal deviate (equivalent_normal_deviates). bulk_link_variance raises RuntimeError when the largest absolute deviate exceeds max_calibration_standard_errors.
  5. estimate_iter(source) then streams any prediction source in batches, yielding BulkVarianceBatch(positions, variance, monte_carlo_se) with a link_se property. Results are on the link scale only.

The calibration checks the selected rows only; it does not bound unselected rows or the iterative-solve bias, which BulkVarianceDiagnostics reports separately as maximum_relative_residual. tests/test_execution/test_operator_bulk_variance.py compares the exact selected-row variances with pinned R's squared link-scale standard errors at STRICT and checks that a biased sketch fails calibration.

flowchart TD
    Call["GAMPredictionResult.bulk_link_variance"] --> Check{"converged operator result,<br/>same family, theta, source?"}
    Check -->|"no"| Err["RuntimeError or ValueError"]
    Check -->|"yes"| Replay["prepare_operator_model<br/>on training source"]
    Replay --> Digest{"replay digest and n_coef match?"}
    Digest -->|"no"| Err
    Digest -->|"yes"| Fisher["FrozenScanSystem with<br/>fisher_curvature"]
    Fisher --> Build["BulkOperatorVariance.build"]
    Build --> Probe["_sample_rhs: one scan<br/>X'W^1/2 z plus S^1/2 q"]
    Probe --> Solve["FrozenScanSystem.solve"]
    Solve -->|"not converged"| SolveErr["BulkVarianceSolveError"]
    Solve -->|"more probes"| Probe
    Solve -->|"all probes done"| Sketch["probes x p sketch"]
    Sketch --> Cal["calibrate: SelectedOperatorVariance<br/>exact solves for selected rows"]
    Cal --> Pivot["equivalent_normal_deviates<br/>chi-square pivot"]
    Pivot --> Gate{"max deviate within<br/>max_calibration_standard_errors?"}
    Gate -->|"no"| Fail["RuntimeError"]
    Gate -->|"yes"| Out["BulkOperatorVariance and<br/>BulkVarianceCalibration"]
    Out --> Stream["estimate_iter yields BulkVarianceBatch"]

The sketch is built once; calibration and streaming both read it, and neither changes the probes.

docs.title: Memory bounds
docs.text: Every stage checks a prospective bound before allocating and raises MemoryError: preparation through _check_budget and per-row charges; fit_operator_fixed_sp through fit_bound plus measured kernel scratch; FrozenScanSystem through its construction and action peak bounds; solve_host_pcg through 14 p-vectors plus measured scratch; prepare_preconditioner through 17p plus block terms; the EFS provider through reserve on its aggregate budget. No p-by-p array is formed for the indexed coefficients; the indexed width is not capped by max_modest_coefficients. The reported byte figures (peak_bound_bytes, known_workspace_bytes) are accounting bounds that exclude source storage and native allocator or compiler memory.

The EFS side adds OperatorEFSState (a fit, its MatchedOperatorEFSComponents, score_error_bound and score_bound_method) and OperatorEFSControllerResult (accepted state, converged, stop_reason, counts and histories).

docs.title: Rules and invariants
docs.text:
• No dense design, penalty or covariance. The route never forms X, a p-by-p penalty or a covariance; tests/test_execution/test_operator_fit.py fails a fit that calls PenaltyStructure.materialize, and tests/test_scaling_allocation_guards.py checks that the dense design builder never sees the training rows.
  • Replay identity. Every scan is checked against the preparation replay digest and every system action against its curvature digest (tests/test_execution/test_operator.py, test_selected_repeated_lineage_and_frozen_curvature_replay).
  • Certified SPD before PCG. solve_host_pcg assumes the caller certified the system; sampled CG curvature does not certify it. Certificate failures raise from GAM.fit rather than returning converged=False.
  • Convergence needs a true residual (tests/test_fitting/test_iterative.py, test_recursive_residual_cannot_claim_convergence_and_false_candidate_restarts).
  • Observed curvature, never Fisher, in the fit; Fisher curvature only in the EFS traces and the bulk variance, each on its own frozen system.
  • Budgets before allocation (test_memory_preflight_rejects_before_source_scan_predictor_or_transfer, test_fit_combined_budget_rejects_before_initial_source_pass, tests/test_fitting/test_preconditioners.py).
  • R parity. Fixed-sp coefficients, deviance and fitted values are compared with pinned R for Gaussian, Poisson, Binomial, Gamma and fixed-theta NB links in tests/test_execution/test_operator_fit.py (test_operator_observed_fixed_sp_fit_matches_pinned_family_reference), and through GAM.fit in tests/test_validation_matrix.py.
  • EFS decisions only with admitted bounds (tests/test_execution/test_operator_score.py, test_common_probe_difference_reports_noise_but_waits_for_calibration).
  • Phase 1 stays NumPy. The modules of jaxgam/formula/operator/ import no JAX.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• fit() defaults to result="full"; this route needs result="prediction".
  • family="nb" is an estimated theta and is refused; use NegativeBinomial(theta, fixed=True).
  • Loosening OperatorControl.tolerance, cg_rtol or cg_atol from their defaults removes every EFS bound, so an EFS fit ends indeterminate_score after one outer iteration with no warning. A Poisson response above 32 does the same.
  • Non-unit weights, an offset, a penalized modest smooth or a random slope are hard NotImplementedError refusals under operator EFS (from the start provider), not indeterminate outcomes.
  • Parametric terms must be numeric; a factor main effect is refused in preparation.
  • A gp penalty can keep signed eigenvalues; a modest penalty with a negative eigenvalue is refused in FrozenScanSystem.
  • No-intercept layouts depend on source null projections, several of which refuse with NotImplementedError.
  • Scan counts are high: every matvec, right-hand side, objective and gradient re-reads and re-hashes every row.
  • The fit and the result use different batch sizes on a small source. The prepared model carries the smaller of FitControl.batch_rows and the source's row count (_operator_fit_batch_rows in jaxgam/api.py), because the kernels pad every batch to that size and every bound charges it. OperatorPredictionGeometry keeps FitControl.batch_rows, so a prediction request may be larger than the training data.
  • PCGControl is not exported from the top-level package; import it from jaxgam/execution/operator/system.py.

docs.title: Where to change things
docs.text:
• Admit a new basis in the modest block: prepare_operator_model's term check and jaxgam/formula/operator/modest.py (or jaxgam/formula/operator/radial.py), plus its evaluator bound in jaxgam/formula/operator/workspace.py.
  • Change the actions: jaxgam/fitting/operator/actions.py; keep to_device_operator_batch's validation and charges in step.
  • Change the SPD certificate or preconditioner: FrozenScanSystem.__init__ in jaxgam/execution/operator/system.py and jaxgam/fitting/operator/preconditioners.py.
  • Change PCG: solve_host_pcg and jaxgam/fitting/operator/iterative.py; keep the true-residual rule.
  • Change the Newton driver, start or step halving: fit_operator_fixed_sp and _initial_null_beta in jaxgam/execution/operator/fit.py.
  • Widen operator EFS admission: the domain, envelopes and admitted_operator_efs_score_bound in jaxgam/execution/operator/efs_controller.py, _fit_operator_efs in jaxgam/api.py, and the start provider; re-measure with scripts/benchmark_operator_efs_calibration.py and update tests/test_execution/test_operator_efs_calibrated.py.
  • Change score assembly: jaxgam/execution/operator/score.py and jaxgam/fitting/operator/efs_score.py.
  • Change bulk variance: jaxgam/execution/operator/bulk_variance.py and GAMPredictionResult.bulk_link_variance in jaxgam/results.py.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: This page covers FitControl(execution="stream"): fitting from a replayable RowSource without ever holding the model matrix or any row-aligned array. It describes the host drivers in jaxgam/execution/ and the per-batch JAX kernels in jaxgam/fitting/ for fixed-sp PIRLS, the positive and signed QR solvers, exact streamed REML with its L-BFGS-B optimizer, streamed negative-binomial theta, streamed Fellner-Schall, and the scan accounting and memory checks around them. Streamed setup (prepare_model) is on the setup page and the sources themselves on the data sources page.
