docs.title: Host drivers and batch kernels
docs.text:
Every streamed driver is a host Python loop over source scans. Inside a scan it evaluates one batch's design with PreparedModel.evaluate_fitting_batch, moves the batch with jax.device_put, calls one jitted kernel that returns only coefficient-sized statistics (p or p x p), adds them to running totals and calls jax.block_until_ready so at most one batch is in flight. The kernels in jaxgam/fitting/ do no file iteration; the drivers in jaxgam/execution/ own iteration, step control and every cross-batch reduction. QR reductions are not JAX: jaxgam/execution/qr.py and jaxgam/execution/stream/signed_qr.py merge row blocks with SciPy (linalg.qr with pivoting, LAPACK ormqr) on the CPU, and the resulting coefficient-sized factors are moved to the device for the jitted triangular actions in jaxgam/fitting/qr.py.

The streamed routes use PreparedFittingMetadata.from_prepared (jaxgam/fitting/data.py), not FittingData: the same penalty structure and log|S+| metadata, but no design matrix, response, weights or offset.

docs.title: Entry and route choice
docs.text:
GAM._fit_stream rejects linear_solver="pcg", data that is not a RowSource, separate weights/offset arrays, and any result other than "prediction". It checks the family statically (_check_stream_fixed_family, _check_stream_efs_family) and requires linear_solver="qr" for exact REML and for EFS. It then opens single_fit_fingerprints() and calls _fit_stream_routes, which runs prepare_model and wraps the result in a StreamDesign. The route is then:

Condition Driver execution_route lambda_strategy eligible gaussian_compression=True request _fit_stream_gaussian_qr stream_gaussian_qr newton_reml, lbfgs_reml or fixed optimizer="efs", sp=None, no penalties _fit_stream_parametric_bypass stream_parametric_qr newton_reml optimizer="efs", sp=None fit_streamed_efs stream_efs_qr efs_reml sp=None, no free parameter at all fixed regular or NB fit stream_exact_reml_qr exact_reml_no_parameters sp=None _fit_stream_exact_reml stream_exact_reml_qr exact_reml sp given, NB _fit_stream_fixed_nb stream_qr fixed sp given, other families, see the solver chart _fit_stream_fixed_regular or fit_streamed_pirls stream_qr or stream fixed 
flowchart TD
    A["_fit_stream_routes"] --> GQ{"eligible Gaussian QR request?"}
    GQ -- yes --> GQR["_fit_stream_gaussian_qr<br/>one replay, coefficient-space trials"]
    GQ -- no --> B{"sp supplied?"}
    B -- "no, optimizer efs" --> EFS["fit_streamed_efs<br/>qr only"]
    B -- "no, newton" --> EX["_fit_stream_exact_reml<br/>qr only"]
    B -- yes --> C{"NegativeBinomial?"}
    C -- yes --> NBF["_fit_stream_fixed_nb<br/>qr only"]
    C -- no --> D{"_stream_legacy_fisher_eligible?"}
    D -- no --> E{"linear_solver qr?"}
    E -- no --> R1["NotImplementedError"]
    E -- yes --> REG["_fit_stream_fixed_regular"]
    D -- yes --> F{"linear_solver qr and scale known?"}
    F -- yes --> REG
    F -- no --> G["fit_streamed_pirls"]
    G --> H{"solver_policy"}
    H -- cholesky --> CH["Cholesky of summed X'WX + S<br/>solve_penalized_system"]
    H -- qr --> PQ["positive QR<br/>qr_update, solve_augmented_qr"]
    EX --> INNER["inner fits"]
    EFS --> INNER
    REG --> INNER
    NBF --> INNER
    INNER --> I{"NegativeBinomial?"}
    I -- yes --> NBS["fit_nb_streamed_pirls<br/>signed QR on observed weights<br/>positive-observed retry"]
    I -- no --> J{"coefficient_system is observed?"}
    J -- "yes, non-canonical link" --> SQ["fit_regular_streamed_pirls<br/>signed QR, step-local Fisher retry"]
    J -- "no, canonical link" --> PF["fit_regular_streamed_pirls<br/>positive Fisher QR"]

Read it from the top. _stream_legacy_fisher_eligible holds when the family declares a Fisher coefficient system equal to observed information and a reported scale of known_one or gaussian_fisher_edf_deviance: among the built-in families that is Gaussian with identity link, Poisson with log and Binomial with logit. Only those can use linear_solver="cholesky", and only with a fixed sp. Gaussian identity keeps fit_streamed_pirls under "qr" too; Poisson log and Binomial logit with "qr" go to the regular controller. A family's coefficient_system is "fisher" for canonical links and "observed" otherwise (ExponentialFamily.execution_capabilities). For an unknown-scale family with a fixed sp (Gamma, non-identity Gaussian), _fit_stream_fixed_regular runs optimize_regular_stream_reml with pin_lambda=True, so the log scale is still optimized; a fixed-sp NB with estimated theta likewise runs optimize_nb_stream_reml with pin_lambda=True.

docs.title: Scanning, lineage and fingerprints
docs.text:
_source_batches in jaxgam/execution/stream/pirls.py is the one replay loop most drivers share. Before the scan it validates the FamilyExecutionLineage and compares source.fingerprint() with the fingerprint recorded at preparation; for each batch it re-validates the lineage, requires a response, rejects padded rows (valid all true) with NotImplementedError, and requires finite y, weights and offset and nonnegative weights (ValueError); after the scan it checks the fingerprint again and that the number of valid rows equals prepared.n_obs (RuntimeError otherwise). _fitting_batches adds the fitting-coordinate design of each batch and rejects non-finite design values.

FamilyExecutionLineage.validate (jaxgam/fitting/family_execution.py) fails closed when the source or basis fingerprint, the family or link name, the family's static configuration or its parameter snapshot changed since preparation. It runs before every cached device dispatch because a compiled executable can be reused without retracing, so trace-time checks alone would not see a mutation.

single_fit_fingerprints() (jaxgam/data/source.py) makes those repeated fingerprint calls cheap: inside the scope each in-memory source is hashed once, and once more when the scope ends, which raises RuntimeError("RowSource changed during the fit") if the data changed.

docs.title: Fixed-smoothing PIRLS: fit_streamed_pirls
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant Drv as fit_streamed_pirls
    participant Scan as _working_factor_scan
    participant Src as RowSource.scan
    participant Kern as stream_kernels batch kernels
    participant Solve as solve_penalized_system or solve_augmented_qr
    participant Trial as _trial_scan
    Drv->>Drv: _preflight checks lineage, rank and family policy
    loop each PIRLS iteration, at most max_iter
        Drv->>Scan: beta, rho
        loop each batch
            Scan->>Src: next RowBatch
            Src-->>Scan: columns, y, weight, offset
            Scan->>Kern: accumulate_working_statistics or positive_qr_working_rows
            Kern-->>Scan: G, b, deviance, domain flag
        end
        Scan->>Solve: summed statistics or merged QR state
        Solve-->>Drv: proposal and coefficient factor
        loop step halving, at most max_halvings
            Drv->>Trial: candidate beta
            Trial->>Kern: trial_deviance per batch
            Kern-->>Trial: deviance, domain flag
            Trial-->>Drv: summed deviance
            Drv->>Drv: accepts_trial
        end
        Drv->>Drv: convergence test from iteration index 3
    end
    Drv->>Scan: final working scan at accepted beta
    Drv->>Drv: EDF, execution summary scan, saturated likelihood scan
    Drv-->>Drv: StreamFitState

Each inner loop box is one full replay of the source. One iteration is one working scan plus at least one trial scan; the final state costs a further working scan, an execution-summary scan and a saturated-likelihood scan.

Details:

  • Systems. With solver_policy="cholesky", accumulate_working_statistics sums G = X'WX, b = X'Wz, the deviance and a domain flag, and solve_penalized_system factors G + S_lambda with a plain Cholesky. A non-finite factor or proposal raises LinAlgError: no jitter is ever added. With "qr", positive_qr_working_rows returns the weighted rows of each batch, qr_update merges them into a PositiveQRState, and solve_augmented_qr attaches the rho-scaled penalty roots (built once per fit by _qr_roots).
  • Acceptance. accepts_trial applies the dense rule accepted_penalized_step: finite, inside the family domain, and no more than 1e-7 |pdev| above the current penalized deviance (any valid trial on the first iteration). Up to 25 halvings toward the current coefficients; if none is accepted the loop stops with line_search_failed.
  • Convergence. From iteration index 3, when the relative coefficient and penalized-deviance changes are below tol (default 1e-7), a working scan at the accepted coefficients computes the normal-equation residual coefficient_stationarity; the fit is converged when it is below tol.
  • Final state. EDF is estimate_edf (Cholesky) or _qr_data_edf (QR, from the data factor, without forming G H^-1). The family's reduction policy gives the reported scale (1, or Gaussian deviance over n - edf) and the score scale (for Gaussian fixed sp, penalized deviance over the positive-weight count minus the penalty null dimension).

The public route sets only batch_rows and solver_policy of StreamPIRLSControl; max_iter=100, tol=1e-7 and max_halvings=25 are not reachable from FitControl.

docs.title: Fixed-smoothing PIRLS: the regular and NB controllers
docs.text:
fit_regular_streamed_pirls (jaxgam/execution/stream/regular.py) ports the gam.fit3 coefficient loop (R/gam.fit3.r) as the dense efs_regular_pirls_loop does, but by replay:

  • Start. A null anchor from project_null_coefficients (or an explicit null_coefficients), and a start from select_initial_working_state_cpu, which replays the source with up to 20 0.9/0.1 shrinks toward the null predictor until every row is valid.
  • Working scan. regular_working_scan replays one predictor and builds, per batch, the Fisher system into a PositiveQRState and, for an observed coefficient system, the signed Newton system into a SignedQRState (signed_qr_update). Rows outside gam.fit3's good set (zero weight or zero mu.eta) are dropped before the QR.
  • Proposal. solve_signed_qr applies pls_fit1's correction. If the signed system is indefinite (fisher_required), the same step is re-solved on the Fisher system, R's step-local Fisher retry, counted in fisher_recoveries.
  • Step control. A candidate is accepted when it is in the domain, finite, and its penalized deviance exceeds the old value by at most 10 (0.1 + |old pdev|) sqrt(eps); otherwise it is halved toward the current coefficients, at most max_halvings times.
  • Convergence. gam.fit3's test: penalized-deviance change below tol (|phi| + |pdev|) and max|2 residual| within tol (|pdev| + |phi|); Gaussian identity (single_step_pirls) converges at its first accepted step.
  • Final solve. As in gam.fit3's closing gdi1 call, one more scan forms the final systems and a last solve gives the reported coefficients, falling back to the accepted ones if that candidate leaves the domain. RegularSourceScore keeps the raw deviance, the solve penalty and the incoming and reported scales apart.

fit_nb_streamed_pirls (jaxgam/execution/stream/nb.py) ports gam.fit4 (R/gam.fit4.r): observed weights from the NB kernels, a signed QR solve, and when that is indefinite a re-scan with positive observed weights (nb_positive_observed_retry, counted in positive_observed_recoveries). When a retained start or estimated theta is present, recovery follows gam.fit4's order: non-finite deviance, then domain, then divergence (at most 100 halvings, toward the null coefficients on the first iteration). With estimate_theta=True it calls conditional_theta_stream after every accepted coefficient step (see Streamed NB theta).

Both controllers require solver_policy="qr", never modify the caller's family object, and run their own workspace preflight before any scan.

docs.title: The QR reductions
docs.text:
• Positive QR (jaxgam/execution/qr.py). qr_update stacks the previous triangular factor on a new block of nonnegative-weight rows and re-factors with column pivoting; the state keeps R, Q'z, the residual tail and the pivots, never the rows. solve_augmented_qr appends the actual (lambda-scaled) penalty roots and solves. The structural rank is decided on balanced_roots, the unscaled roots, so a tiny smoothing parameter cannot hide an identifiable direction; a deficient balanced system needs an explicit identifiable_subspace, while an ill-conditioned actual factor raises. _mgcv_r_cond and structural_rank follow pls_fit1's condition test.
  • Signed QR (jaxgam/execution/stream/signed_qr.py). For a system with some negative weights, SignedQRState holds a QR of the absolute-weight rows, a QR of the negative-weight rows and the right side X'Wz. solve_signed_qr follows pls_fit1: factor the absolute system with the penalty roots, take the SVD of the negative rows in that basis, and correct by I - 2 Q_neg' Q_neg. A correction eigenvalue below -100 eps returns fisher_required=True; zero eigenvalues are treated as pseudoinverse modes and make the result not score_admissible.

Which solver runs follows from the chart above: Cholesky only for fit_streamed_pirls under "cholesky"; positive QR for fit_streamed_pirls under "qr" and for Fisher (canonical) systems in the regular controller; signed QR for observed (non-canonical) regular systems and for NB.

docs.title: Exact streamed REML
docs.text:
With sp=None and the default Newton optimizer, _fit_stream_exact_reml optimizes the REML criterion over [log_lambda, <log_phi>] (regular families) or [log_lambda, <log_theta>] (NB with estimated theta) by SciPy L-BFGS-B with exact gradients. It is not the dense Newton loop.

Start. With penalties, prepare_stream_reml_start replays the source twice: once for the null coefficients (get.null.coef) and once for the weighted diagonal of mgcv's initial.spg. The log scale starts at the startup's score_phi, theta at the family's theta. A model with no penalty, no free scale and no theta is fitted once by the fixed-sp helpers and labelled exact_reml_no_parameters.

One trial. evaluate_regular_stream_reml computes the score and gradient at one exact parameter vector:

  1. fit_regular_streamed_pirls reconverges the coefficients from the accepted trial's coefficients (several scans). A non-converged or invalid inner fit raises RuntimeError; it is never scored.
  2. Coefficient-space work: the observed and source factors give H^-1, both are checked against the observed Hessian (residual below 1e-7), and regular_score_cotangents evaluates the score and the cotangents of its coefficient-space terms.
  3. One more replay: regular_batch_statistics_vjp per batch gives that batch's contribution to the coefficient cotangent and to the log-scale derivative.
  4. The adjoint H^-1 beta_bar (checked again) and penalty_ops.parameter_vjp give the gradient in log_lambda, the implicit-function-theorem derivative through the converged coefficients.

So one trial costs the PIRLS scans plus one derivative scan, and keeps only coefficient-sized arrays. evaluate_nb_stream_reml does the same with nb_batch_statistics_vjp and theta as an explicit coordinate.

The optimizer. optimize_regular_stream_reml and optimize_nb_stream_reml share _run_parameterized_stream_reml.

flowchart TD
    A["optimize_regular_stream_reml or optimize_nb_stream_reml"] --> B["clip free log_lambda to -40..40<br/>tighten inner tolerance"]
    B --> C{"retained optimizer workspace below budget?"}
    C -- no --> M1["MemoryError"]
    C -- yes --> D["_AcceptedParameterizedTrialObjective<br/>evaluate the initial trial"]
    D --> E["open a window: bounds within max_step = 5 of the accepted point"]
    E --> F["SciPy minimize, method L-BFGS-B<br/>each new point is one reconverged exact trial<br/>callback promotes the accepted candidate"]
    F --> G{"window stopped at its own edge or local gtol<br/>while the global projected gradient exceeds gtol?"}
    G -- "yes, fewer than 20 windows" --> E
    G -- "yes, 20 windows" --> WL["message: window limit reached"]
    G -- no --> H{"L-BFGS-B success and projected gradient <= gtol?"}
    WL --> H
    H -- yes --> OK["converged"]
    H -- no --> I{"roundoff stop: relative reduction or ABNORMAL?"}
    I -- no --> NC["not converged, SciPy message kept"]
    I -- yes --> J{"which completion?"}
    J -- "only log scale or log theta free" --> K["_complete_pinned_regular_scale or _complete_pinned_nb_theta"]
    J -- "1 to 4 free coordinates incl. a free log_lambda" --> L["_complete_free_curvature_newton<br/>newton steps on finite-difference curvature"]
    J -- neither --> P
    K --> P["_classify_function_reduction<br/>mgcv newton relative test"]
    L --> P
    P --> R["converged flag and message on the accepted trial"]

Read from the top. Windows cap each move at the scale of fast.REML.fit's maxNstep=5 (an mgcv routine in R/fast-REML.r); each window is a fresh L-BFGS-B run with its own max_iter and maxfun, at most MAX_SOURCE_STEP_WINDOWS = 20 of them. After a roundoff stop, one completion may continue the search by mgcv's newton rules (R/gam.fit3.r): steps of -H^-1 g capped at 5, accepted on decrease with quadratic-model error below 0.8, at most three halvings, converged only with a positive-definite curvature model. The free-coordinate completion builds that curvature from 2m reconverged central-difference gradient probes, so it is limited to four free coordinates. Finally _classify_function_reduction turns an L-BFGS-B relative-reduction exit into convergence only if mgcv's own newton test holds: projected gradient at most 5 * 1e-6 * score.scale and score change at most 1e-6 * score.scale (mgcv_relative_convergence).

Settings: StreamREMLControl defaults are max_iter=100, maxfun=500, maxcor=10, maxls=20, gtol=1e-6, ftol=1e-12, history_size=32. The public route passes ftol=0 for regular families and gtol=1e-9, ftol=0 for NB, and max_step=5.0. Log smoothing parameters are bounded to [-40, 40]; log scale and log theta are unbounded; pinned coordinates are fixed bounds.

What it reports. converged and convergence_info (the SciPy message with the window count and any completion or relative-test note) come from the optimizer; there is no warning. exact_optimizer_diagnostics is a StreamExactOptimizerDiagnostics (jaxgam/results.py): L-BFGS-B status, evaluation and acceptance counts, projected_gradient_inf, the bounded accepted score history, startup scans and cumulative inner iterations.

The objective keeps at most two trials alive, the accepted one and the current candidate (_AcceptedParameterizedTrialObjective), and never an outer Hessian or a list of trial points.

evaluate_stream_reml and optimize_stream_reml in the same module are an earlier canonical Poisson/Binomial-only version; nothing in jaxgam/ outside jaxgam/execution/stream/reml.py calls them, only tests.

docs.title: Streamed NB theta
docs.text:
Theta is handled two ways on this route:

  • Exact REML and pinned fixed sp. log_theta is a joint L-BFGS-B coordinate in optimize_nb_stream_reml; each trial fits coefficients at that theta with fit_nb_streamed_pirls(estimate_theta=False). The selected theta is written into the family with put_theta by _fit_stream_exact_reml and _fit_stream_fixed_nb.
  • EFS. fit_nb_streamed_pirls(estimate_theta=True) calls conditional_theta_stream (jaxgam/execution/stream/nb_theta.py) after every accepted coefficient step. It runs the one-parameter Newton of mgcv's estimate.theta (as gam.fit4 does under EFS) at fixed coefficients; every objective and derivative evaluation is a replay that sums nb_conditional_theta_batch over batches, and nb_conditional_theta_step takes the step. NBThetaStreamControl sets tolerance 1e-7, 100 iterations, step at most 4 and 25 halvings. A failed solve keeps its last valid theta with a non-zero status.

With optimizer="efs" and no penalties, the parametric bypass fits with estimate_theta=False, so theta keeps its start value and is not reported.

docs.title: Streamed Fellner-Schall
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A["_fit_stream_routes, optimizer efs, sp None"] --> B{"any penalty?"}
    B -- no --> BY["_fit_stream_parametric_bypass<br/>stream_parametric_qr"]
    B -- yes --> C["fit_streamed_efs"]
    C --> D{"startup and provider bounds within memory_budget_bytes?"}
    D -- no --> M["MemoryError"]
    D -- yes --> E["NBStreamEFSProvider.create or RegularStreamEFSProvider.create<br/>frozen family copy, PreparedFittingMetadata, prepare_efs_statistics"]
    E --> F["prepare_stream_efs_start<br/>two replays: get.null.coef and initial.spg"]
    F --> G["initial_request<br/>log_lambda + 2.5, null coefficients, incoming scale"]
    G --> H["_run_efs_known_scale or _run_efs_unknown_scale<br/>the dense EFS controller"]
    H --> I["provider call for one trial"]
    I --> J["fit_regular_streamed_pirls<br/>or fit_nb_streamed_pirls with conditional theta"]
    J --> K["attribution checks, efs_factor_statistics, scalar score"]
    K --> L["EFSFitState"]
    L --> H
    H --> N["StreamEFSExecution<br/>fit, metadata, reporting family copy, startup"]
    N --> O["GAMPredictionResult, stream_efs_qr"]

Read from the top; the loop between the controller and the provider is the dense EFS outer iteration of the dense page, unchanged. Only the provider differs:

  • _provider_parts freezes a deep copy of the family, builds PreparedFittingMetadata and the EFS statistics plan, and records an EFSControllerContext with reference_profile="mgcv-1.9-3-efsudr-streamed", trace_method="exact-streamed-fisher" and the source and basis fingerprints.
  • Each call re-validates lineage and fingerprint before and after the fit, runs the coefficient controller with EFSControl.pirls_max_iter and pirls_tolerance, and checks that the returned state belongs to the request (rho, scale, and for NB the theta transition history); a mismatch raises RuntimeError.
  • Statistics come from efs_factor_statistics (jaxgam/fitting/stream/efs_factor.py), which computes the same d, t and q as the dense efs_statistics but through the fit's fisher_coefficient_factor actions, because a streamed fit has a QR factor, not a dense Cholesky.
  • The regular provider scores with reml_criterion_from_penalized_deviance at the incoming scale and returns the fit's Fletcher scale as update_phi; the NB provider uses the score the NB controller computed, at scale 1.
  • The recovery anchor is the zero vector on every refit (regular: source_null_coefficients; NB: beta_old_init), as mgcv's EFS dispatch does not pass G$null.coef on.

Supported families: Gaussian, Binomial, Poisson and Gamma with no theta, and NB with log, identity or sqrt link (_check_stream_efs_family).

docs.title: Streamed Gaussian QR
docs.text: An eligible gaussian_compression=True request (exact Gaussian with identity link, Newton or fixed sp, prior weights within [1e-10, 1e10], at least one penalty, no rank deficit) builds a StreamGaussianQROuterProvider with build_stream_gaussian_qr_provider. prepare_streamed_frozen_gaussian_qr replays the source once into the frozen QR; every smoothing trial then uses coefficient-size arrays, as on the dense Gaussian QR route, with Newton up to 50 penalties and L-BFGS-B above. Either solver setting is accepted. An over-budget QR workspace (preflight_streamed_gaussian_qr_workspace) raises MemoryError and does not fall back; an ineligible request records execution_fallback_reason and takes the ordinary route, except that with sp=None, Newton and "cholesky" there is no ordinary route, and the fit raises NotImplementedError.

docs.title: Observation-independent state
docs.text:
StreamFitState (jaxgam/fitting/state.py) is everything a streamed fit returns: coefficients, log_lambda, deviance, penalized deviance, reported and score scales, saturated log-likelihood, EDF, xtwx and xtwx_fisher, the coefficient and Fisher coefficient factors, iteration and line-search diagnostics, stationarity, and the scan counts. It has no fitted values, working weights or responses; those stay in the RowSource and are recomputed by a later scan when needed (test_stream_fit_state_contains_no_observation_aligned_fields).

A factor is one of three classes with the same action interface (root_inverse, root_transpose_inverse, hessian_inverse, logdet_hessian): CholeskyCoefficientFactor (H = B' B, B = lower'), PivotedQRCoefficientFactor (rank-aware, B = R P' embedded by keep), and SignedQRCoefficientFactor (an absolute QR factor plus the signed correction; logdet_hessian is minus infinity unless score_admissible). Phase 3 uses these actions for standard errors, so a QR factor never has to be turned into a lower-triangular matrix. The legacy properties factor and fisher_factor raise for QR factors.

docs.title: Scan and batch accounting
docs.text:
source_scans and batches_scanned on the result never include the prepare_model setup scans. Otherwise they mean:

  • fit_streamed_pirls, fixed regular and fixed NB fits: the controller's total, including the final summary and likelihood scans;
  • fixed sp with an optimized scale or theta: the optimizer's cumulative count over all trials;
  • exact REML: startup scans plus the optimizer's cumulative count;
  • Gaussian QR: the provider's single replay;
  • streamed EFS: the final accepted fit only. The totals are in optimizer_diagnostics.provider_source_scans and startup_source_scans.

known_workspace_bytes is the preflight value, the controller or optimizer ledger, the exact-REML startup/trial maximum, or the Gaussian QR estimate; it is None on the EFS route and the parametric bypass.

docs.title: Memory preflights and errors
docs.text:
Every streamed driver estimates the arrays it knows it will hold and raises the built-in MemoryError before scanning when the estimate exceeds FitControl.memory_budget_bytes. These are prospective ledgers, not allocator limits: source storage and native LAPACK, BLAS or XLA scratch are excluded (see the RegularStreamWorkspace docstring).

Check Where Charges fixed and exact routes _preflight_stream_workspace (jaxgam/api.py) 12 p^2 (Cholesky) or 14 p^2 (QR) float64 plus batch buffers for the requested batch_rows regular and NB controllers preflight_regular_stream_workspace batch design buffers, coefficient matrices, QR states, histories exact REML optimizer optimize_regular_stream_reml, optimize_nb_stream_reml retained trials, history, L-BFGS-B work, curvature completion exact REML startup _fit_stream_exact_reml startup workspace plus retained start vectors streamed EFS fit_streamed_efs, _provider_parts startup retention, provider metadata, prior fits, trace blocks, histories, conditional theta Gaussian QR preflight_streamed_gaussian_qr_workspace QR design, compression, score derivatives, outer Hessian or L-BFGS-B work

_preflight_stream_workspace charges the requested batch_rows, not the number of rows in the source, so a model with many coefficients can be rejected on a small source until batch_rows is lowered.

Other failures raise rather than return a non-converged result: unpenalized rank deficiency (LinAlgError in _preflight and the EFS provider), a non-finite Cholesky factor or proposal (LinAlgError), current coefficients outside the family domain (ValueError), a non-finite final state (FloatingPointError), a changed source or lineage (RuntimeError), padded batches (NotImplementedError), and, under exact REML and the pinned scale/theta optimizers, any inner fit that does not converge (RuntimeError). A fixed-sp PIRLS that runs out of iterations or halvings returns converged=False with convergence_info "fixed sp streamed PIRLS did not converge".

docs.title: Rules and invariants
docs.text:
• No row-aligned state. Nothing that outlives a scan may be observation sized: not the design, not eta, mu or working weights, not a count-prefix table. Ledgers and tests check this (tests/test_execution/test_stream.py test_stream_fit_state_contains_no_observation_aligned_fields, test_qr_retained_fit_state_is_coefficient_sized_as_source_grows).
  • Kernels see one batch. Batch kernels in jaxgam/fitting/ take one materialized batch and return coefficient-sized values; source iteration stays in jaxgam/execution/ so no reverse-mode trace can capture source rows (module docstring of jaxgam/fitting/stream/reml.py).
  • Validate before every dispatch. Call FamilyExecutionLineage.validate before each jitted call and compare fingerprints before and after each scan (test_scanner_rejects_runtime_source_basis_and_family_mutation, tests/test_execution/test_stream_api.py test_streamed_fit_raises_when_its_source_changes_during_the_fit).
  • No hidden jitter. The streamed Cholesky and QR solves never regularize; a failure raises (test_final_cholesky_offdiagonal_nonfinite_is_rejected).
  • A failed line search is not convergence (test_failed_line_search_is_not_convergence); an iteration-limited exact optimizer is not converged (tests/test_execution/test_regular_reml.py test_regular_stream_reml_optimizer_all_32_cells_report_iteration_limit); neither is an EFS outer limit (tests/test_execution/test_efs_stream.py test_outer_iteration_limit_is_not_reported_as_convergence).
  • Exact gradients are exact. The regular adjoint gradient is compared with pinned mgcv derivatives and with refitted finite differences for all 32 family/link cells (test_regular_source_gradient_matches_all_32_pinned_gdi_cells, test_regular_source_gradient_matches_all_32_refitted_finite_differences).
  • Windows reopen only from accepted trials (test_regular_stream_reml_step_windows_reopen_from_exact_accepted_trial, test_regular_stream_reml_window_cap_stops_truthfully).
  • Results do not depend on batching. Fixed-sp fits are invariant to batch_rows and to the setup partition (test_public_fixed_sp_stream_fit_is_invariant_to_fit_control_batch_rows, test_public_stream_fits_are_invariant_to_setup_partition).
  • Scan counts are real. Reported counts match the source's actual scan calls (test_qr_source_scan_accounting_matches_replayed_source_calls).
  • R parity for the streamed family and link inventory is in tests/test_validation_matrix.py (for example test_public_streamed_efs_regular_family_link_inventory).

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Default solver. FitControl(execution="stream") defaults to linear_solver="cholesky", which supports only fixed sp and only the three canonical families above. Estimating smoothing parameters needs linear_solver="qr" (or an eligible Gaussian QR request).
  • "newton" means L-BFGS-B here. The default optimizer on this route is L-BFGS-B with exact gradients and mgcv newton completions; only streamed Gaussian QR with at most 50 penalties runs the dense NewtonOptimizer.
  • A fixed sp can still optimize. Gamma, non-identity Gaussian and estimated-theta NB optimize the scale or theta with lambda pinned; lambda_strategy stays "fixed" and convergence_info is an optimizer message.
  • EFS scan counts. The result's source_scans on the EFS route covers only the final fit; use optimizer_diagnostics for the cost of the whole fit.
  • Preflight uses batch_rows. A large p with the default batch_rows=65_536 can exceed the budget on any source size.
  • Inner failures raise under exact REML. Code that wraps the optimizer must expect RuntimeError, not a converged=False result.
  • Padding. Kernels can mask padded rows, but the host rejects padded batches; a source must return only real rows.
  • Stale docstrings. Some module docstrings in jaxgam/execution/ still say their code "does not enable public streaming" or is internal until a later PR (jaxgam/execution/stream/pirls.py, jaxgam/execution/stream/nb.py, jaxgam/execution/stream/regular.py); the routes are public through FitControl.

docs.title: Where to change things
docs.text:
• To add a family to the streamed fixed-sp route, give it the execution capabilities and stream_reduction_policy that _check_stream_fixed_family requires (see extension points); no driver dispatches on family names except the NB checks.
  • To change fixed-sp step control, edit fit_streamed_pirls (jaxgam/execution/stream/pirls.py), fit_regular_streamed_pirls or fit_nb_streamed_pirls; the per-batch arithmetic lives in jaxgam/fitting/stream/kernels.py, jaxgam/fitting/stream/regular.py and jaxgam/fitting/stream/nb_kernels.py.
  • To change how a block of rows enters a QR, edit qr_update or signed_qr_update; to change rank or indefiniteness decisions, edit solve_augmented_qr and solve_signed_qr.
  • To change the exact REML gradient, edit evaluate_regular_stream_reml and the kernels in jaxgam/fitting/stream/reml.py (or evaluate_nb_stream_reml and jaxgam/fitting/stream/nb_reml.py).
  • To change optimizer limits or windows, edit StreamREMLControl, MAX_SOURCE_STEP_WINDOWS and _run_parameterized_stream_reml; the values the public route passes are set in _fit_stream_exact_reml, _fit_stream_fixed_regular and _fit_stream_fixed_nb (jaxgam/api.py).
  • To change streamed EFS, edit the providers in jaxgam/execution/stream/efs_provider.py; the outer policy is shared with the dense route in jaxgam/execution/efs.py.
  • To change a memory estimate, edit the ledger that owns it (table above) and its test in tests/test_execution/.

A proposed refactor would replace the near-duplicate scans and per-route controllers with shared ones; see the unified fitting design.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: This page collects the numerical and platform decisions that cut across the package: what import jaxgam configures, which linear-algebra library serves which call, the pinned LAPACK provider that reproduces mgcv's arithmetic for selected routines, the scalar kernels that reproduce mgcv's compiled C loops, the Apple Accelerate guard, thread pinning and determinism, environment variables, device handling, and the rules for JAX and NumPy-only code.

docs.title: Where the code is
docs.text: Path Role jaxgam/__init__.py Enables float64, configures the persistent compilation cache, runs the Accelerate warning, exports the public names. jaxgam/platform_guard.py warn_if_accelerate_lapack and accelerate_warning_applies: the Apple silicon Accelerate warning. jaxgam/smooths/source_lapack.py The pinned LAPACK provider: loads scipy-openblas32==0.3.26.0.4 with ctypes, pins it to one thread, and exposes source-exact ports of mgcv's LAPACK and BLAS calls. Also the NumPy/SciPy Accelerate probes. jaxgam/smooths/source_penalty_coordinates.py Penalty coordinates in pinned mgcv's gauge: R's colMeans centering reflector, qr.qty absorption, and lower-triangle DSYEVR eigensolves on the provider. jaxgam/smooths/source_arithmetic.py Numba kernels that keep mgcv's C loop order and fused multiply-add rounding, and element-wise calls to the C library's exp, log, log10 and pow. jaxgam/jax_utils.py NumPy/JAX array dispatch, the Phase 1 to 2 and Phase 2 to 3 transfers, and JIT-compiled linear-algebra helpers. jaxgam/smooths/cubic.py, jaxgam/smooths/utils.py, jaxgam/summary/_davies.py The other Numba users. jaxgam/api.py _resolve_device, which maps device= to a JAX device.

docs.title: What import jaxgam does
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A["import jaxgam"] --> B["import jax"]
    B --> C["__version__ from installed metadata<br/>or 0+unknown"]
    C --> D["jax.config.update jax_enable_x64 True"]
    D --> E{"JAXGAM_NO_COMPILATION_CACHE<br/>non-empty?"}
    E -->|"yes"| H["no cache configuration by jaxgam"]
    E -->|"no"| F{"JAX_COMPILATION_CACHE_DIR set?"}
    F -->|"no"| G["jax_compilation_cache_dir set to<br/>home/.cache/jaxgam/jax"]
    F -->|"yes"| G2["directory left to JAX, which reads the variable"]
    G --> K["jax_persistent_cache_min_compile_time_secs set to 0"]
    G2 --> K
    H --> W["warn_if_accelerate_lapack"]
    K --> W
    W --> X["import GAM, controls, results, GAMPredictor"]

Read top to bottom: float64 is enabled before any other jaxgam module is imported, so no module-level compilation runs in float32. The Accelerate check runs once, after the JAX configuration and before the public classes are imported. Importing jaxgam loads jaxgam.fitting but not jaxgam.execution, and does not load the pinned provider.

Float64. jax_enable_x64 is set to True in jaxgam/__init__.py. Four fitting modules (jaxgam/fitting/discrete/working_model.py, jaxgam/fitting/stream/efs_factor.py, jaxgam/fitting/discrete/working.py, jaxgam/fitting/stream/nb_theta.py) set it again at import.

Persistent compilation cache. By default compiled XLA executables are cached in ~/.cache/jaxgam/jax, and the minimum compile time for caching is set to 0 seconds so that small programs are cached too. Importing jaxgam already writes entries to the cache. The behaviour is controlled only by environment variables read at import:

  • Redirect: set JAX_COMPILATION_CACHE_DIR before importing jaxgam. jaxgam then sets no directory (JAX reads the variable itself) but still sets the threshold to 0.
  • Disable jaxgam's configuration: set JAXGAM_NO_COMPILATION_CACHE to any non-empty value, including 0; the test is truthiness of the string. If JAX_COMPILATION_CACHE_DIR is also set, JAX still caches there with its own default threshold (1 second in the installed JAX).
  • Not a redirect: a jax.config.update("jax_compilation_cache_dir", ...) made before import jaxgam is overwritten by the default; one made after the import changes the setting but, in a check with jax 0.9.0.1, entries were not written to the new directory, because the import had already initialized the cache.

docs.title: The Accelerate guard
docs.text:
jaxgam/platform_guard.py explains the problem in its module docstring: on Apple silicon the default NumPy and SciPy wheels link Apple Accelerate, and JAX's CPU LAPACK kernels take their function pointers from SciPy. When several LAPACK calls run concurrently inside one compiled computation, the process heap can be corrupted, and no JAX or XLA setting prevents it; the OpenBLAS builds of NumPy and SciPy do. The warning text says this was observed with about 100 smooths (about 1,000 coefficients) and not with 50 or fewer, that Linux is unaffected, and gives uv and pip commands that reinstall the OpenBLAS builds of the installed NumPy and SciPy versions.

accelerate_warning_applies() returns true only when all of these hold, in this order:

  1. os.environ.get("JAXGAM_ALLOW_ACCELERATE") != "1" (exactly the string 1 silences it; 0 or true do not);
  2. sys.platform == "darwin" and platform.machine() == "arm64";
  3. accelerate_lapack_in_process() in jaxgam/smooths/source_lapack.py: NumPy's or SciPy's build configuration names accelerate as its LAPACK;
  4. jax.default_backend() == "cpu". The backend is queried only after the first three hold, so elsewhere importing jaxgam never initializes a JAX backend.

warn_if_accelerate_lapack() issues a RuntimeWarning at most once per process. tests/test_platform_guard.py covers each condition, the once-only behaviour and the opt-out value.

docs.title: Which library serves which call
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    subgraph P1["Phase 1 setup and Phase 3, NumPy"]
        NS["numpy.linalg and scipy.linalg calls"]
        SL["source_lapack.py routines"]
        SA["source_arithmetic.py kernels"]
    end
    subgraph P2["Phase 2 fit"]
        JK["fitting/ kernels<br/>jnp.linalg and jax.scipy.linalg"]
        HC["host calls between compiled steps<br/>stable_reparam, factor_working_model"]
    end
    NS --> VB["BLAS and LAPACK vendored by NumPy and SciPy<br/>OpenBLAS, or Accelerate on default macOS wheels"]
    JK --> XK["JAX CPU LAPACK kernels"]
    XK -->|"function pointers from SciPy"| VB
    SL --> PW["scipy-openblas32 0.3.26.0.4<br/>loaded RTLD_LOCAL, one thread"]
    HC --> PW
    SA --> LM["C libm through ctypes pointers<br/>and Numba loops with explicit FMA"]
    SL -.->|"SciPy built on Accelerate:<br/>selected eigensolves"| VB

Ordinary setup and post-estimation linear algebra goes to whatever NumPy and SciPy vendor. Kernels in the fit go to JAX's CPU LAPACK kernels, which share SciPy's LAPACK. Only the routines listed below go to the pinned provider, both when called from setup and when the fit calls them on the host. The dashed edge is the Accelerate exception described further down.

docs.title: The pinned LAPACK provider
docs.text:
Why it exists. Several smooth constructors are sensitive to exactly which null-space coordinates and eigenvector gauge their LAPACK returns: the cubic shrinkage penalty, the thin-plate and Gaussian-process Lanczos bases, tensor-margin factorizations, and penalty coordinates in rank-deficient fits. Small differences there cascade into different bases and coefficients. jaxgam/smooths/source_lapack.py therefore binds the needed LAPACKE and CBLAS entry points from one declared package, scipy-openblas32==0.3.26.0.4 (OpenBLAS 0.3.26, LP64), because that is the OpenBLAS release the pinned Linux R 4.5.2 links. The wheel is an unconditional runtime dependency in pyproject.toml. The module never searches for R or a system BLAS and does not replace NumPy's or SciPy's backend.

Locating, loading and verifying. _source_lapack() is cached with functools.lru_cache(maxsize=1) and runs on first use, not at import. It calls _declared_provider, which:

  1. checks importlib.metadata.version("scipy-openblas32") equals _PROVIDER_VERSION (0.3.26.0.4), else RuntimeError;
  2. finds the package with importlib.util.find_spec (without running the wheel's __init__, which would load OpenBLAS with RTLD_GLOBAL) and resolves lib/libscipy_openblas.dylib on macOS, lib/libscipy_openblas.so on Linux, or the single DLL on Windows (_provider_library_path);
  3. opens it with ctypes.CDLL(path, ctypes.RTLD_LOCAL), so its symbols do not leak into the process namespace;
  4. reads scipy_openblas_get_config and requires the prefix "OpenBLAS 0.3.26 " and the LP64 ABI (no USE64BITINT);
  5. pins the thread count with _pin_single_thread.

_source_lapack then binds 13 symbols with explicit argtypes and restype and returns a frozen _SourceLapack.

One thread. The wheel is a threaded OpenBLAS whose default thread count follows OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS or the core count, and threaded reductions change last-bit results. _pin_single_thread calls scipy_openblas_set_num_threads(1) once at load and checks scipy_openblas_get_num_threads() == 1, so every provider result is the single-thread arithmetic validated against pinned R, whatever the caller's environment. The setting is local to this library: NumPy's and SciPy's thread counts are unchanged.

sequenceDiagram
    participant S as CubicShrinkageSmooth
    participant F as cubic_shrinkage_penalty
    participant L as _source_lapack
    participant D as _declared_provider
    participant W as libscipy_openblas
    S->>F: _apply_shrinkage calls it with S and shrink
    F->>F: _check_input_shape and cubic_shrinkage_workspace_bound
    F->>L: get the provider
    alt first call in the process
        L->>D: declared package scipy-openblas32
        D->>D: metadata version is 0.3.26.0.4
        D->>D: _provider_library_path with find_spec
        D->>W: ctypes.CDLL with RTLD_LOCAL
        D->>W: scipy_openblas_get_config
        W-->>D: OpenBLAS 0.3.26 prefix, LP64
        D->>W: _pin_single_thread sets and checks one thread
        D-->>L: _DeclaredProvider and the CDLL
        L->>L: bind LAPACKE and CBLAS symbols
    end
    L-->>F: cached _SourceLapack
    F->>W: dsyevr_work workspace query with lwork -1
    F->>F: _query_length caps lwork and liwork
    F->>W: dsyevr_work
    W-->>F: ascending eigenpairs
    F->>F: reverse to descending, shrink the two null values
    F->>W: dgemm
    F-->>S: shrunk penalty

The load block runs once per process; later calls go straight to the cached _SourceLapack. Every routine follows the same pattern: validate shapes and finiteness, check a workspace bound before allocating, query LAPACK workspace, then call.

Routines and callers.

Function Routines mgcv source it reproduces Package callers cubic_shrinkage_penalty DSYEVR, DGEMM the cs eigentransform in smooth.construct.cs.smooth.spec (R/smooth.r) CubicShrinkageSmooth in jaxgam/smooths/cubic.py (setup) natural_cubic_system_solve DPTSV getFS (src/mgcv.c) CubicRegressionSmooth._compute_natural_f_and_penalty (setup) source_lanczos (with source_trisymeig) DSYMV, DDOT, DAXPY, DSTEDC Rlanczos and mgcv_trisymeig (src/mat.c), called by slanczos _source_tprs_knot_basis in jaxgam/smooths/tprs.py, GaussianProcessSmooth.setup, jaxgam/formula/operator/radial.py (setup) source_project_rows DGEMV per row predict_tprs (src/tprs.c) TPRSSmooth._project_design_rows (setup and prediction) source_r_matprod, source_matprod DGEMV or DGEMM R's %*% GaussianProcessSmooth._build_design; tensor margins in jaxgam/smooths/tensor.py source_svd DGESDD R's svd tensor-margin reparameterization in jaxgam/smooths/tensor.py SourceConstraintQR DNRM2, DSCAL, DDOT, DAXPY qr(t(C)) and qr.qty for one constraint column tensor margins; jaxgam/formula/operator/modest.py source_pivoted_qr DGEQP3 mgcv_qr as used by gdiPK (src/gdi.c) jaxgam/formula/rank_coordinates.py, whose map builders are called only from tests source_pivoted_cholesky DPSTRF R's chol(pivot=TRUE) in Sl.fitChol (R/fast-REML.r) factor_working_model in jaxgam/execution/discrete/working_model.py (during the discretized fit) _source_symmetric_eigen, source_symmetric_eigh, source_symmetric_max_eigenvalue (in jaxgam/smooths/source_penalty_coordinates.py) DSYEVR R's eigen on penalties stable_reparam in jaxgam/penalties/stable_reparam.py (setup, and on the host between compiled dense REML evaluations through jaxgam/fitting/stable_log_det.py); _symmetric_eigh in jaxgam/formula/fitting_prepare.py; build_working_penalty_blocks in jaxgam/formula/discrete/working_penalties.py; tensor penalty normalization

source_frobenius_norm is not a provider call: it reproduces gdi.c::frobenius_norm as one column-major running sum in NumPy.

During the discretized fit the provider is called between two compiled JAX executables: a compiled step builds the Hessian and penalty inputs, factor_working_model copies them to the host and factors them with DPSTRF, and the factors go back with jax.device_put to the compiled proposal. See The discretized fit.

On a SciPy built with Accelerate. scipy_uses_accelerate_lapack() routes a few eigensolves to SciPy's own LAPACK instead, because the audited SciPy Accelerate build preserves R's separate libRlapack gauge more closely there: the eigensolve inside cubic_shrinkage_penalty (its DGEMM still uses the provider), _symmetric_eigh in jaxgam/formula/fitting_prepare.py, _dsyevr in jaxgam/penalties/stable_reparam.py, and the largest-eigenvalue normalization of cr/cs tensor margins in jaxgam/smooths/tensor.py. All other provider routines are used on every platform. On such a machine the Accelerate warning also fires.

docs.title: Source arithmetic
docs.text:
jaxgam/smooths/source_arithmetic.py reproduces mgcv's compiled scalar loops (tprs.c, mat.c, matrix.c), which accumulate s += a*b in fixed index order. How those statements round depends on how R's mgcv shared object was compiled: the module records that the aarch64 Linux and macOS arm64 builds contract them into fused multiply-adds and the x86-64 Linux build does not. SOURCE_FMA_CONTRACTION is therefore true on aarch64/arm64 machines. The kernels (sequential_dot, column_squares, squared_distances, knot_squared_distances, matmult_tn, qt_factor, the Householder and Lanczos helpers, ritz_accumulate) are numba.njit functions compiled without fastmath, so LLVM neither reorders nor contracts plain expressions; the fused form uses the llvm.fma intrinsic through _fused.

libm_exp, libm_log, libm_log10 and r_pow call the C math library element by element through ctypes function pointers inside Numba loops. NumPy's own exp/log/power may dispatch to SIMD implementations (AVX-512 on x86_64) whose last bits differ from libm, which is what R calls. r_pow also reproduces R_pow's special cases. These are used across setup and the host side of the fit (for example jaxgam/penalties/stable_reparam.py, jaxgam/execution/discrete/working_model.py, jaxgam/execution/operator/system.py).

jaxgam/smooths/source_penalty_coordinates.py builds R's sum-to-zero centering reflector from column means accumulated in np.longdouble in row order (as R's colMeans does), applies it with BLAS ddot/daxpy in R's qr.qty order (source_centered_penalties, used by the dense design; source_centered_smooth, used for te() centering in jaxgam/smooths/constraints.py), and runs DSYEVR on the lower triangle of the provider. Its purpose is to keep R's penalty coordinate gauge, which decides the canonical coefficients at rank ties and the small eigenvalues of penalty determinants.

Inside JAX kernels, _materialize_source_operation in jaxgam/jax_utils.py applies nextafter(x, x) (an exact identity with an identity derivative) to stop XLA from contracting arithmetic across a source vector-operation boundary. It is used in jaxgam/links/links.py, jaxgam/fitting/family_execution.py and jaxgam/fitting/stream/nb_kernels.py.

docs.title: jaxgam/jax_utils.py
docs.text:
• array_module(x) returns jax.numpy for a JAX array and numpy otherwise; is_jax_array is the test. Families and links use them so one implementation serves both NumPy and JAX inputs.
  • to_jax(*arrays, device=None) is the Phase 1 to 2 boundary: jax.device_put(jnp.asarray(a, dtype=jnp.float64), device). to_numpy is the Phase 2 to 3 boundary: np.asarray.
  • JIT-compiled helpers: cho_factor (plain Cholesky, with a diagonal-relative jitter of 1e-12 then 1e-6 only when the plain factor fails or a relative pivot is below 1e-12, selected by jax.lax.cond), penalized_cholesky, penalized_solve, numerical_rank (pivoted QR), build_S_lambda, block_log_det_S, stable_log_pseudo_det, and StableLogDetTerms, a pytree carrying host gam.reparam log-determinant terms into the compiled criterion.

docs.title: Numba
docs.text:
Module Use jaxgam/smooths/source_arithmetic.py Source-ordered FMA kernels (disk-cached with cache=True) and libm loops (compiled per process, not cached, because they embed process addresses). jaxgam/smooths/cubic.py _compiled_source_cubic_basis: a fused-multiply-add row loop for the cubic basis on macOS arm64. jaxgam/smooths/utils.py row_tensor and interaction_matrix (row-wise Kronecker products for tensor and random-effect designs), and _slanczos_jit, an older Lanczos with no package caller. jaxgam/summary/_davies.py Port of mgcv's src/davies.c for weighted chi-square tail probabilities.

No kernel uses Numba's parallel=True or fastmath options, or its parallel range loops.

docs.title: Determinism across machines
docs.text:
• The provider runs on one thread whatever the environment says.
  • The Docker test image sets OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1. The embedded R, SciPy and the provider all link threaded OpenBLAS, whose reduction order changes with the core count, so without the pin R reference values would differ between a local image and a CI runner. make test-platform-sensitive-ci passes the same variables; make test-local sets none.
  • Apart from the provider pin, jaxgam sets no JAX, XLA, OpenMP or BLAS thread count.
  • FMA contraction is chosen per machine (SOURCE_FMA_CONTRACTION), and element-wise transcendental functions use libm, not NumPy's SIMD loops.
  • Residual differences remain and are acknowledged in the tests rather than hidden: tests that depend on SIMD maths or the OpenBLAS kernel family carry @pytest.mark.platform_sensitive and run on eight CI replicas, and the discretized-fit tie replays have per-platform reviewed bounds keyed by cpu_platform_class(). tests/r_number_format.py models R's number formatting with the platform's long double width (53, 64 or 113 bits). See Testing and CI.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
Variable Read by Effect JAXGAM_NO_COMPILATION_CACHE jaxgam/__init__.py at import Any non-empty value skips jaxgam's cache configuration. JAX_COMPILATION_CACHE_DIR jaxgam/__init__.py at import, and JAX Cache directory; when set, jaxgam does not set one. JAXGAM_ALLOW_ACCELERATE jaxgam/platform_guard.py Exactly 1 suppresses the Accelerate warning. OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS, OMP_NUM_THREADS OpenBLAS in NumPy, SciPy and R (not the provider) Set to 1 in the Docker image and the platform-sensitive target. JAXGAM_TEST_SHARD tests/conftest.py (SHARD_ENV in tests/sharding.py) i/N keeps shard i of N; unset or blank runs everything. COVERAGE_FILE coverage.py Set per shard by make test-cov-shard-ci. R_HOME, LD_LIBRARY_PATH, UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE rpy2, the loader, uv Set in the Dockerfile. JAXGAM_BENCHMARK_TASK_TMPDIR, JAXGAM_SOURCE_COMMIT, JAXGAM_IMAGE_DIGEST, JAXGAM_BENCHMARK_SOURCE_COMMIT, JAXGAM_BENCHMARK_IMAGE_ID scripts under scripts/ Benchmark isolation and provenance only.

The package itself reads only the first three. No code reads MGCV_SOURCE.

docs.title: Devices
docs.text: GAM(..., device=...) accepts None, "cpu" or "gpu"; anything else is a ValueError. _resolve_device in jaxgam/api.py maps "cpu" to jax.devices("cpu")[0] and "gpu" to jax.devices("gpu")[0], raising RuntimeError when no GPU backend exists; None leaves placement to JAX's default device. The device is passed to to_jax/jax.device_put on the dense, streamed and discretized routes. The operator route rejects any device other than CPU with NotImplementedError. Provider calls, setup and post-estimation always run on the host CPU. No CI job runs on a GPU.
