    _SourceLapack *-- _DeclaredProvider
    SourceConstraintQR ..> _SourceLapack : dnrm2, dscal, ddot, daxpy

All are frozen dataclasses. _SourceLapack holds the ctypes function handles; source_pivoted_cholesky returns a SourcePivotedCholesky (upper factor as R's La_chol returns it, zero-based pivots, DPSTRF's rank). StableLogDetTerms (in jaxgam/jax_utils.py) is a registered pytree; its log_det returns NaN away from rho0 so host terms cannot be used at the wrong smoothing parameters.

docs.title: Rules and invariants
docs.text:
• Float64 everywhere. JAX code relies on jax_enable_x64 from jaxgam/__init__.py; to_jax casts to float64. Do not introduce float32 arrays.
  • Phase 1 modules import no JAX. jaxgam/formula/, jaxgam/smooths/, jaxgam/penalties/ and jaxgam/data/ use NumPy, SciPy and Numba only. Because any import jaxgam.<module> first runs jaxgam/__init__.py (which imports JAX), the tests stub the package in a subprocess and assert that no jax module was loaded: tests/test_data/test_discretize.py, tests/test_data/test_continuous_discretize.py, tests/test_data/test_continuous_frame.py, tests/test_data/test_continuous_request.py, tests/test_formula/test_continuous_setup.py, tests/test_formula/test_continuous_design.py, tests/test_formula/test_continuous_metadata.py and tests/test_formula/test_rank_coordinates.py. There is no such check for smooths/ or penalties/.
  • JAX kernels are pure and traceable. Kernels in jaxgam/fitting/ branch with jax.lax.cond and loop with jax.lax.while_loop, scan or fori_loop; Python-level iteration, step control and cross-batch reductions live in the host drivers in jaxgam/execution/ (and in host parts of jaxgam/fitting/newton.py and jaxgam/fitting/stable_log_det.py). See The dense fit.
  • The provider stays single-threaded and local. Load it only through _source_lapack(); never import scipy_openblas32 (its __init__ loads the library globally). tests/test_smooths/test_source_lapack.py checks that the pin leaves NumPy's and SciPy's thread counts unchanged, that outputs are identical with 1 and 8 caller threads, and that a missing or refused thread control raises.
  • Provider version and identity are checked at load. A different wheel version, an unexpected config string or an ILP64 build raises RuntimeError.
  • Workspace is bounded before allocation. source_lanczos, source_pivoted_cholesky and cubic_shrinkage_penalty check *_workspace_bound against available_workspace_bytes and raise MemoryError first.
  • The Accelerate warning fires at most once per process and only on Apple silicon with an Accelerate NumPy or SciPy and a CPU backend (tests/test_platform_guard.py).

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• JAXGAM_NO_COMPILATION_CACHE=0 disables the cache configuration; the variable is tested for being non-empty, not for a true value.
  • Setting the cache directory with jax.config.update does not work around jaxgam's default; use JAX_COMPILATION_CACHE_DIR before import.
  • make test-local runs with your machine's BLAS thread count, so last-bit comparisons with R can differ from CI.
  • On an Accelerate SciPy, some eigensolves deliberately bypass the provider; a gauge difference seen only on macOS may come from that routing, not from the provider.
  • SOURCE_FMA_CONTRACTION follows the machine, so an x86_64 and an arm64 run of the same source test exercise different arithmetic. Native x86-64 CI is the authority for the non-fused path.
  • device="gpu" moves the compiled fit to the GPU but not the host provider calls; the discretized route copies factor inputs to the host every trial.

docs.title: Where to change things
docs.text:
• Bind another LAPACK or BLAS routine: add the symbol and its argtypes in _source_lapack and a field to _SourceLapack in jaxgam/smooths/source_lapack.py, then a public wrapper that validates inputs, bounds workspace and calls it. Add a pinned-R comparison in tests/test_smooths/test_source_lapack.py.
  • Change the provider version: _PROVIDER_VERSION and _OPENBLAS_PREFIX in jaxgam/smooths/source_lapack.py and the pin in pyproject.toml; the version must match the OpenBLAS that pinned R links.
  • Reproduce another mgcv C loop: add a numba.njit kernel to jaxgam/smooths/source_arithmetic.py using _madd/_msub and SOURCE_FMA_CONTRACTION, with tests in tests/test_smooths/test_source_arithmetic.py.
  • Change the compilation cache default or the Accelerate check: jaxgam/__init__.py and jaxgam/platform_guard.py.
  • Add an environment variable: read it in one place, document it in the table above, and add a test.
  • Change device placement: _resolve_device in jaxgam/api.py and the device= arguments of FittingData.from_setup and the route functions.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: This page covers what a fit returns and how it predicts: the result types GAMResults, GAMInferenceResult and GAMPredictionResult, the prediction core GAMPredictor, how each result is built from each route, copying, immutability and pickling, how new data become a prediction matrix, link and response scales, standard errors, batched prediction, behaviour for unseen factor levels, the discretized route's prediction policies, and summary and plot. Phase 3 code runs on the host in NumPy and SciPy.

docs.title: Where the code is
docs.text: Path Role jaxgam/results.py _FitDiagnostics, GAMResults, GAMInferenceResult, GAMPredictionResult, StreamExactOptimizerDiagnostics; the constructors _from_fit, _from_stream_fit, _from_discrete, _from_operator_fit; EDF, covariance and null-deviance helpers. jaxgam/inference/predictor.py GAMPredictor, the frozen picklable prediction core; PivotedQRFisherFactor; prediction budget checks. jaxgam/inference/_core.py predict_core, prepare_prediction (new data to linear predictor, offsets) and finish_prediction (response scale and standard errors). jaxgam/inference/operator_geometry.py OperatorPredictionGeometry: operator-route prediction without dense random-effect columns. jaxgam/formula/predict_matrix.py PredictSpec, build_predict_spec, build_predict_matrix: the one encoder from new data to the constrained prediction matrix. jaxgam/formula/design.py ModelSetup.build_predict_matrix and ModelSetup._lazy_predict_spec, which builds and caches the dense route's PredictSpec. jaxgam/smooths/constraints.py CoefficientMap and TermBlock; transform_X applies a term's identifiability constraint to its raw basis block. jaxgam/data/continuous_request.py RequestCompressionSpec, FrozenRequestGrid: request compression for prediction_policy="mgcv_predict_bamd". jaxgam/formula/discrete/continuous_metadata.py The discretized route's retained metadata and build_request_compression. jaxgam/summary/summary.py summary, GAMSummary, the Wood (2013) smooth test, the random-effect test, psum_chisq_davies. jaxgam/summary/_davies.py Numba port of Davies' algorithm from mgcv's src/davies.c. jaxgam/plot/plot_gam.py plot_gam. jaxgam/execution/operator/bulk_variance.py BulkOperatorVariance, used by GAMPredictionResult.bulk_link_variance.

docs.title: The four types and what they keep
docs.text:
GAMResults and GAMInferenceResult share the frozen dataclass _FitDiagnostics (EDF vectors, deviance, score, scale, theta, smoothing parameters, convergence and route fields). GAMPredictionResult is a separate frozen dataclass with only scalar diagnostics plus scan and memory accounting. The last three hold a GAMPredictor, to which they delegate every prediction.

GAMResults GAMInferenceResult GAMPredictionResult GAMPredictor Produced by dense, result="full" dense, result="inference" dense result="prediction"; the only mode on stream, discrete and operator to_predictor() on any result Coefficients field from predictor from predictor field, read-only copy Vp (Bayesian covariance) always always, via predictor only with FitControl(uncertainty="covariance") optional Fisher factor for standard errors not needed not kept with uncertainty="fisher" (and a QR root alongside Vp on some streamed fits) optional Per-smooth edf, edf1, null_deviance yes yes no no edf_total, deviance, score, scale, theta, smoothing_params, convergence and route fields yes yes yes (score and edf_total may be None on the operator route) no setup (ModelSetup: X, y, weights, offset, penalties, coef_map) yes no no no fitted_values, linear_predictor, training_data yes no no no Scan and memory diagnostics (source_scans, batches_scanned, known_workspace_bytes, fit_peak_bytes) no no yes no predict, predict_matrix, to_predictor yes yes yes predict, predict_matrix predict_iter no no yes yes summary, plot yes no no no materialize_covariance, bulk_link_variance no no yes (bulk_link_variance on operator results only) no

GAMResults exposes the setup through properties: X, y, weights, offset, coef_map, smooth_info, term_names. GAMInferenceResult has coefficients, Vp, family, formula, smooth_info and term_names as properties reading the predictor. tests/test_result_mode.py (test_inference_result_retains_no_banned_training_or_penalty_state) and tests/test_prediction_result.py (test_point_only_result_retains_no_rows_or_dense_covariance) check what the lean types do not retain.

docs.title: How each route builds its result
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    dense["dense route, GAM.fit"] --> _from_fit["GAMResults._from_fit"]
    _from_fit -->|"result full"| GAMResults["GAMResults"]
    _from_fit -->|"result inference"| GAMInferenceResult["GAMInferenceResult"]
    _from_fit -->|"result prediction"| GAMPredictionResult["GAMPredictionResult"]
    stream["stream route"] --> _from_stream_fit["GAMPredictionResult._from_stream_fit"]
    discrete["discrete route"] --> _from_discrete["GAMPredictionResult._from_discrete"]
    operator["operator route"] --> _from_operator_fit["GAMPredictionResult._from_operator_fit"]
    _from_stream_fit --> GAMPredictionResult
    _from_discrete --> GAMPredictionResult
    _from_operator_fit --> GAMPredictionResult
    rowroutes["stream, discrete or operator<br/>with result full or inference"] --> refused["NotImplementedError"]
    GAMResults -->|"to_predictor builds a new one"| GAMPredictor["GAMPredictor"]
    GAMInferenceResult -->|"to_predictor returns its own"| GAMPredictor
    GAMPredictionResult -->|"to_predictor returns its own"| GAMPredictor

Only the dense route chooses among three types; the others always build a GAMPredictionResult, and refuse the other modes in jaxgam/api.py before any work.

GAMResults._from_fit (dense). It deep-copies the family (after Newton or EFS has written the final theta into it), moves the coefficients and scale to NumPy with to_numpy, and reads stable_rotation, the gam.reparam block maps of a fit made in stable coordinates. Then, by result_mode:

  • "prediction": maps the coefficients to public coordinates (_transform_coefficients_cpu), keeps edf_total only, and, depending on FitControl.uncertainty, keeps nothing, the lower Cholesky factor pr.L_fisher with its coordinate maps (_factor_transforms), or a dense Vp built from that factor. Building Vp raises MemoryError when 3 p^2 * 8 bytes exceed memory_budget_bytes. This branch runs before any per-smooth EDF or row output is computed.
  • "inference" and "full": form H^-1 from the Fisher factor by a triangular solve (as mgcv's chol2inv), rotate it out of stable coordinates (_rotate_covariance) and through the block transforms (_transform_covariance_cpu), form F = H^-1 X'WX (or take the Fisher-system hat matrix pr.fisher_hat), and compute per-smooth edf (_compute_per_smooth_edf, the trace of each smooth's block of F) and edf1 (_compute_per_smooth_edf1, 2 edf - tr(F F) per block, as in gam.fit3.post.proc in mgcv's R/mgcv.r). Vp is phi * H^-1 with phi = 1 for known-scale families. null_deviance comes from _compute_null_deviance, which fits an intercept-plus-offset model by IRLS (_fit_null_intercept) when there is a nonzero offset. "inference" stops here and wraps a GAMPredictor; "full" also keeps mu, eta, the ModelSetup and the smooth covariates (_extract_training_data) for plotting.

GAMPredictionResult._from_stream_fit (stream). It maps the streamed coefficients to public coordinates (_prepared_transform_coefficients_cpu), evaluates the REML score from the row-free stream state with the criterion variant that matches its coefficient factor (signed QR, pivoted QR or Cholesky), and overrides score, scale, theta, smoothing parameters, EDF and convergence from selected_fit when an outer optimizer ran. With uncertainty it keeps a PivotedQRFisherFactor when the state's Fisher factor is a PivotedQRCoefficientFactor, otherwise the lower Cholesky fisher_factor; with "covariance" it also builds Vp (MemoryError above 3 p^2 * 8 bytes, or 12 p^2 * 8 for the QR factor) and keeps the QR root beside it.

GAMPredictionResult._from_discrete (discrete). It deep-copies the family, writes a final negative binomial theta into the copy, and builds the predictor from the DiscreteFit: its predict_spec (built on the compact setup), covariance, fisher_factor or fisher_qr_factor, and the request_compression used by mgcv_predict_bamd. It records the effective prediction_policy, the bounded discretization metadata, discretization_strategy="mgcv_range_grid", the fit's scan counts and its memory plan.

GAMPredictionResult._from_operator_fit (operator). It checks that the retained geometry fits memory_budget_bytes (MemoryError), builds an OperatorPredictionGeometry (the modest block's PredictSpec, the IndexedRandomEffect terms and their column offsets), and keeps no covariance. Fixed-sp operator results have score=None, edf_total=None, and scale=None for unknown-scale families. It also stores the source fingerprint, replay digest and family configuration that bulk_link_variance later checks. _fit_operator_efs in jaxgam/api.py replaces the score, its error bound, scale, edf_total and convergence fields with dataclasses.replace.

docs.title: Immutability and copying
docs.text:
• All four types are frozen dataclasses: attributes cannot be reassigned.
  • GAMPredictor.__post_init__ copies coefficients, Vp, the Fisher factor and each Fisher transform, and marks them read-only; it rebuilds a PivotedQRFisherFactor, whose own __post_init__ validates and freezes its arrays. So arrays read through GAMInferenceResult, GAMPredictionResult or a predictor are read-only.
  • GAMResults freezes its attributes but not its array contents: GAMResults.coefficients and GAMResults.Vp are writable NumPy arrays.
  • GAMPredictionResult.__post_init__ copies smoothing_params and marks it read-only.
  • GAMResults.to_predictor() builds a new GAMPredictor on every call. Its arrays are copies, but it shares the result's family object and the PredictSpec cached on setup; it sets no prediction budgets. GAMInferenceResult.to_predictor() and GAMPredictionResult.to_predictor() return the predictor they already hold, without copying.
  • PredictSpec is built by build_predict_spec, which shallow-copies every smooth through copy_for_prediction (the base version in jaxgam/smooths/base.py drops the _X and _S caches) and shares constraint arrays by reference. ModelSetup._lazy_predict_spec builds it once and caches it.
  • tests/test_inference/test_predictor.py (test_coefficients_and_covariance_are_owned_and_read_only, test_family_snapshot_is_independent_and_keeps_final_nb_theta) and tests/test_result_mode.py (test_to_predictor_ownership_lazy_setup_and_memory_reduction) cover these rules.

docs.title: Pickling and version checks
docs.text:
• Every result type and GAMPredictor round-trips through the standard pickle module with identical predictions (tests/test_execution/test_efs_public_api.py for all three result types, tests/test_inference/test_predictor.py, tests/test_prediction_result.py, tests/test_inference/test_operator_geometry.py for operator results).
  • GAMPredictor stamps _jaxgam_version (from jaxgam.__version__) at construction. Its __setstate__ fills fields missing from older pickles (_fisher_qr_factor, _prediction_policy, _request_compression, _operator_geometry), restores the read-only flags, and warns with a UserWarning ("not a cross-version format") when the stamped version differs from the running one. Its docstring scopes pickles to "trusted, same-version transient handoff".
  • The version check lives only in GAMPredictor, so unpickling a GAMInferenceResult or GAMPredictionResult warns through the predictor it contains, and unpickling a GAMResults (which holds no predictor) does not check the version.
  • GAMPredictionResult.__setstate__ defaults a missing discretization to None; OperatorPredictionGeometry.__setstate__ re-freezes its PredictSpec; PivotedQRFisherFactor.__setstate__ re-runs its validation.
  • A family with a link class defined in a local scope cannot be pickled with pickle; test_pickle_cloudpickle_and_version_stamp shows cloudpickle (a development dependency) handling it.

docs.title: The prediction core
docs.text:
All new-data prediction runs through jaxgam/inference/_core.py:

  1. prepare_prediction rejects a pred_type other than "response" or "link" (ValueError). It builds X_p = spec.build_predict_matrix(newdata) and eta = X_p @ coefficients, or, with an operator geometry, eta = geometry.forward(newdata, coefficients) and no matrix. An offset must be one-dimensional with one finite value per row (ValueError) and is added to eta; when none is given and the model was fitted with a nonzero offset (offset_was_nonzero), it warns and leaves the offset out, as predict.gam does for external offsets.
  2. finish_prediction applies link.linkinv(eta) for "response", or returns eta for "link", and computes standard errors when asked (next section).

build_predict_matrix in jaxgam/formula/predict_matrix.py turns new data into the constrained matrix in the fitted column order:

  • _to_dict converts a DataFrame column by column, keeping factor columns as pandas Series so categorical identity survives; all referenced variables must have one length (ValueError).
  • The parametric block is encoded with the factor levels and orderedness stored at fit time (factor_info, ordered_factors), treatment contrasts or contr.poly contrasts for ordered factors, and the training-time drop of aliased columns (parametric_keep_cols).
  • Each smooth TermBlock in the CoefficientMap evaluates its frozen basis on the new data (term.smooth.predict_matrix), and CoefficientMap.transform_X maps the raw block to constrained columns by multiplying by Z_centering and deleting the del_index columns. The TermBlock itself is passed, not its label, so two smooths with one label use their own constraints.
  • The blocks are stacked and the column count checked against total_coefs (RuntimeError).

GAMResults.predict with newdata=None skips the matrix build and finishes the stored linear_predictor with the training X; any offset argument is ignored in that case. GAMResults.predict with new data calls predict_core directly, without the predictor or its budgets. predict_matrix is the equivalent of predict.gam(type="lpmatrix") in mgcv's R/mgcv.r; there is no "terms" prediction type.

sequenceDiagram
    participant GAMPredictionResult as GAMPredictionResult.predict
    participant GAMPredictor as GAMPredictor._predict
    participant RequestCompressionSpec as RequestCompressionSpec
    participant prepare_prediction as prepare_prediction
    participant PredictSpec as PredictSpec.build_predict_matrix
    participant CoefficientMap as CoefficientMap.transform_X
    participant finish_prediction as finish_prediction
    GAMPredictionResult->>GAMPredictor: newdata, pred_type, se_fit, offset
    GAMPredictor->>GAMPredictor: _check_pred_type and _check_prediction_budgets
    GAMPredictor->>GAMPredictor: RuntimeError if se_fit without Vp or Fisher factor
    opt prediction_policy mgcv_predict_bamd
        GAMPredictor->>RequestCompressionSpec: freeze the whole request, then apply the grid
    end
    GAMPredictor->>prepare_prediction: compressed or original newdata
    prepare_prediction->>PredictSpec: newdata
    PredictSpec->>PredictSpec: parametric block with fitted factor levels
    loop each smooth TermBlock
        PredictSpec->>CoefficientMap: smooth.predict_matrix output and the TermBlock
        CoefficientMap-->>PredictSpec: constrained block
    end
    PredictSpec-->>prepare_prediction: X_p
    prepare_prediction->>prepare_prediction: eta = X_p times coefficients, plus offset or warning
    prepare_prediction-->>GAMPredictor: X_p and eta
    GAMPredictor->>finish_prediction: eta, X_p, link, Vp or Fisher factor
    finish_prediction-->>GAMPredictionResult: prediction, or prediction and se

This is the general path. When the predictor holds a dense Vp and no QR factor, _predict calls predict_core, which runs the same prepare_prediction and finish_prediction pair. On the operator route prepare_prediction calls OperatorPredictionGeometry.forward instead of PredictSpec, so no matrix exists.

docs.title: Standard errors
docs.text:
se_fit=True returns (prediction, se). The link-scale standard error of row i is sqrt(x_i' Vp x_i); finish_prediction gets it in one of two ways, and on the response scale multiplies it by |mu_eta(eta)| (the delta method).

flowchart TD
    request["predict with se_fit True"] --> owner{"object predicting"}
    owner -->|"GAMResults, GAMInferenceResult,<br/>GAMResults.to_predictor"| vp_branch["Vp branch<br/>se = sqrt of row sums of X_p Vp times X_p"]
    owner -->|"GAMPredictionResult or its predictor"| uncertainty{"FitControl.uncertainty at fit"}
    uncertainty -->|"none, and always on operator"| no_provider["RuntimeError<br/>no uncertainty provider"]
    uncertainty -->|"fisher"| factor_kind{"retained factor"}
    factor_kind -->|"_fisher_factor, lower Cholesky"| cholesky["apply _fisher_transforms to X_p<br/>Z = solve_triangular of L and X_p transposed"]
    factor_kind -->|"_fisher_qr_factor"| qr["apply _fisher_transforms to X_p<br/>Z = root_transpose_inverse of X_p transposed"]
    cholesky --> factor_se["se = sqrt of _fisher_scale times column sums of Z squared"]
    qr --> factor_se
    uncertainty -->|"covariance"| vp_kept{"QR factor kept beside Vp"}
    vp_kept -->|"no"| vp_branch
    vp_kept -->|"yes"| qr
    vp_branch --> scale{"pred_type"}
    factor_se --> scale
    scale -->|"link"| link_se["return se"]
    scale -->|"response"| response_se["se times abs of mu_eta of eta"]
    no_provider -.->|"later"| materialize_covariance["materialize_covariance builds Vp from a kept factor"]

Read from the top: full and inference results always carry Vp; prediction results carry what FitControl.uncertainty asked for at fit time.

  • Lower Cholesky factors come from the dense route (pr.L_fisher), from streamed fits whose Fisher factor is not a pivoted QR factor, and from fixed-sp discrete Gaussian fits. PivotedQRFisherFactor comes from streamed fits with a PivotedQRCoefficientFactor, from discrete Gaussian working-model fits and from the discrete performance iteration.
  • _fisher_transforms maps the factor's fitting coordinates to public ones, block by block, so X_p is moved into fitting coordinates before the solve; _fisher_scale is phi.
  • materialize_covariance(memory_budget_bytes) returns the kept Vp, or builds it from the kept factor (MemoryError above 3 p^2 * 8 bytes, 12 p^2 * 8 for a QR factor; RuntimeError with no factor). It returns a read-only array and does not change the result.
  • The operator route keeps no uncertainty state (_fit_operator refuses uncertainty != "none"). bulk_link_variance on an operator result instead replays the training source, checks that its fingerprint, replay digest and family configuration match the accepted fit (RuntimeError otherwise), and returns a BulkOperatorVariance provider of approximate link-scale variances with a calibration against exact values on selected rows; see Phase 2: operator fitting.

docs.title: Prediction budgets
docs.text: A predictor built by a prediction-mode result carries _output_budget_bytes and _memory_budget_bytes from FitControl. _check_prediction_budgets raises MemoryError before any work when the returned array (n * 8 bytes, 2 n * 8 with standard errors, n * p * 8 for predict_matrix) exceeds the output budget, or when the known workspace (n * p * 8 times 1 for point prediction, 3 with Vp, 4 with a Cholesky factor, 7 with a QR factor; the operator geometry computes its own bound) exceeds the memory budget. The message suggests predict_iter. Predictors from GAMResults.to_predictor() and inference results have no budgets.

docs.title: Batched prediction with predict_iter
docs.text:
GAMPredictionResult.predict_iter(source, batch_rows=None, *, pred_type, se_fit) delegates to GAMPredictor.predict_iter with batch_rows defaulting to the fit's FitControl.batch_rows. GAMResults and GAMInferenceResult have no predict_iter; call it on their predictor.

  • Checks made when predict_iter is called, before the first batch: a RowSource (TypeError), a positive integer batch_rows (ValueError), the prediction type, and the uncertainty provider (RuntimeError). Under mgcv_predict_bamd it also scans the whole source once (RequestCompressionSpec.freeze_source) to freeze the compression grid.
  • The generator then hashes the source, scans it, and for each non-empty batch yields (row_positions, prediction) or (row_positions, (prediction, se)), computed by the same _predict as a single call, with the batch's offset. Padded batches raise NotImplementedError; row positions must be nonnegative integers (ValueError); too many or too few rows, or a source whose row count or fingerprint changed by the end, raise RuntimeError.
  • A source that declares has_explicit_offset=False passes no offset for its first non-empty batch, so a model fitted with an offset warns once; the later batches pass the source's zero offsets.
  • Each batch is one predict call for the budgets, so a large source is predicted within the output budget by choosing batch_rows.

docs.title: Unseen and missing factor levels
docs.text:
Term Unseen level Missing value (None or NaN) Code s(g, bs="re") zero random-effect contribution, no warning zero contribution RandomEffectSmooth.predict_matrix in jaxgam/smooths/random_effects.py sets non-finite indicator entries to 0; on the operator route IndexedRandomEffect.evaluate in jaxgam/formula/operator/prepare.py sets the amplitude to 0 factor by variable NaN row for the smooth block and a UserWarning ("factor levels ... not in original fit") the same, as a missing value is not a fitted level FactorBySmooth.predict_matrix in jaxgam/smooths/by_variable.py parametric factor ValueError ("Parametric factor ... has new level(s)") NaN row _build_parametric_matrix and _encode_factor in jaxgam/formula/predict_matrix.py

The random-effect rule is a deliberate divergence from mgcv, which returns NA for a missing group: a missing or unseen group predicts the population level. Tests: tests/test_smooths/test_random_effects.py, tests/test_smooths/test_by_variable.py, tests/test_formula/test_design.py, tests/test_execution/test_discrete_prediction.py (both discrete policies), and test_symbolic_large_prediction_budget_avoids_expanded_rows_and_zeros_unknown_levels in tests/test_inference/test_operator_geometry.py.

docs.title: Prediction policies on the discretized route
docs.text:
ContinuousDiscretizationControl.prediction_policy decides how a discrete fit predicts; the result reports it in prediction_policy and the predictor in its prediction_policy property.

  • "continuous_frozen_basis" (default): new covariate values are evaluated exactly by the compact setup's PredictSpec, with no rounding.
  • "mgcv_predict_bamd": the predictor holds a RequestCompressionSpec built by build_request_compression from the fitted variable groups and the policy's DiscretizationBudget. Before the frozen bases are evaluated, the whole request is compressed as predict.bamd does (R/bam.r, through discrete.mf and compress.df): each group keeps its own distinct rows when there are few enough, otherwise its metric variables are rounded to an even grid over the request's own range. So a prediction depends on the other rows in the same request, but not on how predict_iter batches it. Factor-only groups pass through unchanged. predict_matrix returns the matrix of the compressed request. freeze_request(newdata) returns the FrozenRequestGrid for a request (None under the exact policy). A source changed after its grid was frozen raises RuntimeError. Compression beyond the budget raises MemoryError.
  • A model without smooth terms follows "continuous_frozen_basis" even when "mgcv_predict_bamd" was requested (effective_prediction_policy in jaxgam/formula/discrete/continuous_metadata.py); the requested policy stays in discretization.requested_prediction_policy.

tests/test_execution/test_discrete_prediction.py covers both policies, their batching invariance and their agreement with pinned mgcv.

docs.title: Operator-route prediction
docs.text: OperatorPredictionGeometry keeps the modest block's PredictSpec, the coefficient positions of the modest columns, and each IndexedRandomEffect. forward evaluates rows in batches of batch_rows: the modest block through its PredictSpec, and each random effect as one coefficient index and one amplitude per row, never as dense indicator columns. build_predict_matrix forms a dense matrix only for an explicit predict_matrix call, which the budget check bounds. slice_columns passes only the required covariates.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
GAMResults.summary() calls summary in jaxgam/summary/summary.py (a port of summary.gam in mgcv's R/mgcv.r), prints the returned GAMSummary and returns it. It needs the training-backed fields (X, fitted_values, weights, Vp, edf, edf1), which is why only GAMResults has it.

  • Parametric table. Estimates, standard errors from diag(Vp), and a z test for known-scale families or a t test with n - edf_total residual degrees of freedom. Aliased parametric columns dropped at setup appear as NaN rows (dropped_param_names).
  • Smooth table. For each smooth, _test_stat (a port of testStat) computes the Wood (2013) statistic on the Fisher-weighted design block sqrt(W) X with reference rank min(k, edf1). The p-value uses a mixture of chi-squares through psum_chisq_davies (a port of psum.chisq, which calls Davies' method _davies and falls back to _liu2, a port of liu2), or a plain chi-square or F tail for an integer rank. Known scale reports Chi.sq, estimated scale F. Random-effect smooths with no null space use _re_test (a port of reTest and recov), conditioning on the other random effects through _re_test_general when there are several.
  • Model statistics. Adjusted R-squared (_compute_r_squared), deviance explained (_compute_deviance_explained), scale, the REML score and theta.

GAMSummary.__str__ formats the tables as print.summary.gam does. tests/test_summary/test_summary.py compares the tables with mgcv.

docs.title: Plot
docs.text: GAMResults.plot() calls plot_gam in jaxgam/plot/plot_gam.py (the counterpart of plot.gam in mgcv's R/plots.r), which imports matplotlib only when called. It draws one panel per smooth term, one per level for a factor-by smooth: a one-dimensional smooth as its partial effect on the link scale with a band of se_mult (default 2) standard errors from the term's Vp block and a rug of the stored training covariate; a two-dimensional smooth as a filled contour; a random effect as a normal quantile plot of its coefficients (as plot.random.effect); higher dimensions as a labelled placeholder with a warning. Each panel's basis is evaluated with smooth.predict_matrix and CoefficientMap.transform_X on the term's own TermBlock. The pages argument is accepted and unused. tests/test_plot/test_plot.py covers it.

docs.title: Rules and invariants
docs.text:
• One encoder for prediction. Every prediction path, including predict_iter and the full result, builds rows through build_predict_matrix and CoefficientMap.transform_X (or the operator geometry). Full, inference and predictor predictions are byte-identical: test_full_and_inference_predictions_are_byte_identical in tests/test_result_mode.py and test_predict_and_matrix_are_byte_identical_to_full_results in tests/test_inference/test_predictor.py.
  • Self-prediction reproduces the fit. GAMResults.predict() without new data returns the stored fit; predicting the training data through the matrix must agree (tests/test_predict/test_predict.py).
  • Prediction results keep no rows. No training arrays, setup or dense covariance unless asked for (tests/test_prediction_result.py).
  • All missing-group paths agree. A missing or unseen random-effect group gives a zero contribution on every route and every result type.
  • Batching does not change predictions. predict_iter equals one concatenated predict call, also under mgcv_predict_bamd (test_predict_iter_matches_concrete_prediction_with_source_offsets in tests/test_inference/test_predictor.py, tests/test_execution/test_discrete_prediction.py).
  • Phase 3 has no JAX import. jaxgam/inference/, jaxgam/summary/ and jaxgam/plot/ import none; jaxgam/results.py converts every device array with to_numpy before covariance or EDF work.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• GAMResults array fields are writable even though the dataclass is frozen; writing into coefficients changes later predictions of that result (but not of a predictor already taken from it, which owns a copy).
  • GAMResults.predict(offset=...) without newdata ignores the offset.
  • A prediction result made without uncertainty="fisher" or "covariance" cannot give standard errors; refitting is the only remedy.
  • The FitControl docstring says uncertainty="fisher" retains a Cholesky factor; on QR-solver and discrete working-model fits it retains a PivotedQRFisherFactor instead.
  • Discrete mgcv_predict_bamd predictions of one row change when other rows are added to the same request. This is mgcv's behaviour, not a bug.
  • Pickles are not a storage format: a version mismatch only warns.
  • Operator results report score=None and edf_total=None for fixed sp; code that formats results must allow None.

docs.title: Where to change things
docs.text: To do this Edit Keep a new field on a result the dataclass in jaxgam/results.py and every constructor that builds it (_from_fit, _from_stream_fit, _from_discrete, _from_operator_fit) Change what prediction needs from setup PredictSpec and build_predict_spec in jaxgam/formula/predict_matrix.py, and a smooth's copy_for_prediction if it holds new caches Change prediction arithmetic or offsets prepare_prediction and finish_prediction in jaxgam/inference/_core.py Add an uncertainty provider GAMPredictor fields, finish_prediction, _check_prediction_budgets, and the constructor that retains it Change batched prediction GAMPredictor.predict_iter and _predict_iter in jaxgam/inference/predictor.py Change unseen-level behaviour the smooth's predict_matrix (jaxgam/smooths/random_effects.py, jaxgam/smooths/by_variable.py) or _build_parametric_matrix, and IndexedRandomEffect.evaluate for the operator route Change discrete request compression jaxgam/data/continuous_request.py and build_request_compression in jaxgam/formula/discrete/continuous_metadata.py Change summary tables summary and its helpers in jaxgam/summary/summary.py Change plots plot_gam in jaxgam/plot/plot_gam.py Add pickle compatibility for a new predictor field give it a default and add it to GAMPredictor.__setstate__

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: This page covers everything that happens before fitting, on the CPU with NumPy and SciPy: parsing the formula, constructing smooth bases and penalties, absorbing identifiability constraints into a CoefficientMap, and assembling the dense model matrix. It then covers the three row-source setups that never build a dense training matrix: streamed preparation (jaxgam/formula/prepare.py), the compact setup of the discretized route (jaxgam/formula/discrete/continuous_setup.py and its neighbours) and the operator preparation modules. Fitting starts at the Phase 1 to 2 boundary described in fitting_dense.md.

docs.title: Which route uses which setup
docs.text:
Route (FitControl.execution) Setup entry point Training matrix built? dense parse_formula, then ModelSetup.build (jaxgam/api.py) Yes, dense X stream parse_formula, then prepare_model(..., family=...) and StreamDesign No; one batch at a time discrete parse_formula, then build_continuous_discrete_setup from jaxgam/execution/discrete/gaussian.py Only on the compact frame, then discarded operator prepare_operator_model No; random effects stay symbolic

The route dispatch itself is on fit_lifecycle.md.

docs.title: Formula parsing
docs.text:
parse_formula splits the string on the first ~. The left side is taken verbatim as the response column name. The right side is parsed with ast.parse(..., mode="eval") and walked by _TermCollector; no regular expressions are used.

Accepted:

  • + between terms. Long chains are flattened iteratively (_additive_chain), so the recursion depth does not grow with the number of terms.
  • 0 and - 1 (or a leading -1) remove the intercept; 1 restores it. The walk is left to right, so the last token wins, as in R.
  • Bare names become ParametricTerms. A repeated name is dropped, as R's model.matrix does.
  • Calls to s, te and ti only (_SMOOTH_FUNCTIONS). Positional arguments must be bare names. A smooth identical to an earlier one (same variables, bs, k, by, type and extra arguments) is dropped, like R's terms.formula; a repeat with a different configuration is kept.
  • Keywords: k must evaluate to an int, bs to a str, by to a name or string. fx=False, sp=None and id=None are accepted and ignored. TRUE, FALSE and NA are mapped to True, False and None. Every other keyword is evaluated with ast.literal_eval into SmoothSpec.extra_args (for example m, xt, max_knots, seed, and the GP options).

Rejected:

  • ValueError for *, : (not valid Python, so ast.parse fails), - x other than - 1, any function other than s/te/ti (including I(), offset(), factor()), non-name positional arguments, non-literal keyword values, and a non-integer k (so per-margin k=[5, 6] is rejected).
  • NotImplementedError for fx=True, a per-term sp= other than None, and any id= other than None. The id check also runs in SmoothSpec.__post_init__, so a hand-built spec cannot bypass it.

The parser does not check bs. An unregistered basis fails at setup with the registry's KeyError (see families_links_smooths.md). Unread keys in extra_args are ignored without a warning.

Default bases: s() uses tp; te() and ti() use cr (_DEFAULT_BASIS), as in R.

docs.title: Dense model setup
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A["formula string"] --> B["parse_formula"]
    B --> C["FormulaSpec"]
    C --> D["ModelSetup.build"]
    D --> E["_validate_variables, _validate_equal_lengths,<br/>_validate_finite_covariates"]
    E --> F["_build_parametric_matrix"]
    F --> G["_drop_aliased_parametric_columns"]
    E --> H["_build_smooth_components"]
    H --> I["get_smooth_class, then Smooth.setup"]
    I --> J["resolve_by_variable"]
    J --> K["consume_training_design_matrix<br/>and build_penalty_matrices"]
    G --> L["CoefficientMap.build"]
    K --> L
    L --> M["np.column_stack: X"]
    L --> N["make_penalty_structure"]
    M --> O["ModelSetup"]
    N --> O
    O --> P["FittingData.from_setup (Phase 2)"]
    O --> Q["build_predict_spec: PredictSpec (Phase 3)"]

Read it top to bottom: validation, then the parametric block and the smooth blocks are built independently, joined in CoefficientMap.build, and the result is one frozen ModelSetup that feeds both the fit and prediction.

ModelSetup.build in order:

  1. Converts the data to a column mapping (predict_matrix._to_dict, which keeps categorical Series intact).
  2. Validates: the response exists, is finite and has at least two rows; every formula variable exists and has the response's length; weights are finite, non-negative and not all zero; the offset is finite; numeric covariates are finite (factor columns are skipped).
  3. Builds the parametric block (_build_parametric_matrix): an intercept column, numeric columns as given, factors with treatment contrasts and ordered factors with polynomial contrasts (_contr_poly). Without an intercept the first factor is coded in full. A factor needs at least two levels.
  4. Drops exactly aliased parametric columns (_drop_aliased_parametric_columns): a pivoted QR with tolerance |R[0,0]| * eps**0.9, as mgcv's Rrank check; the intercept is never dropped. Dropped names are kept in dropped_param_names and reproduced at prediction through parametric_keep_cols.
  5. Builds each smooth (_build_smooth_components): looks up the class, calls setup, wraps it with resolve_by_variable, takes ownership of the training basis with consume_training_design_matrix and collects the raw penalties from build_penalty_matrices.
  6. Applies constraints with CoefficientMap.build (next sections).
  7. Stacks X = [X_parametric, constrained smooth blocks...] and checks its width against coef_map.total_coefs.
  8. Stores penalties locally with make_penalty_structure. With source_penalty_coordinates=True (the discretized route passes it) a second source_determinant_penalties structure keeps multi-penalty blocks in the coordinates pinned mgcv uses for determinants.
  9. Builds SmoothInfo per smooth (one entry per level for a factor-by smooth, as mgcv's per-level object$smooth), the column names, and the factor levels of parametric factors (factor_info, ordered_factors).

The Phase 1 to 2 transfer, FittingData.from_setup, is in jaxgam/fitting/data.py and is described on fitting_dense.md.

docs.title: Smooth construction
docs.text:
_build_smooth_components resolves the registry key as spec.smooth_type for te/ti and spec.bs otherwise, instantiates the class with the SmoothSpec, and calls setup(data_dict). Each setup builds the training basis (kept in _X), the penalty matrices, and the dimensions n_coefs, rank and null_space_dim, then sets _is_setup. Most constructors end with smoothCon's penalty scaling, dividing the penalty by norm(S, 1) / norm(X, inf)**2 (Smooth._smoothcon_normalize, or _source_smoothcon_normalize, which follows LAPACK dlange's summation order; tensor products scale each margin penalty by its own norm).

Class (bs) mgcv routines ported Notes from the code TPRSSmooth (tp) smooth.construct.tp.smooth.spec, Predict.matrix.tprs.smooth (R/smooth.r); tprs_setup, predict_tprs (src/tprs.c); Rlanczos (src/mat.c) through source_lanczos Default k = M + (8, 27, 100)[min(d,3)-1] where M is the null-space dimension (_default_k); k is raised to M + 1. Knots are the unique centred rows; when there are more than max_knots (default 2000) unique rows, that many are sampled with a port of R's sampler (r_sample_knot_rows). Training rows map to knot rows (training_matrix), which differ from prediction rows. TPRSShrinkageSmooth (ts) smooth.construct.ts.smooth.spec Null-space eigenvalues of S replaced by 0.1 times the smallest non-zero absolute eigenvalue (_uniform_replacement); null_space_dim becomes 0. CubicRegressionSmooth (cr) smooth.construct.cr.smooth.spec, place.knots, Predict.matrix.cr.smooth (R/smooth.r); getFS (src/mgcv.c) Default k = 10, raised with a warning to 3. Knots interpolate equally spaced ranks of the unique values. Sets _noterp = True. CubicShrinkageSmooth (cs) smooth.construct.cs.smooth.spec Geometric null-space shrinkage through cubic_shrinkage_penalty on the pinned provider. CyclicCubicSmooth (cc) smooth.construct.cc.smooth.spec, Predict.matrix.cyclic.smooth Minimum k 4; k - 1 coefficients; null space of dimension 1. GaussianProcessSmooth (gp) smooth.construct.gp.smooth.spec, gpE, Predict.matrix.gp.smooth Kernel from gp_kernel_registry (default matern_3_2); m= raises ValueError; negative truncated eigenvalues are replaced by their absolute values with a warning. RandomEffectSmooth (re) smooth.construct.re.smooth.spec, Predict.matrix.random.effect Design equals model.matrix(~v1:...:vN - 1); identity penalty scaled by norm(X, inf)**2; k ignored; side_constrain = False, _has_centering_constraint = False. Unseen or missing levels predict 0. TensorProductSmooth (te) smooth.construct.tensor.smooth.spec, tensor.prod.penalties, Predict.matrix.tensor.smooth One 1-D margin per variable, all with the term's bs and one scalar k (default 5 per margin); only m is forwarded to the margins. Univariate margins whose class leaves _noterp false (thin plate, GP) are reparameterized at evenly spaced points (_reparameterize_margin); cubic margins are not. One penalty per margin. TensorInteractionSmooth (ti) the same routines, with margin constraints Absorbs a centering constraint into each margin before the product, so CoefficientMap.build skips its centering.

By-variables are resolved after setup by resolve_by_variable, which applies to s, te and ti alike:

  • A factor by (pandas categorical, object or string column; integers are never factors, see is_factor) returns a FactorBySmooth: one block per level, rows non-zero only in their level's block, one penalty per level and base penalty, labels s(x):fLEVEL. An ordered factor drops its first level. An empty level raises ValueError. At prediction an unseen level gives a NaN row and the warning factor levels ... not in original fit.
  • A numeric by returns a NumericBySmooth: the base basis times the column, same penalties. It keeps the centering constraint only when the column is constant (R's sd(by) > mean(by) * eps * 1000 test).

Neither wrapper subclasses Smooth; they duck-type the same members and hold the base smooth in base_smooth.

docs.title: Identifiability constraints and CoefficientMap
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A["raw blocks X_j, S_j per smooth"] --> B{"centering applies?"}
    B -->|"_has_centering_constraint False (re)"| G["no centering"]
    B -->|"NumericBySmooth, non-constant by"| G
    B -->|"TensorInteractionSmooth"| G
    B -->|"FactorBySmooth"| C["apply_sum_to_zero_factor_by<br/>one Z from the base column sums"]
    B -->|"te with cr or cs"| D["source_centered_smooth"]
    B -->|"otherwise"| E["apply_sum_to_zero<br/>Z = Q[:, 1:] of QR(colSums X)"]
    C --> F["CoefficientMap.gam_side"]
    D --> F
    E --> F
    G --> F
    F --> H["fix_dependence on penalty-augmented blocks<br/>(_augment_smooth_x)"]
    H --> I["TermBlock: Z_centering, del_index, col_start, penalty_indices"]
    I --> J["CoefficientMap"]

Each smooth first loses one column to its sum-to-zero constraint (Z has shape (k, k-1)), unless it opts out. Then gam_side (port of gam.side, with fixDependence and augment.smX from R/mgcv.r) runs from low to high dimension and deletes columns of a smooth that are linearly dependent on the intercept plus the smooths processed before it (lower-dimensional ones, or earlier ones of the same dimension) that share one of its variables. It returns early when no two smooths share a variable. A parametric term sharing a smooth's variable (y ~ x + s(x)) never triggers a deletion, as in R. Two 1-D smooths of the same variable are both kept, the later one side-constrained, with the warning model has repeated 1-d smooths of same variable.

CoefficientMap (frozen) holds one TermBlock per term: a single parametric block first, then one block per smooth with its constrained width n_coefs, raw width n_coefs_raw, Z_centering, del_index and penalty_indices. It maps both ways:

  • transform_X and transform_S take a raw design or penalty block to constrained coordinates (X @ Z, then drop del_index).
  • constrained_to_full and full_to_constrained move coefficient vectors between the constrained and raw bases.

Prediction depends on it because the fitted coefficients live in constrained coordinates. build_predict_matrix evaluates each smooth's raw predict_matrix on new data and passes it through coef_map.transform_X with that term's own TermBlock, so new rows get exactly the centering and deletions of the training design. If the map were wrong, the fit could be right and every prediction wrong; tests/test_predict/test_predict.py checks that predicting the training data reproduces fitted_values.

docs.title: Penalties
docs.text:
make_penalty_structure stores each smooth's constrained penalties in that smooth's coefficient block, never padded to p x p:

  • A PenaltyBlock has start/stop, the global sp_indices, the local_penalties and an initial IdentityTransform.
  • Each local matrix becomes an IdentityPenalty (scaled identity), a DiagonalPenalty, or a DenseLocalPenalty.
  • Several penalties with disjoint supports (factor-by levels) become one block per penalty covering only its own interval. Overlapping penalties (tensor margins) share one block.
  • Source-centered te cubic penalties keep their exact bytes (preserve_bytes), because re-symmetrizing them changes the pinned coordinate gauge.

PenaltyStructure.materialize builds the combined S_lambda explicitly when a caller needs it, with smoothing parameters formed by libm_exp. The penalty reparameterization used by the fit (reparameterize_structure, stable_reparam) is described on fitting_dense.md.

docs.title: Prediction state
docs.text: build_predict_spec turns a ModelSetup into a PredictSpec: the CoefficientMap with each smooth replaced by copy_for_prediction() (training design, penalties and other fit caches dropped), the SmoothInfo, column names, factor levels and alias columns. ModelSetup builds it lazily and caches it. In Phase 3 GAMPredictor holds the PredictSpec rather than the ModelSetup, while a full GAMResults also keeps its setup; see results_and_prediction.md. PredictSpec.build_training_matrix instead evaluates training_matrix, which differs from predict_matrix only where a thin-plate basis with data knots is involved (directly, as a tensor margin or under a by wrapper); it is used only to replay setup-source rows (PreparedModel.evaluate_batch).

docs.title: Streamed preparation
docs.text:
prepare_model builds the same frozen metadata as dense setup, for a narrower formula, by scanning a RowSource several times and keeping only coefficient-sized state. It never calls ModelSetup.build. Accepted: univariate s(x, bs="cr") or bs="cs" (and cc when the caller passes allow_cyclic=True, which only the operator route does), distinct smooth variables, numeric parametric terms, with or without an intercept. Everything else raises NotImplementedError before the design scan: by=, te/ti, other bases, factor parametric terms and two smooths of one variable.

flowchart TD
    A["prepare_model"] --> B["two scan(1) probes:<br/>replayable, same row_positions,<br/>response present, variables present"]
    B --> C["SetupWorkspace.for_design, then batch_rows"]
    C --> D{"in_memory_knot_columns > 0?"}
    D -->|"yes"| E["_exact_cubic_knots_in_memory<br/>one scan per group of covariates"]
    D -->|"no"| F["_exact_cubic_knots<br/>one SQLite scan per covariate"]
    E --> G["_cubic_from_knots"]
    F --> G
    G --> H["design scan: _CanonicalTreeR of the parametric block,<br/>exact alias ratios, smooth column sums,<br/>max abs row sums, row_positions digest"]
    H --> I["_drop_aliased_parametric_columns,<br/>_canonicalize_exact_parametric_aliases"]
    I --> J["smoothCon scaling, centering Z, TermBlock,<br/>CoefficientMap, make_penalty_structure"]
    J --> K["PredictSpec and basis fingerprint: PreparedModel"]
    K --> L{"family given?"}
    L -->|"yes"| M["_prepare_fitting scan 1: Gram, QR merge,<br/>rank tree, diag of X'WX, response reductions"]
    M --> N["scan 2: check the start lies in the family domain"]
    N -->|"outside the domain"| O["scan 3: refit the start to the null mean"]
    N --> P["FittingPreparation in PreparedModel.fitting"]
    O --> P

Read each box below the probes as one full scan of the source, except the knot box, which is one scan per group of covariates (in memory) or one per covariate (SQLite).

What each scan produces:

  • Probes. Two scan(1) calls must return equal first row_positions, or the source is not replayable (TypeError). The first batch gives the column dtypes used to size the workspace.
  • Exact cubic knots. mgcv's place.knots interpolates ranks of the sorted unique values, so knots need every distinct value. In memory, a covariate costs 8 bytes per row and as many covariates are gathered per scan as the budget allows. Otherwise each covariate gets a temporary on-disk SQLite table (PRAGMA temp_store = FILE, a 2,048 KiB page cache) and the needed ranks are read with SELECT DISTINCT and ROW_NUMBER(). Both paths share _interpolate_knots and give bitwise-identical knots (test_in_memory_knots_are_bitwise_equal_to_sqlite_knots in tests/test_formula/test_prepare.py).
  • Design scan. Column sums give each smooth's centering constraint; the maximum absolute row sum gives smoothCon's scaling, applied before centering as in dense setup. The parametric block feeds a _CanonicalTreeR.
  • Rank and alias decisions. _CanonicalTreeR cuts rows into fixed 1,024-row leaves by scan ordinal and merges leaf R factors in a binary tree, so the R factor, and every decision made from it, does not depend on the batch partition. The parametric R factor goes through the dense _drop_aliased_parametric_columns, then _canonicalize_exact_parametric_aliases reproduces the dense pivot choice for exactly proportional columns. In _prepare_fitting a second tree on the unpenalized directions gives unpenalized_rank_deficit (an SVD with tolerance max(sv) * max(n, columns) * eps).
  • Fitting scans (_prepare_fitting, only with a family). They compute the start coefficients from family.initialize and family.link, diag(X'WX) for initial_log_sp_from_diagonal, and the response, weight and offset ranges in ResponseReduction. The family is duck-typed: this Phase 1 module never imports jaxgam.families. Its execution_static_config() and execution_parameter_snapshot() are stored and compared again at the end, so a family mutated during preparation raises.

The fingerprint is checked at the start and end of prepare_model and _prepare_fitting; GAM._fit_stream runs the whole preparation inside single_fit_fingerprints() (see data_sources.md).

The setup workspace and its budget. SetupWorkspace.for_design estimates the live bytes per batch row and the fixed bytes of a design scan and, with cubic smooths, of a knot scan. An SQLite knot scan is charged a fixed 16 MiB (_SQLITE_SCOPE_BYTES) whether or not it runs, so every cubic model needs at least that much. batch_rows(requested, maximum_bytes) returns the largest scan size that fits, or raises MemoryError("Streamed setup requires at least ...") before any full scan when one row does not fit. GAM._fit_stream_routes passes FitControl.batch_rows and FitControl.memory_budget_bytes. The estimate covers JaxGAM-owned arrays only; source storage, allocator retention and native BLAS/LAPACK workspace are outside it. test_setup_workspace_bounds_traced_setup_allocations checks it with tracemalloc.

docs.title: Compact setup for the discretized route
docs.text:
The discretized route reproduces bam(discrete=TRUE): covariates are compressed first, and bases are then built on the compact rows.

  1. build_continuous_discrete_setup opens single_fit_fingerprints(verify_on_exit=False) and calls build_compact_setup_frame (in jaxgam/data/continuous_frame.py; see data_sources.md). That returns a padded compact DataFrame and one CompactGroup with row selectors per jointly discretized group.
  2. _prospective_basis_bytes bounds the arrays ModelSetup.build will create on the compact frame; with the frame's retained bytes it must fit DiscretizationBudget.max_table_bytes, or the result is a ContinuousSetupUnavailable.
  3. ModelSetup.build(formula, compact.frame, source_penalty_coordinates=True) runs the ordinary dense setup on the compact frame, so every registered basis is accepted. Only build_predict_spec, the penalties and the source determinant penalties are kept; the compact training X is discarded.
  4. The result is a ContinuousDiscreteSetup with a basis_fingerprint (SHA-256 of the pickled PredictSpec) and a byte ledger.

Then _prepared_discrete in jaxgam/execution/discrete/gaussian.py calls build_discretization_metadata and, for prediction_policy="mgcv_predict_bamd", build_request_compression (both in jaxgam/formula/discrete/continuous_metadata.py), and build_continuous_discrete_design (jaxgam/formula/discrete/continuous_design.py). That last step evaluates each term's frozen predict_matrix on its group's compact representatives and stores the constrained table with the group's selector as a LookupBlock, or as a TensorLookupBlock for tensor and by terms, where margins and the by multiplier are separate indexed tables. Each step returns a typed unavailable value (ContinuousSetupUnavailable, DiscreteDesignUnavailable) instead of raising; _prepared_discrete turns it into MemoryError("{reason}: requires {n} bytes, budget is {m}."). A multi-variable random effect, s(x, g, bs="re"), is refused by _reject_unsupported_formula. The fit itself is on fitting_discrete.md.

jaxgam/formula/discrete/design.py also holds exact (unrounded) descriptor builders, build_discrete_design_from_predict_spec and its build_discrete_design_from_prepared and build_discrete_design_from_setup adapters. They replay a frozen PredictSpec over exact_index_columns rather than re-running setup on unique rows, because re-running it would change centering and normalization. At HEAD only tests call them.

docs.title: Operator preparation
docs.text:
prepare_operator_model accepts numeric parametric terms, cr/cs/cc, tp/ts/gp and re; re cannot have by= or be a tensor. It splits the formula:

  • Random effects are never built densely. One scan discovers factor levels (declared categorical levels are kept in order, otherwise observed levels are sorted) and the maximum interaction amplitude. Each term becomes an IndexedRandomEffect (per row: one level ID and one amplitude; unknown levels get amplitude 0) and a PenaltyBlock with an IdentityPenalty scaled by the squared maximum amplitude, which mirrors smoothCon's scaling of the dense re penalty.
  • The modest part (all other terms) is capped at OperatorPreparationControl.max_modest_coefficients (default 64) raw columns. Plain cubic and numeric terms use prepare_model(..., allow_cyclic=True); terms with by=, te/ti or radial bases use prepare_modest_cubic_by, which calls prepare_radial_smooth for tp/ts/gp. That function harvests knots following uniquecombs(ordered=TRUE) and the R sampler and, for tp/ts, reuses the dense tprs_setup port (_source_tprs_knot_basis).
  • Replay checking. Every scan goes through _CheckedSource, which hashes every row (position, every column value, y, weight, offset) and requires each replay to give the same digest.

jaxgam/formula/operator/workspace.py bounds the prediction scratch of radial smooths, whose knots can make evaluation larger than the coefficient width suggests. The fit is on fitting_operator.md.
