docs.title: Rules and invariants
docs.text:
• No JAX in Phase 1. jaxgam/formula/, jaxgam/smooths/ and jaxgam/penalties/ contain no import jax. They do use SciPy, Numba (jaxgam/smooths/cubic.py, jaxgam/smooths/utils.py, jaxgam/smooths/source_arithmetic.py) and ctypes (jaxgam/smooths/cubic.py, jaxgam/smooths/source_lapack.py, jaxgam/smooths/source_arithmetic.py). Families reach jaxgam/formula/prepare.py duck-typed, never imported. Import guards that stub the package and assert JAX stays unloaded exist for some modules only: test_compact_setup_import_does_not_import_jax (tests/test_formula/test_continuous_setup.py), test_continuous_descriptor_import_does_not_import_jax (tests/test_formula/test_continuous_design.py), test_metadata_module_imports_without_jax (tests/test_formula/test_continuous_metadata.py) and test_global_rank_coordinate_helpers_import_without_jax (tests/test_formula/test_rank_coordinates.py).
  • Bases match pinned mgcv. Knot placement, eigen truncation and normalization are ported operation by operation; R comparisons of the bases are in tests/test_smooths/ (tests/test_smooths/test_tprs.py, tests/test_smooths/test_tprs_source_parity.py, tests/test_smooths/test_cubic.py, tests/test_smooths/test_tensor.py, tests/test_smooths/test_gaussian_process.py, tests/test_smooths/test_random_effects.py, tests/test_smooths/test_by_variable.py), and of whole fits in tests/test_validation_matrix.py.
  • Prediction reproduces training. build_predict_matrix on the training data must equal the training design through the same CoefficientMap (tests/test_predict/test_predict.py, tests/test_constraints.py).
  • Setup owns the training basis. setup must leave the basis in _X; consume_training_design_matrix transfers it and clears it, so no smooth keeps a second n x k matrix (tests/test_smooths/test_prediction_copy.py).
  • Every smooth class chooses a prediction-copy strategy. test_copy_for_prediction_registry_audit fails for a registered class that neither overrides copy_for_prediction nor is on its audited list.
  • Penalties stay local and symmetric. Penalty validates symmetry; make_penalty_structure never pads to p x p (tests/test_penalties/test_structure.py, tests/test_penalties.py).
  • Streamed decisions are partition-invariant. Knots, alias and rank decisions do not depend on batch_rows (test_prepared_model_is_invariant_to_setup_batch_partition, test_canonical_tree_r_is_bitwise_invariant_to_row_chunking in tests/test_formula/test_prepare.py), and the streamed metadata matches dense setup (test_prepared_cubic_matches_dense_setup_and_batch_boundaries).

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Label collisions. s(x, k=6) + s(x, k=8) gives two smooths with the same label. SmoothInfo, column names and transform_X pair smooths with TermBlocks by position, never by label (comments in jaxgam/formula/design.py and jaxgam/formula/predict_matrix.py). New code must do the same; CoefficientMap.get_term(label) returns the first match.
  • Integer columns are not factors. is_factor follows R's is.factor: an integer-coded group in s(g, bs="re") or by=g becomes one numeric column without a warning.
  • te cubic margins. For te with cr/cs, margins are built without smoothCon normalization (setup(data, _normalize_penalty=False)), centered with source_centered_smooth, and stored with preserve_bytes. Re-symmetrizing or normalizing them changes the rank-deficient coordinate gauge pinned R uses.
  • bs="te" inside s(). te and ti are registry keys but are chosen by the function name. s(x, bs="te") recurses until Python raises a RecursionError.
  • Thin-plate training rows are not prediction rows. With data knots, tprs_setup maps each datum to its knot row, which differs from re-evaluating the kernel by the Lanczos residual. Source replay must use training_matrix or copy_for_training(), not predict_matrix.
  • Silently ignored keywords. Unread extra_args keys (for example pc=, select=, d=) are accepted without a warning, and only m is forwarded to tensor margins.

docs.title: Where to change things
docs.text:
• Accept a new formula construct: _TermCollector in jaxgam/formula/parser.py, then FormulaSpec in jaxgam/formula/terms.py and ModelSetup.build; add cases to tests/test_formula/test_parser.py.
  • Add or change a smooth basis: a Smooth subclass in jaxgam/smooths/, registered in jaxgam/smooths/registry.py; see the checklist on families_links_smooths.md.
  • Change centering or side constraints: CoefficientMap.build and CoefficientMap.gam_side in jaxgam/smooths/constraints.py; tests in tests/test_constraints.py.
  • Change parametric or factor encoding: _build_parametric_matrix and _encode_factor in jaxgam/formula/predict_matrix.py. Training and prediction share them, so both change together.
  • Change how penalties are stored: make_penalty_structure in jaxgam/penalties/structure.py, and every consumer of PenaltyBlock in jaxgam/formula/fitting_prepare.py and jaxgam/fitting/.
  • Widen streamed preparation: _cubic_class and the checks at the top of prepare_model; extend SetupWorkspace.for_design for any new per-row array.
  • Change the discretized setup bound: _prospective_basis_bytes in jaxgam/formula/discrete/continuous_setup.py and _memory_plan in jaxgam/formula/discrete/design.py.
  • Widen operator preparation: the term checks in prepare_operator_model and prepare_modest_cubic_by.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: This page explains how JaxGAM establishes and guards numerical correctness. It covers the layout of tests/ and its shared support modules, the R bridge that runs pinned mgcv in the test process, the tolerance classes, the validation matrix and hard-gate invariants, platform-sensitive tests, the Docker test image, the Makefile targets, and the GitHub Actions workflows that run all of it.

docs.title: Where the code is
docs.text: Path Role tests/conftest.py Data fixtures, the r_bridge fixture, shard selection (pytest_collection_modifyitems), the report header and the replay-count terminal summary. tests/helpers.py SEED, N, r_available, r_tolerance, _AssertCollector, check_that, check_flat_ridge_endpoint, make_smooth_spec, data generators, OpenBLAS identity probes and the per-platform replay bounds. tests/tolerances.py ToleranceClass and its three instances STRICT, MODERATE, LOOSE; the sign normalizers normalize_column_signs and normalize_symmetric_signs. tests/sharding.py Shard, shard_of, parse_shard and SHARD_ENV: the CRC-32 split of the suite over CI runners. tests/r_bridge.py RBridge, RBridgeError, the typed frozen result dataclasses, and _r_array, the copy of R values into NumPy memory. tests/r_ast.py Builds R language objects through rpy2 for instrumenting pinned mgcv internals without editing or parsing source. tests/r_number_format.py Exact model of R 4.5.2's numeric paste0 label, whose rounding depends on the platform's long double width. tests/efs_oracle.py Reproducible EFS oracle fixtures and controller traces modelled on mgcv's efsudr; also the make efs-fixture generator. tests/operator_efs_calibration.py Generated rows and a 50-digit decimal REML reference for the operator Fellner-Schall calibration. tests/test_validation_matrix.py The 75-cell R comparison, the hard-gate invariants and route-level parity tests against pinned R. Dockerfile, docker/renv.lock, .dockerignore The test image with pinned R 4.5.2 and mgcv 1.9-3. Makefile Contributor and CI entry points. .github/workflows/test.yml Lint, sharded test suite, combined coverage, focused jobs, platform-sensitive replicas and the gate. .github/workflows/docs.yml, .github/workflows/publish.yml Documentation deployment and PyPI release. .pre-commit-config.yaml ruff, ruff-format and vulture hooks. pyproject.toml pytest markers, coverage settings, ruff and vulture configuration.

docs.title: Test layout
docs.text:
There are 178 test_*.py modules. Each directory mirrors a package area:

Directory Owns tests/ (31 modules at top level) Cross-cutting checks: tests/test_validation_matrix.py, families and links (tests/test_families.py, tests/test_links.py), the R bridge itself (tests/test_r_bridge.py, tests/test_r_ast.py), sharding (tests/test_sharding.py), replay bounds (tests/test_replay_bounds.py), the Accelerate guard (tests/test_platform_guard.py), result modes, constraints, the benchmark harnesses and the tolerance classes (tests/test_infrastructure.py). tests/test_api/ GAM construction and fitting through the public API. tests/test_data/ Row sources, source tokens, discretization, continuous range grids and R number formatting. tests/test_execution/ (60 modules) Phase 2 host drivers in jaxgam/execution/: streamed PIRLS and REML, QR reducers, EFS providers, discretized and operator routes. tests/test_fitting/ (39 modules) Phase 2 JAX kernels in jaxgam/fitting/: PIRLS, REML, Newton, EFS algebra, streamed, discretized and operator kernels, JIT behaviour. tests/test_formula/ Parser, dense design, streamed, discretized and operator setup. tests/test_smooths/ Basis and penalty construction, the pinned LAPACK provider and source arithmetic. tests/test_penalties/ Penalty structure and stable reparameterization (there is also a top-level tests/test_penalties.py). tests/test_inference/, tests/test_predict/, tests/test_summary/, tests/test_plot/ Phase 3: GAMPredictor, operator prediction geometry, prediction, summary tables, plots. tests/test_scripts/ The benchmark scripts under scripts/.

No reference data is stored. .gitignore ignores *.csv and /tests/fixtures/; inputs are generated in code from seeds (SEED = 42, N = 200 in tests/helpers.py) and references come from R at test time.

docs.title: Shared support modules
docs.text:
• tests/conftest.py provides seeded data fixtures (simple_gaussian_data, factor_by_data, re_model_data, gp_2d_data, family_data and others), the r_bridge fixture, the shard hook, pytest_report_header and pytest_terminal_summary, and minimal_git_checkout, which builds a throwaway committed checkout because the Docker image has no .git.
  • tests/helpers.py holds r_available() (true only when the bridge loads R and the versions match), r_tolerance(family_name) (MODERATE for Gaussian, LOOSE otherwise), _AssertCollector and check_that, check_flat_ridge_endpoint (the rule for judging a REML endpoint where pinned R stopped on a flat ridge), _setup_fd (a FittingData without the public API), shared prediction case zoos, r_links_pinned_openblas, platform_report_lines, and the replay-bound machinery described below.
  • tests/tolerances.py and tests/sharding.py are described in their own sections.

docs.title: The R bridge
docs.text:
tests/r_bridge.py (about 9,500 lines) is the only sanctioned way for tests to obtain mgcv reference values. Its constants pin _REQUIRED_R_VERSION = "4.5.2" and _REQUIRED_MGCV_VERSION = "1.9.3" (R's packageVersion spelling of 1.9-3), and _PINNED_MGCV_SOURCE_COMMIT records the mgcv source commit in oracle provenance.

In-process R. _r_packages() imports rpy2.robjects and wraps the mgcv, base, stats and utils packages of the single embedded R interpreter; it is cached with functools.lru_cache, so every RBridge in the process shares one R session. The constructor RBridge(mode="auto") (or mode="rpy2") calls _setup_rpy2(); there is no automatic fallback, so without rpy2 the constructor raises ImportError.

  • RBridge.available() is a static method that returns whether _r_packages() succeeds. It never looks for an Rscript executable.
  • RBridge.check_versions() reads getRversion() and packageVersion("mgcv") through rpy2 and returns (True, "") only for the pinned pair, otherwise (False, reason). It checks nothing about BLAS.
  • _require_rpy2() raises RBridgeError when the bridge is in subprocess mode or the versions do not match. Most typed oracle methods call it first. The rpy2 paths of the dual-mode methods (fit_gam, get_smooth_components, predict_gam, summary_gam) do not, and rely on the caller's skip gate.

Data in and out. Inputs go to R through _to_r_vector (double, integer or logical vectors, with an int32 range check), _to_r_matrix (column-major) and _to_r_dataframe (the pandas converter). Every value that comes back passes through _r_array, which calls np.array(value, copy=True, order="K"). rpy2 exposes R vectors through buffers that np.asarray would wrap without copying, and R's garbage collector may reuse that memory after any later R allocation, so a view could silently change under a test.

Typed methods. The class has about 110 public methods. Simple ones return a dict (for example fit_gam, which fits mgcv::gam and returns coefficients, fitted values, smoothing parameters, EDF, deviance, scale, Vp, the REML score, theta and convergence flags). Many reach mgcv internals with _call_internal (utils::getFromNamespace) or instrument them with tests/r_ast.py, and return frozen dataclasses defined at the top of the module, such as BamDiscreteFit (a pinned bam(discrete=TRUE) fit), SourceLinearAlgebra (R's LAPACK and BLAS identity from La_library()), DiscreteOperatorLayout, SourceStableReparam and SourceWorkingModelTrace. Two representative typed methods: source_slanczos(matrix, k, tol) calls mgcv::slanczos and returns its values, vectors and iteration count; linked_lapack() returns the resolved path of the LAPACK library R links, which r_links_pinned_openblas in tests/helpers.py then identifies by its openblas_get_config string. _preserved_r_seed sets R's seed for a fixture and restores .Random.seed afterwards.

Legacy subprocess mode. RBridge(mode="subprocess") is never selected automatically. In that mode six methods (fit_gam, get_smooth_components, smooth_construct, smooth_construct_list, predict_gam, summary_gam) write CSV files and an R script to a temporary directory and run Rscript with a 120 second timeout; every other method raises RBridgeError through _require_rpy2(). Only tests/test_r_bridge.py constructs this mode, to check that the two modes agree and that typed oracles refuse it.

R is also reached outside the bridge in a few places: tests/test_families.py and tests/test_links.py run Rscript themselves (30 second timeout), and tests/test_summary/test_summary.py and tests/r_ast.py use rpy2 directly.

The sequence below is one validation-matrix cell.

sequenceDiagram
    participant T as TestValidationMatrix
    participant G as GAM
    participant B as RBridge
    participant R as embedded R with mgcv
    participant C as _AssertCollector
    T->>G: fit(data)
    G-->>T: GAMResults
    T->>B: fit_gam(r_formula, data, family)
    B->>B: _to_r_dataframe(data)
    B->>R: mgcv gam(formula, data, family, method)
    R-->>B: fitted R model object
    B->>B: _extract_fit_results_rpy2 copies each field with _r_array
    B-->>T: dict of NumPy arrays and floats
    T->>C: check(name, assertion) for each field
    C->>C: record AssertionError messages
    T->>C: raise_if_any(cell_id)

The R model never leaves the bridge: by the time the test compares anything, every R value has been copied into NumPy-owned memory, and the collector reports all failed fields of the cell in one assertion.

docs.title: Tolerance classes
docs.text:
tests/tolerances.py defines one frozen dataclass and three instances:

Instance rtol atol Files that use it .rtol/.atol references STRICT 1e-10 1e-12 143 about 2,300 MODERATE 1e-4 1e-6 63 about 540 LOOSE 1e-2 1e-4 16 about 50

Counts are from a grep over tests/ at HEAD. In practice STRICT is the default for everything, including most R comparisons of individual routines and matched-state oracles. MODERATE appears for Gaussian final-model R comparisons (r_tolerance, the Gaussian single-smooth cells of the validation matrix) and for derived quantities. LOOSE is used for final-model comparisons of non-Gaussian families against R: r_tolerance() and the validation matrix's _r_tol and _fitted_tol. The module docstring describes the tiers as "CPU self-consistency", "cross-backend" and "JaxGAM vs R mgcv". tests/test_infrastructure.py checks only that the three are ordered. Nothing enforces their use; a few assertions pass literal rtol/atol values.

normalize_column_signs and normalize_symmetric_signs remove the per-column sign ambiguity of eigenvectors before element-wise comparison.

docs.title: The validation matrix
docs.text:
tests/test_validation_matrix.py crosses 15 smooth configurations (SMOOTH_CONFIGS: tp, cr, te, ti, tp_by, cr_by, te_by, re, re_slope, re_mixed, gp, gp_2d, gp_mixed, gp_te, gp_ti) with five families (FAMILIES: gaussian, binomial, poisson, gamma, nb), giving 75 cells (CELL_IDS, ids like tp-gaussian). A SmoothConfig holds the Python formula, the R formula and a data generator key.

In TestValidationMatrix, a class-scoped cell fixture fits the cell with GAM(...).fit(data) on the default dense route and with RBridge().fit_gam, and test_matches_r compares:

Field Tolerance deviance, scale, theta (NB) _r_tol: MODERATE for Gaussian tp, cr, re, re_slope, re_mixed, gp, gp_2d (7 cells); LOOSE for the other 68 fitted values, total EDF _fitted_tol: _r_tol, widened to LOOSE for some tensor and factor-by cells coefficients _r_tol on raw coefficients for cr, re, re_slope only; the other 12 configurations compare fitted values instead (_compare_fitted_not_coefs), because eigenvector signs and flat REML surfaces make coefficients non-unique model.predict() against fitted_values STRICT

gp_mixed compares total model EDF because its parametric x duplicates the GP null space. The gp_2d-gaussian cell is fitted through _fit_matrix_model, which traces the Newton optimizer and prints a GP_GAUSSIAN_TRACE line for CI diagnostics. The rest of the module (37 test functions in all) holds route-level parity tests against pinned R for the streamed, discretized, operator, Gaussian QR and EFS paths.

docs.title: Hard-gate invariants
docs.text:
TestHardGateInvariants in the same module fits every one of the 75 cells again, with no R involved and no skip marker, and test_all_invariants checks eight items through one _AssertCollector:

  1. model.converged.
  2. Deviance is non-negative.
  3. Coefficients, fitted values, linear predictor, scale and deviance are finite.
  4. Every per-smooth EDF is positive, total EDF is at most p and at most n.
  5. Vp is symmetric (STRICT.atol) with no negative eigenvalue.
  6. Every smooth penalty is symmetric with eigenvalues at least -STRICT.atol.
  7. Estimated theta is positive when the family has one.
  8. rank(X) is at least min(X.shape) minus the number of smooth penalties.

Objective monotonicity and Hessian symmetry are not in that class. test_source_loops_hold_the_hard_gates_under_jit in tests/test_fitting/test_dense_source_parity.py replays the source PIRLS loops (Poisson/log, Gamma/log, fixed-theta NB/sqrt) under jax.jit with an increasing iteration cap, checks that the penalized deviance never rises by more than R's divergence threshold, and that the converged penalized Hessian is symmetric positive definite. test_reml_monotonicity in tests/test_fitting/test_newton.py checks that the REML score does not increase at accepted Newton steps. These run in the ordinary shards; there is no separate hard-gate job.

docs.title: _AssertCollector
docs.text: _AssertCollector (in tests/helpers.py) lets one expensive fit feed many named assertions. check(name, fn) runs fn and records an AssertionError message (other exceptions propagate); raise_if_any(label) raises one AssertionError listing every recorded failure. Lambdas cannot contain assert, so check_that(condition, message) raises for boolean conditions. 94 test modules import it.

docs.title: Platform-sensitive tests and replay bounds
docs.text:
Some results depend on the CPU's SIMD maths or on which OpenBLAS kernel family a machine selects. Those tests carry @pytest.mark.platform_sensitive (25 modules, mostly source-parity tests in tests/test_smooths/, tests/test_execution/ discrete and working-model tests, and rank coordinates).

The discretized performance iteration (a port of mgcv's bgam.fitd in R/bam.r) halves a coefficient step when one penalized deviance exceeds another. Near convergence the two can agree to rounding, and pinned R's own outcome there flips under a one-ULP perturbation. Tests in tests/test_execution/test_discrete_regular.py and tests/test_execution/test_discrete_nb.py therefore allow a fit to replay R's step-control outcome at such ties (only where the relative margin is within STRICT.rtol) and then gate every field at STRICT. The number of replayed decisions is bounded per case and per platform:

  • cpu_platform_class() returns macos-arm64, linux-aarch64, x86_64 or x86_64-avx512 (PLATFORM_CLASSES). On x86_64 it reads the CPU's own avx512f flag (from /proc/cpuinfo or sysctl), never the runner name.
  • check_replay_bound(table_name, table, key, measured) looks up {platform class: (bound, measured count)} for the case. A case absent from the table must need zero replays. A listed case on a class with no entry fails and prints the measured count, unless the case lists OTHER_CLASSES_NEED_NONE.
  • Every check is appended to REPLAY_COUNT_RECORDS, and pytest_terminal_summary prints them, so a passing run still reports its counts.

Counts are per platform because the residual last-bit differences between CPU families change how many ties occur; the tables (for example _REVIEWED_TIE_REPLAYS) record each reviewed count with the CI run that measured it. tests/test_replay_bounds.py tests the classifier and the bound logic.

When the -m expression names platform_sensitive, pytest_report_header prints platform_report_lines(): machine, CPU model, AVX-512 flags, NumPy's AVX-512 dispatch, and the OpenBLAS configuration and core of the provider wheel and of R's LAPACK.

docs.title: Pytest markers
docs.text:
pyproject.toml registers two markers and sets no default command-line options:

  • platform_sensitive: selected by make test-platform-sensitive-ci; also runs in the ordinary shards.
  • slow: one use (tests/test_execution/test_operator_bulk_variance.py); no target deselects it.

docs.title: Skipping without the pinned R
docs.text:
R-dependent tests skip unless rpy2 loads the pinned R and mgcv:

  • the r_bridge fixture skips on not RBridge.available() or a failed check_versions() (the skip message suggests make test);
  • 50 modules decorate tests with @pytest.mark.skipif(not r_available(), ...) (190 decorators);
  • tests/test_families.py, tests/test_links.py and tests/test_r_bridge.py define a local _r_available(), and a few tests call pytest.importorskip("rpy2...").

make install runs uv sync --extra dev, which does not install rpy2 (the r extra), so local runs skip these tests. Known cases that do not skip:

  • tests/test_execution/test_discrete_score.py: test_bridge_invalid_inputs_reject_before_r_process (8 cases) constructs RBridge() with no gate, which raises ImportError without rpy2.
  • tests/test_execution/test_efs_stream_provider.py: test_live_source_provider_score_theta_and_fisher_contractions (3 cases) is decorated skipif(not r_available, ...) without calling the function, so the condition is always false and the test reaches RBridge(mode="rpy2").
  • tests/test_r_bridge.py: TestRBridgeAvailability gates on RBridge.available() only and asserts the pinned versions, so it fails by design when rpy2 loads a different R.

docs.title: The Docker test image
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A["r-base<br/>FROM rocker/r-ver:4.5.2<br/>apt build libraries for rpy2"] --> B["r-deps<br/>renv::restore of docker/renv.lock"]
    B --> C["py-deps<br/>uv 0.9.15, uv python install 3.13<br/>uv sync --extra dev --extra r --no-install-project"]
    C --> D["test<br/>OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1<br/>git, copy jaxgam/ tests/ scripts/<br/>uv sync --extra dev --extra r"]
    D --> E["CMD uv run pytest -x --tb=short"]

Each stage is cached until its inputs change: R version, docker/renv.lock, pyproject.toml/uv.lock, then the source tree.

  • docker/renv.lock pins R 4.5.2, mgcv 1.9-3, Matrix 1.7-1, lattice 0.22-6 and nlme 3.1-166.
  • ENV UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE=only-managed, R_HOME=/usr/local/lib/R and LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/lib/R/lib:... let rpy2 build against the rocker R.
  • ENV OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1: the embedded R, SciPy and the pinned LAPACK provider link threaded OpenBLAS, whose reduction order changes with the core count, so R reference values would differ between a local image and a CI runner. One thread gives every R comparison the same reference arithmetic. See Numerics and platform.
  • git is installed for minimal_git_checkout. Only jaxgam/, tests/, scripts/, pyproject.toml and uv.lock are copied; .dockerignore excludes .git, .venv, .github, caches and site/.
  • The suite runs only on the image's Python 3.13 and only on x86_64 Linux in CI, although requires-python is >=3.11.

docs.title: Makefile targets
docs.text:
make help lists targets with a ## description; its pattern excludes digits, so the test-pr82-* targets do not appear, nor do test-operator-fit and test-operator-fit-local, which have no description.

Group Targets Setup and lint (local, uv) install, check, format, lint (ruff check, ruff format --check, vulture), pre-commit, pre-commit-install Local tests test-local (uv run pytest), plus focused local runs such as test-operator-local, test-iterative-local, test-operator-fit-local, test-operator-bulk-local, test-operator-adapters-local, test-scaling-memory, test-discrete-approximation-harness Docker, builds the image first docker-build (depends on colima-start), test (image CMD in one container, stops at the first failure, no coverage), test-file FILE=..., test-cov (line coverage only), and focused runs such as test-discrete, test-continuous-discrete, test-pivoted-cholesky, test-efs-*, test-nb-*, test-operator, test-iterative, test-operator-adapters, test-pr82-* CI, in an already built image test-cov-shard-ci, coverage-combine-ci, test-gaussian-ci, test-platform-sensitive-ci, test-efs-recovery-ci, test-nb-public-ci, test-regular-public-ci, and test-cov-ci (called by no workflow) Benchmarks and fixtures benchmark-* (wrappers for scripts/benchmark_*.py), efs-fixture OUTPUT=...

test-operator-fit builds with its own docker build --target test and skips colima-start. Override DOCKER_IMAGE, DOCKER_TAG, TEST_SHARD and TEST_SHARDS on the command line.

docs.title: CI: the test workflow
docs.text:
.github/workflows/test.yml runs on pull requests and on pushes to main; a newer run cancels an older one for the same ref. Every job runs on ubuntu-latest.

flowchart TD
    EV["pull_request or push to main"] --> CH["changes<br/>dorny/paths-filter output code"]
    CH -->|"code is true"| LI["lint<br/>make lint"]
    LI --> TF["test-full<br/>8 shards, make test-cov-shard-ci"]
    LI --> TG["test-gaussian<br/>make test-gaussian-ci"]
    LI --> TP["test-platform-sensitive<br/>8 replicas, make test-platform-sensitive-ci"]
    LI --> TE["test-efs-recovery<br/>make test-efs-recovery-ci"]
    LI --> TN["test-nb-public<br/>make test-nb-public-ci"]
    LI --> TR["test-regular-public<br/>make test-regular-public-ci"]
    TF --> CO["coverage<br/>make coverage-combine-ci, Codecov upload"]
    LI --> GA["gate<br/>fails on any failure or cancelled"]
    TF --> GA
    CO --> GA
    TG --> GA
    TP --> GA
    TE --> GA
    TN --> GA
    TR --> GA

Every test job also lists changes in needs and runs only when its code output is true; coverage depends on test-full alone; gate runs if: always().

  • changes. The code filter matches jaxgam/**, tests/**, pyproject.toml, uv.lock, Dockerfile, Makefile and .github/workflows/test.yml. It omits scripts/** and docker/renv.lock, although the image copies the first and restores the second, and it omits .pre-commit-config.yaml and docs/**.
  • lint. uv sync --extra dev, then make lint.
  • test-full. An eight-entry matrix (shard: [1..8], fail-fast: false). Each entry builds jaxgam-test:ci with the docker/build-push-action GitHub action from the GitHub Actions layer cache, which only shard 1 writes, then runs make test-cov-shard-ci DOCKER_TAG=ci TEST_SHARD=<n> TEST_SHARDS=<job total> and uploads coverage/coverage-data.<n>. To change the shard count, change the matrix list only.
  • coverage. Downloads every shard's data and runs make coverage-combine-ci, then uploads coverage/coverage.xml to Codecov.
  • Focused jobs. test-gaussian (the gp_2d-gaussian matrix cell with its optimizer trace), test-efs-recovery, test-nb-public and test-regular-public each run one *-ci target with -s -x. They re-run tests that are also in the shards, with output visible.
  • test-platform-sensitive. Eight replicas of pytest -p no:cacheprovider -m platform_sensitive with one BLAS thread. One full-suite run lands on a single random x86_64 runner type; eight replicas make sampling both the AVX-512 and non-AVX-512 types likely, not certain.
  • gate. Fails only when a needed job's result is failure or cancelled. A skipped job passes, so a change confined to paths outside the filter passes the gate without running tests.

docs.title: Sharding and coverage
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A["pytest collects every test item"] --> B["pytest_collection_modifyitems"]
    B --> C["parse_shard reads JAXGAM_TEST_SHARD"]
    C -->|"unset or blank"| D["run the whole suite"]
    C -->|"i/N"| E["Shard.owns per item<br/>shard_of: crc32 of nodeid mod N plus 1"]
    C -->|"malformed"| X["ValueError"]
    E -->|"owned"| F["kept items run<br/>--cov-branch --cov-fail-under=0"]
    E -->|"not owned"| G["pytest_deselected"]
    F --> H["COVERAGE_FILE coverage-data.i<br/>upload-artifact"]
    H --> I["coverage job downloads all shards"]
    I --> J["coverage combine"]
    J --> K["coverage xml"]
    K --> L["coverage report<br/>fail_under 80 on the combined total"]
    L --> M["Codecov upload"]

A test's shard depends only on its pytest node id, through zlib.crc32, which is stable across processes, platforms and Python versions (the built-in hash is salted per process). The N shards of one commit therefore partition the suite: every test runs exactly once. Assignment is per item, so two parametrizations of one test can land in different shards. tests/test_sharding.py pins two CRC-32 values so a change of hash fails loudly. Each shard records statement and branch coverage without a threshold; fail_under = 80 in pyproject.toml applies to the combined data. Local make test-cov measures line coverage only, so its number differs from CI's.

docs.title: Docs and publish workflows
docs.text:
• .github/workflows/docs.yml runs on pushes to main that touch docs/**, mkdocs.yml or jaxgam/**, or on manual dispatch. It installs mkdocs-material and mkdocstrings[python] with pip on Python 3.11, installs the package with --no-deps for docstring introspection, and runs mkdocs gh-deploy --force. No Makefile target builds the docs.
  • .github/workflows/publish.yml runs when a release is published. The publish job sets the pyproject.toml version from the tag (without a leading v), runs uv build and publishes to PyPI; backmerge commits the same version bump to main.

docs.title: Pre-commit hooks
docs.text: .pre-commit-config.yaml configures ruff with --fix, ruff-format (ruff-pre-commit v0.15.1) and vulture jaxgam --min-confidence 80 (vulture v2.14). No hook runs tests. make lint and CI run the same tools without --fix.

docs.title: Key types
docs.text:
classDiagram
    class ToleranceClass {
        +rtol float
        +atol float
        +label str
    }
    class RBridge {
        +mode str
        +available() bool
        +check_versions() tuple
        +fit_gam(formula, data, family, method) dict
        +source_slanczos(matrix, k, tol) dict

        +source_linear_algebra() SourceLinearAlgebra
        +fit_bam_discrete_fixed_sp(formula, data, sp) BamDiscreteFit
        -_require_rpy2() None
        -_to_r_dataframe(data) Any
    }
    class RBridgeError
    class SourceLinearAlgebra {
        +lapack_library str
        +lapack_version str
        +blas_library str
        +openblas_config str
        +lapack_is_openblas(prefix) bool
    }
    class BamDiscreteFit {
        +coefficients ndarray
        +fitted_values ndarray
        +deviance float
        +smoothing_params ndarray
        +converged bool
    }
    class _AssertCollector {
        +failures list~str~
        +check(name, fn) None
        +raise_if_any(label) None
    }
    class Shard {
        +index int
        +count int
        +owns(nodeid) bool
    }
    Exception <|-- RBridgeError
    RBridge ..> RBridgeError : raises
    RBridge ..> SourceLinearAlgebra : returns
    RBridge ..> BamDiscreteFit : returns

ToleranceClass and Shard are frozen dataclasses; SourceLinearAlgebra and BamDiscreteFit stand for the roughly twenty frozen result dataclasses at the top of tests/r_bridge.py. RBridge holds the rpy2 handles _ro, _mgcv, _base, _stats and _utils, shared through _r_packages().

docs.title: Rules and invariants
docs.text:
• R values are copied. Every R-to-NumPy conversion in the bridge goes through _r_array; never use np.asarray on an rpy2 object. tests/test_r_bridge.py exercises the bridge's own contracts.
  • The pinned pair is R 4.5.2 with mgcv 1.9-3. check_versions() and _require_rpy2() enforce it; docker/renv.lock and the rocker/r-ver tag provide it. Changing either means updating _REQUIRED_R_VERSION or _REQUIRED_MGCV_VERSION and re-validating every R comparison.
  • The default bridge launches no process. test_default_reference_never_launches_rscript in tests/test_r_bridge.py patches subprocess.run to fail.
  • Use the tolerance classes. Import STRICT, MODERATE or LOOSE from tests/tolerances.py rather than writing literals.
  • Shards partition the suite. tests/test_sharding.py checks that each node id has exactly one owner, the pinned CRC-32 values, comparable shard sizes and the parsing of JAXGAM_TEST_SHARD.
  • Hard gates hold for every matrix cell, with or without R. TestHardGateInvariants in tests/test_validation_matrix.py.
  • Replays are bounded per platform. A case not listed in a replay table must need zero replays everywhere (check_replay_bound, tested by tests/test_replay_bounds.py).
  • Reference results run with one BLAS thread in the image and in the platform-sensitive target.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• A test that constructs RBridge() outside the r_bridge fixture or an r_available() gate errors instead of skipping on a machine without rpy2 (see the known cases above). Write skipif(not r_available(), ...) with the call; skipif(not r_available, ...) never skips.
  • tests/test_r_bridge.py availability tests fail, rather than skip, when rpy2 loads an R other than 4.5.2.
  • make test stops at the first failure and runs everything in one container; CI runs eight shards without -x. A local make test is slow.
  • Changes to scripts/** or docker/renv.lock alone do not trigger lint or tests in CI, and the gate still passes.
  • make test-local sets no BLAS thread variables, so R comparisons on a many-core machine can differ in the last bits from CI. Use the Docker targets for R parity work.
  • A new platform-sensitive tie case on a platform class without an entry fails with its measured count; add a reviewed entry rather than widening a tolerance.
  • The module docstring of tests/test_validation_matrix.py and the TestHardGateInvariants docstring cite design-document sections that are no longer in the repository.

docs.title: Where to change things
docs.text:
• Add an R oracle: add a typed method to RBridge in tests/r_bridge.py that starts with self._require_rpy2(), converts inputs with _to_r_vector/_to_r_matrix/_to_r_dataframe, copies outputs with _r_array, and returns a frozen dataclass or a dict. Add its own test to tests/test_r_bridge.py.
  • Add a validation-matrix configuration: add an entry to SMOOTH_CONFIGS, a _make_*_data generator and a branch in _get_data, and decide its membership in _r_tol, _fitted_tol and _compare_fitted_not_coefs. The hard gates pick it up automatically.
  • Add a family to the matrix: extend FAMILIES and the data generators.
  • Mark a test platform-sensitive: add @pytest.mark.platform_sensitive; it then runs in the eight replicas as well as in a shard.
  • Add a per-platform replay table: follow _REVIEWED_TIE_REPLAYS in tests/test_execution/test_discrete_regular.py and call check_replay_bound inside an _AssertCollector check.
  • Change the shard count: edit the shard matrix list in .github/workflows/test.yml; TEST_SHARDS follows strategy.job-total.
  • Add a focused CI job: add a *-ci target to the Makefile, a job to .github/workflows/test.yml that needs changes and lint, and add the job to gate's needs.
  • Change pinned R packages: edit docker/renv.lock (and the rocker/r-ver tag in the Dockerfile for R itself), then the version constants in tests/r_bridge.py.

docs.text:

It is not maintained: the file names, line numbers, counts and "current state" descriptions in it are those of the repository at that time, and it may refer to documents that were later removed from the repository (for example docs/design.md and docs/R_SOURCE_MAP.md, which remain in the git history). For how the code is organized today see the architecture pages; for how to use the package see the user guide and the API reference.

docs.title: Test Suite Cleanup: Implementation Plan
docs.text: Historical record. This document was written while this piece of work was being designed and built, and is kept as a record of it. It is not maintained: the file names, line numbers, counts and "current state" descriptions in it are those of the repository at that time, and it may refer to documents that were later removed from the repository (for example docs/design.md and docs/R_SOURCE_MAP.md, which remain in the git history). For how the code is organized today see the architecture pages; for how to use the package see the user guide and the API reference.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Reduce the jaxgam test suite from 2,151 collected tests / 30,020 lines to roughly 1,250 collected tests / ~27,000 lines while preserving every R-bridge comparison, hard-gate invariant, finite-difference AD validation, and documented regression test.

Branch: single working branch off main for the whole cleanup; one PR at the end. Audit reference: scratch/audit_unit_tests_v3.md (synthesis of v1 collection-level audit and v2 per-file agent audit) Per-file cut lists: scratch/audit_unit_tests_v2.md Mandatory-keep regression tests: scratch/audit_unit_tests_v2.md §"Regression Test Inventory"

Scope decision (resolved): Random effects (bs="re") are in v1.0. CLAUDE.md has been updated to remove RE from the "What Is NOT in v1.0" list. All RE tests remain in the default suite.

docs.title: Working Model — How This Plan Is Executed
docs.text:
One PR total. The entire cleanup ships as a single pull request from one working branch.

Work is split into discrete commits, not PRs. Each numbered "Commit" below is a self-contained unit of work that an agent executes end-to-end. Multiple commits land on the same branch in sequence.

The agent must NOT run git commit or git push. The user commits manually after reviewing each unit. The agent's job per commit is:

  1. Read the unit's "What to do" and "Files touched" sections.
  2. Make the code/test changes.
  3. Run make test-cov for validation. This single command runs the full suite in Docker (with R 4.5.2 + mgcv 1.9-3) and enforces the ≥80% coverage gate — do not also run make test or make test-local, they are redundant and slow.
  4. Stop and surface the results to the user (file list, test count delta, coverage delta, validation output). The user reviews, commits, then triggers the next unit.

If a unit's validation fails, fix the issue in the same unit before handing off — do not start the next unit on a broken tree. If the fix changes the scope of the unit, note that in the handoff so the user can adjust the commit message accordingly.

The user manages: branching off main, commit messages, force-pushes (if any), and the final PR. The agent stays inside the working tree.

docs.title: Project Tooling
docs.text:
Per CLAUDE.md, this project uses uv for dependency management and make for task orchestration. All Python execution must go through uv run.

Task Command Validation (use this — only this) make test-cov Count collected tests uv run pytest --collect-only -q tests \| tail -1 Count source-level tests grep -rc "def test_" tests \| awk -F: '{s+=$2} END {print s}' Lint make lint Pre-commit make pre-commit

make test-cov runs the full suite in Docker (R 4.5.2 + mgcv 1.9-3) with coverage and the --cov-fail-under=80 gate. It is a strict superset of make test and make test-local plus the coverage check, so the agent should run it instead of all three. make test and make test-local exist for human use and are not part of the agent validation loop.

docs.title: Success Metrics
docs.text:
Track all three after every commit:

  1. Collected-test count (pytest --collect-only) — primary indicator of CI speed impact.
  2. Source-level test count (grep -c "def test_") — indicator of maintenance surface.
  3. Coverage percentage (must stay ≥80% per CLAUDE.md §Testing Rules).

Baseline (verified 2026-05-11 on branch clean-unit-tests):

  • Collected: 2,151
  • Source-level: ~1,082
  • Coverage: TBD — capture in Phase 0.

Targets after full execution:

  • Collected: ≤ 1,250 (~42% reduction)
  • Source-level: ≤ 800 (~26% reduction)
  • Coverage: ≥ 80% per module

docs.title: Phase 0 — Pre-flight: Baseline Capture (DONE)
docs.text:
Goal: Record current state so each subsequent commit can show measurable progress.

Run on a clean checkout of the working branch (before any cleanup commits):

uv run pytest --collect-only -q tests | tail -3
grep -rc "def test_" tests | grep -v ":0$" | awk -F: '{s+=$2} END {print s}'
time make test-cov 2>&1 | tail -25

make test-cov produces both the coverage report (use the totals line) and the wall-clock when wrapped in time.

Record the four numbers (collected, source-level, coverage %, wall-clock) in this file (or a BASELINE.md next to it). Every subsequent unit references them.

Exit criteria: Baseline metrics captured in the repo so every commit's handoff can show measurable progress against them.

docs.title: Phase 1 — Validation Matrix Consolidation (Commit A) (DONE)
docs.text:
Goal: Reduce tests/test_validation_matrix.py from 15 methods/cell to 2 methods/cell. Saves ~650 collected tests — the single largest reduction in the suite.

Audit reference: v3 §1.

docs.title: Current structure
docs.text:
tests/test_validation_matrix.py has:

  • 50 cells (10 smooth configs × 5 families: gaussian, poisson, binomial, gamma, nb), parameterized via fixtures.
  • TestValidationMatrix: 7 R-comparison methods (test_deviance_vs_r, test_fitted_values_vs_r, test_edf_vs_r, test_scale_vs_r, test_coefficients_vs_r, test_self_prediction_roundtrip, test_theta_vs_r).
  • TestHardGateInvariants: 8 invariant methods (test_convergence, test_deviance_non_negative, test_no_nan_in_converged, test_edf_bounds, test_vp_symmetric_psd, test_penalty_psd, test_theta_positive, test_model_matrix_rank).
  • Total: 50 × 15 = 750 collected tests.

docs.title: Target structure
docs.text:
class TestValidationMatrix:
    def test_matches_r(self, cell):
        # One R fit + one Python fit; all 7 quantities asserted via collector.
        ...

class TestHardGateInvariants:
    def test_all_invariants(self, fitted_model):
        # One model; all 8 invariants asserted via collector.
        ...

Total: 50 × 2 = 100 collected tests.

docs.title: Implementation steps
docs.text:
1. Add a failure-accumulator helper in tests/helpers.py:
class _AssertCollector:
    def __init__(self): self.failures: list[str] = []
    def check(self, name, fn):
        try: fn()
        except AssertionError as e: self.failures.append(f"{name}: {e}")
    def raise_if_any(self, label):
        if self.failures:
            raise AssertionError(
                f"{label} failed:\n  - " + "\n  - ".join(self.failures)
            )

This keeps failure messages debuggable — when consolidation breaks one quantity, the test report still names every broken quantity, not just the first.

  1. Rewrite TestValidationMatrix to one test_matches_r method. Body computes the R reference once, then calls collector.check(...) for each of the 7 quantities, finally collector.raise_if_any(cell_id).

  2. Rewrite TestHardGateInvariants to one test_all_invariants method following the same pattern over the 8 invariants.

  3. Do NOT cut test_self_prediction_roundtrip (v2 flagged it, but it's the CoefficientMap roundtrip check — CLAUDE.md §Common Pitfalls #3 calls this out as load-bearing). Fold it into the consolidated test_matches_r.

  4. Per-cell speedup: since each consolidated test fits once instead of 15 times, also verify the R fit is memoized per cell using a session- or class-scoped fixture. If not, add the memoization in this commit.

docs.text:
• Modify: tests/test_validation_matrix.py
  • Modify: tests/helpers.py (add _AssertCollector)

docs.text:

  • pytest --collect-only -q tests/test_validation_matrix.py reports 100 tests (down from 750).
  • Coverage of jaxgam/ does not drop.
  • Wall-clock for the file shorter (fewer R fits per cell).

docs.text:

docs.title: Phase 2 — R-Parity Ownership Sweep (Commit B) (DONE)
docs.text:
Goal: Assign each R-parity behavior to exactly one canonical file; delete the duplicates.

Audit reference: v3 §2.

docs.title: Ownership rules
docs.text: File Owns Does not own tests/test_validation_matrix.py Broad family × smooth R parity (consolidated test_matches_r) Layer internals tests/test_fitting/test_newton.py Optimizer internals: newton_optimize, objective traces, gradient/Hessian behavior, convergence diagnostics Final-model R parity tests/test_fitting/test_pirls.py PIRLS internals: step-halving, offset equivalence, working-response behavior, curvature regressions Family × R parity tests/test_predict/test_predict.py New-data prediction & SE vs R Self-prediction roundtrip (matrix owns) tests/test_summary/test_summary.py Summary tables, EDF attribution, p-values, Davies Final-model parity tests/test_api/test_gam.py Public API orchestration, routing, input validation, fixed-sp Family × R parity, hard-gate copies

docs.title: Implementation steps
docs.text:
1. For each non-matrix file, walk every test that calls r_bridge. For each:
  2. Asserting on a layer-internal quantity (intermediate newton_optimize output, PIRLS working response, etc.)? → keep.

  3. Asserting only on GAMResults fields the matrix now owns (deviance, fitted_values, edf, scale, coefficients, theta) or any hard-gate invariant? → delete.

  4. Apply specific cuts validated by this sweep:

  5. test_api/test_gam.py::TestEndToEnd::test_gaussian_basic, test_all_fields_finite, test_vp_symmetric_psd.
  6. test_fitting/test_newton.py::TestInvariants::test_deviance_non_negative, test_no_nan_in_converged, test_edf_bounds.

  7. test_results.py self-prediction roundtrips that duplicate the matrix.

  8. Run the audit grep:

grep -rl "r_bridge\.fit_gam\|RBridge(" tests/ | \
  xargs grep -l "deviance\|fitted_values\|edf\|coefficients"

Each file in the result must own at least one behavior from the table. If not, all R comparisons in it are duplicates.

docs.title: Phase 3 — File-Level Cleanup Commits (Commits C through H)
docs.text:
Goal: Apply v2's per-file cut lists. One commit per logical group. Order is biggest mechanical wins first; most numerically sensitive last.

Audit reference: v2 (each section below maps to v2's per-file findings).

For every commit in this phase:

  • Continue on the same working branch (no new branches).
  • Use the cut lists in scratch/audit_unit_tests_v2.md as the work list.
  • Do NOT cut anything in v2's "Regression Test Inventory — MUST PRESERVE" table. Treat that table as a hard allow-list.
  • Run make test-cov after the changes (single command — full Docker suite + R + coverage gate). Do not also run make test or make test-local.
  • When handing off to the user, surface: (1) files touched, (2) test count before/after, (3) coverage delta, (4) make test-cov output. The user uses this for the commit message.
  • Do not run git commit or git push.

Commits in this phase touch disjoint file sets, so the order does not matter for correctness — but executing in the listed order keeps the most sensitive cleanup (fitting) last, after the others have validated the workflow.

docs.title: Phase 4 — Final Sweep (Commit I) (DONE)
docs.text: Goal: After phases 1–3, walk the suite once more and confirm ownership and coverage. This is the last commit before the user opens the PR.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Re-run baseline measurement commands from Phase 0. Confirm targets hit.

  2. Grep for remaining R-bridge duplication:

grep -rl "r_bridge\.fit_gam\|RBridge(" tests/ | \
  xargs grep -l "deviance\|fitted_values\|edf\|coefficients"

For each file in the result, confirm it owns at least one unique behavior per Phase 2's ownership table. Delete any remaining duplicates.

  1. Run validation:
make test-cov

This runs the full Docker suite (with R 4.5.2 + mgcv 1.9-3) and enforces the ≥80% coverage gate. Do not also run make test or make test-local. If any module dropped below 80%, investigate which test was carrying it and either restore it or add a targeted replacement.

  1. Verify regression-test preservation. Grep the test tree for each entry in v2's "MUST PRESERVE" table:
grep -rn "TestFamilyStaticCacheKey\|TestNBJITCacheReuse\|test_halved_step_curvature_matches_accepted_mu\|test_cholesky_stability" tests/

Each must still exist.

  1. Update CLAUDE.md §Testing Rules if any conventions changed during cleanup (e.g., a new helper or parameterization pattern that should be documented).

docs.title: Exit criteria
docs.text:
• Collected count ≤ 1,250.
  • Source-level count ≤ 800.
  • Coverage ≥ 80%.
  • No R-bridge behavior tested in more than one file (per ownership table).
  • All "MUST PRESERVE" regression tests still exist.
  • Agent stops and hands off to user. The user reviews, commits, and opens the PR against main.

docs.title: Risks specific to this cleanup
docs.text:
1. Consolidated validation matrix loses failure granularity. Mitigation: the _AssertCollector helper in Phase 1 accumulates failures so the test message names every broken quantity, not just the first.

  2. Deleting an R-parity test before another file owns it. Mitigation: Phase 2 explicitly enforces the ownership table before file-level cleanup begins. The grep-based audit in Phase 4 catches anything missed.

  3. Cutting a test that uniquely covers a code path under JIT. Mitigation: coverage check after every commit; investigate any per-module drop below 80%.

  4. Regression tests look like toothless tests. Mitigation: v2's "Regression Test Inventory" is referenced from every commit's handoff notes. The user cross-references before committing.

docs.title: Rollback plan
docs.text:
Because each commit lands one logical change on a single working branch, individual commits can be reverted with git revert <sha> without disturbing others. Commits C–H touch disjoint files; only Commit B (ownership sweep) and Commit I (final sweep) depend on earlier work.

Commit A (validation matrix consolidation) is the most disruptive single change. If it causes problems, rollback is git revert <commit-A-sha> — only one file is affected.

docs.title: Sequencing Summary
docs.text:
All commits land on a single working branch off main. The agent executes one unit at a time, validates, hands off; the user commits manually before triggering the next unit.

Phase 0 (baseline capture — no commit)
        │
Commit A  Phase 1 — validation matrix consolidation   ── ~650 collected tests
Commit B  Phase 2 — R-parity ownership sweep          ── ~30-50 source tests
        │
Phase 3 (file-level cleanups; sequential commits on the same branch)
        ├─ Commit C  Families & Links                       ── ~53-58 source tests
        ├─ Commit D  Smooths                                 ── ~68 source tests
        ├─ Commit E  Penalties/Constraints/Linalg/Edge/Validation ── ~44 source tests
        ├─ Commit F  API/Results/Predict/Post-est            ── ~30 source tests
        ├─ Commit G  Summary/Plot/Formula/Bridge/Registry/Infra ── ~39-51 source tests
        └─ Commit H  Fitting (most sensitive — do last)      ── ~32-40 source tests
        │
Commit I  Phase 4 — final sweep + ownership verification + coverage check
        │
User opens single PR against `main`.

Commits A and B must complete before Phase 3 starts (Commit B depends on the matrix being the canonical owner, established in A). Phase 3 commits touch disjoint files, so the order within Phase 3 is for safety (most sensitive last), not correctness.

docs.text:
Met when the user opens the single PR for this cleanup:

docs.text:
1. Overview
  2. R Reference Implementation Analysis
  3. Mathematical Specification

  6. Formula Parsing

docs.title: 1.1 What Are Dense Random Effects?
docs.text:
In mgcv, s(x, bs="re") treats random effects as penalized smooth terms. The smoothing-penalty duality gives random effects the same mathematical treatment as splines: coefficients are penalized by an identity matrix (ridge penalty), and the smoothing parameter λ estimates σ²_ε / σ²_b (the ratio of residual to random-effect variance).

This is not a new estimation method — it exploits the existing PIRLS + REML/ML infrastructure. The smooth's penalty matrix is I_k (identity), making it full rank with null_space_dim = 0. No centering or identifiability constraints are needed because the full-rank penalty makes the term inherently identifiable.

docs.title: 1.2 Use Cases
docs.text:
Random effects with bs="re" support any combination of variables:

Formula Model matrix Interpretation s(g, bs="re") model.matrix(~g - 1) Random intercepts by group g s(x, g, bs="re") model.matrix(~x:g - 1) Random slopes of x by group g s(g1, g2, bs="re") model.matrix(~g1:g2 - 1) Random interaction of g1 and g2 s(x, bs="re") model.matrix(~x - 1) Ridge-penalized numeric effect

Variables can be any mixture of factors and numerics. The model matrix is always the interaction ~v1:v2:...:vN - 1.

docs.title: 1.3 Scope
docs.text:
In scope: - RandomEffectSmooth class with dense basis and identity penalty - Registration in smooth registry as "re" - Correct interaction with constraint pipeline (skip centering + gam_side) - Prediction with unseen factor levels (zero contribution) - Summary p-value type adjustment (type_=1 for RE terms) - Full R comparison tests (basis, penalty, fitted model)

Out of scope (deferred): - Sparse random effects (for high-cardinality factors, deferred to sparse-CPU path) - bs="fs" (factor-smooth interactions — different mechanism, §5.6 design doc) - Custom precision matrices via xt$S argument (future enhancement) - gam.vcomp() variance component extraction (future enhancement) - Tensor-like RE setup (re as tensor.smooth.spec — only used in bam(discrete=TRUE))

docs.title: 1.4 Dense-Only Constraint
docs.text:
Per CLAUDE.md, v1.0 is dense-only. The basis matrix X for a factor with L levels is an n × L dense indicator matrix (mostly zeros). This is memory-inefficient for large L but correct.

The practical limit is the p ≤ n constraint (Section 4). Dense RE works well for L up to a few hundred levels.

docs.title: 2.1 Source Location
docs.text: The canonical R implementation is in: - Constructor: $MGCV_SOURCE/R/smooth.r lines 2571-2646 (smooth.construct.re.smooth.spec) - Predict: $MGCV_SOURCE/R/smooth.r lines 2650-2663 (Predict.matrix.random.effect) - Documentation: $MGCV_SOURCE/man/smooth.construct.re.smooth.spec.Rd - Examples: $MGCV_SOURCE/man/random.effects.Rd

docs.title: 2.2 Constructor Algorithm
docs.text:
smooth.construct.re.smooth.spec <- function(object, data, knots) {
  # 1. Build interaction formula
  form <- as.formula(paste("~", paste(object$term, collapse=":"), "-1"))

  # 2. Build model matrix
  object$X <- model.matrix(form, data)
  object$bs.dim <- ncol(object$X)

  # 3. Construct penalty (identity by default)
  object$S <- list(diag(object$bs.dim))
  object$rank <- object$bs.dim

  # 4. Set key flags
  object$null.space.dim <- 0
  object$C <- matrix(0, 0, ncol(object$X))   # no centering constraint
  object$side.constrain <- FALSE              # skip gam.side()
  object$random <- TRUE                       # p-value test type
  object$noterp <- TRUE                       # skip SVD reparameterization
  object$plot.me <- TRUE
  object$te.ok <- 2

  class(object) <- "random.effect"
  object
}

Key observations: 1. The k argument is ignored — bs.dim is always ncol(X) 2. The penalty is always the identity matrix (full rank, no null space) 3. No centering constraint (C is empty) 4. Explicitly opted out of gam.side() identifiability checks 5. The $random flag signals different p-value computation in summary

docs.title: 2.3 Predict Method
docs.text:
Predict.matrix.random.effect <- function(object, data) {
  data <- data[names needed for form]
  X <- model.matrix(object$form, model.frame(object$form, data, na.action=na.pass))
  X[!is.finite(X)] <- 0   # unseen levels → NA → 0
  X
}

Key: unseen factor levels produce NAs in the model matrix, which are then zeroed out. This means predictions for new factor levels contribute zero. R's predict.gam() sets factor observations to NA if they have levels not present in the training data.

docs.title: 2.4 smoothCon() Integration
docs.text: When smoothCon() processes an RE smooth: - The empty C matrix means no centering absorption occurs - scale.penalty=TRUE still applies penalty normalization (divide by maXX) - The smooth is returned as-is except for normalization

docs.title: 3.1 Model Matrix Construction
docs.text:
For variables v1, v2, ..., vp, the model matrix X is equivalent to model.matrix(~v1:v2:...:vp - 1):

Single factor g with L levels: 

X[i, j] = 1  if g[i] == level_j
X[i, j] = 0  otherwise
Shape: (n, L). This is a one-hot indicator matrix.

Factor × factor g1 (L1 levels) × g2 (L2 levels): 

X[i, (j1-1)*L2 + j2] = 1  if g1[i] == level_j1 AND g2[i] == level_j2
Shape: (n, L1 × L2). This is a one-hot indicator for each combination.

Numeric × factor x (numeric) × g (L levels): 

X[i, j] = x[i]  if g[i] == level_j
X[i, j] = 0     otherwise
Shape: (n, L). Each column holds the numeric value for observations at that level.

Numeric × numeric x1 × x2: 

X[i, 1] = x1[i] * x2[i]
Shape: (n, 1). This is just the elementwise product (rarely used in practice).

docs.title: 3.2 Penalty Matrix
docs.text:
S = I_k    (k × k identity matrix)

This is the ridge penalty. It penalizes all coefficients equally with no unpenalized null space (null_space_dim = 0, rank = k).

The smoothing parameter λ acts as: 

σ²_b = σ²_ε / λ

where σ²_b is the random effect variance and σ²_ε is the residual variance. Large λ → small random effect variance → coefficients shrunk toward zero.

docs.title: 3.3 Normalization
docs.text:
Like all smooths, the penalty is normalized by smoothCon(): 

s_scale = ||S||_1 / ||X||_∞²
S_normalized = S / s_scale

For the identity penalty, ||S||_1 = 1, so: 

s_scale = 1.0 / ||X||_∞²

docs.title: 4.1 mgcv Enforcement
docs.text:
mgcv enforces p ≤ n for penalized models (mgcv.r line 236):

if (ncol(M$X) > nrow(M$X)) {
    if (m > 0) stop("Penalized model matrix must have no more columns than rows")
}

This is a full-model check, not per-smooth. The total number of columns across intercept + parametric + all smooth bases must not exceed n.

docs.title: 4.2 Practical Limits
docs.text:
For a model y ~ s(g, bs="re") + s(x): - Intercept: 1 column - s(x): ~10 columns (default k) - s(g, bs="re"): L columns (one per factor level) - Constraint: L + 11 ≤ n, so max L ≈ n - 11

For factor interactions s(g1, g2, bs="re"): - Columns = L1 × L2 - Max product of levels ≈ n - (other model columns)

docs.title: 4.3 No Explicit Per-Smooth Cardinality Check
docs.text:
There is no per-smooth cardinality check in mgcv. The constraint emerges naturally from the full model matrix dimension check at fit time.

Our implementation: We should validate p ≤ n in the fitting layer (where it's already checked) rather than adding a smooth-level limit. However, we should add a helpful error message when an RE smooth creates a model matrix wider than the data.

docs.title: 5.1 Class: RandomEffectSmooth
docs.text:
# jaxgam/smooths/random_effects.py

class RandomEffectSmooth(Smooth):
    """Dense random effects smooth (bs="re").

    For s(v1, v2, ..., bs="re"), constructs the model matrix equivalent
    to model.matrix(~v1:v2:...:vN - 1) with an identity penalty.
    """

    def __init__(self, spec: SmoothSpec) -> None:
        super().__init__(spec)
        self.side_constrain = False   # skip gam.side()
        self._noterp = True           # skip SVD reparameterization
        self._random = True           # RE flag for summary p-values
        self._has_centering_constraint = False  # skip sum-to-zero

        # Stored at setup time
        self._levels: dict[str, list] | None = None  # var_name → ordered levels
        self._is_factor: dict[str, bool] | None = None
        self._X: np.ndarray | None = None
        self._S: np.ndarray | None = None

docs.title: 5.2 setup() Method
docs.text:
def setup(self, data: dict[str, np.ndarray]) -> None:
    """Construct RE basis from data.

    1. Determine which variables are factors, store levels
    2. Build interaction model matrix (~v1:v2:...:vN - 1)
    3. Set penalty = normalized identity
    """
    variables = self.spec.variables

    # Detect factors and store levels
    self._is_factor = {}
    self._levels = {}
    for var in variables:
        col = data[var]
        if is_factor(col):
            self._is_factor[var] = True
            self._levels[var] = get_factor_levels(col)
        else:
            self._is_factor[var] = False

    # Build interaction model matrix
    X = self._build_interaction_matrix(data)

    self._X = X
    k = X.shape[1]
    self.n_coefs = k
    self.null_space_dim = 0
    self.rank = k

    # Penalty = identity, then normalize
    S = np.eye(k)
    [S], self._s_scale = self._smoothcon_normalize(X, [S])
    self._S = S

    self._is_setup = True

docs.title: 5.3 Model Matrix Construction
docs.text:
The interaction model matrix must replicate R's model.matrix(~v1:v2:...:vN - 1):

Single variable: - Factor: one-hot indicator matrix (n × L) - Numeric: column vector (n × 1)

Multiple variables (interaction): - Kronecker-style row-wise product of individual variable encodings - For each observation: the row of the interaction matrix is the outer product of all individual variable rows, flattened

Implementation approach: 

def _build_interaction_matrix(self, data):
    """Build ~v1:v2:...:vN - 1 interaction matrix."""
    n = len(data[self.spec.variables[0]])

    # Start with column of ones
    result = np.ones((n, 1))

    for var in self.spec.variables:
        col = data[var]
        if self._is_factor[var]:
            # One-hot encode
            levels = self._levels[var]
            indicator = np.zeros((n, len(levels)))
            col_arr = np.asarray(col)
            for j, lev in enumerate(levels):
                indicator[:, j] = (col_arr == lev).astype(float)
            term = indicator
        else:
            term = np.asarray(col, dtype=float).reshape(n, 1)

        # Interaction: row-wise Kronecker product
        new_cols = result.shape[1] * term.shape[1]
        new_result = np.zeros((n, new_cols))
        for i in range(result.shape[1]):
            for j in range(term.shape[1]):
                new_result[:, i * term.shape[1] + j] = result[:, i] * term[:, j]
        result = new_result

    return result

docs.title: 5.4 Column Ordering
docs.text:
The column ordering must match R's model.matrix() for R comparison tests. R's interaction ordering is: first variable varies fastest (leftmost term in the interaction formula changes first).

For s(g1, g2, bs="re") with g1 levels [a,b] and g2 levels [x,y,z]: - R columns: a:x, b:x, a:y, b:y, a:z, b:z - First variable (g1) varies fastest, last (g2) varies slowest

Verified empirically against R 4.5.2 / mgcv 1.9-3 via smoothCon(s(g1, g2, bs="re"), data). The row-wise Kronecker implementation uses the new term's index as the outer (slow) index to match this convention.

docs.title: 5.5 build_design_matrix() and predict_matrix()
docs.text:
def build_design_matrix(self, data):
    self._require_setup()
    return self.predict_matrix(data)

def predict_matrix(self, new_data):
    self._require_setup()
    X = self._build_interaction_matrix(new_data)
    # Zero out rows with unseen factor levels (NaN → 0)
    X[~np.isfinite(X)] = 0.0
    return X

For prediction with new data: - Factor levels not seen during training produce NaN in the indicator encoding - These NaNs are zeroed out, matching R's behavior - This means new factor levels contribute zero to predictions

docs.title: 5.6 build_penalty_matrices()
docs.text:
def build_penalty_matrices(self):
    self._require_setup()
    return [Penalty(self._S, rank=self.rank, null_space_dim=0)]

docs.title: 6.1 No Parser Changes Required
docs.text: The existing formula parser already handles s(fac, bs="re") correctly: - Positional args become SmoothSpec.variables = ["fac"] - bs="re" is captured in SmoothSpec.bs = "re" - Multiple variables: s(g1, g2, bs="re") → variables = ["g1", "g2"]

docs.title: 6.2 k Argument
docs.text: In R, the k argument is ignored for bs="re" — the basis dimension is always ncol(X). Our implementation should do the same: ignore spec.k and set n_coefs = ncol(X).

docs.title: 7.1 Skip Centering Constraint
docs.text:
RE smooths must not have the sum-to-zero centering constraint applied. In R, this is signaled by C = matrix(0, 0, ncol(X)) (empty constraint).

In jaxgam, the centering pipeline in CoefficientMap.build() (constraints.py lines 369-396) applies apply_sum_to_zero() to all smooths unless explicitly skipped.

Required change: Add a check for _has_centering_constraint:

# In CoefficientMap.build(), centering loop:
for i, sm in enumerate(smooths):
    # Skip RE smooths (no centering needed)
    if not getattr(sm, '_has_centering_constraint', True):
        continue

    # ... existing centering logic ...

The RandomEffectSmooth sets _has_centering_constraint = False in __init__.

docs.title: 7.2 Skip gam.side()
docs.text:
RE smooths set side_constrain = False. The existing gam_side() implementation already checks this flag (constraints.py lines 729, 753):

if dim_i == d and CoefficientMap._smooth_side_constrain(sm):

And _smooth_side_constrain() (line 991-1008) correctly reads the side_constrain attribute. No changes needed here.

docs.title: 7.3 CoefficientMap Term Type
docs.text: The TermBlock for an RE smooth should still have term_type = "smooth". The _random flag on the smooth object (not on TermBlock) is used for p-value dispatch.

docs.title: 8.1 Identity Penalty
docs.text:
The penalty for bs="re" is always the identity matrix of dimension k (where k = ncol(X)). After smoothCon normalization:

S_normalized = I_k / s_scale

where s_scale = ||I_k||_1 / ||X||_∞² = 1 / ||X||_∞².

docs.title: 8.2 Embedding in Global Penalty Space
docs.text: The existing CompositePenalty.embed() handles this correctly — it places the k×k penalty into the correct block of the global (total_p × total_p) penalty matrix. No changes needed.

docs.title: 8.3 Properties
docs.text:
• Rank: k (full rank)
  • Null space dimension: 0
  • Number of penalties: 1
  • Smoothing parameter: 1 (one λ for the term)

docs.title: 9.1 Training Data
docs.text: predict_matrix(training_data) should reproduce build_design_matrix(). Since the construction is deterministic (no eigendecomposition), this is straightforward.

docs.title: 9.2 New Data with Known Levels
docs.text: For factor levels present in training: prediction works normally via the indicator matrix.

docs.title: 9.3 New Data with Unseen Levels
docs.text:
For factor levels NOT present in training: 1. The indicator encoding produces NaN for unseen levels 2. NaNs are zeroed out in the prediction matrix 3. The unseen level contributes zero to the linear predictor 4. This matches R's behavior exactly

Implementation: in predict_matrix(), after building the interaction matrix, zero out all non-finite values: 

X[~np.isfinite(X)] = 0.0

docs.title: 9.4 Level Storage for Prediction
docs.text: Factor levels must be stored at setup() time and reused in predict_matrix(). The stored levels define which columns exist in the basis. New data is encoded against these stored levels.

docs.title: 10.1 R Behavior
docs.text: In R's summary.gam(), RE terms (identified by $random == TRUE) receive a different p-value test: - type_ = 1 in testStat() (integer rank rounding instead of fractional) - The test statistic interpretation changes for random effects

docs.title: 10.2 Required Change
docs.text:
In jaxgam/summary/summary.py, the smooth p-value loop (line 213-220) currently hardcodes type_=0:

res = _test_stat(p_i, X_i, V_i, rank=..., type_=0, res_df=rdf)

This needs to check whether the smooth is a random effect:

# Determine test type: RE terms use type_=1 (integer rank)
is_re = getattr(si_smooth, '_random', False)
test_type = 1 if is_re else 0

res = _test_stat(p_i, X_i, V_i, rank=..., type_=test_type, res_df=rdf)

The SmoothInfo dataclass may need an additional field, or we access the smooth object through the coef_map. The cleanest approach is to add an is_random field to SmoothInfo.

docs.title: 10.3 SmoothInfo Extension
docs.text:
Add is_random: bool = False to SmoothInfo (design.py):

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SmoothInfo:
    # ... existing fields ...
    is_random: bool = False  # True for bs="re" terms

Populate from the smooth object in _build_smooth_info():

is_random = getattr(getattr(sm, 'base_smooth', sm), '_random', False)

docs.title: 12. Testing Strategy
docs.text:
Testing is split across two locations following the existing project pattern:

  • tests/test_smooths/test_random_effects.py — basis-level unit tests and smooth-construct R comparisons (analogous to test_cubic.py, test_tprs.py). These test the RandomEffectSmooth class in isolation.

  • tests/test_validation_matrix.py — full-model R comparisons across all smooth × family combinations. RE smooth configs are added as new cells in the existing parametrized matrix, inheriting all the existing test methods (deviance, fitted values, EDF, scale, coefficients, self-prediction roundtrip, hard-gate invariants).

docs.title: 12.1 Validation Matrix Integration
docs.text: The validation matrix (test_validation_matrix.py) systematically tests every smooth config × family cell. RE adds 3 new smooth configs and a new data generator, expanding the matrix from 35 cells to 50 cells.

docs.title: 12.1.1 New Smooth Configs
docs.text:
# Added to SMOOTH_CONFIGS in test_validation_matrix.py

"re": SmoothConfig(
    py_formula="y ~ s(g, bs='re')",
    r_formula="y ~ s(g, bs='re')",
    data_type="re",
),
"re_slope": SmoothConfig(
    py_formula="y ~ s(x, g, bs='re')",
    r_formula="y ~ s(x, g, bs='re')",
    data_type="re",
),
"re_mixed": SmoothConfig(
    py_formula="y ~ s(x, k=10, bs='tp') + s(g, bs='re')",
    r_formula="y ~ s(x, k=10, bs='tp') + s(g, bs='re')",
    data_type="re",
),

These cover the three most important RE patterns: - re — random intercepts (RE-only model) - re_slope — random slopes (numeric × factor interaction) - re_mixed — RE alongside a standard smooth (most common real-world usage)

docs.title: 12.1.2 New Data Generator
docs.text:
def _make_re_data(family_name: str, seed: int = SEED) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Random effects data: continuous x + factor g with group-level effects."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    n = 300
    n_groups = 20
    x = rng.uniform(0, 1, n)
    g = rng.choice([f"g{i}" for i in range(n_groups)], size=n)

    # True group effects
    b_intercept = rng.normal(0, 1.0, n_groups)
    group_idx = {f"g{i}": i for i in range(n_groups)}
    group_effect = np.array([b_intercept[group_idx[gi]] for gi in g])

    # Smooth + RE truth
    eta = np.sin(2 * np.pi * x) + group_effect

    if family_name == "gaussian":
        y = eta + rng.normal(0, 0.5, n)
    elif family_name == "binomial":
        prob = 1.0 / (1.0 + np.exp(-eta))
        y = rng.binomial(1, prob, n).astype(float)
    elif family_name == "poisson":
        y = rng.poisson(np.exp(eta * 0.5 + 0.5)).astype(float)
    elif family_name == "gamma":
        mu = np.exp(eta * 0.3 + 1.0)
        y = rng.gamma(5.0, scale=mu / 5.0, size=n)
    elif family_name == "nb":
        mu = np.exp(eta * 0.5 + 0.5)
        theta = 2.0
        y = rng.negative_binomial(
            n=theta, p=theta / (mu + theta), size=n
        ).astype(float)
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown family: {family_name}")

    return pd.DataFrame({
        "x": x,
        "g": pd.Categorical(g),
        "y": y,
    })

Wire into _get_data(): 

if config.data_type == "re":
    return _make_re_data(family)

docs.title: 12.1.3 Tolerance Rules
docs.text:
# In _r_tol(): RE models use MODERATE for Gaussian, LOOSE otherwise
# (same rule as single-smooth models — RE has one sp, deterministic basis)
if family_name == "gaussian" and smooth_key in ("tp", "cr", "re"):
    return MODERATE
return LOOSE

# In _compare_fitted_not_coefs(): RE coefficients are directly comparable
# (no sign ambiguity, no flat REML surface with multiple sp)
# re and re_slope: compare coefficients directly
# re_mixed: compare fitted values (contains TPRS with sign ambiguity)
return smooth_key in ("tp", "tp_by", "te", "ti", "te_by", "cr_by", "re_mixed")

docs.title: 12.1.4 Inherited Tests
docs.text:
Adding RE configs to SMOOTH_CONFIGS automatically inherits all existing test methods in both TestValidationMatrix and TestHardGateInvariants:

TestValidationMatrix (R comparison, 15 new cells): - test_deviance_vs_r — deviance matches R - test_fitted_values_vs_r — fitted values match R - test_edf_vs_r — total EDF matches R - test_scale_vs_r — scale parameter matches R - test_coefficients_vs_r — coefficients or fitted values match R - test_self_prediction_roundtrip — predict() reproduces fitted_values - test_theta_vs_r — theta matches R (NB family only)

TestHardGateInvariants (no R required, 15 new cells): - test_convergence — model converges - test_deviance_non_negative — deviance ≥ 0 - test_no_nan_in_converged — no NaN/Inf in coefficients, fitted values - test_edf_bounds — EDF in valid range - test_vp_symmetric_psd — Bayesian covariance is symmetric PSD - test_penalty_psd — penalty matrices are symmetric PSD - test_theta_positive — theta > 0 (NB only) - test_model_matrix_rank — model matrix has sufficient rank

docs.title: 12.2 Unit Tests (test_random_effects.py)
docs.text:
These test RandomEffectSmooth in isolation, without the full GAM fitting pipeline. They live in tests/test_smooths/test_random_effects.py, following the pattern of test_cubic.py and test_tprs.py.

Structural tests (no R): - Identity penalty is symmetric PSD with correct rank - Basis matrix shape matches number of factor levels - null_space_dim == 0 and rank == n_coefs - side_constrain == False and _has_centering_constraint == False - _random == True - predict_matrix reproduces build_design_matrix on training data

Factor handling (no R): - Single factor: correct indicator matrix - Multiple factors: correct interaction columns and ordering - Numeric × factor: correct weighted indicator - Numeric only: correct single-column matrix - Factor with many levels (stress test)

Prediction edge cases (no R): - Unseen factor levels → zero rows in prediction matrix - Subset of training levels → correct subset of columns

R basis comparison (requires R + mgcv): - s(g, bs="re") — single factor basis X and penalty S vs R - s(g1, g2, bs="re") — factor × factor interaction vs R - s(x, g, bs="re") — numeric × factor vs R - Compare X, S, rank, null_space_dim at STRICT tolerance (deterministic)

docs.title: 12.3 Tolerance Summary
docs.text: What Location Tolerance Rationale Basis matrix X test_random_effects.py STRICT Deterministic, no eigendecomposition Penalty matrix S test_random_effects.py STRICT Identity matrix — exact after normalization Deviance validation matrix MODERATE/LOOSE Standard fitting tolerance Fitted values validation matrix MODERATE/LOOSE Standard fitting tolerance Coefficients (re, re_slope) validation matrix MODERATE Single sp, direct comparison Fitted values (re_mixed) validation matrix MODERATE/LOOSE Contains TPRS sign ambiguity EDF validation matrix MODERATE/LOOSE Derived from fitting Hard-gate invariants validation matrix per-invariant Structural, must always hold
