docs.title: Definition of Done
docs.text:
Met when the user opens the single PR for this feature:

  • Direct GP via s(..., bs="gp") works in 1D, 2D, and 3D, with the Python-native kwargs documented in design §1.6 / §6: s(x, bs="gp") (defaults), s(x, z, bs="gp", k=30), s(x, bs="gp", kernel="matern_3_2", rho=0.5), s(x, bs="gp", kernel="power_exponential", rho=0.5, power=2.0), and s(x, bs="gp", kernel="spherical", stationary=True) all parse, construct, fit, and predict via the public gam() API.
  • m= is rejected. Passing m=... to a GP smooth raises a clear ValueError from GaussianProcessSmooth.__init__ at construction time, naming the four replacement kwargs. R-style c(...) is rejected one layer earlier, at the parser, by ast.literal_eval.
  • Tensor-margin GP via the existing wrappers works: te(x1, x2, bs="gp", k=5) and ti(x1, x2, bs="gp", k=5) parse, construct, fit, and predict — through TensorProductSmooth / TensorInteractionSmooth instantiating GaussianProcessSmooth per margin via the registry. No code change in tensor.py.
  • Kernel registry reuses the existing jaxgam.registry.Registry[T] generic (same abstraction used by smooth, family, and link registries) — no bespoke wrapper. The registry's keys are the canonical kernel names; lookups are case-insensitive but there are no aliases.
  • mgcv-side conversion happens only at the R-bridge boundary via tests/r_bridge.py:gp_config_to_mgcv_m. No production code consumes mgcv's m= numeric encoding.
  • All 5 kernels (spherical, power-exponential, Matérn 3/2, 5/2, 7/2) are supported and tested at STRICT against closed-form.
  • Stationary and non-stationary modes both work.
  • Indefinite-eigenvalue clip in Commit D fires on at least one regression test and produces a non-negative penalty diagonal; no GP cell ever sees an indefinite S reach fitting (direct or tensor).
  • 20-25 new validation-matrix cells (4 or 5 configs × 5 families) all pass test_matches_r and test_all_invariants (2 methods/cell — matches the consolidated structure from docs/clean_unit_tests/). Direct cells (gp, gp_2d, gp_mixed) and tensor cells (gp_te, optionally gp_ti) are both present; gp_2d and gp_te are not redundant — they exercise mathematically distinct constructions. gp_mixed uses x + s(x, bs='gp') (same variable) and exercises gam.side identifiability.
  • R smooth-construct comparison tests pass at STRICT (with explicit knots threaded through the Commit-F bridge knots= argument, via X @ X.T for sign-invariance). The STRICT eigenvalue check is skipped on R-side indefinite spectra (documented deviation, §8.3).
  • Consolidation discipline held: total new collected tests in the ~55-80 range (widened from the original ~45 budget because of tensor-margin coverage), not the 120+ a naive per-assertion approach would yield. Every multi-assertion test that shares a fixture/R fit uses _AssertCollector; every kernel-family enumeration uses @pytest.mark.parametrize.
  • No R-parity duplication: smooth-construct R parity lives only in test_gaussian_process.py; final-model R parity lives only in test_validation_matrix.py; bridge-level GP round-trip lives only in test_r_bridge.py. Verified by the Commit J grep.
  • make test-cov passes on the final commit with ≥ 80% coverage.
  • Hard allow-list intact: all TPRS, RE, CoefficientMap roundtrip, step- halving, Cholesky stability, and R-bridge version tests still pass. Existing non-GP bridge tests pass with the new knots=None default unchanged.
  • docs/gaussian_process/design.md status is "Implemented".
  • docs/api.md documents GP usage with Python-literal extra_args.
  • CLAUDE.md does not list GP under §What Is NOT in v1.0 (fixed 2026-05-23; verify still correct at PR time).
  • All nine active commit slots (A-G, H, I, J — the old H is an empty marker) are present in the branch history as individual commits authored by the user.

docs.title: Choosing a route
docs.text:
jaxgam can fit the same kind of model in several ways. This page tells you which one to use for your data and what each one gives back. A route is the way the fit is carried out; you choose it with FitControl(execution=...) and, for smoothing parameter selection, with a few GAM arguments.

Use the default fit when your data fit in memory as a pandas DataFrame. It supports every family, smooth type and result mode.

Pick another route when the data do not fit in memory, when you want the estimates of mgcv's bam(discrete=TRUE) rather than gam(), or when a random effect has a very large number of levels.

docs.title: The six ways to fit at a glance
docs.text:
Way to fit How you ask for it Data How smoothing parameters are chosen Details Default fit (dense route) GAM(formula) DataFrame or dict Exact REML by Newton's method, as mgcv's gam(method="REML"), or fixed with sp= Smoothing parameter selection Fellner-Schall GAM(formula, optimizer="efs") DataFrame, or a row source on the streamed and operator routes Extended Fellner-Schall updates, as gam(method="REML", optimizer="efs") Smoothing parameter selection Gaussian QR compression FitControl(gaussian_compression=True) DataFrame, or a row source on the streamed route Exact REML on one QR reduction of the weighted design (Gaussian, identity link) Smoothing parameter selection Streamed route FitControl(execution="stream", ...) Row source Fixed, exact REML or Fellner-Schall, reading the rows in batches Streamed fitting Discretized route FitControl(execution="discrete", discretization=...) Row source Fixed, or mgcv's bam(discrete=TRUE) performance iteration Discretized fitting Operator route FitControl(execution="operator", linear_solver="pcg") Row source Fixed sp=; Fellner-Schall for one supported Poisson model shape Operator fitting

A row source is an object that hands the fit your data in batches of rows, and can do so again as many times as the fit asks. See Row sources.

Fellner-Schall and Gaussian QR compression are not separate places to put data: they change how smoothing parameters are found on the dense route and, where the table says so, on a row-source route.

docs.title: Which route for your situation
docs.text:
Your situation Use Data fit in memory, you want the same estimates as gam(method="REML") Default fit Data fit in memory, you want mgcv's optimizer="efs" behaviour Fellner-Schall Data fit in memory, Gaussian family with identity link Default fit with gaussian_compression=True Data do not fit in memory, you want gam() estimates, the model has only one-variable cubic regression splines (bs="cr" or "cs") and numeric terms Streamed route Data do not fit in memory, you accept bam(discrete=TRUE) estimates, any smooth type Discretized route A random effect s(g, bs="re") with very many levels Operator route

The streamed route reads every row on every pass and gives the exact estimates; the discretized route first rounds covariates onto grids, as bam(discrete=TRUE) does, so its estimates are those of that model, not of gam().

docs.title: What each route takes and returns
docs.text:
Route data argument Weights and offset Result modes FitControl.uncertainty Dense (including Fellner-Schall and Gaussian QR) DataFrame or dict fit(data, weights=..., offset=...) "full", "inference", "prediction" "none", "fisher", "covariance" (prediction mode only) Streamed Row source Held by the row source "prediction" only "none", "fisher", "covariance" Discretized Row source Held by the row source "prediction" only "none", "fisher", "covariance" Operator Row source Held by the row source "prediction" only "none" only

fit() defaults to result="full", so a row-source fit must pass result="prediction". Otherwise it raises, for example on the streamed route:

NotImplementedError: Streamed fitting supports result='prediction' only; full and inference results retain unsupported row diagnostics.

A row source given to the dense route raises:

TypeError: A RowSource requires FitControl execution 'operator', 'stream' or 'discrete'; the dense route accepts only a DataFrame or dict.

docs.title: The three result modes
docs.text:
GAM.fit(..., result=...) chooses how much the result keeps.

Mode Returns Keeps Use it for "full" (default) GAMResults Training data, fitted values, Vp, per-smooth EDF summary(), plot(), in-sample diagnostics "inference" GAMInferenceResult Vp, per-smooth EDF, scalar diagnostics; no training rows New-data prediction with standard errors "prediction" GAMPredictionResult Coefficients, scalar diagnostics, and covariance only if you ask for it Prediction on new data; the only mode on row-source routes

Only the dense route offers all three. See Prediction results for the prediction result and Fit result modes in the API reference for the field lists.

docs.title: What is the same on every route
docs.text:
• Formula syntax. Every route parses the same mgcv-style formula (s(), te(), ti(), bs=, k=, by=). Each route accepts a subset: the streamed route takes one-variable bs="cr" or "cs" smooths and numeric terms; the operator route takes numeric terms, cr/cs/cc, tp/ts/gp and re smooths; the discretized and dense routes take every smooth type. See Formula syntax.
  • Families. The same family names and objects ("gaussian", "binomial", "poisson", "gamma", "nb", or an instance such as Gamma(link="log")). Which family and link combinations a route accepts is listed on its own page. See Families.
  • Prediction. Every result has predict(newdata, pred_type="response", se_fit=False, offset=None) with the same meaning, and to_predictor().
  • Convergence reporting. Every result has converged, n_iter, convergence_info, smoothing_params and execution_route.

docs.title: Two short examples
docs.text:
The setup block makes a small data set used by both examples.

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from jaxgam import GAM, FitControl
from jaxgam.data import DataFrameRowSource

rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
n = 500
x = rng.uniform(0, 1, n)
z = rng.uniform(0, 1, n)
y = np.sin(2 * np.pi * x) + 0.5 * z + rng.normal(0, 0.3, n)
data = pd.DataFrame({"x": x, "z": z, "y": y})
newdata = pd.DataFrame({"x": [0.25, 0.75], "z": [0.5, 0.5]})

The default fit takes the DataFrame and returns a full result:

fit = GAM("y ~ s(x) + z").fit(data)
print(fit.execution_route, fit.converged, fit.convergence_info)
print(fit.predict(newdata))

dense True full convergence
[ 1.30141681 -0.76120126]

The same kind of model on the streamed route takes a row source and returns a prediction result. The smooth uses bs="cr" because the streamed route accepts only cubic regression splines, and linear_solver="qr" because estimating the smoothing parameters there requires it:

source = DataFrameRowSource(data, response="y")
control = FitControl(execution="stream", linear_solver="qr")
fit = GAM("y ~ s(x, bs='cr') + z", control=control).fit(source, result="prediction")
print(type(fit).__name__, fit.execution_route, fit.converged)
print(fit.predict(newdata))

GAMPredictionResult stream_exact_reml_qr True
[ 1.31145334 -0.75912431]

The two predictions differ slightly because the bases differ (thin plate against cubic regression spline), not because of the route.

docs.title: Which route ran
docs.text:
execution_route on every result names the route that actually ran:

Value Meaning "dense" Default fit, including Fellner-Schall and fixed sp "gaussian_qr" Dense fit with Gaussian QR compression "stream", "stream_qr" Streamed fit with fixed sp (Cholesky or QR solver) "stream_exact_reml_qr" Streamed exact REML "stream_efs_qr" Streamed Fellner-Schall "stream_parametric_qr" Streamed Fellner-Schall request on a model with no penalties "stream_gaussian_qr" Streamed fit with Gaussian QR compression "discrete" Discretized fit "operator" Operator fit

When you asked for Gaussian QR compression and the model did not qualify, execution_fallback_reason says why. lambda_strategy names how the smoothing parameters were chosen ("newton_reml", "fixed", "efs_reml", "exact_reml", "lbfgs_reml", "working_model_reml" and so on).

docs.title: Discretized fitting
docs.text:
The discretized route is jaxgam's counterpart of mgcv's bam(discrete=TRUE). Select it with FitControl(execution="discrete"). It fits from a row source and stores each part of the model matrix once per distinct covariate value, instead of once per row.

What discretization does. Each smooth's covariates are reduced to their distinct values. When a covariate has more distinct values than a grid allows (1,000 for a smooth of one variable, by default), its values are first rounded to an evenly spaced grid over their observed range. The basis is then evaluated once per distinct value, and each row keeps only an index into that small table. Memory for the model matrix then grows with the number of distinct values, not with the number of rows.

This is a different estimator from the default fit, as bam is from gam in mgcv: the covariates may be rounded, and the smoothing parameters are chosen by bam's performance iteration rather than by the nested REML optimization of the default fit. Expect close, not identical, results.

Use it when

  • you have many rows, and want what bam(discrete=TRUE) would give you;
  • the model needs smooth types the streamed route does not accept: thin plate, cyclic, Gaussian process, random-effect and tensor smooths, by= variables and factor terms all work here.

Do not use it when

  • you need the exact default-fit estimate, summary() or plot(): use the default fit;
  • your random effects have very many levels and dominate the model: see the operator route.

The setup block makes the data and the row sources used throughout the page.

import os
import tempfile
import warnings

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from jaxgam import GAM, ContinuousDiscretizationControl, FitControl
from jaxgam.data import DataFrameRowSource, DiscretizationBudget
from jaxgam.families import NegativeBinomial

rng = np.random.default_rng(2)
n = 20_000
x = rng.uniform(0, 1, n)
z = rng.uniform(0, 1, n)
g = rng.integers(0, 20, n)
eta = np.sin(2 * np.pi * x) + (z - 0.5) ** 2 + rng.normal(scale=0.5, size=20)[g]
data = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "x": x,
        "z": z,
        "g": pd.Categorical(g),
        "y": eta + rng.normal(scale=0.3, size=n),
        "count": rng.poisson(np.exp(0.5 * eta)),
    }
)
source = DataFrameRowSource(data, response="y")
counts = DataFrameRowSource(data, response="count")
newdata = pd.DataFrame({"x": [0.1, 0.5], "z": [0.3, 0.3], "g": pd.Categorical([0, 1])})

See Row sources for the built-in sources, prior weights and offsets.

docs.title: A minimal fit
docs.text:
A discretized fit needs four things:

  1. a row source as the data;
  2. an explicit ContinuousDiscretizationControl (the discretization policy);
  3. either sp= or smoothing_strategy="working_model_reml";
  4. result="prediction".
control = FitControl(
    execution="discrete",
    discretization=ContinuousDiscretizationControl(),
    smoothing_strategy="working_model_reml",
)
fit = GAM("y ~ s(x, bs='cr') + s(z, bs='cr')", control=control).fit(
    source, result="prediction"
)
print(fit.execution_route, fit.converged)
# discrete True
print(fit.convergence_info)
# Gaussian working-model REML converged after 12 iterations and 11 proposals
print(fit.predict(newdata))
# [0.63771438 0.05804595]

Leaving out any of the four raises an error:

policy = ContinuousDiscretizationControl()
attempts = {
    "no policy": lambda: FitControl(execution="discrete"),
    "no strategy and no sp": lambda: GAM(
        "y ~ s(x, bs='cr')",
        control=FitControl(execution="discrete", discretization=policy),
    ).fit(source, result="prediction"),
    "default result": lambda: GAM("y ~ s(x, bs='cr')", control=control).fit(source),
    "DataFrame data": lambda: GAM("y ~ s(x, bs='cr')", control=control).fit(
        data, result="prediction"
    ),
}
for name, attempt in attempts.items():
    try:
        attempt()
    except (ValueError, TypeError, NotImplementedError) as error:
        print(f"{name}: {type(error).__name__}: {error}")

no policy: ValueError: execution='discrete' requires an explicit discretization policy.
no strategy and no sp: NotImplementedError: Discrete fitting requires explicit fixed sp or opt-in smoothing_strategy='working_model_reml'.
default result: NotImplementedError: Discrete fitting currently supports result='prediction' only; full and inference results retain unsupported row diagnostics.
DataFrame data: TypeError: FitControl(execution='discrete') requires a replayable RowSource.

Passing fit(weights=...) or fit(offset=...) raises ValueError: weights and offset must be owned by the RowSource for execution='discrete'; do not pass separate arrays.

docs.title: The grid size m
docs.text:
ContinuousDiscretizationControl(m=...) sets the grid. The covariates of one s() term are discretized together as a group; each te() or ti() margin and each by variable is its own group.

  • m=None (the default): 1,000 grid points per variable for a group of one variable, 100 for two, 25 for three or more. These are mgcv's defaults.
  • an integer: used as given for a group of one variable; for a group of d variables, round(m ** (1 / d)) + 1 points per variable.
  • a tuple: one value per smooth term, in formula order.

A group is rounded only when it has more distinct rows than its grid can hold. Otherwise its values are kept exactly. On small data nothing is rounded, and a fixed-sp fit then matches the default fit:

small = data.iloc[:800]
fixed = FitControl(execution="discrete", discretization=policy)
discrete_fit = GAM("y ~ s(x, bs='cr') + s(z, bs='cr')", sp=[1.0, 2.0],
                   control=fixed).fit(
    DataFrameRowSource(small, response="y"), result="prediction")
dense_fit = GAM("y ~ s(x, bs='cr') + s(z, bs='cr')", sp=[1.0, 2.0]).fit(small)
print(np.max(np.abs(discrete_fit.coefficients - dense_fit.coefficients)) < 1e-12)
# True

fit.discretization.groups records each group's decision:

for group in fit.discretization.groups:
    print(group.variables, group.points_per_metric, group.discretized, group.n_unique)
# ('x',) 1000 True 1000
# ('z',) 1000 True 1000
# ('y',) 1000 True 808

Here both covariates had more than 1,000 distinct values, so each was rounded to its 1,000-point grid. The list also has a group for the response and one for each parametric variable, which the setup frame compresses as mgcv's does.

Because the basis is built on the distinct values, an m smaller than a smooth's k fails, for example ValueError: Basis dimension k=10 exceeds number of unique data values (5). Reduce k or add more distinct data. for m=5 and k=10.

docs.title: Families and links
docs.text:
Family Links Gaussian identity Poisson log, identity, sqrt Binomial logit, probit, cloglog, log Gamma inverse, identity, log Negative binomial log, identity, sqrt

Gaussian identity models read the source twice; smoothing selection then works on the stored statistics without further scans. The other families use bam's performance iteration (mgcv's bgam.fitd): each iteration reads the source once, forms the working weights and working response, and takes one smoothing-parameter step. The Gamma scale is estimated; Poisson and Binomial use a scale of one. Anything else raises, for example NotImplementedError: Discrete fitting supports Gaussian identity, the Poisson (log, identity, sqrt), Binomial (logit, probit, cloglog, log) and Gamma (inverse, identity, log) families, and the negative binomial (log, identity, sqrt); got Gaussian(link=LogLink).

docs.title: Fixed or estimated smoothing
docs.text:
An explicit sp= always gives a fixed-smoothing fit (lambda_strategy is "fixed"), whatever smoothing_strategy says. Without sp, smoothing_strategy="working_model_reml" selects the smoothing parameters by bam's method: one Newton proposal on each iteration's working model (mgcv's Sl.fitChol), until the penalized deviance stops changing.

optimizer="efs" does not apply here: without sp it raises NotImplementedError: optimizer='efs' does not apply to discrete fitting; smoothing_strategy='working_model_reml' selects its smoothing parameters. With sp it has no effect.

Compare fits by deviance and fitted values

With many smooths the REML criterion is often flat in some direction (for example when one smoothing parameter heads towards a very large value), and the point where the search stops is then not sharply determined. This is true of bam too: the tests record cases where mgcv's own selected smoothing parameters move under input changes at rounding level. Compare the deviance and the fitted values, not the smoothing parameters.

The discretized fit above against the default fit on the same rows:

dense = GAM("y ~ s(x, bs='cr') + s(z, bs='cr')").fit(data)
print(fit.deviance, dense.deviance)
print(np.max(np.abs(fit.predict(data) - dense.predict(data))))
print(fit.smoothing_params, dense.smoothing_params)
# 7414.301445351851 7414.480596587477
# 0.0011857272687984428
# [  53.3540798 6202.072597 ] [  52.70551092 6139.62446449]

docs.title: Random effects
docs.text:
Factors are not inferred from the data type on this route. Every factor (a parametric factor, a by factor, or the grouping variable of bs="re") must be listed in factor_names; any other column is treated as a numeric covariate:

with_factor = FitControl(
    execution="discrete",
    discretization=ContinuousDiscretizationControl(factor_names=("g",)),
    smoothing_strategy="working_model_reml",
)
fit_re = GAM("y ~ s(x, bs='cr') + s(g, bs='re')", control=with_factor).fit(
    source, result="prediction"
)
print(fit_re.converged, fit_re.smoothing_params.shape)
# True (2,)

Without the declaration a categorical column raises TypeError: Metric column 'g' must be real numeric data, got dtype category. Variables not listed in factor_names are discretized as metric. .... An integer-coded grouping column that is not declared is silently treated as one numeric covariate. List only columns the formula uses: a name it does not use raises ValueError: factor_names must be distinct referenced variables.

A random-effect level that is missing from the prediction data or was not seen in training contributes zero to the prediction (where mgcv's predict.bam gives NA for a missing group). A multi-variable random effect such as s(x, g, bs="re") is refused (see Limits).

docs.title: Negative binomial
docs.text:
With family="nb" theta is estimated by mgcv's estimate.theta at every iteration from the second. Each estimate reads the source several times, so the fit makes many more scans. NegativeBinomial(theta, fixed=True) holds theta:

estimated = GAM("count ~ s(x, bs='cr') + s(z, bs='cr')", family="nb",
                control=control).fit(counts, result="prediction")
held = GAM("count ~ s(x, bs='cr') + s(z, bs='cr')",
           family=NegativeBinomial(3.0, fixed=True),
           control=control).fit(counts, result="prediction")
print(round(estimated.theta, 2), estimated.source_scans)
print(round(held.theta, 2), held.source_scans)
# 13.45 45
# 3.0 10

docs.title: Budgets
docs.text:
Two kinds of limit apply. The DiscretizationBudget (passed as ContinuousDiscretizationControl(budget=...)) bounds the setup pass that builds the compact tables. FitControl.memory_budget_bytes bounds the fit. Each is a check made before allocation, against arrays the code knows it will need, and each raises MemoryError naming the step that did not fit.

Field Default Message names DiscretizationBudget.max_table_bytes 64 MiB "table", "lookup", "basis setup", "predictor workspace" or "metadata" DiscretizationBudget.max_selector_bytes 256 MiB "selector" DiscretizationBudget.max_batch_bytes 64 MiB "batch workspace" (grows with FitControl.batch_rows) DiscretizationBudget.max_unique_rows 1,000,000 "uniquecombs rows exceed row cap" (the message reports bytes, not rows) FitControl.memory_budget_bytes 512 MiB "Discrete fit workspace requires ..."

The default table budget fits the cubic regression splines above but not, at this data size, the default thin plate smooth s(x):

try:
    GAM("y ~ s(x)", control=control).fit(source, result="prediction")
except MemoryError as error:
    print(error)
# compact smooth predictor workspace exceeds budget: requires 89472425 bytes,
# budget is 67108864.

The byte count varies slightly between runs. Raise the table budget, or use a coarser grid:

larger_table = ContinuousDiscretizationControl(
    budget=DiscretizationBudget(max_table_bytes=256 * 1024 * 1024)
)
fit_tp = GAM("y ~ s(x)", control=FitControl(
    execution="discrete", discretization=larger_table,
    smoothing_strategy="working_model_reml",
)).fit(source, result="prediction")
coarse = ContinuousDiscretizationControl(m=200)
fit_tp_coarse = GAM("y ~ s(x)", control=FitControl(
    execution="discrete", discretization=coarse,
    smoothing_strategy="working_model_reml",
)).fit(source, result="prediction")
print(fit_tp.converged, fit_tp_coarse.converged)
# True True

When a "batch workspace" message appears, lower FitControl.batch_rows or raise max_batch_bytes. When the fit itself does not fit:

try:
    GAM("y ~ s(x, bs='cr') + s(z, bs='cr')", control=FitControl(
        execution="discrete", discretization=policy,
        smoothing_strategy="working_model_reml", memory_budget_bytes=10_000_000,
    )).fit(source, result="prediction")
except MemoryError as error:
    print(error)
# Discrete fit workspace requires 26306232 bytes, exceeding
# FitControl.memory_budget_bytes=10000000.

fit.fit_peak_bytes is the figure this check uses, so a successful fit tells you how much it needed.

docs.title: Row selectors on disk
docs.text:
During setup each row's index into the compact tables is held in memory, charged to max_selector_bytes. selector_memmap_directory writes these selectors to files in an existing directory instead. The files (compact-selector-{group}.dat) are removed when the fit ends, and the directory must not already contain them:

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
    on_disk = ContinuousDiscretizationControl(selector_memmap_directory=directory)
    fit_disk = GAM("y ~ s(x, bs='cr') + s(z, bs='cr')", control=FitControl(
        execution="discrete", discretization=on_disk,
        smoothing_strategy="working_model_reml",
    )).fit(source, result="prediction")
    print(fit_disk.converged, os.listdir(directory))
# True []

docs.title: Prediction policy
docs.text:
ContinuousDiscretizationControl(prediction_policy=...) sets how new data are predicted. Both reuse the fitted knots and constraints.

Value What it does "continuous_frozen_basis" (default) Evaluates each new value exactly, as predict.gam does. Rows are independent, so a prediction never depends on the rest of the request or on batching. "mgcv_predict_bamd" Follows mgcv's predict.bamd: the whole request is first discretized on the default (m=None) grid, then evaluated. Results then depend on what else is in the request, as in mgcv, but not on how it is batched.

The difference shows when a request has more distinct values than the grid:

bamd = FitControl(
    execution="discrete",
    discretization=ContinuousDiscretizationControl(prediction_policy="mgcv_predict_bamd"),
    smoothing_strategy="working_model_reml",
)
fit_bamd = GAM("y ~ s(x, bs='cr') + s(z, bs='cr')", control=bamd).fit(
    source, result="prediction"
)
print(fit.predict(data)[:2], fit.predict(data.iloc[:5])[:2])
# [1.13731702 1.16322397] [1.13731702 1.16322397]
print(fit_bamd.predict(data)[:2], fit_bamd.predict(data.iloc[:5])[:2])
# [1.13767284 1.16329154] [1.13731702 1.16322397]

With the whole training data as the request, mgcv_predict_bamd rounds the 20,000 values to the grid first; five rows are evaluated exactly.

A model without smooths has nothing to discretize; its result records "continuous_frozen_basis".

docs.title: Other options
docs.text:
Option Default What it does ContinuousDiscretizationControl.factor_names () Columns to treat as factors. ContinuousDiscretizationControl.seed 8547 Seed of the shuffle that mgcv applies to the compact rows (a signed 32-bit integer). ContinuousDiscretizationControl.pair_policy "histogram_or_direct" How a pair of compact blocks is reduced: by a weight histogram when that is no larger than gathering rows, or always by gathering rows ("direct_only"). FitControl.working_model_max_iterations 200 Limit of the performance iteration. FitControl.working_model_epsilon 1e-7 Relative change of the penalized deviance that stops it. FitControl.uncertainty "none" "fisher" or "covariance" keeps what predict(se_fit=True) needs. FitControl.batch_rows 65_536 Rows per source scan.

Field-level detail is in the API reference.

docs.title: What you get back
docs.text:
A GAMPredictionResult (see the API reference), with no summary() or plot().

Attribute Meaning on this route converged, n_iter, convergence_info Whether the iteration met its stopping test, and how it stopped. execution_route "discrete". smoothing_strategy, lambda_strategy "fixed" or "working_model_reml". smoothing_params, deviance, scale, edf_total The fitted values. edf_total is the total effective degrees of freedom. theta The negative binomial theta (fixed or estimated), else None. score bam's criterion at the stopping point. source_scans, batches_scanned Scans made by the fit, not by the setup pass. known_workspace_bytes The compact design and solver workspace. fit_peak_bytes, fit_memory_budget_bytes The figure checked against memory_budget_bytes, and that budget. working_model_proposal_evaluations Smoothing-parameter proposals tried (0 for a fixed-sp Gaussian fit). prediction_policy, discretization The prediction policy and the per-group grid record.

docs.title: Telling whether the fit converged
docs.text:
A fixed-sp Gaussian fit is a direct solve and always reports converged=True; its n_iter counts the scale iterations. Every other fit stops when, from the third iteration, the relative change of the penalized deviance is below working_model_epsilon (and, when a scale is estimated, so is the change of the log scale). At working_model_max_iterations the fit is still returned, with converged=False and a RuntimeWarning:

short = FitControl(execution="discrete", discretization=policy,
                   smoothing_strategy="working_model_reml",
                   working_model_max_iterations=3)
with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught:
    warnings.simplefilter("always")
    fit_short = GAM("y ~ s(x, bs='cr') + s(z, bs='cr')", control=short).fit(
        source, result="prediction")
print(fit_short.converged, [str(w.message) for w in caught])
# False ['Gaussian working-model REML did not converge within its iteration limit.']

For the other families the warning reads {family} discrete performance iteration did not converge within its iteration limit.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
Not accepted Error linear_solver="qr" NotImplementedError: linear_solver='qr' currently requires execution='stream'. linear_solver="pcg" NotImplementedError: linear_solver='pcg' currently requires execution='operator'. A multi-variable random effect, for example s(x, g, bs='re') NotImplementedError: s(x,g, bs='re') is not supported by execution='discrete': mgcv's bam discretizes each variable of a multi-variable random effect as a separate tensor margin, which the compact setup does not reproduce. Smooths that group shared variables differently, for example s(x, z) + s(x) ValueError: continuous discretization has incompatible nesting A non-finite covariate value ValueError: Metric column 'x' contains non-finite values method other than "REML" (including "fREML") ValueError when the GAM is created

Other known rough edges:

  • gaussian_compression=True is not used here; the fit runs unchanged and execution_fallback_reason reads Gaussian QR compression requires execution 'dense' or 'stream'.
  • As in mgcv, the performance iteration does not check that the mean stays in the family's range, and its second iteration has no step control. A first step that leaves the range raises FloatingPointError: Non-finite working-model deviance at iteration 2., where bam also stops.
  • A fixed-sp Gaussian fit whose coefficient system is not positive definite (an unidentifiable model) raises LinAlgError: rank-deficient fitting is not available for that fit.
  • A row source you write yourself that does not declare has_explicit_weights and has_explicit_offset is treated as supplying both, as bam treats supplied weights= and offset= arguments. That changes mgcv's seeded padding of the compact rows, and so the fitted numbers slightly. See Row sources.

docs.title: Memory and performance
docs.text:
This page lists the settings that bound how much memory a fit or a prediction may use, the error each one raises when a fit would exceed it, and what to change. It also covers compile time, BLAS threads and a problem specific to Apple silicon Macs.

Use this page when a fit or prediction raises MemoryError, when you want to bound the memory of a row-source fit, or when you set up a machine to run jaxgam.

Keep in mind that every budget is jaxgam's own estimate of the arrays it allocates, checked before it allocates them. None is a hard cap on the process: the row source's own storage, allocator overhead and the workspace of the underlying linear algebra libraries are outside it. The dense fit itself is not budgeted at all.

All examples on this page use this setup block:

import tempfile

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from jaxgam import GAM, ContinuousDiscretizationControl, FitControl
from jaxgam.data import DataFrameRowSource, DiscretizationBudget

rng = np.random.default_rng(1)
n = 20_000
x = rng.uniform(0, 1, n)
z = rng.uniform(0, 1, n)
y = np.sin(2 * np.pi * x) + 0.5 * z + rng.normal(0, 0.3, n)
data = pd.DataFrame({"x": x, "z": z, "y": y})
source = DataFrameRowSource(data, response="y")
newdata = pd.DataFrame({"x": np.linspace(0, 1, 500), "z": 0.5})


def discrete_control(discretization=None, **options):
    """FitControl for the discretized route with smoothing parameters estimated."""
    return FitControl(
        execution="discrete",
        discretization=discretization or ContinuousDiscretizationControl(),
        smoothing_strategy="working_model_reml",
        **options,
    )

docs.title: Which setting bounds what
docs.text:
Setting Default Bounds FitControl.batch_rows 65_536 Rows per scan of a row source on the streamed, discretized and operator routes, and the default batch of predict_iter(). Streamed setup scans use smaller batches when needed to fit memory_budget_bytes. The dense route ignores it. FitControl.memory_budget_bytes 512 MiB Streamed route: setup scans and the fit workspace. Discretized route: the whole fit workspace. Operator route: preparation and fit. Prediction results on every route: Vp and the workspace of each prediction call. FitControl.output_budget_bytes 512 MiB Bytes one predict() or predict_matrix() call on a prediction result may return; each predict_iter() batch counts as one call. DiscretizationBudget.max_table_bytes 64 MiB Discretized route: the compact tables of distinct rows and the basis evaluated on them, summed over all groups of variables. DiscretizationBudget.max_selector_bytes 256 MiB Discretized route: the in-memory row selectors (one index per row and group) and their validation state. DiscretizationBudget.max_batch_bytes 64 MiB Discretized route: the workspace of one batch, which grows with batch_rows. DiscretizationBudget.max_unique_rows 1_000_000 Discretized route: distinct rows in any one group. ContinuousDiscretizationControl.selector_memmap_directory None Discretized route: when set to an existing directory, row selectors are written there as files instead of held in memory, and are removed when the fit ends.

DiscretizationBudget comes from jaxgam.data and goes into ContinuousDiscretizationControl(budget=...). uncertainty, batch_rows and both FitControl budgets act on the dense route only with result="prediction"; full and inference results are not budgeted.

docs.title: Errors and what to change
docs.text:
Error message (numbers vary) Raised by Change Streamed setup requires at least N bytes to scan one row, exceeding the setup memory budget of M bytes (FitControl.memory_budget_bytes). Streamed setup pass Raise memory_budget_bytes. Any model with a cubic smooth needs at least about 17 MB here. Known streamed QR PIRLS workspace requires N bytes, exceeding FitControl.memory_budget_bytes=M. Setup scans are budgeted separately. (or Known streamed PIRLS workspace ...) Streamed fit Lower batch_rows, or raise memory_budget_bytes. The estimate is for a full batch of batch_rows rows even when the source has fewer. Discrete fit workspace requires N bytes, exceeding FitControl.memory_budget_bytes=M. Discretized fit Raise memory_budget_bytes, or lower batch_rows. Operator preparation needs at most N bytes; budget is M. Lower batch_rows or raise the memory budget., Frozen operator requires N bytes; budget is M. Lower batch_rows or raise the memory budget. Operator setup pass and fit Lower batch_rows, or raise memory_budget_bytes. The operator fit already plans for no more rows per batch than the source holds. In the second message M is what is left of the budget after the fit's other arrays. uniquecombs rows exceed construction byte budget: requires N bytes, budget is M., compact smooth predictor workspace exceeds budget: requires N bytes, budget is M. max_table_bytes Raise max_table_bytes, or use a coarser grid (m=). row selector/validation state exceeds in-memory selector budget: requires N bytes, budget is M. max_selector_bytes Raise max_selector_bytes, or set selector_memmap_directory. range-analysis batch workspace exceeds budget: requires N bytes, budget is M. max_batch_bytes Raise max_batch_bytes, or lower batch_rows. uniquecombs rows exceed row cap: requires N bytes, budget is M. max_unique_rows Raise max_unique_rows, or use a coarser grid. The numbers in this message are table bytes, not rows. Prediction output requires N bytes, exceeding output budget M bytes. Use predict_iter() with smaller batches. predict() on a prediction result Use predict_iter() with a smaller batch_rows, or raise output_budget_bytes. Prediction workspace requires N bytes, exceeding memory budget M bytes. Use predict_iter() with smaller batches. predict() on a prediction result As above, or raise memory_budget_bytes. Vp requires N bytes, exceeding FitControl.memory_budget_bytes=M. uncertainty="covariance" Raise memory_budget_bytes, or use uncertainty="fisher". Vp materialization requires N workspace bytes, exceeding budget M bytes. materialize_covariance() Pass a larger budget.

All of these are MemoryError. A budget that is not a positive integer raises ValueError when you construct the control.

The streamed fit workspace check, for example, charges a full batch of batch_rows rows, whatever the size of the source. With a 24 MiB budget, a small model on 2,000 rows fails at the default batch size of 65,536 rows and fits once batch_rows is lowered:

small_source = DataFrameRowSource(data.iloc[:2000], response="y")
budget = 24 * 1024 * 1024
formula = "y ~ s(x, bs='cr') + z"
try:
    control = FitControl(execution="stream", linear_solver="qr", memory_budget_bytes=budget)
    GAM(formula, control=control).fit(small_source, result="prediction")
except MemoryError as error:
    print(str(error)[:44])

control = FitControl(
    execution="stream", linear_solver="qr", memory_budget_bytes=budget, batch_rows=4096
)
fit = GAM(formula, control=control).fit(small_source, result="prediction")
print(fit.converged)

Known streamed QR PIRLS workspace requires 2
True

A prediction larger than output_budget_bytes goes through predict_iter() instead:

small = FitControl(output_budget_bytes=1_000)
fit = GAM("y ~ s(x) + z", control=small).fit(data, result="prediction")
try:
    fit.predict(newdata)
except MemoryError as error:
    print(error)
rows = sum(len(p) for _, p in fit.predict_iter(DataFrameRowSource(newdata), batch_rows=100))
print(rows)

Prediction output requires 4000 bytes, exceeding output budget 1000 bytes. Use predict_iter() with smaller batches.
500

docs.title: Thin-plate smooths on the discretized route
docs.text:
The default DiscretizationBudget is too small for a default thin-plate smooth, s(x), on the discretized route, while a cubic regression spline fits within it:

try:
    GAM("y ~ s(x) + z", control=discrete_control()).fit(source, result="prediction")
except MemoryError as error:
    print(error)

cubic = GAM("y ~ s(x, bs='cr') + z", control=discrete_control())
print(cubic.fit(source, result="prediction").converged)

compact smooth predictor workspace exceeds budget: requires 89497761 bytes, budget is 67108864.
True

To fit the thin-plate smooth, raise max_table_bytes, or use a coarser grid with m= (which changes the discretization and therefore the estimates):

larger = ContinuousDiscretizationControl(
    budget=DiscretizationBudget(max_table_bytes=128 * 1024 * 1024)
)
print(GAM("y ~ s(x) + z", control=discrete_control(larger)).fit(
    source, result="prediction"
).converged)

coarser = ContinuousDiscretizationControl(m=200)
print(GAM("y ~ s(x) + z", control=discrete_control(coarser)).fit(
    source, result="prediction"
).converged)

True
True

Row selectors can go to disk when max_selector_bytes is the limit. The directory must exist; its selector files are removed when the fit ends:

directory = tempfile.mkdtemp()
on_disk = ContinuousDiscretizationControl(
    selector_memmap_directory=directory,
    budget=DiscretizationBudget(max_selector_bytes=100_000),
)
fit = GAM("y ~ s(x, bs='cr') + z", control=discrete_control(on_disk)).fit(
    source, result="prediction"
)
print(fit.converged)

True

See Discretized fitting for the grid (m=) and the rest of the discretization policy.

docs.title: First call and the compilation cache
docs.text:
The first fit of a model in a Python process takes longer than later fits of the same model and data sizes, because JAX compiles the computations it runs. Importing jaxgam also compiles a few helper functions.

To save that work across processes, importing jaxgam turns on JAX's persistent compilation cache in ~/.cache/jaxgam/jax, and caches every compiled computation however quickly it compiled. Entries are written from the first import on.

To put the cache elsewhere, set JAX_COMPILATION_CACHE_DIR before Python imports jaxgam. A jax.config.update("jax_compilation_cache_dir", ...) made before the import is overwritten by jaxgam's default.

JAX_COMPILATION_CACHE_DIR=/path/to/cache python fit_model.py

To stop jaxgam from configuring the cache, set JAXGAM_NO_COMPILATION_CACHE to any non-empty value before the import (even 0 counts). If JAX_COMPILATION_CACHE_DIR is also set, JAX itself still caches there.

JAXGAM_NO_COMPILATION_CACHE=1 python fit_model.py

docs.title: BLAS threads
docs.text:
jaxgam is tested with one BLAS thread, and we recommend the same:

OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 python fit_model.py

Set them in the environment before Python starts. A multithreaded BLAS adds up sums in an order that depends on the number of cores, so the last digits of results can differ from machine to machine; with one thread they do not. The LAPACK library jaxgam ships for its own basis computations (the scipy-openblas32 package) always runs on one thread, whatever these variables say.

There is no thread-count argument in jaxgam. JAX's CPU backend still uses several cores by itself.

docs.title: Apple silicon
docs.text:
On Apple silicon Macs the default NumPy and SciPy wheels use Apple Accelerate, and JAX's CPU linear algebra routines take their LAPACK from SciPy. When several LAPACK calls run at the same time inside one compiled computation, memory can be corrupted: the process may abort, and occasionally results are wrong with no error. This has been seen fitting models with about 100 smooths (about 1,000 coefficients), and not with 50 smooths or fewer. Linux is not affected.

Importing jaxgam on an affected Mac issues a RuntimeWarning that names the fix for the NumPy and SciPy versions you have installed. The fix is to install the OpenBLAS builds of the same versions. For numpy 2.3.5 and scipy 1.17.0 (the versions in jaxgam's lock file), with uv:

uv pip install --reinstall --no-deps --python-platform aarch64-apple-darwin \
    numpy==2.3.5 scipy==1.17.0

or with pip:

pip download --only-binary=:all: --no-deps --platform macosx_12_0_arm64 \
    numpy==2.3.5 scipy==1.17.0 -d wheels
pip install --force-reinstall --no-deps wheels/*.whl

Running uv sync afterwards can put the Accelerate builds back; repeat the step after it. To silence the warning without changing the install, set JAXGAM_ALLOW_ACCELERATE=1 (exactly 1).

docs.title: Operator fitting
docs.text:
The operator route fits models whose random effects have very many levels without ever forming the coefficient matrix. Select it with FitControl(execution="operator", linear_solver="pcg").

Each coefficient system is solved by preconditioned conjugate gradients (PCG), an iterative solver that needs only products of the system with a vector. Each product is computed by scanning the row source, so neither the model matrix nor any matrix of size coefficients by coefficients is held in memory. A random effect s(g, bs="re") is stored as one level index per row.

Use it when

  • a random effect has so many levels that the default fit would need a coefficient matrix too large for memory;
  • you know the smoothing parameters (sp=), or the model is a Poisson random intercept inside the shape where Fellner-Schall is admitted (see below).

Do not use it when

  • you need the smoothing parameters estimated for any other model: use the discretized route or the default fit;
  • you need predict(se_fit=True), summary() or EDF per term. There is an approximate variance (see below), but no exact standard errors.

The setup block makes a random-intercept model with 1,000 levels.

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from jaxgam import GAM, FitControl, OperatorControl
from jaxgam.data import DataFrameRowSource
from jaxgam.families import NegativeBinomial

rng = np.random.default_rng(4)
levels = 1000
n = 3000
g = rng.integers(0, levels, n)
x = rng.uniform(0, 1, n)
effect = rng.normal(scale=0.5, size=levels)
eta = 0.2 + 0.5 * x + effect[g]
data = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "x": x,
        "g": pd.Categorical(g, categories=range(levels)),
        "y": eta + rng.normal(scale=0.3, size=n),
        "count": rng.poisson(np.exp(eta)),
    }
)
source = DataFrameRowSource(data, response="y")
counts = DataFrameRowSource(data, response="count")
newdata = pd.DataFrame({"x": [0.2, 0.4], "g": pd.Categorical([0, 5000])})

See Row sources for the built-in sources, prior weights and offsets.

docs.title: A minimal fit with fixed smoothing parameters
docs.text:
control = FitControl(execution="operator", linear_solver="pcg")
fit = GAM("y ~ x + s(g, bs='re')", sp=[1.0], control=control).fit(
    source, result="prediction"
)
print(fit.converged, fit.convergence_info)
# True Operator observed Newton fit converged.
print(len(fit.coefficients), fit.source_scans)
# 1002 21
print(fit.predict(newdata))
# [0.12566849 0.4141132 ]

sp must be given in formula order, one value per penalty. A model with no penalized term still needs sp=[]. Level 5000 was not in training: an unseen level contributes zero, so its prediction is the fixed part only.

The levels of a random effect are a categorical column's declared categories (unused ones included), otherwise the sorted observed values.

docs.title: What you get back
docs.text:
A GAMPredictionResult (see the API reference) with predict, predict_iter and predict_matrix. pred_type is "response" or "link". With fixed smoothing parameters no REML score, trace or covariance is computed, so several attributes are None:

print(fit.score, fit.edf_total, fit.scale, fit.known_workspace_bytes)
# None None None None
try:
    fit.predict(newdata, se_fit=True)
except RuntimeError as error:
    print(error)
# Prediction standard errors are not available on the operator route. Use
# bulk_link_variance() on the fit result for approximate link-scale variances.

scale is None for families with an unknown scale and 1.0 for Poisson, Binomial and the negative binomial. The advice in the se_fit message does not apply here: this route refuses any uncertainty other than "none". materialize_covariance raises RuntimeError: No covariance provider was retained for this result. For approximate variances, see Approximate variances below.

Attribute Meaning on this route converged, convergence_info, n_iter Newton iterations for fixed sp; outer iterations for Fellner-Schall. execution_route, lambda_strategy "operator"; "fixed" or "efs_reml". smoothing_params, deviance, theta The fitted values. score, edf_total, score_error_bound, score_bound_method Fellner-Schall only. source_scans, batches_scanned Scans made by the fit, not by the setup pass. known_workspace_bytes None for fixed sp; the planned workspace for Fellner-Schall. operator_diagnostics Solver and scan detail (below).

docs.title: Telling whether the fit converged
docs.text:
The fit is a Newton iteration on the penalized deviance, using the observed curvature of the family. It stops when the relative change of the objective is below OperatorControl.tolerance and the gradient is small; a Gaussian identity model stops after its first solve. convergence_info is one of:

  • "Operator observed Newton fit converged.";
  • "Maximum operator iterations reached." (raise max_iterations);
  • "Operator PCG failed with status N." (raise cg_max_iterations, or try use_coarse=True).

The last two return converged=False without raising. Some failures raise instead: when the system cannot be shown to be positive definite, a LinAlgError such as Actual weighted system has no sufficient Schur SPD certificate., and after 100 step halvings RuntimeError: Operator step halving could not recover a valid step.

fit.operator_diagnostics holds the detail: inner_status (status of the last PCG solve, 1 means converged), final_gradient_norm, krylov_iterations, completed_solves, peak_bound_bytes, and the scans used for each purpose (rhs_scans, objective_scans, certificate_scans, preparation_scans):

diagnostics = fit.operator_diagnostics
print(diagnostics.inner_status, diagnostics.completed_solves, diagnostics.krylov_iterations)
# 1 1 6

Every byte figure on this route is an accounting bound for arrays jaxgam knows it will hold; it excludes the source's own storage and allocator or compiler memory.

docs.title: Models and families
docs.text:
Random effects. Any number of s(..., bs="re") terms. Factors in the term form the levels (two factors give one level per combination), and a numeric variable in the term gives a random slope, for example s(g, x, bs="re"). Their width is not limited by max_modest_coefficients.

The small block. Everything else (the intercept, numeric parametric terms and s(), te() or ti() smooths with cr, cs, cc, tp, ts or gp bases, with or without a factor or numeric by) is held as an ordinary small matrix. Its raw width is capped by OperatorControl.max_modest_coefficients (64):

try:
    GAM("y ~ s(x, bs='cr', k=70) + s(g, bs='re')", sp=[1.0, 1.0],
        control=control).fit(source, result="prediction")
except MemoryError as error:
    print(error)
# Modest operator width 71 exceeds hard cap 64.

Families. There is no fixed list: any family that provides a row-wise deviance with its derivatives and observed information is accepted. The tests compare with mgcv for Gaussian (identity, log, inverse), Poisson (log, identity, sqrt), Binomial (logit, probit, cloglog, log), Gamma (inverse, log, identity) and the negative binomial with fixed theta (log, identity, sqrt). Theta must be fixed:

try:
    GAM("count ~ x + s(g, bs='re')", family="nb", sp=[1.0], control=control).fit(
        counts, result="prediction")
except NotImplementedError as error:
    print(error)
# Operator fitting currently requires fixed theta.

fit_nb = GAM("count ~ x + s(g, bs='re')", family=NegativeBinomial(3.0, fixed=True),
             sp=[1.0], control=control).fit(counts, result="prediction")
print(fit_nb.converged)
# True

A thin plate, Gaussian process or tensor smooth in the small block needs workspace for every row of a batch. The fit plans for batch_rows rows, or for the number of rows in the source when that is smaller, so a source of a few hundred rows fits at the defaults. On the 3,000 rows above the default budget is not enough for y ~ s(x, k=8) + s(g, bs='re'):

MemoryError: Frozen operator requires 487335048 bytes; budget is 48614104. Lower batch_rows or raise the memory budget.

The budget in the message is what is left of memory_budget_bytes after the fit's other arrays. Lower batch_rows (or raise memory_budget_bytes):

smaller_batches = FitControl(execution="operator", linear_solver="pcg",
                             batch_rows=1024)
fit_tp = GAM("y ~ s(x, k=8) + s(g, bs='re')", sp=[1.0, 1.0],
             control=smaller_batches).fit(source, result="prediction")
print(fit_tp.converged)
# True

docs.title: Options that matter
docs.text:
Option Default What it does FitControl.linear_solver "cholesky" Must be "pcg" on this route. FitControl.batch_rows 65_536 Rows per source scan. The fit uses the source's row count when that is smaller. FitControl.memory_budget_bytes 512 MiB Bound on the arrays the setup pass and the fit know they will hold. OperatorControl.max_modest_coefficients 64 Cap on the width of the small block. OperatorControl.max_iterations 200 Newton iterations. OperatorControl.tolerance 1e-7 Newton stopping tolerance. OperatorControl.cg_max_iterations 1000 PCG iterations per solve. OperatorControl.cg_rtol, cg_atol 1e-10, 1e-12 PCG stops when the residual is below max(cg_atol, cg_rtol * norm of the right-hand side). OperatorControl.use_coarse False Adds a coarse correction to the preconditioner.

Pass them as FitControl(operator=OperatorControl(...)). Field-level detail is in the API reference.

docs.title: Fellner-Schall on this route
docs.text:
Without sp, optimizer="efs" selects the smoothing parameter by the extended Fellner-Schall update (mgcv's efsudr), but only inside the model shape over which its score error bound was measured:

  • Poisson with the log link;
  • exactly one random effect, made of factors only (no random slopes), with 257 to 4,096 levels and between 1 and 16 rows per level on average;
  • at most 4 other coefficients, all unpenalized (the intercept and numeric parametric terms);
  • unit prior weights and no offset;
  • batch_rows from 64 to 65,536.
def efs_frame(levels, rows_per_level, seed):
    rows = levels * rows_per_level
    gen = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    group = np.arange(rows) % levels
    xs = np.linspace(-1, 1, rows)
    ys = gen.poisson(np.exp(0.2 + 0.5 * xs + 0.3 * np.sin(group / 31.0)))
    return pd.DataFrame({"y": ys, "x": xs, "g": pd.Categorical(group)})

efs_data = efs_frame(300, 2, 32031)
efs_source = DataFrameRowSource(efs_data, response="y")
fit_efs = GAM("y ~ x + s(g, bs='re')", family="poisson", optimizer="efs",
              control=control).fit(efs_source, result="prediction")
print(fit_efs.converged, fit_efs.convergence_info, fit_efs.n_iter)
# True score_window 4
print(fit_efs.smoothing_params, fit_efs.score_bound_method)
# [27.99472604] arrowhead_poisson_empirical_v2
print(fit_efs.edf_total, fit_efs.score_error_bound)
# 27.524338405228207 8.67825993407174e-08

Outside that shape the fit raises before it starts:

Not admitted Error Another family or link NotImplementedError: Operator EFS currently supports calibrated Poisson/log indexed fits. batch_rows outside 64 to 65,536 NotImplementedError: Calibrated operator EFS requires batch_rows 64-65536. Levels, rows per level or other coefficients outside the shape NotImplementedError: Calibrated operator EFS requires 257-4096 indexed levels, 1-16 rows per level and batch_rows 64-65536, and at most 4 modest coefficients. A penalized smooth, a random slope, weights or an offset NotImplementedError beginning Operator EFS source start needs ...

The Fellner-Schall controls (outer_limit, score_tolerance, pirls_tolerance, log_lambda_max, history_limit) come from FitControl(efs=EFSControl(...)); the inner fits use OperatorControl. On these results operator_diagnostics describes only the final accepted fit, while source_scans counts the whole search.

docs.title: What an "indeterminate" stop means
docs.text:
The score on this route is computed with a known error bound. Fellner-Schall compares each trial's score with the accepted one, and the comparison counts only when the difference is larger than the two bounds added together. If it is not, or if a bound could not be given, the comparison is indeterminate. The fit then stops, keeps the last accepted smoothing parameter, and returns converged=False with convergence_info="indeterminate_score". No warning is issued. operator_diagnostics.efs_indeterminate_comparisons counts these comparisons.

A bound needs, among other conditions, all responses at most 32, a converged PCG solve, and OperatorControl no looser than its defaults (tolerance <= 1e-7, cg_rtol <= 1e-10, cg_atol <= 1e-12). Loosening any of them removes the bound, and the fit stops after one iteration:

loose = FitControl(execution="operator", linear_solver="pcg",
                   operator=OperatorControl(tolerance=1e-6))
fit_loose = GAM("y ~ x + s(g, bs='re')", family="poisson", optimizer="efs",
                control=loose).fit(efs_source, result="prediction")
print(fit_loose.converged, fit_loose.convergence_info, fit_loose.n_iter)
# False indeterminate_score 1
print(fit_loose.score_bound_method)
# unavailable

An indeterminate stop can also happen at the default controls, because the fitted coefficients are then less exact than the score comparison needs. Tighter controls make the comparisons decidable more often; the test suite fits these models with OperatorControl(tolerance=1e-11, cg_rtol=1e-13, cg_atol=1e-15).

The other stops are "score_window" and "deviance_change" (converged), and "iteration_limit", "inner_failure" and "invalid_update" (not converged).

docs.title: Approximate variances
docs.text:
fit.bulk_link_variance estimates the variance of the linear predictor (the link scale) for any number of new rows, from random probes of the penalized Fisher information. It needs a converged operator fit and the original training source, which it scans again. calibration_data (at most 256 rows) is checked against exact solves; the call raises RuntimeError when the estimate disagrees with them by more than max_calibration_standard_errors (default 5).

variance, calibration = fit_nb.bulk_link_variance(
    counts, newdata, probes=16, seed=0, memory_budget_bytes=256 * 1024 * 1024
)
print(calibration.exact, calibration.estimated)
# [0.3246366  0.00154859] [0.11842111 0.00343223]
for batch in variance.estimate_iter(DataFrameRowSource(newdata)):
    print(batch.positions, batch.link_se, batch.monte_carlo_se)
# [0 1] [0.34412368 0.05858525] [0.02807059 0.00109346]

With 16 probes the estimate is rough (compare exact and estimated); the second row, at an unseen level, has only the fixed part's variance.

estimate_iter takes any row source with the model's covariates and yields batches with positions, variance, monte_carlo_se (the Monte Carlo error of the estimate) and link_se (the square root of variance). More probes give a smaller Monte Carlo error and more training scans; each probe is one PCG solve. For a family with an unknown scale (Gaussian, Gamma), pass scale= yourself: ValueError: Unknown-scale family requires an explicit Fisher scale. variance.diagnostics reports the solves, scans and maximum_relative_residual. The calibration checks only the selected rows; it does not bound the other rows or the bias of the iterative solves.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
Not accepted Error linear_solver other than "pcg" (the default included) ValueError: execution='operator' requires linear_solver='pcg'. result="full" or "inference" NotImplementedError: Operator full/inference results need planned score/EDF/variance providers; this route currently requires result='prediction'. uncertainty="fisher" or "covariance" NotImplementedError: Operator uncertainty needs a planned selected-variance provider. No sp (without optimizer="efs") NotImplementedError: Operator fitting requires explicit fixed sp. Estimated theta NotImplementedError: Operator fitting currently requires fixed theta. device="gpu" NotImplementedError: Frozen-system operator PCG currently uses CPU. A DataFrame instead of a row source TypeError: Operator fitting requires a replayable RowSource. fit(weights=...) or fit(offset=...) ValueError: Operator weights/offset must be owned by the RowSource. by= on a random effect, te() with re, other bases NotImplementedError: Operator preparation supports numeric terms, cr/cs/cc, tp/ts/gp and re. Extra options (such as xt) on cr, cs, cc or re smooths NotImplementedError: Operator custom smooth/precision/id options are unsupported. A factor parametric term NotImplementedError: Prepared setup currently supports numeric parametric terms only. Wrong number of smoothing parameters ValueError: sp must have N elements for this model.

gaussian_compression=True is ignored on this route. Models without an intercept are fitted, but some layouts are refused with a NotImplementedError (for example General no-intercept operator null projection is not yet available.). A gp smooth whose penalty has a negative eigenvalue raises ValueError: Each modest penalty must be positive semidefinite.

docs.title: Prediction results
docs.text:
GAMPredictionResult is the small result that fit(..., result="prediction") returns. It keeps the coefficients, a few scalar diagnostics and, only if you ask for it, what is needed for standard errors. It keeps no training rows, so its size does not grow with the data.

Use it when you fit on a row-source route (it is the only result those routes return), or when you fit a DataFrame and only need to predict on new data.

Do not use it when you need summary(), plot(), per-smooth EDF or in-sample fitted values: fit the DataFrame with result="full" instead.

All examples on this page use this setup block. It fits on the dense route and keeps what standard errors need:

import pickle

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from jaxgam import GAM, FitControl
from jaxgam.data import DataFrameRowSource

rng = np.random.default_rng(1)
n = 400
x = rng.uniform(0, 1, n)
z = rng.uniform(0, 1, n)
y = np.sin(2 * np.pi * x) + 0.5 * z + rng.normal(0, 0.3, n)
data = pd.DataFrame({"x": x, "z": z, "y": y})
newdata = pd.DataFrame({"x": [0.1, 0.4, 0.7], "z": [0.5, 0.5, 0.5]})

control = FitControl(uncertainty="fisher")
fit = GAM("y ~ s(x) + z", control=control).fit(data, result="prediction")

docs.title: predict()
docs.text:
print(fit.predict(newdata))
prediction, se = fit.predict(newdata, se_fit=True)
print(se)

[ 0.85121636  0.84844347 -0.78349386]
[0.04486273 0.04101813 0.04336924]
Option Default What it does newdata required DataFrame or dict holding every variable the formula uses. pred_type "response" "response" for the mean, "link" for the linear predictor. Anything else raises ValueError. se_fit False Also return standard errors, as (prediction, se). On the response scale the standard error is the link-scale one times the absolute derivative of the inverse link. offset None One finite value per row of newdata. A model fitted with a nonzero offset warns when you leave it out, and predicts without it.

predict_matrix(newdata) returns the matrix that maps the coefficients to the linear predictor (mgcv's type="lpmatrix").

docs.title: predict_iter(): new data from a row source
docs.text:
When the new data are themselves too large for one call, pass a row source. predict_iter(source, batch_rows=None, *, pred_type="response", se_fit=False) yields one (row_positions, prediction) pair per batch, or (row_positions, (prediction, se)) with se_fit=True. The source needs no response. Offsets come from the source.

new_source = DataFrameRowSource(newdata)
for positions, (batch_prediction, batch_se) in fit.predict_iter(
    new_source, batch_rows=2, se_fit=True
):
    print(positions, batch_prediction.round(4), batch_se.round(4))

[0 1] [0.8512 0.8484] [0.0449 0.041 ]
[2] [-0.7835] [0.0434]

batch_rows defaults to the FitControl.batch_rows of the fit. Each batch is one prediction call, so each must fit the output and memory budgets (see Memory and performance). Writing your own source is covered in Row sources.

docs.title: Standard errors and FitControl(uncertainty=...)
docs.text:
A prediction result keeps nothing for standard errors unless you ask for it when you fit:

uncertainty Keeps predict(se_fit=True) "none" (default) Nothing Raises RuntimeError "fisher" A factor of the penalized Fisher information (size grows with the number of coefficients squared, not with rows) Exact standard errors for the requested rows "covariance" The coefficient covariance matrix Vp, built at the end of the fit (the streamed QR routes also keep their factor) Standard errors

The standard errors match those of a full result of the same fit:

full = GAM("y ~ s(x) + z").fit(data)
_, full_se = full.predict(newdata, se_fit=True)
print(np.allclose(se, full_se))

True

Without uncertainty, se_fit=True raises:

RuntimeError: Prediction uncertainty is unavailable for this prediction-only result. Fit with FitControl(uncertainty='fisher' or 'covariance').

With "fisher" you can still build Vp later, under a budget you give:

Vp = fit.materialize_covariance(memory_budget_bytes=10_000_000)
print(Vp.shape)

(11, 11)

The dense, streamed and discretized routes support all three values. The operator route accepts only "none"; its approximate variances come from bulk_link_variance(), described in Operator fitting, and se_fit=True on an operator result raises an error that points there. "covariance" raises MemoryError when Vp would exceed FitControl.memory_budget_bytes. A prediction result has no Vp attribute; with "covariance" read it as fit.to_predictor().Vp.

docs.title: What you get back
docs.text:
GAMPredictionResult attributes worth reading:

Attribute Meaning converged, n_iter, convergence_info Whether the fit converged, its outer iteration count, and the stop reason in words. Always check converged. smoothing_params Selected or supplied smoothing parameters. edf_total Total effective degrees of freedom (None on fixed-sp operator fits). score, deviance, scale REML score, deviance and scale (score is None on fixed-sp operator fits). theta Negative binomial theta. None for other families. coefficients, family, formula, n The fitted coefficients, family, formula and number of rows. execution_route, execution_fallback_reason Which route ran, and why Gaussian QR compression was not used, if you asked for it. lambda_strategy, method How the smoothing parameters were chosen, and "REML". source_scans, batches_scanned Full scans and batches the fit read from a row source, excluding the setup pass (None on the dense route). known_workspace_bytes The route's estimate of its fit workspace, where it has one. optimizer_diagnostics EFSOptimizerDiagnostics for Fellner-Schall fits. 
print(fit.converged, fit.convergence_info, fit.execution_route)
print(fit.edf_total, fit.scale, fit.theta, fit.source_scans)

True full convergence dense
9.799818771624803 0.09034243612941105 None None

Route-specific fields (for example prediction_policy and discretization on the discretized route, operator_diagnostics and score_error_bound on the operator route) are described on each route's page and in GAMPredictionResult in the API reference.

For a negative binomial with fixed theta, theta is None from a Newton fit on the dense or streamed route, and the fixed value from a Fellner-Schall, discretized or operator fit.

docs.title: What is not available
docs.text: A prediction result has no summary(), plot(), fitted_values, linear_predictor, Vp, per-smooth edf or null_deviance, and predict() always needs newdata. To get the in-sample fit, predict on the training data (on a row-source route, with predict_iter() on the training source).

docs.title: to_predictor() and pickling
docs.text:
to_predictor() returns the GAMPredictor the result holds, an object with predict(), predict_matrix() and predict_iter() and nothing else. Hand it to code that should only predict.

predictor = fit.to_predictor()
restored = pickle.loads(pickle.dumps(predictor))
print(np.allclose(restored.predict(newdata), fit.predict(newdata)))

restored_fit = pickle.loads(pickle.dumps(fit))
print(np.allclose(restored_fit.predict(newdata), fit.predict(newdata)))

True
True

Both the result and the predictor pickle with the standard library. Treat a pickle as a short-lived handoff between processes running the same jaxgam version: loading a predictor pickled by another version issues a UserWarning that predictions may be wrong or fail. A family whose link class is defined inside a function cannot be pickled with pickle; the separate cloudpickle package can do it.

docs.title: How it compares with the other result modes
docs.text: "full" (GAMResults) "inference" (GAMInferenceResult) "prediction" (GAMPredictionResult) Routes Dense Dense All Training rows, fitted values Yes No No summary(), plot() Yes No No Vp, per-smooth EDF Yes Yes No (covariance only on request) Standard errors Always Always With uncertainty="fisher" or "covariance" predict_iter() Through to_predictor() Through to_predictor() Yes Prediction budgets Not applied Not applied output_budget_bytes, memory_budget_bytes

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• predict_iter() needs a row source: TypeError: predict_iter requires a replayable RowSource.
  • A prediction whose output exceeds FitControl.output_budget_bytes raises, for example MemoryError: Prediction output requires 4000 bytes, exceeding output budget 1000 bytes. Use predict_iter() with smaller batches.
  • A level of a parametric factor not seen in fitting raises ValueError: Parametric factor 'f' has new level(s) ['w'] not seen during fitting. Predictions for unseen levels of a parametric factor are undefined. An unseen or missing level of a random effect s(g, bs="re") predicts with a random-effect contribution of zero (mgcv returns NA for a missing one).
