docs.title: Row sources
docs.text:
A row source hands a fit your data in batches of rows, and can replay them from the start as often as the fit asks. The streamed, discretized and operator routes read their data only through a row source, so the data never have to sit in memory as one table.

Use a row source when you fit with FitControl(execution="stream"), "discrete" or "operator", or when you predict on new data with predict_iter() (see Prediction results).

Do not use one for the default dense fit: it takes a DataFrame or dict and rejects a row source with TypeError.

Formally, a row source is any object that satisfies the protocol jaxgam.data.RowSource:

Member What it must do n_rows Property: the number of rows the source yields in one scan. scan(batch_rows) Yield RowBatch objects of at most batch_rows rows each, covering every row once, in the same order on every call. fingerprint() Return a string that stays the same while the data stay the same, and changes when they change. has_explicit_weights, has_explicit_offset Optional booleans: False says the batches carry default weights (ones) or offset (zeros).

jaxgam ships three row sources in jaxgam.data. They are not exported from the top-level jaxgam package. All three accept weights=, offset= and row_selection=, and a response (response= names a column of a DataFrame, y= gives it directly to the other two); see Row sources in the API reference for every argument.

All examples on this page use this setup block:

import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from jaxgam import GAM, ContinuousDiscretizationControl, FitControl
from jaxgam.data import (
    ArrayRowSource,
    DataFrameRowSource,
    MemmapRowSource,
    RowBatch,
    RowSource,
)

rng = np.random.default_rng(1)
n = 400
x = rng.uniform(0, 1, n)
z = rng.uniform(0, 1, n)
y = np.sin(2 * np.pi * x) + 0.5 * z + rng.normal(0, 0.3, n)
data = pd.DataFrame({"x": x, "z": z, "y": y})

control = FitControl(execution="stream", linear_solver="qr")
model = GAM("y ~ s(x, bs='cr') + z", control=control)

docs.title: DataFrameRowSource: a DataFrame you already have
docs.text:
DataFrameRowSource(data, response="y") wraps a DataFrame. The column named by response becomes the response; every other column is a covariate. Categorical columns keep their categories and ordering.

source = DataFrameRowSource(data, response="y")
fit = model.fit(source, result="prediction")
print(source.n_rows, fit.converged, fit.execution_route)

400 True stream_exact_reml_qr

A fit needs the response: a source made without response= raises ValueError: Prepared fitting requires a response in the RowSource. on the streamed route. For predict_iter() the response is not needed.

docs.title: ArrayRowSource: aligned arrays
docs.text:
ArrayRowSource(columns, y=..., weights=..., offset=...) takes a mapping of column names to one-dimensional arrays (or pandas Series, or memory maps) of equal length.

weights = rng.uniform(0.5, 2.0, n)
source = ArrayRowSource({"x": x, "z": z}, y=y, weights=weights)
fit = model.fit(source, result="prediction")
print(source.has_explicit_weights, source.has_explicit_offset, fit.converged)

True False True

docs.title: MemmapRowSource.from_npy_files: data on disk
docs.text:
MemmapRowSource.from_npy_files opens one .npy file per column as a read-only NumPy memory map, so a scan reads only the rows of the current batch. Write each column with np.save as a one-dimensional array.

directory = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
for name, values in {"x": x, "z": z, "y": y}.items():
    np.save(directory / f"{name}.npy", values)

source = MemmapRowSource.from_npy_files(
    {"x": directory / "x.npy", "z": directory / "z.npy"},
    y=directory / "y.npy",
)
fit = model.fit(source, result="prediction")
print(source.n_rows, fit.converged)

400 True

weights= and offset= take file paths here too.

docs.title: Weights and offset belong to the source
docs.text:
On a row-source route, prior weights and the offset come from the source. Passing them to fit() raises, for example on the streamed route:

ValueError: weights and offset must be owned by the RowSource for execution='stream'; do not pass separate arrays.

The built-in sources check them when you construct the source: weights must be finite and non-negative with a positive sum over the selected rows, and the offset must be finite.

docs.title: row_selection: fit a subset of rows
docs.text:
row_selection= takes integer positions into the columns. The source then yields only those rows, in the order given, and n_rows is their count.

even_rows = ArrayRowSource({"x": x, "z": z}, y=y, row_selection=np.arange(0, n, 2))
fit = model.fit(even_rows, result="prediction")
print(even_rows.n_rows, fit.n)

200 200

An empty selection, or a position outside the columns, raises ValueError.

docs.title: What a fit requires of a source
docs.text:
A fit scans the source several times: the setup pass reads it to place knots and build constraints, and the fit reads it again for every iteration. Every scan must therefore:

  • yield the same rows in the same order, whatever batch_rows is (the fit asks for different batch sizes; the streamed route, for example, first calls scan(1) twice to check that two scans start with the same rows);
  • yield batches of at most batch_rows rows, with every row marked valid (padded batches are not supported);
  • give each row the same row_positions on every scan;
  • keep the same columns and, for categorical columns, the same categories in every batch.

The fit compares fingerprint() before and after its scans. If the source changed, it raises RuntimeError, for example RuntimeError: RowSource changed during the fit or RuntimeError: RowSource changed after preparation; prepare again. The built-in sources hash their whole content. On the streamed and discretized routes that hash is computed once when the fit starts and once more when it ends, so a change made during the fit raises at the end.

docs.title: Writing your own source
docs.text:
Write your own source when your data live somewhere the built-in sources do not read: CSV or Parquet files, a database, or files spread over a directory. The class below reads a CSV file in chunks with pandas, so only one batch is in memory at a time. It treats the columns listed in factor_levels as factors with fixed categories.

class CsvRowSource:
    """Replay a CSV file in batches; categorical columns get fixed levels."""

    has_explicit_weights = False  # batches carry weight 1 for every row
    has_explicit_offset = False  # batches carry offset 0 for every row

    def __init__(self, path, response, factor_levels=None):
        self.path = Path(path)
        self.response = response
        self.factor_levels = factor_levels or {}
        self._n_rows = sum(len(chunk) for chunk in pd.read_csv(self.path, chunksize=65_536))

    @property
    def n_rows(self):
        return self._n_rows

    def fingerprint(self):
        # Called many times per fit: keep it cheap, but change it when the file changes.
        status = self.path.stat()
        return f"{self.path.resolve()}|{status.st_size}|{status.st_mtime_ns}"

    def scan(self, batch_rows):
        start = 0
        for chunk in pd.read_csv(self.path, chunksize=batch_rows):
            rows = len(chunk)
            columns = {}
            for name in chunk.columns:
                if name == self.response:
                    continue
                if name in self.factor_levels:
                    columns[name] = pd.Series(
                        pd.Categorical(chunk[name], categories=self.factor_levels[name])
                    )
                else:
                    columns[name] = chunk[name].to_numpy()
            yield RowBatch(
                columns=columns,
                y=chunk[self.response].to_numpy(dtype=float),
                weight=np.ones(rows),
                offset=np.zeros(rows),
                valid=np.ones(rows, dtype=bool),
                row_positions=np.arange(start, start + rows, dtype=np.intp),
            )
            start += rows

Write a CSV file, check the class against the protocol and fit with it:

csv_path = directory / "data.csv"
data.to_csv(csv_path, index=False)

source = CsvRowSource(csv_path, response="y")
print(isinstance(source, RowSource))
fit = model.fit(source, result="prediction")
print(fit.converged, fit.execution_route)

True
True stream_exact_reml_qr

The streamed route takes no factor terms. The discretized route does, so the same class with a grouping column can fit a random effect there. That route also needs the factor named in factor_names (see Discretized fitting):

group = rng.integers(0, 20, n)
grouped = data.assign(g=group, y=data["y"] + rng.normal(0, 0.5, 20)[group])
grouped_path = directory / "grouped.csv"
grouped.to_csv(grouped_path, index=False)

source = CsvRowSource(grouped_path, response="y", factor_levels={"g": list(range(20))})
discrete = FitControl(
    execution="discrete",
    discretization=ContinuousDiscretizationControl(factor_names=("g",)),
    smoothing_strategy="working_model_reml",
)
fit = GAM("y ~ s(x, bs='cr') + z + s(g, bs='re')", control=discrete).fit(
    source, result="prediction"
)
print(fit.converged, fit.execution_route, len(fit.smoothing_params))

True discrete 2

What a custom source must get right:

  • A cheap fingerprint(). The fit calls it many times (hundreds of times for a small streamed fit), and the reuse of one hash per fit described above applies only to the built-in sources. Derive it from metadata such as a path, size and modification time, or a version string you control, and make sure it changes when the data change.
  • Batches of at most batch_rows rows. A larger batch raises, on the streamed route ValueError: RowSource yielded N rows for a setup scan requesting at most M. (with the actual counts).
  • The same rows in the same order on every scan, with stable row_positions (here the row number in the file).
  • The same factor levels in every batch. Give a factor column as a pandas Categorical Series with a fixed categories= list. Levels that depend on which rows happen to be in a batch raise, for example RuntimeError: Factor column 'g' changed levels during scan on the discretized route.
  • has_explicit_weights and has_explicit_offset. Declare them False when your batches carry the defaults, as above. If you leave them out, jaxgam treats the source as supplying both, as mgcv's bam() treats weights= and offset= arguments; on the discretized route they are then carried through the compression as extra columns, and predict_iter() applies the batch offset without warning.
  • A response for fitting. Set y on every batch; it may be None in a source used only for prediction.

Reading Parquet works the same way: scan() can loop over pyarrow's ParquetFile.iter_batches(batch_size=batch_rows) (a third-party method, not part of jaxgam) and convert each record batch to columns, with the fingerprint taken from the file's path, size and modification time.

docs.title: Smoothing parameter selection
docs.text:
Each smooth term carries one or more smoothing parameters that set how wiggly it may be. This page covers the ways jaxgam chooses them, or lets you fix them, when your data are an in-memory DataFrame (the dense route).

Use this page when you fit from a DataFrame and want to control how smoothing parameters are chosen.

Do not use it when your data come from a row source: the streamed, discretized and operator routes have their own rules (see Streamed fitting, Discretized fitting and Operator fitting).

The four choices:

Choice How you ask for it lambda_strategy Exact REML by Newton's method (default) GAM(formula) "newton_reml" Fixed smoothing parameters GAM(formula, sp=[...]) "fixed" Extended Fellner-Schall GAM(formula, optimizer="efs") "efs_reml" Gaussian QR compression GAM(formula, control=FitControl(gaussian_compression=True)) "newton_reml", or "lbfgs_reml" above 50 penalties

All examples on this page use this setup block:

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from jaxgam import GAM, EFSControl, FitControl

rng = np.random.default_rng(1)
n = 400
x = rng.uniform(0, 1, n)
z = rng.uniform(0, 1, n)
y = np.sin(2 * np.pi * x) + 0.5 * z + rng.normal(0, 0.3, n)
counts = rng.poisson(np.exp(0.5 + np.sin(2 * np.pi * x)))
data = pd.DataFrame({"x": x, "z": z, "y": y, "counts": counts})

docs.title: Default: exact REML by Newton's method
docs.text:
With no sp= and the default optimizer="newton", jaxgam minimizes the restricted maximum likelihood (REML) criterion over the log smoothing parameters by Newton's method, refitting the coefficients by penalized iteratively reweighted least squares at each trial. This is the estimate of mgcv's gam(method="REML").

fit = GAM("y ~ s(x) + z").fit(data)
print(fit.converged, fit.n_iter, fit.convergence_info)
print(fit.lambda_strategy, fit.smoothing_params)

True 7 full convergence
newton_reml [0.01101987]

What you get back. converged is True when the Newton iteration met its tolerance. convergence_info is "full convergence", "step failed", "iteration limit" or "non-finite REML score or gradient", sometimes with a note appended (for example that an inner fit did not converge, or that a small diagonal jitter was added to a factorization, which also issues a RuntimeWarning). n_iter counts outer Newton iterations. score is the REML criterion and smoothing_params the selected values. For Gaussian and Gamma models scale is estimated; for family="nb" theta is estimated and reported in theta (only when the model has at least one smooth; otherwise theta stays at its starting value and theta is None).

The Newton iteration has no public settings: its iteration limit and tolerances are fixed.

docs.title: Fixed smoothing parameters with sp=
docs.text:
Pass one positive value per penalty, on the natural (not log) scale. The order is the order of the penalties in the formula: smooth terms left to right, each term's penalties together. A te() term has one penalty per margin, so te(x, z) takes two values.

fixed = GAM("y ~ s(x) + z", sp=[0.01]).fit(data)
print(fixed.lambda_strategy, fixed.smoothing_params)

fixed_counts = GAM("counts ~ s(x)", family="poisson", sp=[0.01]).fit(data)
print(fixed_counts.n_iter, fixed_counts.convergence_info)

tensor = GAM("y ~ te(x, z)").fit(data)
print(len(tensor.smoothing_params))

fixed [0.01]
0 fixed sp
2

smoothing_params reports the values exactly as you supplied them. For Poisson, Binomial and fixed-theta negative binomial models a fixed sp means one coefficient fit (n_iter=0, convergence_info="fixed sp"). For Gaussian and Gamma models the scale is still estimated, and for family="nb" theta is still estimated, so an outer iteration still runs over those parameters with the smoothing parameters held, as in mgcv.

A supplied sp takes precedence over optimizer: GAM(formula, sp=..., optimizer="efs") is a fixed-sp fit.

Limits. A wrong count or a non-positive value raises ValueError:

ValueError: sp has 2 elements but model has 1 penalty terms.
ValueError: sp must contain strictly positive, finite values (smoothing parameters are on the natural scale and are log-transformed internally); got invalid value(s) [0.0].

Per-term sp= inside s(), te() or ti() is not supported and raises NotImplementedError; use the model-level GAM(formula, sp=[...]).

docs.title: Extended Fellner-Schall (optimizer="efs")
docs.text:
The extended Fellner-Schall method updates each smoothing parameter by a closed-form step instead of a Newton step. It follows mgcv's gam(method="REML", optimizer="efs") (the routine efsudr).

Use it when you want mgcv's optimizer="efs" results.

Do not use it when you need a fixed sp (it is then ignored), or when the family or link is outside the list below.

efs = GAM("y ~ s(x) + z", optimizer="efs").fit(data)
print(efs.converged, efs.n_iter, efs.convergence_info, efs.lambda_strategy)
print(efs.smoothing_params)
d = efs.optimizer_diagnostics
print(d.stop_reason, d.outer_iterations, len(d.accepted_score_history))

True 4 deviance_change efs_reml
[0.01101975]
deviance_change 4 4

Settings go in FitControl(efs=EFSControl(...)):

Option Default What it does outer_limit 200 Maximum outer iterations. Stopping on the last one is reported as an iteration limit. log_lambda_max 15.0 Cap on trial log smoothing parameters. score_tolerance 0.1 Stop when the last four REML scores differ by less than this and the largest proposed log step is below 0.05 (after iteration 3). pirls_tolerance 1e-7 Inner coefficient-fit tolerance; also stop when the deviance changes by less than 100 * pirls_tolerance relative. pirls_max_iter 200 Maximum inner coefficient-fit iterations. history_limit 200 Longest score history kept in the diagnostics. 
short = GAM(
    "counts ~ s(x)",
    family="poisson",
    optimizer="efs",
    control=FitControl(efs=EFSControl(outer_limit=2)),
).fit(data)
print(short.converged, short.convergence_info)

False iteration limit reached

Families and links on the dense route. Gaussian and Gamma (scale estimated), Poisson and Binomial with any link, and the negative binomial with log, identity or sqrt link, theta fixed or estimated.

What you get back. converged is True when the fit stopped on "score_window" or "deviance_change"; convergence_info holds that stop reason, or "iteration limit reached". n_iter is the number of outer iterations. optimizer_diagnostics is an EFSOptimizerDiagnostics with, among others, stop_reason, outer_iterations, inner_iterations, theta_iterations, accepted_score_history and, for Gaussian and Gamma, accepted_score_phi_history. For a negative binomial with fixed theta, theta is the fixed value (a Newton fit reports None there).

Limits. These raise:

Case Error Another family or link (for example NegativeBinomial(link="probit")) NotImplementedError: optimizer='efs' does not support this known-scale family/link (or unknown-scale) Estimated-theta negative binomial with identity or sqrt link and no offset that makes the zero-coefficient mean positive ValueError: Estimated NB identity/sqrt EFS has no valid default zero-coefficient recovery anchor for this offset; mgcv rejects the same input. Supply an offset whose zero-coefficient means are positive. Rank-deficient penalized model ValueError (for example EFS known-scale path requires an identifiable penalized system) Prior weights outside 1e-10 to 1e10 (zero weights are allowed only for Gaussian with log or inverse link) ValueError (for example EFS known-scale path requires finite positive prior weights inside PIRLS clipping bounds) Fixed-theta negative binomial with responses strictly between 0 and 1 ValueError: Fixed-theta NB EFS does not support fractional responses below one

A model without penalties skips Fellner-Schall and is fitted directly.

docs.title: Gaussian QR compression (gaussian_compression=True)
docs.text:
For a Gaussian model with identity link, jaxgam can reduce the weighted design to one QR factorization and then run every REML trial on coefficient-sized arrays instead of the rows.

Use it when the model is Gaussian with identity link and has at least one smooth.

Do not use it when you want Fellner-Schall: the request is then not applied.

qr = GAM("y ~ s(x) + z", control=FitControl(gaussian_compression=True)).fit(data)
print(qr.execution_route, qr.execution_fallback_reason, qr.smoothing_params)

ineligible = GAM(
    "counts ~ s(x)",
    family="poisson",
    control=FitControl(gaussian_compression=True),
).fit(data)
print(ineligible.execution_route, "|", ineligible.execution_fallback_reason)

gaussian_qr None [0.01101987]
dense | Gaussian QR requires the exact Gaussian family with identity link

Eligibility. The family is exactly Gaussian with identity link, the model has at least one penalty, the coefficients are identifiable (no rank deficiency), the data are finite and every prior weight is between 1e-10 and 1e10. It also works with a fixed sp.

How to tell whether it was used. An ineligible request never raises: the ordinary dense fit runs, execution_route is "dense" and execution_fallback_reason holds the reason. Possible reasons:

  • Gaussian QR requires the exact Gaussian family with identity link
  • Gaussian QR smoothing optimization requires at least one penalty
  • Gaussian QR currently requires a full identifiable coefficient map
  • Gaussian QR requires finite dense fitting data
  • Gaussian QR currently requires unclipped finite positive weights
  • Gaussian QR compression requires Newton smoothing selection. (with optimizer="efs" and no sp)

When it is used, execution_route is "gaussian_qr".

Many penalties. Up to 50 penalties the same Newton iteration runs on the compressed problem (lambda_strategy="newton_reml"). Above 50 it switches to SciPy's L-BFGS-B (lambda_strategy="lbfgs_reml"). The tests cover this switch only just above the threshold, at 51 penalties. There, where the REML criterion is flat, L-BFGS-B can stop at smoothing parameters far from the Newton fit's while the score and fitted values agree closely; compare score and predictions, not smoothing_params, if you check one against the other.

docs.title: Only REML is available
docs.text:
method="REML" is the default and the only accepted method. method="ML" raises at construction:

try:
    GAM("y ~ s(x)", method="ML")
except NotImplementedError as error:
    print(type(error).__name__, str(error).split(". ")[0])

NotImplementedError method='ML' is not supported

The full message is method='ML' is not supported. mgcv's ML criterion uses the penalty range-space projection of log|X'WX+S| (the C routine MLpenalty1 in gdi.c), which differs from REML's full-space determinant. Only method='REML' is available; ML is deferred until the range-space determinant is implemented. Any other method, such as GCV, raises ValueError.

Also rejected at construction with NotImplementedError: select=True, gamma other than 1.0 and knots=. In the formula, fx=TRUE, per-term sp= and id= raise NotImplementedError. optimizer accepts only "newton" and "efs".

docs.title: Streamed fitting
docs.text:
The streamed route fits a GAM from a row source, reading the data in batches, so the full model matrix is never held in memory. Select it with FitControl(execution="stream").

Use it when

  • the data do not fit in memory as a model matrix, but can be read again and again in batches (from arrays, a DataFrame or .npy files on disk);
  • the model uses one-dimensional cubic regression splines (bs="cr" or bs="cs") and numeric parametric terms.

Do not use it when

  • the model needs thin plate (the default s(x)), cyclic, random-effect or tensor smooths, a by= variable or factor terms: use the discretized route or the default fit;
  • you need summary(), plot() or per-term EDF: a streamed fit returns only a prediction result.

Every example on this page runs in order in one Python session. The setup block makes the data and a row source used throughout.

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from jaxgam import GAM, FitControl
from jaxgam.data import DataFrameRowSource
from jaxgam.families import Poisson

rng = np.random.default_rng(1)
n = 2000
x = rng.uniform(0, 1, n)
z = rng.normal(size=n)
eta = np.sin(2 * np.pi * x) + 0.3 * z
data = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "x": x,
        "z": z,
        "y": eta + rng.normal(scale=0.3, size=n),
        "count": rng.poisson(np.exp(eta)),
    }
)
source = DataFrameRowSource(data, response="y")
counts = DataFrameRowSource(data, response="count")
newdata = pd.DataFrame({"x": [0.1, 0.5, 0.9], "z": [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]})

A row source is an object that can replay the same rows, batch by batch, every time it is scanned. See Row sources for the built-in sources, prior weights and offsets, and how to write your own.

docs.title: Fixed smoothing parameters
docs.text:
Pass sp= to fix the smoothing parameters. A streamed fit always needs result="prediction".

control = FitControl(execution="stream", batch_rows=500)
fit = GAM("y ~ z + s(x, bs='cr')", sp=[1.0], control=control).fit(
    source, result="prediction"
)
print(fit.execution_route, fit.converged, fit.source_scans, fit.batches_scanned)
# stream True 11 44
print(fit.predict(newdata))
# [ 0.57438901 -0.03205741 -0.57433759]

Each PIRLS iteration (penalized iteratively reweighted least squares, the coefficient fit) reads the whole source once, so source_scans grows with the number of iterations. The scans made by the setup pass (knots, bases and constraints) are not counted.

docs.title: Choosing the linear solver
docs.text:
FitControl.linear_solver picks how each coefficient system is solved: "cholesky" (the default) or "qr".

Family and link "cholesky" "qr" Gaussian identity, Poisson log, Binomial logit yes yes Other links of Gaussian, Poisson and Binomial no yes Gamma (any supported link) no yes Negative binomial (log, identity, sqrt) no yes

The Cholesky solve covers only the families whose Fisher information equals the observed information and whose scale is known or is the Gaussian residual scale. Everything else asks for QR:

try:
    GAM("count ~ z + s(x, bs='cr')", family=Poisson(link="sqrt"), sp=[1.0],
        control=control).fit(counts, result="prediction")
except NotImplementedError as error:
    print(error)
# Streamed observed-information fitting requires linear_solver='qr'.

qr = FitControl(execution="stream", batch_rows=500, linear_solver="qr")
fit = GAM("count ~ z + s(x, bs='cr')", family=Poisson(link="sqrt"), sp=[1.0],
          control=qr).fit(counts, result="prediction")
print(fit.execution_route, fit.converged)
# stream_qr True

For the negative binomial the message is Streamed NB observed-information fitting requires linear_solver='qr'.

A fixed sp does not always mean nothing else is estimated. For Gamma and for a non-identity Gaussian link the scale is still estimated, and for family="nb" the theta parameter is still estimated, with the smoothing parameters held. lambda_strategy is still "fixed", and convergence_info then holds the optimizer's message. To hold the negative binomial theta too, pass NegativeBinomial(theta, fixed=True).

docs.title: Estimated smoothing by exact REML
docs.text:
Omit sp to estimate the smoothing parameters by REML. On this route that requires linear_solver="qr":

try:
    GAM("y ~ z + s(x, bs='cr')", control=control).fit(source, result="prediction")
except NotImplementedError as error:
    print(error)
# Exact streamed REML requires linear_solver='qr'.

fit = GAM("y ~ z + s(x, bs='cr')", control=qr).fit(source, result="prediction")
print(fit.execution_route, fit.lambda_strategy, fit.converged)
# stream_exact_reml_qr exact_reml True
print(fit.convergence_info)
# CONVERGENCE: NORM OF PROJECTED GRADIENT <= PGTOL; 1 source step window(s).
diagnostics = fit.exact_optimizer_diagnostics
print(diagnostics.status, diagnostics.n_evaluations, diagnostics.n_accepted)
# 0 16 14

The criterion is the same exact REML score as the default fit, but the optimizer is different: SciPy's L-BFGS-B with exact gradients, not the Newton iteration of the default fit. It works on the log smoothing parameters (bounded to [-40, 40]), plus the log scale for families with an unknown scale and log theta for a negative binomial with estimated theta. Every score evaluation is a full coefficient fit over the source, so this sub-route makes many scans (146 in the example above, including 2 start-up scans). Each step is limited to 5 on the log scale per "window"; at most 20 windows are opened.

exact_optimizer_diagnostics holds the L-BFGS-B status (0 means it met its stopping test), n_evaluations, n_accepted, projected_gradient_inf, the accepted score history and the start-up scan counts. A model with no penalty, a known scale and no theta skips the optimizer: it reports lambda_strategy="exact_reml_no_parameters".

docs.title: Streamed Fellner-Schall
docs.text:
optimizer="efs" selects the smoothing parameters by the extended Fellner-Schall update (mgcv's efsudr method, which the dense optimizer="efs" fit also follows) instead of L-BFGS-B. It also requires linear_solver="qr":

fit = GAM("y ~ z + s(x, bs='cr')", optimizer="efs", control=qr).fit(
    source, result="prediction"
)
print(fit.execution_route, fit.lambda_strategy, fit.converged, fit.convergence_info)
# stream_efs_qr efs_reml True deviance_change
efs = fit.optimizer_diagnostics
print(fit.source_scans, efs.startup_source_scans + efs.provider_source_scans)
# 8 26

The top-level source_scans counts only the final accepted fit; the sum of the two diagnostics counts is the whole search.

It accepts Gaussian, Binomial, Poisson, Gamma and the negative binomial with a log, identity or sqrt link; estimated theta is updated inside the fit. Other families raise Streamed EFS supports registered Gaussian, Binomial, Poisson, Gamma, and NegativeBinomial families only. The limits and tolerances come from FitControl(efs=EFSControl(...)); see Smoothing selection.

convergence_info is "score_window" or "deviance_change" when it converged. With no penalties, Fellner-Schall has nothing to select: the fit runs one coefficient fit (execution_route="stream_parametric_qr") and, for the negative binomial, leaves theta at its starting value and reports theta=None.

docs.title: Streamed Gaussian QR
docs.text:
For a Gaussian identity-link model, gaussian_compression=True reads the source once to build a weighted QR reduction, then selects the smoothing parameters using only coefficient-sized arrays, with no further scans:

gaussian_qr = FitControl(execution="stream", batch_rows=500,
                         gaussian_compression=True)
fit = GAM("y ~ z + s(x, bs='cr')", control=gaussian_qr).fit(
    source, result="prediction"
)
print(fit.execution_route, fit.lambda_strategy, fit.source_scans)
# stream_gaussian_qr newton_reml 1

It works with either linear_solver. It needs the exact Gaussian family with the identity link, at least one penalty, a full-rank coefficient map, and prior weights between 1e-10 and 1e10. When a request does not qualify, the fit takes the route it would take without the request and says why in execution_fallback_reason:

request = FitControl(execution="stream", batch_rows=500, linear_solver="qr",
                     gaussian_compression=True)
fit = GAM("count ~ z + s(x, bs='cr')", family="poisson", control=request).fit(
    counts, result="prediction"
)
print(fit.execution_route)
# stream_exact_reml_qr
print(fit.execution_fallback_reason)
# Gaussian QR requires the exact Gaussian family with identity link

With estimated smoothing and the default "cholesky" solver there is no route to fall back to, so an ineligible request raises Estimated-sp RowSource fitting requires an eligible Gaussian QR route (...) or linear_solver='qr' for exact streamed REML. With optimizer="efs" the request is not used and the reason is Gaussian QR compression requires Newton smoothing selection.

Up to 50 penalties the smoothing parameters are selected by Newton (lambda_strategy="newton_reml"). Above 50 penalties L-BFGS-B is used instead ("lbfgs_reml"), limited to 100 iterations. If it stops at that limit the fit returns with converged=False and convergence_info="iteration limit". With sp= the smoothing parameters are held, the scale is still estimated, and lambda_strategy is "fixed".

docs.title: Options that matter
docs.text:
Option Default What it does execution "dense" "stream" selects this route. linear_solver "cholesky" "qr" is needed for estimated smoothing, Fellner-Schall and most families. "pcg" is refused. batch_rows 65_536 Rows per batch in every fit scan, and the default batch size of predict_iter. memory_budget_bytes 512 MiB Bound on the arrays the setup pass and the fit know they will hold. output_budget_bytes 512 MiB Bound on what one predict call may return. uncertainty "none" "fisher" or "covariance" keeps what standard errors need. gaussian_compression False Requests the Gaussian QR sub-route. efs EFSControl() Fellner-Schall limits, used with optimizer="efs".

There is no option for the PIRLS iteration limit or tolerance on this route. Field-level detail is in the API reference.

docs.title: Batch size and memory budget
docs.text:
memory_budget_bytes is a check made before arrays are allocated, against the arrays the setup pass and the fit know they will need. It is not a cap on the process: the row source's own storage and native LAPACK or XLA workspace are outside it. A failed check raises MemoryError before the work starts.

The setup pass shrinks its own scan size until it fits the budget. If not even one row fits, it stops before reading the data. A model with a cubic smooth always needs a fixed 16 MiB allowance for exact knot placement, so budgets below about 17 MB fail this way:

try:
    GAM("y ~ s(x, bs='cr')", sp=[1.0],
        control=FitControl(execution="stream", memory_budget_bytes=1_000_000)
        ).fit(source, result="prediction")
except MemoryError as error:
    print(error)
# Streamed setup requires at least 17318011 bytes to scan one row, exceeding
# the setup memory budget of 1000000 bytes (FitControl.memory_budget_bytes).

The fit does not shrink its scans: its check charges a full batch_rows batch, whatever the number of rows in the source. When it fails, lower batch_rows (or raise the budget):

tight = FitControl(execution="stream", memory_budget_bytes=18_000_000)
try:
    GAM("y ~ z + s(x, bs='cr')", sp=[1.0], control=tight).fit(
        source, result="prediction"
    )
except MemoryError as error:
    print(error)
# Known streamed PIRLS workspace requires 21507776 bytes, exceeding
# FitControl.memory_budget_bytes=18000000. Setup scans are budgeted
# separately.

smaller = FitControl(execution="stream", memory_budget_bytes=18_000_000,
                     batch_rows=4096)
fit = GAM("y ~ z + s(x, bs='cr')", sp=[1.0], control=smaller).fit(
    source, result="prediction"
)
print(fit.converged, fit.known_workspace_bytes)
# True 1355456

The QR solver's message reads Known streamed QR PIRLS workspace requires .... The Gaussian QR sub-route raises Known streamed Gaussian QR workspace requires ... and does not fall back. See Memory and performance for every budget.

docs.title: Standard errors
docs.text:
By default a streamed fit keeps nothing for standard errors, and predict(se_fit=True) raises RuntimeError. Fit with uncertainty="fisher" to keep the factor of the penalized Fisher information:

fisher = FitControl(execution="stream", linear_solver="qr", uncertainty="fisher")
fit = GAM("y ~ z + s(x, bs='cr')", control=fisher).fit(source, result="prediction")
mean, se = fit.predict(newdata, se_fit=True)
print(se)
# [0.02150264 0.01786659 0.02194168]
Vp = fit.materialize_covariance(memory_budget_bytes=10_000_000)
print(Vp.shape)
# (11, 11)

materialize_covariance builds the coefficient covariance on request, under its own budget. uncertainty="covariance" builds it during the fit instead (checked against memory_budget_bytes); read it from fit.to_predictor().Vp. See Prediction results.

docs.title: What you get back
docs.text:
A GAMPredictionResult (see the API reference). It has predict, predict_iter, predict_matrix, to_predictor and materialize_covariance, but no summary(), plot() or per-term EDF.

Attribute Meaning on this route converged, convergence_info, n_iter Whether the fit, or the smoothing search, met its stopping test, and how it stopped. execution_route "stream", "stream_qr", "stream_exact_reml_qr", "stream_efs_qr", "stream_parametric_qr" or "stream_gaussian_qr". lambda_strategy "fixed", "exact_reml", "exact_reml_no_parameters", "efs_reml", "newton_reml" or "lbfgs_reml". smoothing_params, scale, theta, edf_total, deviance, score The fitted values of these quantities. source_scans, batches_scanned Fit scans, not setup scans. Exact REML adds its start-up scans. On Fellner-Schall they count only the final fit; the totals are optimizer_diagnostics.startup_source_scans + provider_source_scans. known_workspace_bytes The fit's known-array bound. None on Fellner-Schall and on the parametric bypass. exact_optimizer_diagnostics Exact REML only (see above). optimizer_diagnostics Fellner-Schall only: an EFSOptimizerDiagnostics. execution_fallback_reason Why a gaussian_compression=True request was not used, else None.

docs.title: Telling whether the fit converged
docs.text:
Check fit.converged and read fit.convergence_info. The streamed route issues no warning when it stops short; a fit that did not converge is returned with converged=False. The messages you can see:

  • fixed sp: "fixed sp streamed PIRLS" or "fixed sp streamed PIRLS did not converge". The PIRLS limit (100 iterations) cannot be changed here.
  • exact REML: the L-BFGS-B message plus the window count. If the window limit was reached it adds Window limit 20 reached with descent beyond the last window.
  • Fellner-Schall: "score_window" or "deviance_change" when converged, otherwise "iteration limit reached" or a failure label. Raise EFSControl(outer_limit=...) for the first.
  • Gaussian QR: "iteration limit" or "step failed" when not converged.

Some failures raise instead of returning. Under exact REML, a coefficient fit that does not converge at any trial raises RuntimeError (for example Regular streamed REML requires a converged, valid final source state., or NB streamed REML requires a converged valid coefficient state for the negative binomial). An unpenalized model matrix that is rank deficient raises LinAlgError. A source that changes during the fit raises RuntimeError.

docs.title: 1.1 What Is the Negative Binomial Family?
docs.text:
The Negative Binomial (NB) distribution models count data with overdispersion (variance exceeds the mean). It generalizes Poisson by adding a dispersion parameter theta (also called "size" or "shape"):

  • Mean: mu
  • Variance: mu + mu^2/theta
  • As theta -> infinity, NB -> Poisson

In mgcv, NB is an extended family -- unlike standard families (Gaussian, Poisson, Binomial, Gamma), it has an extra distributional parameter theta that must be estimated alongside the smoothing parameters and coefficients.

docs.title: 1.2 Why This Is High-Risk
docs.text:
NB touches nearly every layer of the fitting pipeline:

  1. Family layer: New ExtendedFamily base class between ExponentialFamily and NegativeBinomial, with pure-function factories (deviance_fn, working_weights_fn) for AD inside the custom_jvp.
  2. custom_jvp on PIRLS: Must be extended to compute d(beta*)/d(theta) via the implicit function theorem, matching R's ift2 in gdi.c.
  3. Newton outer loop: params vector grows from [log_lambda] to [log_lambda, log_theta]. The REML criterion and its gradient/Hessian include theta dimensions.
  4. REML criterion: The saturated log-likelihood ls_sat must take log_theta as an explicit JAX-traced argument so jax.grad captures it.

docs.title: 1.3 Scope
docs.text:
This design covers the nb() extended family with: - Estimated theta (default) and fixed theta modes - Log link (default), identity link, sqrt link - Joint theta optimization in the existing Newton optimizer - Full R-matching correctness

Out of scope (deferred): - negbin() standard family (fixed theta with grid search) - Truncated NB, zero-inflated NB - Other extended families (Tweedie, Beta, SHASH, etc.) -- though NB establishes the infrastructure they will reuse - Fellner-Schall optimizer -- the family interface is designed to not block a future EFS implementation (which would use estimate_theta() separately rather than joint optimization), but EFS itself is not built here

docs.title: 2. R Reference Implementation Analysis
docs.text: mgcv provides two NB implementations.

docs.title: 2.1 negbin() -- Standard Family (Fixed theta)
docs.text:
File: $MGCV_SOURCE/R/gam.fit3.r lines 2564-2642

  • theta is fixed (passed as argument, never estimated during fitting)
  • Uses gam.fit3 -- standard PIRLS with V(mu) * g'(mu)^2 weights
  • Class is "family" (standard), not "extended.family"

docs.title: 2.2 nb() -- Extended Family (Estimated theta)
docs.text:
File: $MGCV_SOURCE/R/efam.r lines 161-310

  • theta can be estimated (default) or fixed
  • Uses gam.fit4 -- extended PIRLS with Dd() deviance derivatives
  • theta stored internally as log(theta) for unconstrained optimization
  • n.theta = 1 when estimated, 0 when fixed
  • getTheta(trans=FALSE) returns log(theta); getTheta(trans=TRUE) returns theta
  • Dd() provides deviance derivatives up to 4th order w.r.t. mu plus mixed partials w.r.t. theta (efam.r lines 207-237)
  • ls() provides saturated log-likelihood with first and second derivatives w.r.t. theta via digamma/trigamma (efam.r lines 248-275)

docs.title: 2.3 How R's Newton Jointly Optimizes Theta
docs.text:
This was a critical finding during design. R's Newton optimizer does jointly optimize theta -- it is NOT an outer iteration.

The sp vector passed through the pipeline is [theta, log_lambda, <log_scale>]. gam.fit3 dispatches to gam.fit4 for extended families (gam.fit3.r line 111). gam.fit4 returns REML1 and REML2 -- the gradient and Hessian of the REML criterion w.r.t. the full parameter vector including theta (gam.fit4.r lines 738-764). newton() then takes a joint Newton step over all dimensions.

The REML gradient has four components for the theta dimensions:

Component R variable Source What it captures Deviance gradient D1[1:nth] gdi2 C routine d(beta*)/d(theta) . dD/d(eta) + dD/d(theta) -- both indirect (through beta) and direct Penalty gradient P1[1:nth] gdi2 C routine 2 * beta' . S . d(beta*)/d(theta) -- indirect through beta only Log-det gradient ldet1[1:nth] gdi2 C routine tr(H^{-1} . dH/d(theta)) -- through working weights changing with theta Saturated loglik lsth1 family$ls() d(ls_sat)/d(theta) -- direct via digamma/trigamma

The d(beta*)/d(theta) terms come from ift2 (gdi.c lines 1368-1462) which applies the implicit function theorem:

d(beta*)/d(theta) = -H^{-1} . 0.5 . X' . d^2D/(d(eta) d(theta))

where d^2D/(d(eta) d(theta)) is the mixed derivative of deviance w.r.t. linear predictor and theta. R computes this analytically via Dd$Dmuth -> dDeta$Detath (gam.fit4.r lines 4-77).

The estimate.theta() function (efam.r lines 5-96) is used only by the EFS score type (gam.fit4.r line 509: if (scoreType=="EFS")), not by Newton REML/ML.

docs.title: 2.4 Key R Source File Map
docs.text: File Lines What $MGCV_SOURCE/R/efam.r 161-310 nb() extended family definition $MGCV_SOURCE/R/efam.r 5-96 estimate.theta() (used by EFS only) $MGCV_SOURCE/R/gam.fit3.r 2564-2642 negbin() standard family $MGCV_SOURCE/R/gam.fit3.r 106-116 gam.fit3 dispatch to gam.fit4 $MGCV_SOURCE/R/gam.fit4.r 4-77 dDeta() -- mu-to-eta derivative conversion $MGCV_SOURCE/R/gam.fit4.r 240-548 gam.fit4() -- PIRLS for extended families $MGCV_SOURCE/R/gam.fit4.r 725-764 REML criterion with theta derivatives $MGCV_SOURCE/src/gdi.c 1368-1462 ift2() -- IFT for d(beta*)/d(theta) $MGCV_SOURCE/src/gdi.c 1953-2250 gdi2() -- full derivative computation

docs.title: 3. Architectural Decision: Which R Family to Port
docs.text:
Decision: Port nb() (extended family).

  1. Theta estimation is the key feature -- users rarely know theta a priori.
  2. negbin() (fixed theta) is trivial to add later as NegativeBinomial(theta=5.0, fixed=True).
  3. NB establishes the extended family infrastructure for Tweedie, Beta, etc.

Key design choice: AD replaces hand-coded derivatives.

R's gam.fit4 uses Dd() -- ~50 lines of hand-coded analytical derivatives of the deviance up to 4th order, passed to the C routine gdi2. We replace all of this with jax.grad through stable forward passes (per design.md section 9.3). No custom_jvp needed for NB itself -- only for the PIRLS IFT.

docs.title: 4.1 Log-Likelihood (Per-Observation)
docs.text:
l(y, mu, theta) = lgamma(y + theta) - lgamma(theta) - lgamma(y + 1)
                  + theta * log(theta) - theta * log(mu + theta)
                  + y * log(mu) - y * log(mu + theta)

docs.title: 4.2 Variance Function
docs.text:
V(mu) = mu + mu^2/theta
V'(mu) = 1 + 2*mu/theta

docs.title: 4.3 Deviance Residuals
docs.text:
Per-observation unit deviance (R's dev.resids, efam.r lines 199-205):

d_i = 2 * wt_i * [y_i * log(max(1, y_i) / mu_i)
                   - (y_i + theta) * log((y_i + theta) / (mu_i + theta))]

docs.title: 4.4 Saturated Log-Likelihood
docs.text:
R's family$ls() (efam.r lines 248-275):

ls = -sum(wt * [(y + theta)*log(y + theta) - ylogy + lgamma(y + 1)
                - theta*log(theta) + lgamma(theta) - lgamma(theta + y)])

where ylogy = y*log(y) for y > 0, else 0.

docs.title: 4.5 Initialize
docs.text: R's initialization (efam.r line 280): mustart = y + (y == 0) / 6

docs.title: 5.1 Joint Optimization Matching R's Newton
docs.text:
R's Newton jointly optimizes [theta, log_lambda] with the full REML gradient and Hessian. We match this: log_theta is appended to the params vector and jax.grad/jax.hessian of the REML criterion capture all theta dependencies automatically.

The params vector for NB is:

params = [log_lambda_1, ..., log_lambda_m, log_theta]

This follows the identical pattern used for unknown-scale families (Gaussian, Gamma) where log_phi is appended:

params = [log_lambda_1, ..., log_lambda_m, log_phi]

The static flag joint_theta (analogous to joint_scale) controls whether log_theta is present in params.

docs.title: 5.2 How Theta Enters the AD Trace
docs.text:
Theta affects the REML criterion through two paths:

Path A: Direct (outside PIRLS). The saturated log-likelihood ls_sat(theta) depends on theta directly. This is handled by calling family.saturated_loglik_theta(y, wt, phi, log_theta) with log_theta as a traced JAX value inside _diff_score. jax.grad differentiates through it automatically. This is structurally identical to how phi enters for Gaussian/Gamma via family.saturated_loglik(y, wt, phi).

Path B: Indirect (through PIRLS). The PIRLS solution (beta*, XtWX, deviance) depends on theta because the deviance formula and variance function both contain theta. R captures this via ift2 (the implicit function theorem in gdi.c). We capture it by extending the custom_jvp on PIRLS to include log_theta as a primal -- see Section 6.

Both paths are needed for the full gradient. Path A alone (the "partial joint" approach considered earlier) would miss 3 of 4 gradient terms and give poor Newton convergence in the theta dimension.

docs.title: 5.3 Design Constraint: Future Optimizer Compatibility
docs.text:
The family interface provides both: - Mutable state (get_theta/put_theta + methods reading self._log_theta) -- used by PIRLS at runtime and available for future optimizers (e.g. EFS) that estimate theta separately - Explicit-argument pure functions (deviance_fn, working_weights_fn, saturated_loglik_theta) -- used by Newton's custom_jvp and criterion

This separation means a future optimizer can use the same family object with a different theta-update strategy without any family changes.

docs.title: 6.1 Current custom_jvp (Standard Families)
docs.text:
The existing custom_jvp (newton.py lines 179-222) has 2 primals:

_pirls_out(S_lambda, beta_warm) -> (beta, XtWX, dev)

The JVP computes how (beta, XtWX, dev) change when S_lambda is perturbed, using the IFT:

dbeta = -H^{-1} . (dS @ beta)        # IFT for lambda
deta = X @ dbeta
dW = JVP of W(eta) w.r.t. eta        # chain through working weights
ddev = JVP of D(eta) w.r.t. eta      # chain through deviance
dXtWX = X' . diag(dW) . X

docs.title: 6.2 Extended custom_jvp (Extended Families)
docs.text:
For n_theta > 0, the custom_jvp gains a 3rd primal:

_pirls_out(S_lambda, log_theta, beta_warm) -> (beta, XtWX, dev)

The JVP now handles tangents (dS, dtheta, _):

Step 1: IFT with both lambda and theta contributions.

The IFT at the PIRLS stationary point d(0.5*PenDev)/d(beta) = 0:

For lambda: d^2(0.5*PenDev)/(d(beta) d(S)) in direction dS = dS . beta
For theta:  d^2(0.5*PenDev)/(d(beta) d(theta)) . dtheta = 0.5 * X' . d^2D/(d(eta) d(theta)) . dtheta

R computes d^2D/(d(eta) d(theta)) analytically via Dd$Dmuth -> dDeta$Detath. We compute it with JAX AD:

dev_fn = family.deviance_fn(y, wt)  # pure function D(eta, log_theta) -> scalar
grad_D_eta = jax.grad(dev_fn, argnums=0)  # dD/d(eta)
_, d_grad_D = jax.jvp(
    lambda lt: grad_D_eta(eta, lt),
    (log_theta,), (dtheta,)
)  # d^2D/(d(eta) d(theta)) . dtheta, shape (n,)

Combined IFT solve:

rhs = dS @ beta + 0.5 * (X.T @ d_grad_D)
dbeta = cho_solve((L, True), -rhs)

This matches R's ift2 (gdi.c lines 1396-1408) where the first n_theta columns of b1 use Db_th = -0.5 * X' @ Det_th and the remaining columns use Db_th = -sp[i] * S_i @ beta.

Step 2: ddev and dW via joint (eta, theta) JVPs.

Unlike standard families where only eta changes, here both eta and theta change. We use joint JVPs to capture both effects in one call:

deta = X @ dbeta
_, ddev = jax.jvp(dev_fn, (eta, log_theta), (deta, dtheta))
_, dW = jax.jvp(ww_fn, (eta, log_theta), (deta, dtheta))
dXtWX = (X.T * dW) @ X

This captures: - ddev = dD/d(eta) . deta + dD/d(theta) . dtheta (indirect + direct) - dW = dW/d(eta) . deta + dW/d(theta) . dtheta (indirect + direct)

Matching all four R gradient terms from Section 2.3.

Step 3: Standard families unchanged.

When family.n_theta == 0 (compile-time constant via static family arg), the standard 2-primal custom_jvp is used. Zero cost for existing families.

docs.title: 6.3 Performance Impact
docs.text: Adding log_theta as a 3rd primal adds one tangent direction. For jax.hessian, cost goes from O(m^2) to O((m+1)^2) JVP passes where m = number of smoothing parameters. Since the theta JVP involves a scalar tangent (vs the (p,p) matrix tangent for S_lambda), each theta-related pass is cheap. The increase is marginal.

docs.title: 6.4 Concrete Code Structure in _diff_score
docs.text:
def _diff_score(params, beta_warm, X, y, wt, offset, S_list, ...,
                family, ..., joint_theta, joint_scale, n_lambda, ...):

    # Parse params
    idx = n_lambda
    log_lambda = params[:idx]
    if joint_theta:
        log_theta = params[idx]; idx += 1
    if joint_scale:
        phi = jnp.exp(params[idx])
    else:
        phi = jnp.array(1.0)

    # ls_sat -- direct theta dependence (outside custom_jvp)
    if joint_theta:
        ls_sat = family.saturated_loglik_theta(y, wt, phi, log_theta)
    else:
        ls_sat = family.saturated_loglik(y, wt, phi)

    S_lambda = build_S_lambda(log_lambda, S_list, p)

    if family.n_theta > 0 and joint_theta:
        # --- Extended family path: 3 primals ---
        dev_fn = family.deviance_fn(y, wt)
        ww_fn = family.working_weights_fn(wt)

        @jax.custom_jvp
        def _pirls_out(S_lam, lt, bw):
            result = pirls_loop(X, y, bw, S_lam, family, wt, offset, ...)
            return result.coefficients, result.XtWX, result.deviance

        @_pirls_out.defjvp
        def _pirls_jvp(primals, tangents):
            S_lam, lt, bw = primals
            dS, dlt, _ = tangents
            beta, XtWX, dev = _pirls_out(S_lam, lt, bw)

            H = XtWX + S_lam
            L, _ = cho_factor(H)
            eta = X @ beta + offset

            # IFT: lambda + theta
            rhs = dS @ beta
            grad_D_eta = jax.grad(dev_fn, argnums=0)
            _, d_grad_D = jax.jvp(
                lambda lt_: grad_D_eta(eta, lt_), (lt,), (dlt,)
            )
            rhs = rhs + 0.5 * (X.T @ d_grad_D)
            dbeta = cho_solve((L, True), -rhs)
            deta = X @ dbeta

            # ddev and dW: joint JVPs over (eta, theta)
            _, ddev = jax.jvp(dev_fn, (eta, lt), (deta, dlt))
            _, dW = jax.jvp(ww_fn, (eta, lt), (deta, dlt))
            dXtWX = (X.T * dW) @ X

            return (beta, XtWX, dev), (dbeta, dXtWX, ddev)

        beta, XtWX, dev = _pirls_out(S_lambda, log_theta, beta_warm)

    else:
        # --- Standard family path: 2 primals (existing, unchanged) ---
        @jax.custom_jvp
        def _pirls_out(S_lam, bw):
            ...  # existing code

        beta, XtWX, dev = _pirls_out(S_lambda, beta_warm)

    # Criterion (unchanged)
    core = _criterion_core(log_lambda, XtWX, beta, dev, ls_sat, ...)
    ...

docs.title: 7.1 ExtendedFamily Base Class
docs.text:
Extended families have extra distributional parameters (theta) that are jointly estimated with smoothing parameters via Newton. The ExtendedFamily base class sits between ExponentialFamily and concrete families like NegativeBinomial:

ExponentialFamily          (variance, deviance_resids, aic, initialize, ...)
  |
  +-- Gaussian, Binomial, Poisson, Gamma    (n_theta = 0, standard families)
  |
  +-- ExtendedFamily       (get_theta, put_theta, deviance_fn, working_weights_fn, ...)
        |
        +-- NegativeBinomial                 (n_theta = 1)
        +-- (future: Tweedie, Beta, SHASH)

# families/extended.py

class ExtendedFamily(ExponentialFamily):
    """Base class for families with extra parameters estimated via Newton.

    Extended families provide:
    - Mutable theta state (get_theta/put_theta) for PIRLS runtime
    - Pure-function factories (deviance_fn, working_weights_fn) for the
      custom_jvp on PIRLS, where theta must be a traced JAX value
    - Explicit-theta saturated loglik for the REML criterion AD trace

    The theta interface uses arrays of shape (n_theta,) throughout,
    so families with multiple extra parameters (e.g. scat with df + scale)
    work without interface changes.

    The fitting code branches on `family.n_theta > 0` (compile-time check)
    to select the extended custom_jvp path. The abstractmethods here
    ensure any new extended family implements the required interface.
    """

    @abstractmethod
    def get_theta(self, transformed: bool = False) -> np.ndarray:
        """Extra parameter vector, shape (n_theta,).

        Log-scale by default. transformed=True returns natural scale
        (e.g. exp(log_theta) for positive parameters).
        """
        ...

    @abstractmethod
    def put_theta(self, log_theta: np.ndarray) -> None:
        """Set extra parameter vector (log-scale), shape (n_theta,).

        Called by Newton after each accepted step.
        """
        ...

    @abstractmethod
    def deviance_fn(self, y: np.ndarray, wt: np.ndarray):
        """Return pure JAX function D(eta, log_theta_vec) -> scalar.

        log_theta_vec has shape (n_theta,).
        Used by the custom_jvp for IFT theta terms and joint JVPs.
        Must capture (y, wt, link) in closure; theta is an explicit arg.
        """
        ...

    @abstractmethod
    def working_weights_fn(self, wt: np.ndarray):
        """Return pure JAX function W(eta, log_theta_vec) -> (n,) array.

        log_theta_vec has shape (n_theta,).
        Used by the custom_jvp for joint dW JVPs.
        Must capture (wt, link) in closure; theta is an explicit arg.
        """
        ...

    @abstractmethod
    def saturated_loglik_theta(
        self, y: np.ndarray, wt: np.ndarray, scale: float, log_theta: np.ndarray
    ):
        """Saturated log-likelihood with explicit theta for AD trace.

        log_theta has shape (n_theta,).
        Called inside _diff_score where log_theta is a traced JAX array.
        jax.grad differentiates through this w.r.t. log_theta.
        """
        ...

This is ~30 lines with no logic -- just abstract method declarations that enforce the contract. ExponentialFamily is unchanged; n_theta: int = 0 stays on it so the fitting code can check family.n_theta > 0 without caring about the type hierarchy.

docs.title: 7.2 NegativeBinomial Class
docs.text:
# families/negative_binomial.py

class NegativeBinomial(ExtendedFamily):

    family_name: str = "nb"
    scale_known: bool = True   # phi = 1
    n_theta: int = 1           # overridden in __init__ based on theta arg

    def __init__(self, theta=1.0, *, fixed=False, link=None):
        super().__init__(link)
        if theta <= 0:
            raise ValueError(f"theta must be positive, got {theta}")
        self._log_theta = np.array([np.log(theta)])
        self.n_theta = 0 if fixed else 1

    @property
    def default_link(self) -> Link:
        return LogLink()

    # -- ExtendedFamily interface --

    def get_theta(self, transformed=False):
        if transformed:
            return np.exp(self._log_theta)
        return self._log_theta

    def put_theta(self, log_theta):
        self._log_theta = np.asarray(log_theta, dtype=np.float64).reshape(self._log_theta.shape)

docs.title: 7.3 Standard Family Methods (Read Theta from self)
docs.text:
Used by PIRLS (Phase 2 runtime) and post-estimation (Phase 3). These read self._log_theta which is fixed during a single PIRLS run.

All standard family methods read self._log_theta[0] (scalar) from the stored vector. The [0] index extracts the single NB dispersion parameter. Future multi-theta families (e.g. scat) would index multiple elements.

    def variance(self, mu):
        xp = array_module(mu)
        theta = xp.exp(self._log_theta[0])
        return mu + mu**2 / theta

    def dvar(self, mu):
        theta = jnp.exp(self._log_theta[0])
        return 1.0 + 2.0 * mu / theta

    def deviance_resids(self, y, mu, wt):
        # R: efam.r lines 199-205
        xp = array_module(y)
        theta = xp.exp(self._log_theta[0])
        mu_safe = xp.maximum(mu, 1e-10)
        y_safe = xp.where(y > 0, y, 1.0)
        d = 2.0 * wt * (
            y * xp.log(y_safe / mu_safe)
            - (y + theta) * xp.log((y + theta) / (mu_safe + theta))
        )
        d = xp.maximum(d, 0.0)
        return xp.sign(y - mu_safe) * xp.sqrt(d)

    def saturated_loglik(self, y, wt, scale):
        # R: efam.r lines 248-275 (forward pass only, no theta derivs)
        theta = jnp.exp(self._log_theta[0])
        ylogy = jnp.where(y > 0, y * jnp.log(y), 0.0)
        term = (
            (y + theta) * jnp.log(y + theta) - ylogy
            + jsp.gammaln(y + 1.0) - theta * jnp.log(theta)
            + jsp.gammaln(theta) - jsp.gammaln(theta + y)
        )
        return -jnp.sum(term * wt)

    def aic(self, y, mu, wt, scale):
        # R: efam.r lines 239-246. Phase 3 only (NumPy).
        theta = np.exp(self._log_theta[0])
        mu_safe = np.maximum(mu, 1e-10)
        term = (
            (y + theta) * np.log(mu_safe + theta) - y * np.log(mu_safe)
            + gammaln(y + 1.0) - theta * np.log(theta)
            + gammaln(theta) - gammaln(theta + y)
        )
        return float(2.0 * np.sum(term * wt))

    def initialize(self, y, wt):
        # R: mustart <- y + (y == 0)/6
        y_arr = np.asarray(y, dtype=float)
        return np.where(y_arr == 0, y_arr + 1.0/6.0, y_arr)

    def valid_mu(self, mu):
        return mu > 0

    def valid_eta(self, eta):
        return np.isfinite(eta)

docs.title: 7.4 Pure-Function Factories (Explicit Theta for AD)
docs.text:
Used by the custom_jvp (Section 6) and by the criterion's ls_sat term. These return pure JAX functions that take log_theta as an explicit array argument of shape (n_theta,) so it participates in the AD trace. NB indexes log_theta[0] for its single parameter.

    def saturated_loglik_theta(self, y, wt, scale, log_theta):
        """Saturated log-likelihood with explicit theta for AD trace.
        log_theta has shape (n_theta,) = (1,) for NB."""
        theta = jnp.exp(log_theta[0])
        ylogy = jnp.where(y > 0, y * jnp.log(y), 0.0)
        term = (
            (y + theta) * jnp.log(y + theta) - ylogy
            + jsp.gammaln(y + 1.0) - theta * jnp.log(theta)
            + jsp.gammaln(theta) - jsp.gammaln(theta + y)
        )
        return -jnp.sum(term * wt)

    def deviance_fn(self, y, wt):
        """Return pure JAX function D(eta, log_theta_vec) -> scalar.
        log_theta_vec has shape (n_theta,) = (1,) for NB.

        Used by the custom_jvp for IFT theta terms and joint JVPs.
        Captures (y, wt, link) in closure; theta is an explicit arg.
        """
        link_inv = self.link.inverse
        def _dev(eta, log_theta):
            theta = jnp.exp(log_theta[0])
            mu = link_inv(eta)
            mu_safe = jnp.maximum(mu, 1e-10)
            y_safe = jnp.where(y > 0, y, 1.0)
            return jnp.sum(2.0 * wt * (
                y * jnp.log(y_safe / mu_safe)
                - (y + theta) * jnp.log((y + theta) / (mu_safe + theta))
            ))
        return _dev

    def working_weights_fn(self, wt):
        """Return pure JAX function W(eta, log_theta_vec) -> (n,) array.
        log_theta_vec has shape (n_theta,) = (1,) for NB.

        Used by the custom_jvp for joint dW JVPs.
        Captures (wt, link) in closure; theta is an explicit arg.
        """
        link_inv = self.link.inverse
        link_deriv = self.link.derivative
        def _ww(eta, log_theta):
            theta = jnp.exp(log_theta[0])
            mu = link_inv(eta)
            V = mu + mu**2 / theta
            g_prime = link_deriv(mu)
            return wt / (V * g_prime**2)
        return _ww

docs.title: 7.5 Why This Interface
docs.text:
Method Who calls it Why theta handling differs variance(mu) PIRLS hot loop (JIT) Reads self._log_theta -- theta is fixed during PIRLS deviance_resids(y, mu, wt) PIRLS, post-estimation Same -- fixed theta saturated_loglik(y, wt, scale) Criterion (fixed theta) Standard families, or NB with fixed theta saturated_loglik_theta(y, wt, scale, log_theta) Criterion (joint theta) log_theta is a traced JAX value for jax.grad deviance_fn(y, wt) custom_jvp only Returns D(eta, log_theta) -- both args traced for IFT + JVP working_weights_fn(wt) custom_jvp only Returns W(eta, log_theta) -- both args traced for dW JVP

Standard families don't implement the last three methods (they're @abstractmethod on ExtendedFamily, not on ExponentialFamily). The if family.n_theta > 0 branch in _diff_score (compile-time constant) ensures they're never called for standard families.

docs.title: 8.1 No PIRLS Changes Required
docs.text:
For the log link (canonical for NB), Fisher scoring weights from wt / (V(mu) * g'(mu)^2) give correct results. The existing pirls_loop calls family.working_weights(mu, wt) and family.working_response(y, mu, eta), which NB inherits from ExponentialFamily (using variance and link).

NB overrides variance(mu) to return mu + mu^2/theta and dev_resids for the NB deviance formula. Everything else works unchanged.

docs.title: 8.2 Non-Canonical Links (Deferred)
docs.text:
For identity and sqrt links, R's gam.fit4 uses observed-Hessian weights via Dd$Deta2 instead of Fisher weights. This would require overriding working_weights with AD-based observed weights. Deferred -- log link covers

95% of NB use cases.

docs.title: 9.3 After Each Accepted Step
docs.text:
Update the family's stored theta so the next PIRLS run uses the correct value:

if self._joint_theta:
    new_log_theta = float(params_new[self._fd.n_penalties])
    self._fd.family.put_theta(new_log_theta)

This triggers JIT recompilation (family is a static arg with changed internal state). Acceptable cost: theta changes once per Newton iteration (~5-10 times total), recompilation is ~50ms vs ~500ms PIRLS work.

docs.title: 9.4 _build_result
docs.text: Extract log_lambda from the joint params vector (skip theta/phi components) for the returned NewtonResult. Store estimated theta on the result.

docs.title: 9.5 Clamping
docs.text: _clamp_params should only clamp log_lambda, not log_theta. Theta has no natural bounds (though very large |log_theta| values are unlikely).

docs.text:
Family methods against R values: - variance(mu) matches mu + mu^2/theta for various theta - deviance_resids(y, mu, wt) matches R's nb()$dev.resids() - saturated_loglik(y, wt, scale) matches R's nb()$ls()$ls - aic(y, mu, wt, scale) matches R's nb()$aic() - initialize(y, wt) matches y + (y == 0)/6 - Edge cases: y=0, large y, large theta, theta -> infinity (Poisson limit)

Theta management: - get_theta() / put_theta() round-trip - Constructor: positive theta -> fixed (n_theta=0) - Constructor: negative theta -> estimated, starting at -theta - Constructor: None -> estimated, starting at 1

custom_jvp validation: - dβ*/d(log_theta) from IFT matches finite-difference perturbation of theta - d(deviance)/d(log_theta) matches finite differences - d(XtWX)/d(log_theta) matches finite differences - Full REML gradient w.r.t. log_theta matches finite differences

docs.title: 12.2 R Comparison Tests (test_nb_fitting.py)
docs.text:
Using r_bridge.py:

  1. Simple: y ~ s(x) with nb(), estimated theta
  2. Fixed theta: y ~ s(x) with nb(theta=2)
  3. Multiple smooths: y ~ s(x1) + s(x2) with nb()
  4. With offset: y ~ s(x) + offset(log(exposure))
  5. Factor-by smooth: y ~ s(x, by=group) with nb()
  6. High overdispersion (theta small): test convergence
  7. Low overdispersion (theta large, near Poisson): test theta -> infinity

Tolerances: - Coefficients: STRICT (rtol=1e-4) - Deviance: STRICT - Theta: MODERATE (rtol=1e-3) -- REML surface is flat near theta optimum - Smoothing parameters: MODERATE - EDF: MODERATE - Fitted values: STRICT

docs.title: 12.3 Hard-Gate Invariants
docs.text:
• Deviance >= 0
  • No NaN in converged model
  • EDF bounds: 1 <= edf_j <= k_j
  • Penalty PSD, H symmetry/PSD
  • Objective monotonicity (penalized deviance decreases each PIRLS iteration)
  • Theta > 0 after estimation

docs.title: R1: custom_jvp Correctness
docs.text:
Risk: The extended JVP with theta IFT terms could have sign errors or missing factors (the 0.5 factor from the PenDev convention is subtle).

Mitigation: Validate every JVP output against finite differences. Test dbeta, ddev, dXtWX individually, not just the final REML gradient. R's ift2 in gdi.c is the reference for the exact formula.

docs.title: R2: JIT Recompilation on Theta Change
docs.text:
Risk: put_theta() changes self._log_theta on the family object (static JIT arg), triggering recompilation.

Mitigation: Acceptable cost -- theta changes ~5-10 times per fit, recompilation is ~50ms vs ~500ms PIRLS. Future optimization: pass theta as a dynamic arg (requires broader refactor).

docs.title: R3: Numerical Stability of AD Through lgamma
docs.text:
Risk: lgamma(y+theta) - lgamma(theta) cancellation at large theta.

Mitigation: Per design.md section 9.3, JAX differentiates lgamma to digamma (stable special function). At large theta, NB -> Poisson and gradient imprecision is harmless. Validated by extreme-theta AD tests.

docs.title: R4: Non-Canonical Link Support
docs.text:
Risk: Identity/sqrt links need observed-Hessian weights, not Fisher.

Mitigation: Deferred. Log link covers >95% of NB use. Document limitation.

from abc import abstractmethod
import numpy as np
from jaxgam.families.base import ExponentialFamily

class ExtendedFamily(ExponentialFamily):
    """Base class for families with extra parameters estimated via Newton.

    Subclasses must implement:
    - get_theta / put_theta: mutable theta state
    - deviance_fn: pure function D(eta, log_theta) for custom_jvp
    - working_weights_fn: pure function W(eta, log_theta) for custom_jvp
    - saturated_loglik_theta: explicit theta for REML criterion AD trace
    """

    @abstractmethod
    def get_theta(self, transformed: bool = False) -> float: ...

    @abstractmethod
    def put_theta(self, log_theta: float) -> None: ...

    @abstractmethod
    def deviance_fn(self, y: np.ndarray, wt: np.ndarray): ...

    @abstractmethod
    def working_weights_fn(self, wt: np.ndarray): ...

    @abstractmethod
    def saturated_loglik_theta(self, y, wt, scale, log_theta): ...

jaxgam/families/negative_binomial.py (~250 lines)

Implement all methods from design.md Section 7.2-7.4: - __init__(theta, link) with R's sign convention (None/0=estimate, >0=fixed, <0=initial) - get_theta(transformed) / put_theta(log_theta) - variance(mu), dvar(mu) - deviance_resids(y, mu, wt) - saturated_loglik(y, wt, scale) -- reads self._log_theta - aic(y, mu, wt, scale) - initialize(y, wt) -- y + (y == 0) / 6 - valid_mu(mu), valid_eta(eta) - saturated_loglik_theta(y, wt, scale, log_theta) -- explicit arg - deviance_fn(y, wt) -- returns pure function D(eta, log_theta) - working_weights_fn(wt) -- returns pure function W(eta, log_theta) - alpha property -- convenience, returns 1 / get_theta(transformed=True)

• [x] Simple: y ~ s(x), NegativeBinomial(), simulated NB data (true theta=2) Verify: convergence, theta in reasonable range, deviance finite
  • [x] Fixed theta: NegativeBinomial(theta=2, fixed=True) fits without theta estimation

(R gets theta≈10 on same data, not >50 — the REML surface is flat in the theta direction for equi-dispersed data. See docs/nb_implementation/experiments_theta_newton.md.)

Numerical edge cases:

  • [x] Constant response (all y=5):

  • [x] mu near machine epsilon (sparse predictor, log link):

docs.text:
The baseline uses fixed smoothing parameters so the four fits measure retained result state without adding optimizer runtime:

The throwaway walker recursively traversed dataclasses, object attributes, and containers from the GAMResults root. It counted every distinct numpy.ndarray once by id() and summed .nbytes. docs.title: Robust API Redesign: result Mode + Lean Inference Core
docs.text:
Historical record. This document was written while this piece of work was being designed and built, and is kept as a record of it. It is not maintained: the file names, line numbers, counts and "current state" descriptions in it are those of the repository at that time, and it may refer to documents that were later removed from the repository (for example docs/design.md and docs/R_SOURCE_MAP.md, which remain in the git history). For how the code is organized today see the architecture pages; for how to use the package see the user guide and the API reference.

  • Status: Implemented (2026-08-01)
  • Design Date: 2026-06-05 (revised 2026-07-28 over ten review rounds)
  • Target Branch: production-api
  • Builds on: docs/refactor_gam_api/design.md (spec/results split)
  • Release context: jaxgam is pre-release (1.0.0a1, unreleased). No downstream users to keep compatible, so this makes the clean change — no deprecation cycle, no __getattr__ forwarding.

Scope (round 1). An earlier draft bundled an MLOps serving layer (versioned/integrity artifact, save()/load(), a JAX-free import guarantee, family rehydration from a key, posterior sampling). Removed. The design keeps two goals: (1) a robust, SOLID/DRY API and (2) a result that does not crush memory, with the inference core a plain picklable object. Durable/cross-version persistence is out of scope (§8).

Lifecycle/layering (rounds 2–3). The mode is a fit() option, not model spec; Phase 1 owns prediction-state construction and cache-dropping, Phase 3 only consumes; the predictor is mode-specific (never eagerly cloned); the no-retention invariant is framed by banned owners/attributes, not array shapes; pickle is same-version/transient.

Interface & correctness (round 4). result="inference" returns a distinct narrower type (GAMInferenceResult) via @overload, not a partially-disabled GAMResults. Stripping uses a copy_for_prediction() hook; Phase 3 predict is CPU/NumPy; the mode keyword is keyword-only.

Tightening (round 5). Two result types; Vp required; defensive-copy read-only on coefficients/Vp; null-deviance DRY rewrite deferred (left byte-identical by not touching it).

Honesty pass (round 6). Nine fixes after a parity-focused review: (1) copy_for_prediction() also drops penalty caches (_S/_penalties) — verified: no predict_matrix reads them (tprs.py:599, tensor.py:365–374,517–533, cubic.py:419, random_effects.py:222), and tensor _penalties are O(n_coefs²) (often the dominant cost). The round-5 "drop _X, keep everything else" was wrong (§7). (2) offset_was_nonzero is an explicit GAMPredictor field, not pulled off the one-method Protocol (§5.3, §6). (3) the public read-only guarantee is downgraded to exactly "coefficients and Vp are read-only" (§5.3, §9). (4) PredictSpec is owned as the explicit Phase-1→Phase-3 boundary value object (_predict_spec, reversing round-5's Protocol-typed field — pickle exposes the concrete type anyway); the DIP claim is softened and the Protocol survives only as predict_core's parameter seam (§5.1, §9). (5) ModelSetup's PredictSpec is lazy (§5.2), and tests add direct R parity for the inference/pickled path (§12.2). (6) the family snapshot has one owner — _from_fit, after put_theta finalizes theta — distinct from api.py's pre-fit NB copy (§5.3, §11.2). (7) the user-facing flag is result="full"|"inference" (names the outcome). (8) the summary() CQS change is deferred out of scope (§9, §10.3). (9) the @overload typing claim is editor-aid-only unless make typecheck is added (§12.5).

Contract precision (round 7). Eight fixes after an implementability review: (1) offset is removed from the direct-R hard gate — RBridge has no offset argument at fit or predict (r_bridge.py:241,1068), and offset parity is covered transitively (§12.2.1b). (2) GP overrides copy_for_prediction() to drop _E_knot — an O(n_knots²) setup-only cache not read by predict (gaussian_process.py:206 vs _build_design/predict_matrix at :163,253); at that round it was considered a result-retention miss, corrected in round 10 (§7.2). (3) offset_was_nonzero is removed from PredictSpec (the builder never reads it) — it lives only on GAMPredictor/setup (§5.2). (4) the public result= kwarg collides with the internal optimizer-output result (the optimizer-output local and _from_fit parameter); internal renames (fit_result, result_mode) are required (§11.2). (5) the lazy PredictSpec on a frozen ModelSetup (design.py:81) uses a field(init=False) cache + object.__setattr__, not cached_property (§5.2, §6). (6) stdlib pickle is the public default; cloudpickle (only for locally-defined custom links) stays dev-only — persistence is downstream's concern, not a runtime dep (§8). (7) family is described as a snapshot, not "read-only family" (§5.3). (8) predict_core stays private; at that round inference/ exported GAMPredictor plus a PredictMatrixBuilder Protocol for typing, which round 10 subsequently cut (§5.1, §11.1).

Consistency & implementability polish (rounds 8–9). No design changes — doc-internal fixes after two verification passes against the repo: the direct-R link example is now a bridge-expressible key — Gamma(link="log") (the existing gamma_log, r_bridge.py:213, rpy2-only with a bridge.mode != "rpy2" skip-guard per test_gaussian_process.py:93) — rather than the unwired poisson(link="identity") (§12.2.1b); _E_knot is listed in every banned-cache enumeration and gaussian_process.py added to the modified-file list (§11.2); fitting/* is correctly labeled Phase 2 (§11.3); stdlib pickle is stated as the public default over cloudpickle (§8); and _X is restored to every drop/absence summary to match the hard gate (§4.2).

Subtraction pass (round 10). Seven changes after an independent verification pass re-derived §2.1 from the code rather than from the doc. The central claim held (no predict_matrix reads _S/_penalties/_E_knot), but the rounds had been purely additive — round 10 removes rather than patches. (1) GP's _E_knot is a dead store, not a retention problem: it is assigned at gaussian_process.py:206, cleared at :209, and read nowhere in jaxgam/. It is 89% of the GP baseline footprint (32.0 MB of 36.08 MB at n=5000), so result="full" leaks it too. Freed unconditionally at the end of GP setup() by a separate one-line prerequisite commit (B0); the copy_for_prediction() override is retained as defense-in-depth, no longer load-bearing (§2.1, §7.2, §13, §14). (2) the PredictMatrixBuilder Protocol is cut — after §6's delegation, ModelSetup and PredictSpec are not two implementations but one implementation and a forwarder; predict_core is typed directly on PredictSpec (§5.1, §6, §9, §11.1). (3) the lean type exposes smooth_info/term_names (all-scalar metadata already carried by PredictSpec) so edf is interpretable off a GAMInferenceResult — zero bytes (§5.4, §5.5). (4) formula was about to become a ninth stored duplicate (on both GAMPredictor and _FitDiagnostics); the lean type reads it as a property (§5.4, §5.5). (5) the design reduces retention, not peak — stated explicitly rather than implied (§1.1, §3.2). (6) a _jaxgam_version stamp + __setstate__ mismatch warning makes the same-version pickle contract detectable instead of silent (§8) — a guardrail, not the versioned format that stays out of scope. (7) setup.penalties (CompositePenalty, embedded (total_p, total_p)) added to the §2.1 inventory so the Metric-#3 delta is fully attributable. Citation drift fixed: one registry line and one result-test line.
