docs.title: 2.2 Near-duplicate scans
docs.text:
Two scans were run, both over functions with at least 15 body lines. - Token scan: token 5-gram Jaccard, which finds copy-paste. - Structural scan: normalised-AST SequenceMatcher ratio, which finds "same algorithm, renamed".

Representative results:

Pair Structural Token fitting/efs_theta.py::_conditional_theta_nll_jit ↔ fitting/stream/nb_theta.py::objective 0.98 — fitting/efs_regular_pirls.py::midpoint ↔ fitting/pirls.py::midpoint 0.98 — execution/stream/nb_reml.py::evaluate ↔ execution/stream/reml.py::evaluate 0.97 — execution/stream/nb.py::scan_at ↔ execution/stream/regular.py::scan_at 0.96 — execution/efs.py::_run_efs_known_scale (175 L) ↔ _run_efs_unknown_scale (192 L) 0.86 — execution/stream/reml.py::optimize_regular_stream_reml ↔ execution/stream/nb_reml.py::optimize_nb_stream_reml 0.72 — execution/stream/reml.py::evaluate_regular_stream_reml (195 L) ↔ execution/stream/nb_reml.py::evaluate_nb_stream_reml (193 L) 0.80 0.36 fitting/family_execution.py::batch_saturated_loglikelihood ↔ fitting/stream/kernels.py::saturated_loglik_reduction 0.80 0.42 execution/operator/efs_controller.py::_indexed_poisson_score_bound ↔ _indexed_gaussian_score_bound — 0.68 execution/operator/efs_controller.py::_run_operator_efs (284 L) ↔ execution/efs.py::_run_efs_known_scale 0.42 — fitting/efs_regular_pirls.py::_efs_regular_pirls_loop_jit ↔ fitting/pirls.py::_pirls_loop_jit 0.12 —

Exact helper copies: _factor_inverse_residual is identical in execution/stream/reml.py and execution/stream/nb_reml.py; _link_name is near-identical in execution/stream/nb.py and fitting/stream/nb_reml.py.

The low PIRLS and operator-EFS ratios matter. Most of the duplication is algorithmic, not textual: the same R procedure is re-derived with different names and data access. A copy-paste linter alone will not find it.

docs.title: 2.3 Observed drift between ports
docs.text:
• efsudr ratio order. fitting/efs.py::efs_raw_update computes phi * numerator / max(0, q). execution/operator/efs_controller.py::_raw_ratio computes numerator / max(0, q) * phi. Both claim pinned efsudr order, and they can differ in the last bit.
  • Family allowlists. Between 36 and 43 isinstance(family, (Gaussian|Poisson|…)) checks in execution/ and fitting/ per line, instead of capability queries; on main after the merge there are 46. The family capability contract exists so that such allowlists are not needed.
  • Host control flow in fitting/. fitting/newton.py::NewtonOptimizer (while loops with bool(jnp.isfinite(...)) host pulls) and fitting/data.py::FittingData.from_setup (NumPy preparation) break the "fitting/ is JIT-only" rule. The scaling plan's audit already noted this. At the time of the October measurement nothing in fitting/ imported execution/ or host SciPy. On main after the merge there is one such import: fitting/data.py::_structural_penalty_roots imports structural_rank from execution/qr.py inside the function, to avoid a circular import. Phase 2 should remove it.
  • Misleading pairs. fitting/reml.py is the dense criterion. execution/stream/reml.py is the streamed driver and does not use it; its kernels are in fitting/stream/reml.py. The same holds for execution/stream/nb_reml.py ↔ fitting/stream/nb_reml.py.

docs.title: 2.4 Root cause
docs.text:
There is no shared interface between "how data is accessed" and "which mgcv algorithm runs on it". EFS has one (EFSFitProvider), and that is why dense and streamed EFS share a controller. Everything else couples: - data access (in-memory X, RowSource batches, discrete tables, operators); - coefficient solving (Cholesky, positive QR, signed QR, PCG, Sl.fitChol); - the inner loop; - the outer optimizer.

All four are coupled in each route.

docs.title: 3. Decision: keep GAM; BAM features are strategies, not a replacement
docs.text:
Deprecating the dense gam() path in favour of a BAM-only design was considered and rejected:

  1. Different estimator. bam's performance iteration re-estimates smoothing parameters on a working model at each IRLS step. For non-Gaussian families its fixed point differs from gam's Laplace-REML optimum, and it is not guaranteed to converge. Only Gaussian/identity is equivalent.
  2. Discretization is an approximation. bam(discrete=TRUE) changes the fitted model.
  3. The correctness contract is gam parity. AGENTS.md, the validation matrix and all published PRs validate against pinned gam at STRICT.
  4. mgcv keeps both deliberately: gam is exact and usually faster at moderate n; bam is for data that does not fit.

BAM's distinctive pieces remain opt-in strategies on the shared engine: performance iteration (smoothing_strategy="working_model_reml"), fREML working-model criterion, and discretization (execution="discrete").

docs.title: 4. Goals and non-goals
docs.text:
Goals

  1. One implementation per mgcv procedure:
  2. PIRLS step control;
  3. each outer optimizer (newton, exact L-BFGS-B plus newton() completion, efsudr, bgam.fitd);
  4. REML score assembly from sufficient statistics;
  5. the efsudr update;
  6. each NB theta strategy;
  7. the saturated log-likelihood.
  8. Data access behind one provider interface. Dense becomes the in-memory provider, not a separate stack.
  9. Capability-driven routing. Families, providers and solvers declare capabilities, and the router derives a FitPlan. No family-name allowlists.
  10. An honest boundary. fitting/ holds only pure JIT kernels; host loops live in execution/. Both are enforced by tests.
  11. Bit-identical numerics. Every unification is proven by before/after equality of fit outputs, not by tolerance.
  12. Guardrails (architecture tests plus duplicate-code lint) so the duplication does not come back.

Non-goals

  • No public API change. GAM, FitControl, result types and execution_route labels are preserved. The labels become derived from the FitPlan.
  • No numerical change. Tolerances, oracle tests and digest-bound allowances are untouched. Where two current ports disagree (§2.3), the plan picks the one that matches pinned R and proves every affected STRICT gate still passes. That is the only permitted output change, and it must be documented per case.
  • No new features, families, solvers or performance work.
  • No change to Phase 1 (setup) or Phase 3 (post-estimation), beyond consuming a unified result builder.

docs.title: 5. Target architecture
docs.text:
jaxgam/api.py                  GAM facade: validate → plan → execute → build result
jaxgam/execution/routing.py    capability matching → FitPlan(provider, solver, inner, optimizer, uncertainty)
jaxgam/execution/optimizers/   host controllers, one per mgcv outer algorithm
    newton.py                    gam.outer/newton(); exact or finite-difference curvature from the provider
    exact_lbfgs.py               bounded L-BFGS-B + shared newton() completion (pinned and free)
    efs.py                       efsudr, incl. scale and theta options and uncertain score comparisons
    performance_iteration.py     bgam.fitd (working-model Sl.fitChol steps, estimate.theta nuisance)
    completion.py                shared newton() acceptance (today's _newton_model_rejection and friends)
jaxgam/execution/inner/        one PIRLS host driver; nuisance (theta/scale) strategies
    pirls.py                     the step-control policy, parameterised by provider + solver + system
    theta.py                     joint-REML, conditional (estimate.theta) and EFS in-PIRLS theta
jaxgam/execution/providers/    data access; each implements FitProvider
    in_memory.py                 today's dense X/FittingData path
    stream.py                    RowSource batches (regular and NB), replay/lineage checks
    gaussian_qr.py               frozen Gaussian QR statistics (PR9)
    discrete.py                  compressed tables / discrete operators (PR11)
    operator.py                  matvec/Krylov providers, arrowhead/indexed (PR12/EFS6)
jaxgam/execution/solvers/      coefficient-system solvers behind CoefficientSolver
    cholesky.py  qr.py  signed_qr.py  pcg.py  working_model.py (Sl.fitChol, pinned DPSTRF)
jaxgam/execution/uncertainty/  selected and bulk variance (PR13), Fisher/observed factors
jaxgam/fitting/                pure JAX kernels only (no host loops, no I/O, no SciPy)
    family/ (link/variance/deviance/derivative kernels), pirls_step.py, penalty_ops.py,
    reml_terms.py (score from sufficient statistics), efs_update.py, linalg actions (qr/signed_qr),
    the route kernels: stream/, discrete/, operator/, gaussian_qr/

Today execution/ and fitting/ are grouped by route, not by role: execution/stream/, execution/discrete/, execution/operator/ and execution/gaussian_qr/ each hold one route's drivers, and fitting/ has the same four folders for its kernels. Each provider above is carved out of the matching route folder; the optimizers, the inner driver and the solvers are what the route folders have in common.

Dependency rule: api → routing → optimizers → inner → providers/solvers → fitting. Nothing in fitting/ imports execution/. Providers and solvers never import optimizers. Phase-1 modules never import JAX (already enforced).

docs.title: 5.1 Core interfaces
docs.text:
These are typed Protocols and frozen dataclasses, following existing JaxGAM style. The names are indicative; the existing EFSFitProvider is the seed.

class FitProvider(Protocol):
    capabilities: ProviderCapabilities  # exact_gradient, exact_hessian, hessian_vector,
                                        # approximate_score (with error bound), replayable,
                                        # memory model, supported solver kinds
    def start(self, request: StartRequest) -> FitState: ...
    def fit(self, request: FitRequest, warm: FitState | None) -> FitState:
        """Reconverged coefficients at (rho, theta, phi) via the plan's inner loop and solver."""
    def score(self, state: FitState) -> ScoreTerms:
        """Exact score terms, or an estimate plus an error bound."""
    def gradient(self, state: FitState) -> np.ndarray: ...  # adjoint / exact derivative
    def curvature(self, state: FitState) -> Curvature | None: ...  # exact Hessian, HVP, or None
    def efs_statistics(self, state: FitState) -> EFSStatistics: ...  # d, t, q (+ bounds)
    def work(self) -> WorkCounters: ...  # scans, batches, PIRLS passes, refits, timings

class CoefficientSolver(Protocol):
    kind: Literal["cholesky", "qr", "signed_qr", "pcg", "working_model"]
    def factor(self, system: WorkingSystem) -> Factor: ...
    def solve(self, factor: Factor, rhs) -> ...: ...
    def log_determinant(self, factor: Factor) -> ...: ...
    def traces(self, factor: Factor, penalties) -> ...: ...

class Optimizer(Protocol):
    def run(self, provider: FitProvider, start: FitState,
            control: OptimizerControl) -> OptimizationResult: ...
  • FitState is observation-independent: β, ρ, θ, φ, factors, the fit fingerprint and lineage. Providers own row access.
  • OptimizationResult carries truthful convergence, the stop reason, completion diagnostics and the work counters.
  • One result builder maps (FitPlan, OptimizationResult, provider diagnostics) to GAMResults, GAMInferenceResult or GAMPredictionResult.

docs.title: 5.2 How each existing route maps
docs.text: Today FitPlan dense gam() REML in-memory provider + cholesky solver + PIRLS (Fisher/observed system per family capability) + newton optimizer (exact AD Hessian) streamed fixed sp stream provider + qr/signed_qr solver + PIRLS + no optimizer (or the pinned-scale/theta completion only) streamed exact REML (#68) stream provider + qr/signed_qr + PIRLS + exact_lbfgs (+ completion) Gaussian frozen QR (PR9) gaussian_qr provider + qr + no PIRLS (closed form) + newton/exact_lbfgs dense or streamed EFS in-memory or stream provider + PIRLS (EFS system) + efs optimizer discrete working model (PR11) discrete provider + working_model solver + performance_iteration optimizer operator fixed sp / operator EFS (PR12/EFS6) operator provider + pcg solver + PIRLS + efs optimizer (score comparison may return "uncertain") bulk uncertainty (PR13) uncertainty module consuming the final FitState + provider factor/trace actions

docs.title: 5.3 Where the variation lives
docs.text:
Each difference between routes moves to exactly one place:

  • Coefficient system (Fisher vs observed vs signed): a WorkingSystem strategy chosen from family capabilities. This removes the parallel PIRLS loops; efs_regular_pirls becomes PIRLS plus the EFS system and gam.fit3 scoring option.
  • Scale and theta handling: optimizer options (EFS known/unknown scale become one loop) and inner/theta.py strategies (joint REML, conditional estimate.theta, EFS in-PIRLS theta).
  • Exact vs approximate scores: ScoreTerms carries an optional error bound. Optimizers use a three-way comparison (better / worse / uncertain). This is what the operator EFS controller does today in its own copy.
  • Curvature availability: the provider capability. The newton optimizer uses the exact Hessian (in-memory AD), HVPs, or central differences of exact gradients (as the free completion in #68 already does).
  • Family/link support: capabilities only. Unsupported combinations are rejected by the router with the same messages as today.

docs.title: 6. Numerical-fidelity rules
docs.text:
1. Operation order is part of the contract. A unified kernel must reproduce the exact floating-point sequence of the implementation it replaces. Where routes legitimately differ in order (e.g. gam.fit3 vs gam.fit4 scoring), the difference becomes an explicit, named strategy, not an accident.
  2. Bit-identity first. Every unification PR runs the fingerprint harness (plan Phase 0) before and after. All fitted fields of the validation matrix and the execution tests must be bitwise identical, on host and on pinned Linux. Any intended exception (§2.3 drift) is listed per case with its R comparison, and must keep every STRICT gate.
  3. No tolerance edits. tests/tolerances.py, digest-bound allowances and oracle tests are not modified. A failing gate means the refactor is wrong.
  4. R references stay typed rpy2. No new oracles are needed; existing gates are the regression net.

docs.title: 7. Guardrails
docs.text:
• Architecture test (tests/test_architecture.py). It checks:
  • fitting/ never imports execution/, host scipy, sqlite3 or file I/O;
  • Phase-1 packages never import JAX;
  • providers and solvers never import optimizers;
  • no isinstance(<family>, <concrete family>) in execution/ or fitting/ outside a short reviewed allowlist (target: empty).
  • Duplicate-code lint. A make lint step runs a duplicate detector, pylint duplicate-code or jscpd, chosen in Phase 0. It starts in report-only mode against a committed baseline and becomes blocking in the final phase.
  • Review checklist (in docs/unify_fit/ and the PR template): a new execution mode implements FitProvider, or a solver or strategy, and must not add a controller or PIRLS loop.
  • AGENTS.md: propose wording for the user to apply, covering the layers, the dependency rule and "extend via providers". Agents do not edit AGENTS.md themselves.

docs.title: 8. Risks
docs.text: Risk Mitigation Behaviour change in the validated v1.0 dense path Do the dense → in-memory-provider step last, behind bitwise fingerprints and the full validation matrix Hidden operation-order dependence breaks STRICT parity Fingerprint harness at every step; one unification per PR; keep the old path behind an internal switch until the fingerprint matches, then delete it in the same PR series JIT recompilation or performance regressions from extra indirection Keep kernels monomorphic and jitted at the same boundaries; record compile counts and §8 benchmark timings before and after; abstractions live on the host side Large churn conflicts with other work Start only after all current lines are published; the unification series is the only active work Over-abstraction Interfaces are extracted from the existing EFS provider and real routes, not designed speculatively; each protocol method has at least two implementations

docs.title: 9. Open questions (resolve in Phase 0)
docs.text:
1. Duplicate-detector tool: pylint duplicate-code (already Python tooling) or jscpd (token-based, faster). Confirm the threshold and baseline format.
  2. FittingData: should it become the in-memory provider's internal state, or stay as a shared Phase-1→2 transfer type? Decide from its current call sites.
  3. Retiring optimize_stream_reml (canonical known-scale): retire it outright, or keep it as a mode of exact_lbfgs. Its regime is a strict subset of optimize_regular_stream_reml.
  4. The two §2.3 port disagreements: which order matches pinned efsudr? Verify against R/gam.fit4.r 1.9-3 before unifying.
  5. Sub-packages by route first? (raised 2026-11-20; decided and done the same day) fitting/, execution/ and formula/ were grouped into sub-packages by route (stream/, discrete/, operator/ and, in the first two, gaussian_qr/) in one move-only change; dense and shared modules stay at the top of each package. It replaced the renames that plan Phase 2 item 1 listed, removed the module names that existed in both packages without being a pair, and makes each route folder the starting point of the matching provider in §5.

docs.title: Unified Fitting Engine: Implementation Plan
docs.text:
Design reference: design.md

When: start only after the current body of work is complete (see Entry criteria). This series must be the only active work on the stack, so that every step composes once.

Shape: a sequence of PRs, one logical unification each, starting from main (the stacked PRs this plan was written against were merged into main as one squash commit, #87). Each PR proves bit-identical numerics. Nothing is merged without the user.

docs.title: Entry criteria
docs.text:
All of the following must hold before Phase 0 starts:

  1. PR9, PR11 (incl. its NB estimate.theta, approximation and runtime studies), PR12, EFS6 and PR13 are composed, published as stacked PRs and native-CI green.
  2. The scaling plan's §8 performance and numerical acceptance gates are met and recorded.
  3. verify_active_stack.py (or its successor) passes: every head, base edge and native-stack position is verified.
  4. No other implementation branch is in flight.

Status (2026-11-20): criteria 1 and 2 are met: that work was consolidated and merged into main as pull request #87 (commit e919938) with CI green, after the acceptance measurements were taken. Criterion 3 belonged to the stacked-PR workflow and no longer applies; the equivalent check is that Phase 0 starts from main. Criterion 4 must be checked again when Phase 0 starts.

docs.title: Project tooling
docs.text:
Per AGENTS.md, use uv and make; never call python or pytest directly.

Task Command Install make install Lint (ruff, format, vulture; later the duplicate check) make lint Focused local tests uv run pytest <path> -x --tb=short Full pinned suite (R 4.5.2 + mgcv 1.9-3, one BLAS thread) make test / make docker-build then docker run --rm … Focused pinned file make test-file FILE=…

Further rules: - R comparisons use typed rpy2 RBridge only. No saved fixtures, raw evidence or local diagnostic scripts are tracked. - The fingerprint harness below is tooling and is tracked; its outputs are not.

docs.title: Global rules for every PR in this series
docs.text:
1. One logical unification per PR. PR title format: [phase2] execution: … or [refactor] fitting: ….
  2. Bit-identity gate. Run make fit-fingerprint (Phase 0) on the PR base and on the PR head, on the host and on the pinned Linux image. Every fingerprinted field must be byte-identical.
  3. Any intended difference must be listed in the PR body, per case, with its pinned-R comparison still at the original tolerance class. The only expected case is the §2.3 drift in the design.
  4. No tolerance, oracle or digest edits. If a gate fails, the refactor is wrong.
  5. Full pinned Linux suite and native CI green. Branch coverage must not fall below the base. New modules need >80%.
  6. Delete as you go. A PR that introduces the unified path removes the replaced implementation in the same PR. No dead parallel copies survive a merge point.
  7. Record the reduction. Report line counts and duplicate-scan results for the touched modules, before and after.
  8. JIT tests. Any changed Phase-2 kernel keeps or gains a compile-and-run test. Record compile counts on the fingerprint cases; a regression needs justification.

docs.title: Phase 0: Baseline, harness and guardrails (no production change)
docs.text: Goal: make every later step measurable and protected.

docs.title: 0.1 Fingerprint harness
docs.text:
Add scripts/fit_fingerprint.py and make fit-fingerprint. The harness: - runs a fixed, runtime-generated case list over every route, family/link and mode that the validation matrix covers (dense, stream fixed-sp, exact REML, Gaussian QR, EFS dense/stream, discrete, operator, bulk uncertainty); - writes a SHA-256 per result field (coefficients, smoothing parameters, scale, theta, score, EDF, fitted values, SEs, convergence fields, work counters) to a local JSON outside the repo; - in --compare A B mode, diffs two checkouts, as benchmark_scaling.py --checkout does today: commit and dirty-tree provenance per child, refusing mixed provenance.

Tests cover the harness itself: deterministic output, provenance refusal and diff reporting.

docs.title: 0.2 Architecture test, report-only
docs.text: Add tests/test_architecture.py, with an AST import scan and a scan for isinstance checks against concrete family classes. - Enforced now: fitting/ never imports execution/, host scipy, sqlite3 or file I/O; Phase-1 packages have no JAX. These hold on main with one exception to allowlist and then remove in Phase 2: fitting/data.py::_structural_penalty_roots imports execution/qr.py inside the function. - Recorded as an explicit allowlist: the current host-loop exceptions (fitting/newton.py::NewtonOptimizer, fitting/data.py preparation) and the current family isinstance sites (36–43 per line in October 2026; 46 on main after the merge). Later phases shrink the allowlist to empty.

docs.title: 0.3 Duplicate-code check, report-only
docs.text: Choose pylint duplicate-code or jscpd (design §9 Q1) and add it to make lint in report mode, with a committed baseline. Also commit the structural scan used in design §2.2, normalised-AST similarity over functions with at least 15 body lines, as scripts/duplicate_scan.py. The textual tools miss renamed copies.

docs.title: 0.4 Re-measure
docs.text:
Re-run the design §2 inventory on the final composed stack and update design.md §2 tables with the real starting point.

Acceptance: - the harness is deterministic across two runs on the same commit, on host and on Linux; - the architecture test and duplicate report pass in report-only mode; - the inventory is updated.

docs.title: Phase 1: Exact and near-exact duplicates (small, low risk)
docs.text:
Each item is its own commit, and the phase ships as one PR.

  1. _factor_inverse_residual: keep one copy, move it to a shared execution utility, and use it from both execution/stream/reml.py and execution/stream/nb_reml.py.
  2. _link_name: delete both copies, execution/stream/nb.py and fitting/stream/nb_reml.py. Use a family/link capability (e.g. link.name, or a capability enumerating supported streamed NB links).
  3. Saturated log-likelihood: keep one kernel and make the other call site use it. The two are fitting/family_execution.py::batch_saturated_loglikelihood and fitting/stream/kernels.py::saturated_loglik_reduction. Prove reduction-order identity by fingerprint.
  4. NB theta objective: keep one jitted NB negative log-likelihood kernel, used by fitting/efs_theta.py and fitting/stream/nb_theta.py (structural similarity 0.98).
  5. efsudr update: the operator EFS controller uses fitting/efs.py::efs_raw_update (or a NumPy wrapper over the same kernel), and _raw_ratio/_trial_rho are deleted.
  6. First resolve the phi*n/q vs (n/q)*phi order against pinned R/gam.fit4.r::efsudr (1.9-3).
  7. The non-matching route's change is the one documented exception. Its R gates must stay STRICT.
  8. Score-bound helpers: make _indexed_poisson_score_bound, _indexed_gaussian_score_bound and _arrowhead_poisson_score_bound one family-generic bound, parameterised by family capability terms.

Acceptance: global rules. Fingerprint identical except item 5's documented case.

docs.title: Phase 2: Names and boundary moves (mechanical)
docs.text:
1. Renames: done, by a different route. This item proposed renaming the exact streamed REML drivers so that their names no longer suggested a pair with the dense kernels in fitting/reml.py. The move into route sub-packages on 2026-11-20 (design §9, question 5) settled it: the drivers are execution/stream/reml.py and execution/stream/nb_reml.py, beside their kernels fitting/stream/reml.py and fitting/stream/nb_reml.py. Check the remaining same-named pairs (efs.py, qr.py and regular.py, nb_theta.py, efs_provider.py across packages) for a kernel/driver relationship that does not exist.
  2. Move host code out of fitting/:
  3. NewtonOptimizer's host loop moves to execution/optimizers/newton.py. Its jitted derivative pieces stay in fitting/newton.py, renamed to reflect that they are kernels.
  4. FittingData.from_setup NumPy preparation moves to execution/providers/in_memory.py, or stays as a transfer type, per design §9 Q2.
  5. Re-export shims: add them only where something outside the package imports the old path. Check jaxgam/__init__.py, docs and benchmark scripts. Internal modules get no shims.
  6. Architecture test: remove the host-loop exceptions from its allowlist.

Acceptance: global rules (pure moves, so the fingerprint must be identical). git log --follow history is preserved by using git mv.

docs.title: Phase 3: Provider and solver interfaces (adapters, no behaviour change)
docs.text:
1. Introduce the interfaces: FitProvider, ProviderCapabilities, FitState, CoefficientSolver, WorkingSystem and OptimizationResult (design §5.1). Generalise the existing EFSFitProvider/EFSFitRequest/EFSControllerContext rather than adding a parallel set.
  2. Wrap existing data access as providers, delegating to today's functions:
  3. in_memory (dense);
  4. stream, regular and NB (pirls.py, regular.py and nb.py in execution/stream/);
  5. gaussian_qr (PR9);
  6. discrete (PR11);
  7. operator (PR12/EFS6).
  8. Wrap the solvers: cholesky, qr, signed_qr, pcg, and working_model (Sl.fitChol with the pinned DPSTRF host factor).
  9. Contract tests for each provider:
  10. exact gradient vs finite differences of the score at STRICT where exact;
  11. replay determinism;
  12. work-counter monotonicity;
  13. the capability flags truthfully reflect implemented methods.

Acceptance: global rules. Routes are not yet switched, so the fingerprint is identical.

docs.title: Phase 4: One EFS optimizer
docs.text:
1. Merge the two dense loops. _run_efs_known_scale and _run_efs_unknown_scale become execution/optimizers/efs.py, with scale handling as an option. Preserve each loop's exact step and scale-update order, as named branches where they differ.
  2. Fold in the operator controller. _run_operator_efs becomes the same optimizer plus a provider whose ScoreTerms carries an error bound. The optimizer's three-way comparison (better / worse / uncertain) reproduces the operator controller's "retain accepted state on uncertain comparisons" policy and its calibration boundaries.
  3. Delete the old loops and OperatorEFSFitProvider (now a FitProvider).

Acceptance: - global rules; - every EFS gate passes (dense, stream, operator, p257–512 calibration, test_validation_matrix.py -k efs), with an identical fingerprint; - EFS controller code is roughly halved; record the actual figure.

docs.title: Phase 5: One exact streamed REML optimizer
docs.text:
1. Merge the evaluators. evaluate_regular_stream_reml and evaluate_nb_stream_reml become one evaluator, with theta as an optional coordinate supplied by the provider.
  2. Merge the drivers. optimize_regular_stream_reml and optimize_nb_stream_reml become one exact_lbfgs optimizer. It keeps the shared pinned-first newton() completions (pinned scale/theta, free m≤4) and their routing precedence. The completion helpers move to optimizers/completion.py.
  3. Merge preflight. _preflight_regular_reml and _preflight_nb_reml become one capability-driven preflight.
  4. Canonical driver: retire optimize_stream_reml (canonical known-scale), or keep it as a mode, per design §9 Q3. Either way it shares the evaluator.

Acceptance: - global rules; - every streamed REML, NB theta-mode, completion-routing and forced-stop test passes with an identical fingerprint; - #67/#68 public parity cells unchanged.

docs.title: Phase 6: One PIRLS driver
docs.text:
1. Extract the step policy. Create fitting/pirls_step.py for the pure kernels (step, midpoint, divergence/domain recovery) and execution/inner/pirls.py for the host driver. The policy covers gam.fit3/gam.fit4 step halving, divergence and domain recovery, and convergence.
  2. Make the system a strategy. WorkingSystem selects Fisher, observed, signed, or the EFS system with gam.fit3 scoring. Choose it from family capabilities.
  3. Port the inner loops one at a time, each as its own commit with a fingerprint check:
  4. dense fitting/pirls.py;
  5. fitting/efs_regular_pirls.py;
  6. streamed canonical (execution/stream/pirls.py);
  7. streamed signed (execution/stream/regular.py);
  8. streamed NB (execution/stream/nb.py);
  9. operator (execution/operator/fit.py);
  10. discrete working model (PR11).

Fused lax.while_loop kernels stay fused where they are today. The unification is in the step-policy functions they call, not in turning jitted loops into host loops. 4. Theta strategies. Move the nuisance theta strategies to execution/inner/theta.py: joint REML, conditional estimate.theta, and EFS in-PIRLS theta.

Acceptance: - global rules, with an identical fingerprint for every route; - JIT compile counts unchanged or justified; - the PIRLS-loop count goes from about 7 to 1 driver plus strategies; record it.

docs.title: Phase 7: Newton over providers; dense becomes the in-memory provider
docs.text:
1. Generalise the newton optimizer. execution/optimizers/newton.py takes curvature from the provider: exact AD Hessian (in-memory), HVP, or central differences of exact gradients.
  2. Route dense through the engine. Dense gam() becomes in-memory provider + cholesky + PIRLS + newton, and the dense-specific orchestration is deleted. This is the highest-risk step: it touches the validated v1.0 path, so it runs last of the numerical phases.
  3. PR9. optimize_gaussian_qr_lbfgs becomes the gaussian_qr provider plus newton/exact_lbfgs.
  4. PR11. The performance-iteration controller (advance_*_working_model) becomes optimizers/performance_iteration.py over the discrete provider and working_model solver.

Acceptance: - global rules; - the complete validation matrix and the v1.0 dense R gates pass with an identical fingerprint on host and Linux; - §8 benchmark timings within noise of the baseline, recorded.

docs.title: Phase 8: Routing and results
docs.text:
1. Router. Add execution/routing.py, which builds a FitPlan from FitControl, family capabilities and provider/solver capabilities. The api.py route functions (_fit_stream_*, _fit_operator*, _fit_discrete, _fit_fixed_sp, …) collapse into validate → plan → execute → build result.
  2. execution_route and lambda_strategy labels are derived from the plan.
  3. Rejection messages are preserved; add a test per message.
  4. Results. One result builder replaces the per-route constructors (_from_stream_state and siblings).
  5. Routing tests. A table-driven test covers every FitControl × family × sp-mode cell, asserting the selected plan and the label.

Acceptance: - global rules; - the public API is unchanged: same signatures, same result fields; - every route-selection, rejection and validation test passes.

docs.title: Phase 9: Lock in
docs.text:
1. Blocking guardrails. Switch the duplicate-code check to blocking. Shrink the architecture-test allowlists to empty, or to a reviewed and justified minimum.
  2. Docs. Update the architecture pages under docs/architecture/ and docs/api.md where internals are described. Add the review checklist from design §7.
  3. AGENTS.md. Propose wording to the user covering the layers, the dependency rule and "extend via FitProvider/solver/strategy, never by copying a controller or PIRLS loop". The user applies it.
  4. Final report. Before/after line counts per package, duplicate-scan results, compile counts and benchmark timings.

Acceptance: - full pinned Linux suite and native CI green; - fingerprint identical to the Phase-0 baseline, apart from the documented Phase-1 item 5 case; - guardrails blocking.

docs.title: Sequencing and rough size
docs.text:
Phase PRs Risk Depends on 0 Harness and guardrails 1 low entry criteria 1 Exact duplicates 1 low 0 2 Renames and moves 1 low 1 3 Interfaces and adapters 1–2 medium 2 4 EFS optimizer 1 medium 3 5 Exact REML optimizer 1 medium 3 6 PIRLS driver 2–3 (one per inner-loop group) high 3 (4 and 5 recommended first) 7 Newton and dense provider 1–2 high 6 8 Routing and results 1 medium 7 9 Lock in 1 low 8

Phases 4 and 5 are independent and may be developed in parallel worktrees, but they publish in order.

Rollback: each PR is self-contained and deletes only what it replaces, so reverting the PR restores the previous path. Do not start a phase until the previous one is published and native-green.
